nodes.label: Cyber Resilience Act (CRA)
nodes.rationale: Applicable to TinyTask as manufacturer of a digital product (SaaS) placed on EU market. 26 clauses in scope. Key quantitative thresholds: 5-year support period (Art. 13(8)), 10-year security update retention (Art. 13(9)), 10-year documentation retention (Art. 13(13)).

nodes.label: CRA Quantitative Thresholds
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(8): 5-year minimum support period per release. Art. 13(9): 10-year security update retention. Art. 13(13): 10-year technical documentation retention. These are absolute floors that do not scale with company size.

nodes.label: DomainCoverageEntry (AEGIS Class)

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32 Processor Obligations
nodes.rationale: Art. 32 applies directly to both controllers AND processors. TinyTask as processor has NativeCompliance obligations (encryption, access control, breach notification) — not merely InheritedCompliance via DPA. Art. 33(2) processor→controller notification is 'without undue delay' (suggested 4-8h internal).

nodes.label: Inherited Compliance

nodes.label: Native Compliance

nodes.label: AG-D-04.3-002: Regulatory Notification (CRA-driven)
nodes.rationale: Anchor goal for T-001. Highest-priority SG in the case and only HIGH-risk profile: internal notification workflow runs on max-SLA 24h routing so shorter of two regulatory deadlines governs the single internal clock.

nodes.label: AG-D-09.1-002: Information Security Policies (CRA-driven)
nodes.rationale: Dual-coverage with AG-D-09.1-001; same policy architecture discharges both. Technical documentation retention is 10 years or support period whichever is longer (CRA Art. 13(13)). Normalised Intensity 2.500 authoritative per Sprint 4 reconciliation.

nodes.label: AG-D-09.2-002: Impact & Risk Assessments (CRA-driven)
nodes.rationale: Dual-coverage with AG-D-09.2-001; same assessment framework serves both per T-M-001.

nodes.label: T-001: Notification Timing Difference
nodes.rationale: HIGH-severity timing tension: GDPR 72h vs CRA 24h notification deadlines on same event. Resolved via single internal workflow with max-SLA 24h routing so shorter deadline governs the single clock.

nodes.label: T-002: Vendor-Management Scope
nodes.rationale: MEDIUM-severity scope tension: GDPR governs downstream data processors; CRA governs entire product supply chain. Resolved via single vendor-management template producing dual-output documentation.

nodes.label: T-003: Documentation Overlap
nodes.rationale: MEDIUM-severity requirement tension: GDPR records-of-processing vs CRA technical documentation describe same system. Resolved via unified documentation repository with retention aligned to longest regulatory floor (10 years or support period).

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28 — Processor Obligations
nodes.rationale: Art. 28(1) sufficient guarantees, Art. 28(3) mandatory DPA content, Art. 28(5) sub-processor flow-down. Governs SO-D-06.1 and SO-D-06.3.

nodes.label: T-004: Data-Protection vs Product-Security Competence
nodes.rationale: LOW-severity intensity tension: 8-person team must carry both data-protection and product-security competence. Resolved via competency matrix with separation of duties at role-documentation level.

nodes.label: OBL-D-03.4-001 Secure Default Configuration
nodes.rationale: CRA-C03 (Annex I §1(7)) sole authority; preventive complement to D-03.1 authentication; ONE_TIME setup but CONTINUOUS effect

nodes.label: OBL-D-08.1-001 Staff Security Awareness Training
nodes.rationale: GDPR-C27 (Art. 39(1)(b)); human-layer complement to technical controls; PERIODIC annual

nodes.label: OBL-D-08.2-001 Role-Specific Security Training
nodes.rationale: GDPR-C28 (Art. 47); depth-extension of awareness training; PERIODIC annual + per-joiner

nodes.label: SO-D-03.4-001: Disable Unused Ports/Services
nodes.rationale: CRA Annex I §1.3 attack-surface minimisation. CIS L1 standard. Hardened base images, security groups, feature flags defaulting to off, quarterly port-scan.

nodes.label: CNCS (Centro Nacional de Cibersegurança)
nodes.rationale: PT CSIRT for early-warning + incident coordination; receives CRA Art. 14 notifications alongside ENISA

nodes.label: D-04 Incident Response Sub-Domain
nodes.rationale: Covers full incident lifecycle: severity limitation, containment, notification, restoration; D-04.3 is the CONTEXTUAL obligation activating on compound events

nodes.label: D-05 Data Lifecycle Sub-Domain
nodes.rationale: Covers data subject lifecycle: minimisation, storage limitation, erasure, portability; all four GDPR-led; CRA only co-obligates D-05.3

nodes.label: D-10 Monitoring & Audit Sub-Domain
nodes.rationale: see-then-prove triad: monitoring (detection), logging (observational substrate), testing (verification); unverified posture equivalent to insecure posture

nodes.label: Max-SLA Routing Pattern (24h)
nodes.rationale: Use most stringent deadline (24h CRA) as internal standard for ALL notifications; single workflow generates per-recipient submissions; eliminates risk of forgetting stricter clock

nodes.label: D-01: Data Protection & Encryption
nodes.rationale: Cluster covering at-rest encryption (D-01.1), in-transit encryption (D-01.2), key management (D-01.3), and integrity (D-01.4). 3 POs + 0 SOs in Phase 2 catalog.

nodes.label: D-04: Incident Response
nodes.rationale: Cluster covering detection/triage (D-04.1), containment (D-04.2), notification (D-04.3), and recovery (D-04.4). 4 SOs.

nodes.label: Conflict CONF-001: Erasure vs Immutable Logs
nodes.rationale: PO-D-05.3 (erasure) conflicts with SO-D-10.2 (immutable logs). Resolved via cryptographic sharding: logs are anonymised (key destroyed) at retention boundary, not deleted wholesale.
nodes.norm_label: conflict conf-001: erasure vs immutable logs

nodes.label: NIST PF 1.0 (Privacy Framework)
nodes.rationale: Privacy control mapping framework. Each PO maps to 2-12 PF 1.0 controls (e.g., CT.DM-P1, PR.DS-P1, GV.PO-P1).

nodes.label: CNPD (Comissão Nacional de Proteção de Dados)
nodes.rationale: Portuguese data protection supervisory authority. Lead GDPR SA for TinyTask's PT establishment. Receives 72h breach notifications (GDPR Art. 33). Context-correct for Portuguese-domiciled SaaS (not DPB/BfDI).
nodes.norm_label: cnpd (comissao nacional de protecao de dados)

nodes.label: CONF-001 — Cryptographic Sharding (Anonymise Not Delete)
nodes.rationale: Resolution of conflict between SO-D-10.2 (log retention 7y) and PO-D-05.3 (erasure within 7d). PII scrubbed at ingest; logs retained but personal data rendered unintelligible.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 11 — Single Reporting Platform
nodes.rationale: 24h early warning, 72h notification, 14d final report. Drives the 24h internal clock in SO-D-04.3-001. ENISA is lead supervisory body.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33 — Breach Notification 72h
nodes.rationale: 72h SA notification deadline. Slower of the two deadlines (vs CRA 24h). Art. 83(5) fine exposure (€20M/4% turnover) if missed.

nodes.label: Max-SLA Routing (T-003)
nodes.rationale: Doc 09 §4 strategic tension resolution: single event record produces per-recipient submissions applying the fastest deadline (ENISA 24h) as workflow driver, with CNPD 72h as secondary.

nodes.label: OBL-D-04.1-001 Exploit Severity Limitation
nodes.rationale: CRA-C13 (Annex I §1(8)) sole authority; design-time counterpart to D-04.2 containment; ONE_TIME design but CONTINUOUS monitoring

nodes.label: OBL-D-04.2-001 Availability Restoration + DoS Resilience
nodes.rationale: GDPR-C18 + CRA-C11 jointly drive; mixed TRIGGERED + ONE_TIME; 4-hour containment playbook

nodes.label: OBL-D-04.3-001 Breach Notification (T-001)
nodes.rationale: CONTEXTUAL obligation; TRIGGERED by compound event (personal-data breach AND exploited vulnerability); max-SLA 24h routing per T-001; most time-sensitive obligation in matrix

nodes.label: OBL-D-04.4-001 Data Restoration Post-Incident
nodes.rationale: GDPR-C16 (Art. 32(1)(b)(c)); CONTINUOUS; RTO 24h, RPO 1h targets

nodes.label: OBL-D-05.1-001 Data Minimization
nodes.rationale: GDPR-C01 + CRA-C10 jointly drive; enforced at schema, application, and onboarding UX layers

nodes.label: OBL-D-05.2-001 Storage Limitation
nodes.rationale: GDPR-C02 + GDPR-C03; temporal counterpart to data minimisation; CONTINUOUS daily retention checks

nodes.label: OBL-D-05.3-001 Right to Erasure
nodes.rationale: GDPR-C06 + CRA-C16; 7-day SLA (over-compliance vs GDPR 1-month); TRIGGERED per DSAR + ONE_TIME API

nodes.label: OBL-D-05.4-001 Right to Data Portability
nodes.rationale: GDPR-C07 sole authority; 48-hour SLA (over-compliance); positive counterpart to erasure

nodes.label: OBL-D-09.4-001 Records of Processing
nodes.rationale: GDPR-C13 (Art. 30) + GDPR-C22 (Art. 33(5)); operational expression of accountability; CONTINUOUS + TRIGGERED

nodes.label: OBL-D-10.1-001 Continuous Security Monitoring
nodes.rationale: CRA-C12 sole authority; detection layer; CONTINUOUS; ENISA 24h reporting routing for exploited vulnerabilities

nodes.label: OBL-D-10.2-001 Security Audit Logging
nodes.rationale: CRA-C14 (Annex I §2(2)) sole authority; observational substrate of every other control; CONTINUOUS; 10-year retention with Object Lock

nodes.label: OBL-D-10.3-001 Regular Security Testing
nodes.rationale: GDPR-C19 + CRA-C20 jointly drive; verification layer for every other control; PERIODIC quarterly + annual

nodes.label: T-001 Notification Timing (Contextual HIGH)
nodes.rationale: TEMPORAL_CONFLICT; GDPR 72h vs CRA 24h; resolved via max-SLA routing (24h internal clock); OPERATIONAL_PROCEDURE resolution type

nodes.label: T-L-001 DORA Logs vs GDPR Erasure (INACTIVE)

nodes.norm_label: t-l-001 dora logs vs gdpr erasure (inactive)

nodes.label: PO-D-01.1-001: Personal Data at Rest Confidentiality
nodes.rationale: Structural and continuous obligation: all persistent stores must be protected at the storage layer with segregated cryptographic material management. Prerequisite for D-05.3 erasure cascading to backups.
nodes.norm_label: po-d-01.1-001: personal data at rest confidentiality

nodes.label: PO-D-01.2-001: Personal Data in Transit Confidentiality
nodes.rationale: Covers all network channels carrying personal data: ingress, egress to third-party services, and inter-component channels. Channel-classification-aligned cryptographic protection.
nodes.norm_label: po-d-01.2-001: personal data in transit confidentiality

nodes.label: PO-D-01.4-001: Personal Data Integrity
nodes.rationale: Layered integrity controls: schema-level constraints, application-boundary cryptographic checks, infrastructure redundancy. Integrity limb of GDPR Art. 5(1)(d) accuracy principle.

nodes.label: PO-D-05.3-001 Enable Complete Data Erasure
nodes.rationale: CRITICAL priority; derived from OBL-D-05.3-001; erasure workflow test within deadline

Sprint 4: Doc 07c + Track B decision table + tensions. Sprint 5: deep enrichment (74 cards × 12 fields).

nodes.label: Best Practice Rules Catalog (16 BPR)
nodes.rationale: 16 rules derived from frameworks (ISO 27001, NIST, OWASP, CIS), 15-column schema, no regulatory reporting. All P3/SHOULD. 13 NATIVE, 3 INHERITED.

nodes.norm_label: bpr-d-01.1-001 — strong symmetric encryption for data at rest

nodes.label: BPR-D-03.1-001 — Implement Role-Based Access Control
nodes.rationale: Framework: ISO 27001 A.9.2. NI=2 SHOULD. INHERITED (managed identity service). Strengthens CR-D-03.1-001 and CR-D-03.3-001.

nodes.label: BPR-D-07.1-001 — Follow NIST SSDF Secure Development
nodes.rationale: Framework: NIST SSDF PO.5.1. NI=2 SHOULD. Gives CR-D-07.1-001 a recognised structure without requiring formal SDL certification.
nodes.norm_label: bpr-d-07.1-001 — follow nist ssdf secure development

nodes.label: CR-D-01.1-001 — Data at Rest Encryption

nodes.label: CR-D-01.2-001 — Data in Transit Encryption
nodes.rationale: Operationalises OBL-D-01.2. Sources: GDPR-C15, CRA-C08. NI=3 MUST. CSF: PR.DS-02, PR.IR-01, PR.PS-04. Privacy FW: PR.DS-P2.

nodes.label: CR-D-01.3-001 — Cryptographic Key Management

nodes.label: Dual Maturity Model (CSF + Privacy)
nodes.rationale: Per D11 decision: two independent scores per control (maturity_csf, maturity_privacy). No aggregation into single score. Heatmap uses MIN(gap_csf, gap_priv) with N/A-privacy rule.

nodes.label: Consolidated Governance View (§2)
nodes.rationale: Fuses CSF GV + Privacy FW GV-P + AI RMF GOVERN into one view per SPEC §4.4. 6 governance concepts × 3 frameworks. AI RMF uniformly pending Case_02/03.

nodes.rationale: Inherited from Framework_Crosswalk_ARM.md. First/primary control listed in crosswalk used when multiple match sub-domain. 5 BPR derive from ISO 27001 controls.

nodes.label: NIST SSDF

nodes.rationale: 3 BPR derive from OWASP: ASVS V1 (BPR-D-02.1), ASVS V3 (BPR-D-07.2), Testing Guide (BPR-D-10.3-002).

nodes.label: BPR-D-03.2-001 — FIDO2 Phishing-Resistant MFA
nodes.rationale: SHOULD NI=2. Framework-derived (NIST IA-2). Maps to CSF PR.AA-03/04/05/06 + Privacy UNMAPPED_PF. FIDO2 origin binding noted. Maturity: cur 1→tgt 3 (gap 2).

nodes.label: AEGIS Methodology
nodes.rationale: Research methodology mapping 5 EU regulations to 38 security sub-domains in 3 phases (UNDERSTAND→DERIVE→DECOMPOSE). Core principle: 'Regulations are inputs, not checklists. We derive controls from obligations, not from compliance frameworks.'

nodes.label: Case_01 — TinyTask SaaS (MICRO tier)
nodes.rationale: B2B task management, 10-50 employees, 8-person team. Applicable regulations: GDPR + CRA only (2/5). 30 obligation-bearing + 1 BPR-only + 7 N/A sub-domains = 38. No AI (AI Act NOT APPLICABLE).

nodes.label: DR-002 Normative Intensity Rule (AVG)
nodes.rationale: Resolves MAX vs AVG contradiction: NI(rule) = AVG(NI(clause) for clause in source_clauses). Preserves SHOULD differentiation that MAX would eliminate (anti-pattern AP-P2-09). Bucketing: P1≥2.5 MUST, P2 2.0-2.499 SHOULD, P3<2.0 COULD.

nodes.label: Dual Maturity Model (CSF + Privacy FW)
nodes.rationale: Two independent scores per control: maturity_csf and maturity_privacy. Tiers 1-4 at program/Function level; 0-4 per-subcategory at control level. Preserves security/privacy desynchronization (D11). Heatmap uses MIN(gap_csf, gap_priv) with N/A rule.

nodes.label: CSF Frozen List Integrity Findings
nodes.rationale: CSF 2.0 frozen list declares 106 subcategories but only enumerates 98 IDs. Two referenced-but-missing IDs: ID.AM-08 (v1.1 carry-over or typo) and RS.MA-01 (v1.1→v2.0 migration to RC.RP-*). Flagged, no new IDs invented.

nodes.label: Govern Consolidated View
nodes.rationale: Fuses GV (CSF) + Govern-P (Privacy) + GOVERN (AI RMF placeholder) into unified governance objectives: mission, legal, policy, roles, risk, strategy. Doc 13 §2 deliverable.

nodes.label: Heatmap Formula (MIN gap with N/A rule)
nodes.rationale: gap_display = MIN(gap_csf, gap_priv) with N/A rule: when privacy is N/A, gap_display = gap_csf. Colours: green(0), yellow(1), orange(2), red(3-4), grey(N/A). Avoids visual artefact where unmapped privacy appears artificially low-risk.
nodes.norm_label: heatmap formula (min gap with n/a rule)

nodes.label: Sprint Pipeline (0-5 + Validator)

nodes.rationale: Determines target maturity per sub-domain: LIGHTWEIGHT→2-3, MINIMAL→2, STANDARD→3, RIGOROUS→3-4, DEFERRED→no target. Case_01 MICRO tier: most at LIGHTWEIGHT, D-02.4 DEFERRED.

nodes.label: Unified Matrix (Doc 13 §1)
nodes.rationale: Single table with rows = 38 sub-domains, columns = CSF 2.0 subcats + Privacy FW subcats + AI RMF (pending) + ISO 27001 + SSDF. Avoids triplication of layers across documents.

nodes.label: CR-D-01.1-001 — Data Encryption at Rest
nodes.rationale: MUST NI=3. Maps to CSF PR.DS-01, PR.DS-10, PR.PS-04 + Privacy PR.DS-P1. Source: GDPR Art. 5(1)(f) + Art. 32(1)(b) + CRA Art. 24. Maturity: cur 2→tgt 3 (gap 1).

nodes.label: CR-D-04.3-001 — Regulatory Breach Notification
nodes.rationale: MUST NI=3. Maps to CSF RS.CO-02, RS.MA-01/02/03 + Privacy CM.AW-P7/P8, CM.PO-P1/P2. Source: GDPR Art. 33 + CRA Art. 20. Maturity: cur 1→tgt 3 (gap 2). Largest single-area gap in D-04.x.

nodes.label: CR-D-09.4-001 — Records of Processing (RoPA)
nodes.rationale: MUST NI=3. Maps to CSF GV.PO-02, ID.AM-08 (flagged: not in frozen list), ID.RA-05 + Privacy ID.IM-P1/P4/P6/P8. Source: GDPR Art. 30. Illustrates AVG≠MAX case (GDPR-C13 NI=3 + GDPR-C22 NI=2 → AVG=2.5).

nodes.label: NIST Privacy Framework 1.0
nodes.rationale: Used for dual-maturity mapping alongside CSF 2.0. 10 PF IDs using v1.0 redirects flagged as false positives (documented as 'redirect - not used'). 1 BPR has empty privacy mapping (justified).

nodes.label: Privacy & Security Objectives Document (Doc 10)
nodes.rationale: Master compliance document defining 31 operational objectives (11 PO + 20 SO) for TinyTask, mapping GDPR and CRA obligations to verifiable security and privacy controls.

nodes.label: BPR-D-10.3-001 — Conduct Annual Penetration Testing
nodes.rationale: Framework: NIST CA-2. NI=2 SHOULD. Supplements automated testing under CR-D-10.3-001 with chained-weakness evaluation.

nodes.label: Compliance Rules Catalog (30 CR)
nodes.rationale: 30 rules derived from regulatory obligations (GDPR + CRA), 17-column schema, 1:1 mapping to obligations. 27 NATIVE, 3 INHERITED. Average NI 2.842.

nodes.label: CR-D-02.1-001 — Vulnerability-Free Release
nodes.rationale: Operationalises OBL-D-02.1. Sources: CRA-C01, CRA-C17. NI=3 MUST. Requires zero known exploitable vulnerabilities at release. ENISA 24h reporting.

nodes.label: CR-D-04.3-001 — Dual Regulatory Incident Notification
nodes.rationale: Operationalises OBL-D-04.3. Sources: GDPR-C21, GDPR-C23, CRA-C25. NI=3 MUST. Resolves Tension T-001 (24h workflow). Dual CNPD 72h + ENISA 24h max-SLA routing.

nodes.label: CR-D-05.1-001 — Data Minimisation
nodes.rationale: Operationalises OBL-D-05.1. Sources: GDPR-C01, CRA-C10. NI=3 MUST. GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation principle.

nodes.label: CR-D-09.2-001 — Unified Privacy and Cybersecurity Risk Assessment
nodes.rationale: Operationalises OBL-D-09.2. Sources: GDPR-C20, GDPR-C24, CRA-C23. NI=3 MUST. Resolves Tension T-003 (unified DPIA + cybersecurity assessment).
nodes.norm_label: cr-d-09.2-001 — unified privacy and cybersecurity risk assessment

nodes.label: DR-002 Normative Intensity Resolution (AVG rule)
nodes.rationale: DR-002 defined as AVG (not MAX). MAX kills differentiation (AP-P2-09). AVG preserves SHOULD signal. Applied retroactively to all 46 cards. Affects CR-D-01.4-001 (2.500), CR-D-09.1-001 (2.500), CR-D-03.2-001 (2.0), CR-D-05.4-001 (2.0), CR-D-08.2-001 (2.0).

nodes.label: EU AI Act
nodes.rationale: NOT APPLICABLE to TinyTask — no AI/ML systems deployed. Design decision D-003 (CONDITIONAL — pending CEO decision before any AI feature development).

nodes.label: Conditional Block B6: Supply Chain
nodes.rationale: ACTIVATED because supplyChainVisibility = Low. SBOM not started, no supplier security assessment, manual component vulnerability management. Feeds D-06 sub-domains.

nodes.label: Conditional Block B7: CRA Classification
nodes.rationale: ACTIVATED because CRA applicable. Product class: Default. Conformity regime: Self-assessment. Art. 24 exclusion confirmed. No EU certification scheme available for SaaS.

nodes.label: Conditional Block B8: Multi-Actor Role Resolution
nodes.rationale: ACTIVATED because 2+ regulations applicable AND dataRole = Mixed. Controller for account data, Processor for client content. CRA=manufacturer, GDPR=controller/processor. No native processor compliance.
nodes.norm_label: conditional block b8: multi-actor role resolution

nodes.label: Complexity Tier (MEDIUM)
nodes.rationale: Derived from: 2 regulations applicable (2-3 range), 3 active conditional blocks (2-3 range), 1 temporal conflict (1-2 range). All criteria map to MEDIUM tier.

nodes.label: CRA (Cyber Resilience Act)
nodes.rationale: Applicable to TinyTask as Manufacturer (Default class). 26 clauses, 22/38 sub-domains covered (57.9%). Mean NI: 2.923 (92.3% Weight 3). Drives vulnerability management, secure development, and supply chain obligations.

nodes.label: DORA (Digital Operational Resilience Act)
nodes.rationale: NOT APPLICABLE to TinyTask — not a financial entity. Sole authority for D-07.2, D-07.4, D-09.3 become gaps. 100% Weight 3 normative intensity (most prescriptive regulation).

nodes.label: GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation)
nodes.rationale: Applicable to TinyTask as Controller+Processor. 28 clauses, 19/38 sub-domains covered (50%). Mean NI: 2.714 (71.4% Weight 3). Drives data protection, lifecycle, and governance obligations.

nodes.label: NIS 2 (Network and Information Security Directive 2)
nodes.rationale: NOT APPLICABLE to TinyTask — below 50-employee threshold and not in Annex I/II sectors. Design decision D-002. Sole authority for D-07.3 (CI/CD Pipeline Security) becomes a gap.

nodes.label: Normative Intensity (T9)
nodes.rationale: Clause-level weight assignment (1-3) per design decision D-005. TinyTask combined: 2.778 mean NI, 81.5% Weight 3. CRA drives prescriptiveness (92.3% W3) vs GDPR flexibility (71.4% W3).

nodes.label: Sole Authority Analysis
nodes.rationale: 8/38 sub-domains (21.1%) have sole authority. For TinyTask: 4 covered (CRA/GDPR), 4 gaps (D-07.2, D-07.3, D-07.4, D-09.3 — all DORA/NIS2 exclusive). Mitigation: Level 2 frameworks (ISO 27001, NIST CSF).

nodes.label: Temporal Conflict TC-001 (CRA 24h vs GDPR 72h)
nodes.rationale: Same event (vulnerability/breach) triggers different deadlines: CRA Art. 14 = 24h, GDPR Art. 33 = 72h. Resolution: Max-SLA principle — use 24h workflow to satisfy both.

nodes.label: PG-D-05.3-001 Right to Erasure
nodes.rationale: Privacy goal for D-05.3, GDPR Art. 17, HIGH risk if not met, erasure cascades to backups

nodes.label: PG-D-06.1-001 Vendor Risk Assessment
nodes.rationale: Privacy goal for D-06.1, GDPR Art. 28(1), DPA validation against AWS/Stripe/Firebase

nodes.label: PG-D-07.1-001 Secure-by-Design Principles
nodes.rationale: Privacy goal for D-07.1, GDPR Art. 25, NIST SSDF + OWASP SAMM baseline

nodes.label: PG-D-09.2-001 Impact & Risk Assessments
nodes.rationale: Privacy goal for D-09.2, GDPR Art. 35+36, DPIA + CRA risk assessment unified dual-output, HIGH risk

nodes.label: PG-D-10.2-001 Audit Logging & Traceability
nodes.rationale: Privacy goal for D-10.2, GDPR Art. 5(2)+30, CloudTrail + tamper-evident S3, 7-year retention

nodes.label: SG-D-02.1-001 Vulnerability Identification
nodes.rationale: Security goal for D-02.1, CRA Art. 17+5, Trivy + npm audit + SAST in CI

nodes.label: SG-D-03.1-001 Identity Lifecycle Management
nodes.rationale: Security goal for D-03.1, CRA Art. 10, Firebase Auth user records lifecycle

nodes.label: SG-D-06.2-001 Software Bill of Materials
nodes.rationale: Security goal for D-06.2, CRA Art. 18(2), CycloneDX SBOM per release, 10y retention

nodes.label: SG-D-07.3-001 CI/CD Pipeline Security
nodes.rationale: Security goal for D-07.3, CRA Art. 18(2), CI gates + OIDC + pipeline-as-code

nodes.label: SG-D-10.1-001 Continuous Security Monitoring
nodes.rationale: Security goal for D-10.1, CRA Art. 12, CloudWatch + GuardDuty + AWS Config

nodes.label: AEGIS Compliance Framework
nodes.rationale: Multi-phase regulatory compliance methodology (Phase 1: Context, Phase 2: Rules, Phase 3: Decomposition) with class model, taxonomy, and gate criteria. Traced to PhD Thesis Chapter 5.

nodes.label: Auth0/Okta (Identity Provider)
nodes.rationale: Sole identity provider. MFA + password storage. DPA in place, Art. 28 compliant. SOC 2 + ISO 27001/27018. Risk: Low.

nodes.label: AWS (Cloud Infrastructure Provider)
nodes.rationale: Sole cloud provider for compute, database, object storage, and KMS. DPA in place, Art. 28 compliant. Risk: Low. Exit plan NOT documented (GAP-TPL-02).

nodes.label: CompanyContext Class
nodes.rationale: Monolithic entity (8 attributes + 30 derived) per design decision D-001. Not decomposed into RegulatoryApplicability + OperationalProfile. Simplicity over premature optimization; all attributes map to T8.4 ComplianceContext Applicability Conditions.

nodes.label: ComplementarityAnalysis Class
nodes.rationale: PERSISTENT entity (not derived query) per design decision D-006. Versioned artifact with audit trail for thesis validation. Enables reproducibility and T7 metrics (SharedScope, ComplementarityIndex, StructuralConnectedness).

nodes.label: Datadog (Monitoring/Telemetry)
nodes.rationale: Sole telemetry/detection supplier. Pseudonymised logs only. DPA in place. Risk: Medium (outage degrades D-10.1 monitoring).

nodes.label: D-001: CompanyContext Monolithic
nodes.rationale: Keep CompanyContext as monolithic entity (8 attributes + 30 derived). Rationale: simplicity over premature optimization, class model annotation states 'Manter monolítico', Phase 1 scope is input artifact not analytical construct.

nodes.label: D-006: ComplementarityAnalysis Persistent
nodes.rationale: Store as versioned artifact with audit trail (not derived query). Rationale: Phase 1 outputs must be auditable for thesis validation, enables reproducibility, T7 metrics require documented calculation basis.

nodes.label: D-008: Taxonomy Fixed (10×38)
nodes.rationale: Lock 38 sub-domains from 00_Taxonomy_Reference.md. Rationale: common vocabulary enables cross-regulation comparison, fixed taxonomy enables consistent Sub-Domain ID references, taxonomy is the 'common language' between regulations and implementation.

nodes.label: GAP-RACI-01: No Formal Security Training
nodes.rationale: MEDIUM severity. No annual security-awareness training programme in place. Linked to D-08.1. All 8 employees affected.

nodes.label: GAP-TPL-03: No Pipeline-Integrated SBOM
nodes.rationale: HIGH severity (CRA-mandated). Snyk configured but SBOM export not wired to release artefacts. Required for CRA Annex I Part II (1). Linked to D-06.2.

nodes.label: Security Maturity Model (0-4 Scale)
nodes.rationale: 5-level scale: 0=None, 1=Ad-hoc, 2=Defined, 3=Managed, 4=Optimized. TinyTask overall: 1.3 current, 2.6 target, 1.3 gap. DEPRECATED FOR MATURITY — moved to Phase 2 Doc 13.

nodes.label: AEGIS Phase 1 (Context & Regulatory Inference)
nodes.rationale: Covers CompanyContext, RegulatoryClause, ComplianceContext, ComplementarityAnalysis, ImplementationMapping. Steps: A (Company Context), B (Regulatory Mapping), C (Complementarity), D (Third-Party), E (Roles/RACI).

nodes.label: AEGIS Phase 2 (Elaboration & Secure Design)
nodes.rationale: Covers RegulatoryObligation, StrategicTension, RulesCatalog. Maturity model moved here (Doc 13). Rules Catalog organization uses taxonomy.

nodes.label: AEGIS Phase 3 (Decomposition & Risk)
nodes.rationale: Covers ArchitecturalNode, FunctionalNode, ComplianceGate. Functional Node allocation uses taxonomy. Technical NFRs (distinct from Phase 1 RegulatoryObligations).

nodes.label: RACI Matrix (10 Macro-Domains)
nodes.rationale: 30 RACI rows across 10 macro-domains. A (Accountable) on CTO/CISO for security, CEO/DPO for data-protection-specific. Proportionate for 8-employee micro-SaaS. D-08.3 row explicitly INACTIVE.

nodes.label: RegulatoryClause Class
nodes.rationale: Includes ALL Nuances (1-3) per design decision D-004: Nuance 1 (isAtomic, parentClauseId, siblingClauseIds), Nuance 2 (obligationType), Nuance 3 (obligatedParty[]). Supports complete clause characterization and Phase 2 Strategic Tension Analysis.

nodes.label: RegulatoryObligation Class
nodes.rationale: RENAMED from 'AbstractNFR' per design decision D-010 for semantic accuracy. These ARE regulatory obligations, NOT technical NFRs (those come in Phase 3). Clear derivation path: RegulatoryClause → RegulatoryObligation → Privacy/Security Goal (Phase 2).

nodes.label: 10×38 Security Control Domain Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Fixed taxonomy of 10 domains and 38 sub-domains serving as common vocabulary between regulations and implementation. Design decision D-008 locks this for Phase 1. Enables cross-regulation comparison (T6 Domain Coverage Matrix).

nodes.label: Snyk (Vulnerability Scanning)
nodes.rationale: Feeds vulnerability identification (D-02.1) and SBOM-derivation (D-06.2). Can output CycloneDX/SPDX. Weekly scans. Risk: Low.

nodes.label: Stripe (Payment Processor)
nodes.rationale: Sole payment processor. PCI-DSS Level 1. Card PAN tokenised by Stripe; TinyTask stores only billing metadata. DPA in place. Risk: Low.

nodes.label: SYS-01: Main SaaS Application
nodes.rationale: Cloud SaaS application (Node.js API, React web client, PostgreSQL driver). Criticality: Important. Hosts personal data. Owner: CTO and development team.

nodes.label: SYS-02: Auth Service (Auth0)
nodes.rationale: Managed identity service using OAuth 2.0 and OIDC. MFA enforced for admins only, optional for customers. Criticality: Important. Hosts personal data.

nodes.label: SYS-03: Customer Data Store (PostgreSQL)
nodes.rationale: Managed relational database (PostgreSQL on EU cloud region). Criticality: CRITICAL. Hosts personal data. AES-256 provider-managed encryption using SYS-04 keys.

nodes.label: TinyTask Lda.
nodes.rationale: Micro-enterprise (8 employees, <€2M revenue) B2B SaaS productivity tool in Lisbon, Portugal. GDPR Controller+Processor, CRA Manufacturer (Default class). Complexity Tier: MEDIUM.

nodes.label: 17-Field Rich Schema (uniform across all card types)
nodes.rationale: 12 base + 3 Case_01-specific + 2 context fields. Excludes Effort/Cost/Timeline by directive. Applied uniformly to 107 cards (30 OBL + 31 goals + 46 rules) = 1,819 cells.
nodes.norm_label: 17-field rich schema (uniform across all card types)

nodes.label: 54 Source Clauses (28 GDPR + 26 CRA)
nodes.rationale: The regulatory clause base from which obligations are derived. 28 GDPR clauses (GDPR-C01..C28) + 26 CRA clauses (CRA-C01..C26). NIS2, DORA, AI Act all NOT APPLICABLE per Doc 05 applicability determination.

nodes.label: DR-002: obligationNI = AVG(clauseNIs)
nodes.rationale: Derivation rule for normative intensity. AVG chosen over MAX (AP-P2-09: MAX kills differentiation). Applied retroactively to all 46 cards. Resolved F-10: OBL-D-01.4-001 and OBL-D-09.1-001 both = 2.500.

nodes.label: Finding F-01: Phantom PO-D-01.3-001
nodes.rationale: OBL-D-01.3-001 (Cryptographic Key Management) has no corresponding PO or SO in Doc 10. CR-D-01.3-001 references PO-D-01.3-001 which does not exist. Carry-over from Sprint 1, deferred to human arbiter. Severity: LOW.

nodes.label: Finding F-07: Cross-Document Orphan Risk
nodes.rationale: 4 new OBLs (D-07.2/3/4, D-10.1) reference placeholder PO/SO/CR IDs that do not yet exist in Doc 10/11. Structural cross-doc orphan risk until follow-on contract populates those docs. Severity: MEDIUM.

nodes.label: F-01: OBL-D-01.3-001 has no PG/SG (phantom PG-D-01.3-001)
nodes.rationale: Carried from Sprint 1. CR-D-01.3-001 references phantom PG-D-01.3-001. Deferred to human arbiter per P7. No Sprint 5 blocker.
nodes.norm_label: f-01: obl-d-01.3-001 has no pg/sg (phantom pg-d-01.3-001)

nodes.label: F-04a: PG Count Discrepancy (12 vs 11)
nodes.rationale: Legacy §3.2 summary claims 12 PG but §3.1 lists 11. D-09.3 is DORA-exclusive, not applicable to TinyTask. Resolved Sprint 4: 11 PG authoritative.

nodes.label: F-04b: SG Count Discrepancy (18 vs 20)
nodes.rationale: Legacy §4.2 summary claims 18 SG but §4.1 lists 20. Legacy summary stale from v1.0. Resolved Sprint 4: 20 SG authoritative. Total: 31 goals (11+20).

nodes.label: F-10: NI Divergence (OBL-D-01.4-001, OBL-D-09.1-001)
nodes.rationale: Raised Sprint 3, resolved Sprint 4. Legacy NI (3.000/2.750) vs DR-002 AVG (2.500/2.500). Rich Mode adopts DR-002 AVG as authoritative. Catalog average NI: 2.842→2.800.

nodes.label: F-11: Doc 10/11 frontmatter fields_per_card stale (15 vs actual 17)
nodes.rationale: Raised Sprint 5. Frontmatter scalar inherited from Sprint 4 catalog schema (15 fields) not updated when Sprint 5 added 2 context fields. Orchestrator to re-emit at merge time.
nodes.norm_label: f-11: doc 10/11 frontmatter fields_per_card stale (15 vs actual 17)

nodes.label: Normative Intensity Propagation (DR-002)
nodes.rationale: Rule: obligationNI = AVG(clauseNIs). All 34 obligations verified. F-10 reconciliation: OBL-D-01.4-001 (2.500) and OBL-D-09.1-001 (2.500) use Rich DR-002 AVG as authoritative over legacy values (3.000 and 2.750 respectively).

nodes.label: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
nodes.rationale: Used for framework mapping in Block G. 3 CSF IDs (DE.DP-04, ID.AM-08, RS.RP-01) flagged as not in frozen list. 30 CR + 16 BPR mapped to CSF subcategories.

nodes.label: 34 Regulatory Obligations (Phase 2)
nodes.rationale: 34 obligations across 10 sub-domains (D-01..D-10): 30 inherited from legacy + 4 added in Sprint 6+ P7 orphan fix (D-07.2/3/4, D-10.1). Each has 17-field detail card. NI distribution: 24 at 3.000, 7 at 2.500-2.999, 3 at 2.000-2.499.

nodes.label: Doc 10 — Privacy & Security Goals (v2.0 DEEP_ENRICHED)
nodes.rationale: 2,035 lines. 31 goal cards (11 PG + 20 SG) × 17 fields = 527 cells. F-04a/b resolved: 31 goals authoritative (not 30).

nodes.label: Doc 12 — Rules Catalog Workbook (14 sheets)
nodes.rationale: 42.6KB, 14 sheets. Built with openpyxl. Derived from source docs with assertions. Sheets include NI_Propagation, Affected_Stakeholders, Schema_15_Fields.

nodes.label: D-02: Vulnerability Management
nodes.rationale: Cluster covering identification (D-02.1), patch management (D-02.2), and CVD (D-02.3). 3 SOs, CRA-primary.

nodes.label: D-03: Access Control
nodes.rationale: Cluster covering identity lifecycle (D-03.1), MFA (D-03.2), authorisation (D-03.3), and secure defaults (D-03.4). 4 SOs.

nodes.label: D-05: Data Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Cluster covering minimisation (D-05.1), retention (D-05.2), erasure (D-05.3), and portability (D-05.4). 4 POs, all GDPR-driven.

nodes.label: D-09: Governance & Documentation
nodes.rationale: Cluster covering policies (D-09.1), assessments (D-09.2), DORA (D-09.3, N/A), and RoPA (D-09.4). 3 POs + 2 SOs with intentional dual-coverage for D-09.1 and D-09.2.

nodes.label: Conflict CONF-002: Data Minimization vs Vulnerability Tracking
nodes.rationale: PO-D-05.1 (minimisation) conflicts with SO-D-02.1 (vulnerability tracking). Resolved by collecting only vulnerability metadata, not user data.
nodes.norm_label: conflict conf-002: data minimization vs vulnerability tracking

nodes.label: ENISA (European Union Agency for Cybersecurity)
nodes.rationale: CRA single reporting platform. 24h early warning for actively exploited vulnerabilities. Lead authority for CRA Art. 11/12 compliance.

nodes.label: Unified Assessment Template (DPIA + CRA)
nodes.rationale: DD-10 design decision: single template producing dual output for GDPR DPIA and CRA risk assessment. Shared by PO-D-09.2 and SO-D-09.2 (T-M-001).

nodes.label: Finding F-04a: Stale PO Count (12 vs 11)
nodes.rationale: Legacy §3.2 summary claims 12 POs but §3.1 lists 11. D-09 has 3 POs (not 4) because D-09.3 is DORA-exclusive and not applicable to TinyTask.
nodes.norm_label: finding f-04a: stale po count (12 vs 11)

nodes.label: Finding F-04b: Stale SO Count (18 vs 20)
nodes.rationale: Legacy §4.2 summary claims 18 SOs but §4.1 lists 20. SO-D-02.4 was renamed to SO-D-06.2 in v1.1 and never re-counted.
nodes.norm_label: finding f-04b: stale so count (18 vs 20)

nodes.label: PO-D-05.1-001: Minimize Personal Data Collection
nodes.rationale: Operationalised at three layers: database schema (column allow-list), API input validation (reject-unknown), and analytics pipeline (no personal data in logs). Resolves CONF-002 with SO-D-02.1 via metadata-only collection.

nodes.label: PO-D-05.2-001: Retain Personal Data Only as Needed
nodes.rationale: Retention matrix: 30d active-task, 7y financial records (Portuguese commercial law), 7y audit logs. Managed object-storage lifecycle rules automate deletion.
nodes.norm_label: po-d-05.2-001: retain personal data only as needed

nodes.label: PO-D-05.4-001: Provide Data Export on Request
nodes.rationale: GDPR Art. 20 data portability. JSON-only export endpoint bundling all customer data within 48h. GDPR-only (no CRA sub-SO).
nodes.norm_label: po-d-05.4-001: provide data export on request

nodes.label: PO-D-07.1-001: Integrate Privacy into Design
nodes.rationale: GDPR Art. 25 data protection by design. Operationalised via PR-review gates, threat modelling, and maturity self-assessment. Upstream enabler for PO-D-05.1 and PO-D-09.2.

nodes.label: PO-D-09.1-001: Maintain Privacy Policies
nodes.rationale: Seven policy documents (Privacy Policy, Cookie Policy, DPA, AUP, Retention Policy, IS Policy, Breach Procedure). Dual-coverage with SO-D-09.1 is intentional — same ISMS framework satisfies both GDPR Art. 24 and CRA Art. 31.

nodes.label: PO-D-09.2-001: Conduct DPIA Pre-Launch
nodes.rationale: Unified assessment pattern: same risk-analysis workflow produces both GDPR DPIA and CRA cybersecurity risk assessment, halving effort. Deliberate design choice (DD-10).

nodes.label: PO-D-09.4-001: Maintain Records of Processing
nodes.rationale: GDPR Art. 30 RoPA as living Markdown document with quarterly reviews. Primary accountability artefact requested by CNPD during investigations.

nodes.label: SO-D-02.1-001: Zero Known Exploitable Vulnerabilities
nodes.rationale: CRA Annex I §1.3 baseline. CI blocks merge on CRITICAL findings; HIGH findings create 7-day remediation SLA. Automated scanning in CI: container scanner, dependency audit, advisory feed, static analysis.

nodes.label: AEGIS Methodology Phase 3
nodes.rationale: Core engineering engine translating regulatory obligations into implementable functional requirements and architectural nodes. Operates on two-track model (Technology→Process) with iterative decomposition and stop conditions.

nodes.label: Compliance Gates
nodes.rationale: Validation checkpoints (GATE-D-xx.x-xxx) that verify FRs satisfy rules. Use verification methods: TEST, INSPECT, DEMONSTRATE, ANALYZE. Status: PASS/FAIL/PARTIAL/NOT_EVALUATED.

nodes.label: D3FEND Defense Framework
nodes.rationale: Defense technique mapping: D3-MA (MFA), D3-DE (Encryption), D3-TL (Traffic Limiting), D3-DP (Data Partitioning), D3-SD (Secret Detection), D3-IL (Immutable Logging), D3-RBAC, D3-VA, D3-IR, D3-AT. 100% KG inferences mapped.

nodes.label: Requirement Derivation Formula
nodes.rationale: Three-element formula: Actor (WHO triggers) + Behavior (WHAT system must do) + Constraint (security/privacy from Rules Catalog) → Requirement. Ensures every FR has regulatory justification.

nodes.label: Functional Requirements (60 FRs)
nodes.rationale: 60 technology-agnostic FRs: IAM(10), DP(12), SEC(15), DEV(10), GOV(10), TRN(3). Derived via Actor+Behavior+Constraint formula. 100% UC coverage, 98% NFR coverage, 100% regulatory coverage.

nodes.label: Functional Tree Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Hierarchical decomposition: L1 (6 enterprise capability areas) → L2 (18 processes/systems) → L3 (45+ detailed nodes). Each node has track assignment (BUILD/BUY/CONFIGURE/OUTSOURCE) and verification method.

nodes.label: Knowledge Graph Inference Engine
nodes.rationale: SPARQL-based inference over traceability chain: Regulation→Clause→Rule→NFR→FR→UC→Gate. 215 total inferences (98% high confidence). Enables gap detection, rule satisfaction checks, and threat→mitigation→FR chains.

nodes.label: LINDDUN Privacy Threat Modeling
nodes.rationale: Privacy-specific threat categories: Linkability, Identifiability, Non-repudiation, Detectability, Disclosure, Unawareness, Non-compliance. 7 privacy threats mapped to GDPR articles.

nodes.label: Mitigation Controls (CTRL-01 to 08)
nodes.rationale: 8 security controls: RBAC, Encryption, Account Lockout, Immutable Logging, Privilege Separation, Rate Limiting, CI/CD Security, 24/7 Monitoring. Strategies: NEW_FUNCTIONAL_NODE(3), STRENGTHEN_EXISTING(3), ARCHITECTURAL_CHANGE(1), PROCESS_CONTROL(1).

nodes.label: Mitigation Feedback Loop
nodes.rationale: Class model v2.0 requirement: mitigation requirements feed back into decomposition cycle. 8 controls → 3 new UCs + 5 refined UCs → 4 new/enhanced gates. Creates iterative refinement until all residual risks are LOW.

nodes.label: Minimum Viable Compliance (MVC)
nodes.rationale: Feasibility-driven approach for micro-enterprise: implement 14 critical FRs first (80% compliance) at €3.7K over 16 weeks. Reduces 60 FRs to 20-25, 35 UCs to 15-20, 42 threats to top 10. Uses AWS native tools instead of enterprise solutions.

nodes.label: Non-Functional Requirements (46 NFRs)
nodes.rationale: 46 measurable NFRs: CONF(7), INT(7), AVAIL(7), PRIV(10), ACC(7), COMP(8). 100% measurable with quantifiable criteria. Derived from GDPR(28), CRA(15), NIS2(3).

nodes.label: Risk Register (10 Risks)
nodes.rationale: 10 assessed risks: 7 HIGH (score 12), 3 MEDIUM (score 8-10). All mitigated to LOW residual via 8 controls. Categories: Confidentiality, Availability, Integrity, Privacy, Compliance.

nodes.label: Rules Catalog (18 Rules)
nodes.rationale: Static validation oracle: 11 compliance-driven (RULE-COM-01 to 11) + 7 best-practice (RULE-BST-01 to 07) constraints. Every Functional Tree node must satisfy at least one rule. 100% coverage achieved.

nodes.label: Phase 3 Stop Conditions
nodes.rationale: SC1: Compliance Coverage — every node satisfies ≥1 rule, every rule has ≥1 node (18/18 satisfied). SC2: Risk Residual — all residual risks within organizational tolerances (all LOW). SC5: No unmitigated CRITICAL/HIGH risks.

nodes.label: STRIDE Threat Modeling

nodes.label: DORA Applicability (Financial Entity, 38 clauses)

nodes.label: NIS 2 Applicability (Essential Entity, 29 clauses)
nodes.rationale: Financial sector + 5000+ employees = Essential Entity. 24h incident notification. Management liability (Art. 20). DORA is lex specialis for ICT risk. IR 2024/2690 does NOT apply to credit institutions. Directive (not Regulation) — German transposition applies.

nodes.label: SI-004: NIS2+DORA 24h Notification
nodes.rationale: Both NIS 2 and DORA require 24h early warning — unified incident response workflow (Max-SLA routing) required. CRITICAL priority.

nodes.label: ComplianceContext (Class)

nodes.rationale: Phase 2 entity capturing conflicts between regulations. 4 tensions resolved: T-001 (24h workflow), T-002 (crypto sharding), T-003 (IPSARA), T-004 (CRA secure-by-default).

nodes.label: D-01.3 Cryptographic Key Management (Sub-domain Pipeline)
nodes.author: SubDomains merge (Executor sub-agent)
nodes.rationale: Unified sub-domain document merging Cross-Regulation Analysis, Hierarchical Security Objectives, and Security Requirements into a single pipeline for cryptographic key management across GDPR, CRA, and DORA.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(1)(f): Integrity and Confidentiality
nodes.rationale: Processed in a manner that ensures appropriate security, including protection against unauthorised or unlawful processing and against accidental loss, destruction or damage, using appropriate technical or organisational measures. The 'appropriate' qualifier anchored to Art. 32(1) risk-based test.

nodes.label: AI Act (absent from D-01.1)
nodes.rationale: AI Act is not a participant in D-01.1. Per taxonomy §4.1, AI Act §D-01.1 marks CRA Annex I (2)(e) as sole authority. AI Act is listed in related_documents but explicitly absent from the pairwise analysis.

nodes.label: CRA (Regulation)
nodes.rationale: Participant in D-01.1. Scope: products with digital elements (personal or other data). Threshold: 'state-of-the-art mechanisms' (strictest). Recipient: MSA + ENISA. Legal anchor: Annex I Part I (1)+(2)(e).

nodes.label: CRA Annex I Part I (1)+(2)(e) — Essential Requirements
nodes.rationale: Part I(1): appropriate level of cybersecurity based on risks. Part I(2)(e): confidentiality of stored/transmitted/processed data — personal or other — by encrypting at rest or in transit using state-of-the-art mechanisms. 'Personal or other' extends beyond GDPR scope. Art. 3(47) cross-references GDPR Art. 4(1).
nodes.norm_label: cra annex i part i (1)+(2)(e) — essential requirements

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13 — Obligations of Manufacturers
nodes.rationale: 25 paragraphs, ~35 atomic clauses. Operational core of CRA (analog of GDPR Art. 32 and NIS2 Art. 21). Defines 6-phase product-lifecycle obligations, cybersecurity risk assessment, due-diligence on third-party components, support period (min 5 years), technical documentation, corrective measures. 36 atomic clauses mapped (CRA-CL14 through CRA-CL50).

nodes.label: CRA Art. 6 — Essential Requirements Gate
nodes.rationale: Products with digital elements shall be made available on market only where they meet essential cybersecurity requirements (Annex I Part I). Proviso: properly installed, maintained, used for intended purpose or reasonably foreseeable conditions, necessary security updates installed. Berry-flagged: 'essential', 'meet', 'properly', 'intended purpose', 'necessary security updates', 'installed'.

nodes.label: CSF Cross-Validation (PR.DS-01 pivot)
nodes.rationale: All four regulations converge on PR.DS-01 (Data-at-rest protected). CRA additionally maps to PR.DS-02 (in-transit). DORA additionally maps to PR.DS-02/PR.DS-10/PR.DS-12. Shared PR.DS-01 anchor is the operational pivot; divergence at supplementary layer. No contradictory CSF mappings observed.

nodes.label: D-01 Data Protection & Encryption (parent domain)
nodes.rationale: Parent macro-domain of D-01.1. Referenced as ../../DomainAnalysis/D-01_Data-Protection/D-01.1.md for domain analysis context.

nodes.label: DORA (Regulation)
nodes.rationale: Participant in D-01.1. Scope: ICT-supported data of financial entities. Threshold: 'high standards'. Recipient: national CA + ESAs. Legal anchor: Art. 9(2). OJ-explicit on 3-state OR.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(2) — ICT Security Policies
nodes.rationale: ICT security policies ensuring resilience, continuity, availability and high standards of availability/authenticity/integrity/confidentiality of data whether at rest, in use or in transit. 4×3 CIA+A matrix. Art. 9(4)(d) classification-driven cipher strength. Art. 7(2) annual scenario review. 'High standards' anchor: R1 best practice / R2 published standards / R3 frontier research.

nodes.label: Emergent Tensions (3+ regulations)
nodes.rationale: Four parallel threshold anchors diverge: GDPR 'appropriate', NIS2 'where appropriate', CRA 'state of the art', DORA 'high standards'. CRA 'personal or other' scope extension creates compliance-population gap beyond GDPR. A DORA financial entity that is NIS2 essential + processes personal data + uses CRA products must reconcile four parallel thresholds.

nodes.label: GDPR (Regulation)
nodes.rationale: Participant in D-01.1. Scope: personal data. Threshold: 'appropriate' (risk-based). Recipient: supervisory authority. Legal anchors: Art. 5(1)(f) + Art. 32(1)(a)/(b).

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 10 — Criminal Convictions
nodes.rationale: Processing of criminal conviction data only under official authority control or Union/Member State law with appropriate safeguards. Comprehensive register only under official authority control.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 21(1) — Right to Object
nodes.rationale: Objection grounds with 'compelling legitimate grounds' overriding test. Berry-flagged: 'compelling' stronger than Art. 6(1)(f) 'legitimate interests'. R1 (strictly necessary) vs R2 (materially more weighty) yield distinct balance-tests.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 25 — Privacy by Design and Default
nodes.rationale: Art. 25(1) privacy by design: 'state of the art' + 'appropriate' + 'effective' + 'necessary'. Art. 25(2) privacy by default: 4 AND-coordinated dimensions (amount/extent/period/accessibility). R1 (all 4 minimised) vs R2 (some relaxable) yield distinct engineering scope.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 25 — privacy by design and default

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 9(2)(g)/(j) — Special Category Lawfulness
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(2)(g) substantial public interest: inherits Art. 6(1)(e) ambiguity plus undefined 'substantial' qualifier. Art. 9(2)(j) research/statistics/archiving: cross-references Art. 89(1) safeguards but does not define 'archiving'. Both per-member-state-law obligations.

nodes.label: NIS2 (Regulation)
nodes.rationale: Participant in D-01.1. Scope: network and information systems (broader than personal data). Threshold: 'where appropriate' hedge. Recipient: CSIRT or CA. Legal anchor: Art. 21(2)(h).

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(h) — Cryptography Policy
nodes.rationale: Requires essential/important entities to establish policies and procedures regarding use of cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption. Art. 21(1) 'appropriate and proportionate' qualifier propagates to all 10 sub-points. Berry-flagged: 'appropriate', 'proportionate', 'manage the risks', 'impact'.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 2(1) — Network and Information System Definition
nodes.rationale: Three-part OR definition: (a) electronic communications network, (b) device/group of devices with automatic processing, (c) digital data stored/processed/retrieved/transmitted. Berry-flagged: 'related' undefined, 'device' polysemous (hardware/virtual/software-only). Resolving this determines scope of all Chapter IV obligations.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 2(1) — network and information system definition

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 2(2) — Security of NIS Definition
nodes.rationale: Ability to resist at a given level of confidence any event compromising availability/authenticity/integrity/confidentiality. Berry-flagged: 'level of confidence' (subjective/relative/absolute), 'ability to resist' (binary/threshold/probabilistic), 'authenticity' undefined in NIS2. Distinct from Art. 2(3) 'cybersecurity' (cross-ref to Reg. 2019/881).
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 2(2) — security of nis definition

nodes.label: Phase 1C Doc 07 (Cross-Regulation Consolidation)
nodes.rationale: Downstream target document for company profile consolidation. D-01.1 feeds as stack-merge sub-domain. Proportionality guidance: 5-FTE SaaS defaults to CRA floor; 500-FTE financial entity adds DORA overlay.

nodes.label: Stack-Merge Downstream Implication
nodes.rationale: D-01.1 is a stack-merge sub-domain: a single at-rest control (e.g. disk encryption with key custody) typically satisfies all four regulators when documentation links each one. Proportionality: 5-FTE SaaS defaults to CRA state-of-the-art floor; 500-FTE financial entity must additionally document DORA classification-driven cipher strength overlay.

nodes.label: Threshold Anchor Divergence
nodes.rationale: Four parallel thresholds: GDPR 'appropriate' (risk-based), NIS2 'where appropriate' (appropriate-and-proportionate), CRA 'state of the art' (harmonised-standards floor), DORA 'high standards' (OJ-literal, no measurement criterion pending ESAs RTS). CRA state-of-the-art floor likely sufficient for other three on at-rest dimension.

nodes.norm_label: nist csf rc.rp-03: backup integrity verified before restoration

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(1)(c): Timely Restoration of Availability
nodes.rationale: Requires ability to restore availability and access to personal data in a timely manner in the event of a physical or technical incident.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 32(1)(c): timely restoration of availability

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-014: CIA + Resilience (Cross-Reference)
nodes.rationale: Cross-reference objective linking CIA+resilience requirements across multiple sub-domains.

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-001: CIA + resilience baseline for personal data processing
nodes.rationale: Art. 5(1)(f) and Art. 32(1)(b) establish a continuous obligation to maintain the CIA triad augmented by resilience across the entire processing surface, anchored to a risk-based test.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-001: cia + resilience baseline for personal data processing

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-001: CIA Baseline for Personal Data Processing
nodes.norm_label: so-gdpr-001: cia baseline for personal data processing

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-024: Timely Availability Restoration After Incident
nodes.rationale: Art. 32(1)(c) requires ability to restore availability and access in a timely manner. 'Timely manner' is read as RTO defined per processing activity, documented in business continuity policy. Recital 49 is directionally useful but non-binding.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-024: timely availability restoration after incident

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32: Security of Processing
nodes.rationale: Four-element list: pseudonymisation/encryption, ongoing CIA+R, timely restoration, regular testing; state-of-the-art qualifier and appropriate-level-of-security test.

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.DS-11: Backups Created, Protected, Maintained, Tested
nodes.rationale: Backup foundation that makes restoration possible; satisfies the recovery-from-known-good-state requirement.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ds-11: backups created, protected, maintained, tested

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.IR-04: Adequate Resource Capacity for Availability
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ir-04: adequate resource capacity for availability

nodes.label: SR-DORA-015: Risk-Calibrated Backup with Verified Restoration
nodes.rationale: Art. 12(1) backup policies based on criticality/confidentiality + restoration procedures. Recital 57: testing backups not merely writing them.
nodes.norm_label: sr-dora-015: risk-calibrated backup with verified restoration

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-035: Processor auditability with continuous external-activity monitoring
nodes.rationale: Art. 28(3)(c) and (h) combined with Art. 32(1) to give controller substantive and evidentiary access to processor security, mapped to GV.SC-03, GV.SC-04, and DE.CM-06.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-035: processor auditability with continuous external-activity monitoring

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-049: Five-event threat model with monitoring and event analysis
nodes.rationale: Art. 32(2) five-event OR enumeration (destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure, unauthorised access) as inclusive threat-model scope, mapped to DE.CM-01, DE.CM-03, DE.AE-02.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-049: five-event threat model with monitoring and event analysis

nodes.label: Pair Analysis: CRA ↔ DORA
nodes.rationale: CRDA classified as COMPLEMENTARY; verified as SAME (corrected — wording only). CRA product-side floor + DORA entity-side overlay (in-use + classification-driven cipher strength). Stack-merge: CRA supplies at-rest floor; DORA adds in-use + key custody.

nodes.label: Pair Analysis: GDPR ↔ CRA
nodes.rationale: CRDA classified as COMPLEMENTARY; verified as SAME (corrected — wording only). CRA state-of-the-art baseline is stricter than GDPR risk-based 'appropriate'. Scope-disjoint in baseline (CRA manufacturer ≠ GDPR controller); Y on integrated-stack. Disjoint baseline / scope-conditional pair.

nodes.label: Pair Analysis: GDPR ↔ DORA
nodes.rationale: CRDA classified as COMPLEMENTARY; verified as SAME (corrected — wording only). DORA 4×3 CIA+A vs GDPR 3×CIA is scope dimension difference, not at-rest cell difference. Stack-merge with overlay: DORA classification-driven cipher-strength tiering sits on top of joint at-rest encryption.

nodes.label: Pair Analysis: GDPR ↔ NIS2
nodes.rationale: CRDA classified as COMPLEMENTARY; verified as SAME (corrected — terminology only). Both impose continuous risk-anchored encryption-at-rest obligations. NIS2 broader in scope (NIS vs personal data); GDPR stricter in anchor ('appropriate' vs 'where appropriate'). Stack-merge with documentation: single at-rest encryption deployment + joint Art. 32/Art. 21(2)(h) risk-assessment artefact discharges both.

nodes.label: Pair Analysis: NIS2 ↔ CRA
nodes.rationale: CRDA classified as COMPLEMENTARY; verified as SAME (corrected — wording only). Layered obligations: CRA is product-side state-of-the-art baseline; NIS2 is entity-side policy + appropriate-and-proportionate deployment. Structurally complementary (different layers) but operationally joint — stack-merge.

nodes.label: Pair Analysis: NIS2 ↔ DORA
nodes.rationale: CRDA classified as EQUAL; verified as SAME (no change). Both entity-level cryptography-policy obligations. DORA more demanding by inclusion (in-use dimension) but not on at-rest anchor. Lex specialis: DORA absorbs NIS2 for financial entities.

nodes.label: SR-DORA-014: BC implementation with independent audit review
nodes.rationale: Art. 11(2)-(3) requires dedicated arrangements for five objectives plus independent internal audit review for non-microenterprises.
nodes.norm_label: sr-dora-014: bc implementation with independent audit review

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-002: In-Transit Confidentiality
nodes.rationale: Extends Art. 5(1)(f) CIA obligation to network and transport layers via Art. 32(1)(b) and Art. 32(2) five-event risk enumeration, requiring encryption-in-transit and network segmentation.

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-003: Pseudonymisation and Encryption with Key Separation
nodes.rationale: Operationalises Art. 32(1)(a) pseudonymisation/encryption with the Art. 4(5) de-attribution test requiring additional information kept separately under distinct technical and organisational control.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-003: pseudonymisation and encryption with key separation

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-004: Cryptographic Unintelligibility for Breach Carve-Out
nodes.rationale: Art. 34(3)(a) exempts data-subject notification when breached data was rendered unintelligible via encryption with sufficient key separation, operationalised as zero-trust assumption that storage layer will be breached.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-004: cryptographic unintelligibility for breach carve-out

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-007: Periodic Testing of Security Controls
nodes.rationale: Art. 32(1)(d) mandates a process for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating security measure effectiveness, with cadence scaled to Art. 32(1) risk-based preamble factors rather than fixed numeric interval.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-007: periodic testing of security controls

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-008: DPIA and Risk-Profile Review on Material Change
nodes.rationale: Art. 35(11) requires DPIA review on change of risk; combined with Art. 32(1)(d) periodic testing creates dual-mode (periodic + triggered) continuous-improvement obligation for security-relevant processing.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-008: dpia and risk-profile review on material change

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-014: Continuous Breach Detection Enabling 72-Hour Clock
nodes.rationale: Art. 32(1)(b) monitoring is the regulatory foundation for the Art. 33(1) 72-hour notification clock: no detection, no awareness, no notification, no compliance. Obligation is continuous and joint (controller + processor).
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-014: continuous breach detection enabling 72-hour clock

nodes.label: D-01 Data-Protection Index
nodes.rationale: Top-level index for the D-01 Data-Protection macro-domain, listing 4 sub-subdomains (D-01.1 through D-01.4), 66 article copies, and 116 ambiguity sections.

nodes.label: SR-DORA-029: ICT Asset Inventory and Classification
nodes.rationale: Inventory-onboarding substrate for every downstream obligation. Runs in parallel with GDPR Art. 30 and NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(a). OJ-corrective note flags Art. 7(1) to Art. 8(1) misattribution.
nodes.norm_label: sr-dora-029: ict asset inventory and classification

nodes.label: SR-DORA-019: ICT Third-Party Risk Management
nodes.rationale: Manage ICT third-party risk taking into account nature, scale, complexity and importance of ICT-related dependencies, and risks from contractual arrangements.

nodes.label: SR-DORA-026: Management Body ICT Risk Framework Ownership
nodes.rationale: Top-of-pyramid governance rule: management body shall define, approve, oversee and be responsible for implementation of all arrangements related to ICT risk management framework.
nodes.norm_label: sr-dora-026: management body ict risk framework ownership

nodes.label: SO-DORA-016: Management Body Responsibility + Framework
nodes.rationale: Management body defines, approves, oversees and is responsible for ICT risk management framework, supported by sound, comprehensive and well-documented framework.

nodes.label: SR-DORA-004: Continuous ICT Risk-Source Identification
nodes.rationale: Requires continuous identification of all sources of ICT risk, in particular risk exposure to and from other financial entities, and assessment of cyber threats and ICT vulnerabilities.

nodes.label: SR-DORA-005: Annual Risk-Scenario Register Refresh
nodes.rationale: Hard numeric anchor of 'at least yearly' closes temporal ambiguity. The at-least-yearly floor is binding even where entity-internal cadence is set tighter.

nodes.label: SR-DORA-008: Multi-Modality Resilience Testing
nodes.rationale: Requires a sound and comprehensive digital operational resilience testing programme as integral part of the ICT risk-management framework, with 12 testing modalities in Art. 25(1).

nodes.label: SR-DORA-009: Threat-Led Penetration Testing (TLPT)
nodes.rationale: At least every 3 years advanced testing by means of TLPT. Defined by reference to TIBER-EU framework. Applies to significant entities under Art. 26(8).

nodes.label: DORA Art. 6 (ICT Risk Management Framework)
nodes.rationale: Requires sound, comprehensive and well-documented ICT risk management framework with three-lines-of-defence independence and strategy/policy/protocol/procedure/tool components.

nodes.label: SR-DORA-027: Sound ICT Risk Management Framework
nodes.rationale: Sound, comprehensive and well-documented ICT risk management framework enabling quick, efficient and comprehensive ICT risk addressing. Top-of-stack governance artefact.
nodes.norm_label: sr-dora-027: sound ict risk management framework

nodes.label: SR-DORA-028: Three-Lines-of-Defence Independence
nodes.rationale: Assign ICT risk oversight to a control function with appropriate independence per three-lines-of-defence model or internal risk management and control model.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 24-26 (Testing Programme)
nodes.rationale: Chapter IV: Art. 24(1) sound and comprehensive testing programme; Art. 25(1) twelve testing modalities; Art. 26(1) TLPT at least every 3 years for significant entities.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 28 (ICT Third-Party Risk)
nodes.rationale: Foundational third-party risk-governance rule with four-factor proportionality. Contractual minimum elements at Art. 30(1)-(2) and audit rights at Art. 30(3)(e).

nodes.label: DORA Art. 7 (Identification)
nodes.rationale: Continuous identification of all sources of ICT risk and annual review of risk scenarios. OJ-corrective notes flag Art. 7(1)→Art. 8(1) and Art. 7(2)→Art. 8(2) misattributions.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 GV (Governance)
nodes.rationale: Policy (GV.PO-01), mission alignment (GV.OC-01), legal/regulatory (GV.OC-03), leadership accountability (GV.RR-01, GV.RR-02), risk roles (GV.RM-02, GV.RM-04), strategy review (GV.OV-02), supply chain (GV.SC-02).

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 ID.AM (Asset Management)
nodes.rationale: Hardware (ID.AM-01), software (ID.AM-02), data (ID.AM-03), supplier (ID.AM-04) inventories and asset prioritisation (ID.AM-05).

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 ID.RA (Risk Assessment)
nodes.rationale: Vulnerability identification (ID.RA-01), threat identification (ID.RA-03), impact/likelihood (ID.RA-04), and risk-informed decisions (ID.RA-05) subcategories.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 4 Analysis (D-01.3)
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering authentication, risk-scenario refresh, patch governance, third-party risk, management-body training, staff training, and management-body ownership rules.

nodes.label: CRA Regulation (EU) 2024/2847
nodes.rationale: Cyber Resilience Act: Art. 13 conformity-assessment and vulnerability-handling duties apply where ICT assets are digital products. Art. 13(5) vulnerability handling feeds DORA entities; Art. 13(8) secure-update is upstream.

nodes.label: SO-CRA-001: Confidentiality Security Objective
nodes.rationale: Umbrella confidentiality objective linked to SR-CRA-001/002/003; the 'confidentiality + state-of-the-art encryption' cluster.

nodes.label: SO-DORA-002: Strong Authentication and Key Protection
nodes.rationale: Strong authentication mechanisms based on relevant standards + protection measures of cryptographic keys; Art. 9(4)(d).
nodes.norm_label: so-dora-002: strong authentication and key protection

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.DS-01: Data-at-Rest Protected
nodes.rationale: Encryption-at-rest with validated cryptographic modules, AES-class symmetric primitives for bulk data. Anchors confidentiality and integrity for at-rest data state.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-005: Data integrity protection and corruption reporting
nodes.rationale: Operationalises Annex I Part I (2)(f)+(l) integrity duty through PR.DS-01, PR.DS-10, and PR.PS-04, transforming silent tampering into observable events.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-005: data integrity protection and corruption reporting

nodes.label: SR-CRA-001: State-of-the-art cryptographic confidentiality baseline
nodes.rationale: Anchors the Annex I Part I (2)(e) confidentiality obligation to NIST CSF PR.DS-01/PR.DS-02, establishing the cryptographic floor for all other controls.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-002: Confidentiality of Stored Data via State-of-the-Art Encryption
nodes.rationale: At-rest encryption obligation under Annex I Part I (2)(e); operationalises PR.DS-01; the 'relevant data' scope is POLY-S2 with R2 reading chosen (intended purpose + risk-assessment scope).
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-002: confidentiality of stored data via state-of-the-art encryption

nodes.label: SR-DORA-001: Cross-State CIA+A Protection Matrix with Risk-Tiered Controls
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(2) 4×3 protection matrix (availability, authenticity, integrity, confidentiality × at-rest, in-use, in-transit); 'high standards' read as R1 best practice with R2 published standards; maps to PR.DS-01/02/10/12.
nodes.norm_label: sr-dora-001: cross-state cia+a protection matrix with risk-tiered controls

nodes.label: SR-DORA-002: Strong Authentication and Cryptographic-Key Protection Baseline
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(4)(d) strong authentication + key protection; T4-vs-text gap: OJ says 'strong authentication mechanisms' not 'MFA'; maps to PR.AA-03 and PR.AA-04.
nodes.norm_label: sr-dora-002: strong authentication and cryptographic-key protection baseline

nodes.label: SR-DORA-003: Classification-Driven Cryptographic-Key Protection with Policy Linkage
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(4)(d) ties encryption to approved data classification and ICT risk assessment; 'approved' read as entity-internal governance approval; maps to PR.DS-01 and GV.RM-04.
nodes.norm_label: sr-dora-003: classification-driven cryptographic-key protection with policy linkage

nodes.label: SR-DORA-013: ICT Business Continuity Policy
nodes.rationale: Art. 11(1) comprehensive ICT BC policy as integral part of overall BC. 'May be adopted as dedicated specific policy' permits either form-factor.

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-005: Accuracy and Currency of Stored Personal Data
nodes.rationale: Art. 5(1)(d) accuracy principle read as output-accuracy (against data subject's current real-world state), harmonising with Art. 16 rectification right. Both technical integrity (PR.DS-01) and governance (PR.DS-12) dimensions required.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-005: accuracy and currency of stored personal data
