nodes.norm_label: so-dora-008: security objective (linked to incident management)

nodes.label: SR-DORA-016: End-to-end ICT-related Incident Management with Root-cause Analysis
nodes.rationale: Art. 17(1) requires define/establish/implement incident management to detect/manage/notify. Twin 3-verb coordinations: process setup and process operation. RS.AN-03 root-cause analysis feeds back into SR-DORA-005 scenario register and SR-DORA-007 patch priority.
nodes.norm_label: sr-dora-016: end-to-end ict-related incident management with root-cause analysis

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 27(1): EU Representative Designation
nodes.rationale: Non-EU controllers/processors under Art. 3(2) must designate in writing a Union representative; exception in Art. 27(2)(a) is conjunctive (occasional AND small-scale AND low-risk).

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OC-02: Stakeholders Understood and Considered
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-038 for non-EU controller stakeholder recognition of EU data subjects and supervisory authorities.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.oc-02: stakeholders understood and considered

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RR-02: Roles and Responsibilities Established and Enforced
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-038 for representative role-accountability discipline.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.rr-02: roles and responsibilities established and enforced

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-038: Written EU Representative for Non-EU Controllers and Processors
nodes.rationale: Art. 27(1) designation in writing; Art. 27(2)(a) exception is conjunctive (occasional AND small-scale AND low-risk); all three qualifiers must hold for exception to apply; 'occasional' read as not regular/periodic per EDPB Guidelines 3/2018.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-038: written eu representative for non-eu controllers and processors

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 39(1): DPO Tasks and Responsibilities
nodes.rationale: Art. 39(1)(a) inform/advise + Art. 39(1)(b) awareness-raising and training; DPO as internal awareness catalyst distinct from controller's substantive training obligation.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 39(1): dpo tasks and responsibilities

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AT-01: Users Informed and Trained on Cybersecurity
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-042 for broad-coverage general awareness training duty.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.at-01: users informed and trained on cybersecurity

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AT-02: Workforce Understand Roles and Responsibilities
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-042 for role-specific training layer beyond general awareness.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.at-02: workforce understand roles and responsibilities

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-042: DPO-Driven GDPR Awareness and Role-Specific Training
nodes.rationale: Art. 39(1)(a) inform/advise + Art. 39(1)(b) awareness/training; split into general annual awareness (PR.AT-01) and role-specific quarterly/event-triggered training (PR.AT-02); rejects one-off induction as insufficient.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-042: dpo-driven gdpr awareness and role-specific training

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OC-03: Legal and Regulatory Requirements Management
nodes.rationale: Mapped to SR-CRA-084, SR-CRA-085, SR-CRA-086 for documentation retention, EU declaration, and CE marking compliance.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.oc-03: legal and regulatory requirements management

nodes.label: SR-CRA-084: Ten-year documentation retention for economic operators
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(13) requires 10-year retention of technical documentation; Art. 19(6) applies to importer; Art. 23(2) applies to economic operators for supply-chain identification.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-084: ten-year documentation retention for economic operators

nodes.label: SR-CRA-085: Pre-market documentation, declaration, and CE marking chain
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(12) requires technical documentation, conformity assessment, EU declaration, and CE marking before placing on market; Art. 28 sets declaration content and format.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-085: pre-market documentation, declaration, and ce marking chain

nodes.label: SR-CRA-086: CE marking affixed and EU declaration accompanies product
nodes.rationale: Art. 30(1) requires CE marking affixed visibly/legibly/indelibly; Art. 30(3) before placing on market; Art. 13(20) requires EU declaration with product.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-086: ce marking affixed and eu declaration accompanies product

nodes.label: SR-CRA-092: Corrective measures, withdrawal, or recall on non-conformity
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(21)/Art. 21: immediate corrective measures, withdrawal, or recall upon knowledge of non-conformity. Three-stage control: contain, mitigate, re-baseline. Mapped to RS.MI-01, RS.MI-02, GV.OV-02.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-092: corrective measures, withdrawal, or recall on non-conformity

nodes.label: SR-CRA-093: MSA cooperation on reasoned request for conformity evidence
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(22): manufacturer must provide all information/documentation to MSA upon reasoned request, in easily understood language. Mapped to GV.OC-03 and RS.CO-04.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-093: msa cooperation on reasoned request for conformity evidence

nodes.label: SR-CRA-094: Cross-regulation risk-assessment consolidation permitted
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(4) s.2: permissive provision allowing CRA risk assessment to be combined with other Union-acts risk assessments (AI Act, Machinery, RED). Mapped to GV.OC-03 and ID.RA-05.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-102: Risk assessment as durable MSA-reviewable record
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(4) s.1 + Annex VII §3 + Art. 13(22): risk assessment included in technical documentation, available to MSA on reasoned request. Mapped to ID.RA-05 and GV.OC-03.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-102: risk assessment as durable msa-reviewable record

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.SC-02: Third parties assessed via supply chain risk process
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.sc-02: third parties assessed via supply chain risk process

nodes.label: DORA Art. 28(1): ICT third-party risk management
nodes.rationale: Foundational third-party risk-governance rule with four-factor proportionality.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 28(1): ict third-party risk management

nodes.label: SO-NIS2-023: Effectiveness assessment of risk-management measures
nodes.rationale: Security objective: policies and procedures to assess effectiveness, results feeding back into risk-management cycle.
nodes.norm_label: so-nis2-023: effectiveness assessment of risk-management measures

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-037: Policy framework for assessing cybersecurity risk-management measure effectiveness
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(f): policies and procedures to assess effectiveness. Mapped to NIST CSF GV.PO-01, ID.IM-01, GV.OV-03.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-037: policy framework for assessing cybersecurity risk-management measure effectiveness

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-038: Scheduled procedures operationalise cybersecurity effectiveness measurement
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(f) procedural limb: assessment cadence, evidence requirements, responsible-function allocation. Mapped to NIST CSF GV.PO-02 and GV.OV-03.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-038: scheduled procedures operationalise cybersecurity effectiveness measurement

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-042: Root-cause corrective measures triggered by non-compliance findings
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(4): without undue delay, necessary, appropriate and proportionate corrective measures. Mapped to NIST CSF ID.IM-01, GV.OV-03, RS.MI-02.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-042: root-cause corrective measures triggered by non-compliance findings

nodes.label: NIST CSF DE.AE-02: Event Analysis
nodes.rationale: Captures analysis layer converting raw monitoring output into breach-relevant signal: events across all five Art. 32(2) categories analysed to understand attack targets and methods.

nodes.label: NIST CSF DE.CM-03: Personnel and Technology Monitoring
nodes.rationale: Captures personnel-activity and technology-usage monitoring addressing 'otherwise processed' events including alteration and unauthorised access from inside trust boundary.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf de.cm-03: personnel and technology monitoring

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.DS-10: Data-in-use integrity
nodes.rationale: Shared operational pivot: runtime integrity controls (signed firmware, control-flow integrity, tamper-detection instrumentation). Second shared anchor across GDPR, CRA, DORA.

nodes.label: SO-AIACT-009: AI system resilience (AI Act canonical SO)
nodes.rationale: Canonical AI Act security objective: Art. 15(3) high-risk AI systems as resilient as possible regarding errors/faults/inconsistencies; technical redundancy (backup/fail-safe); AI-system-level.
nodes.norm_label: so-aiact-009: ai system resilience (ai act canonical so)

nodes.label: SO-CRA-005: Data integrity protection (CRA canonical SO)
nodes.rationale: Canonical CRA security objective: Annex I Part I (2)(f) integrity of data+commands+programs+configuration against any unauthorised manipulation; corruption reported; product-level universal quantifier.
nodes.norm_label: so-cra-005: data integrity protection (cra canonical so)

nodes.label: SO-DORA-001: ICT-system CIA+A integrity (DORA canonical SO)
nodes.rationale: Canonical DORA security objective: Art. 9(2) high standards of availability, authenticity, integrity, confidentiality across at-rest/in-use/in-transit; ICT-system-level.
nodes.norm_label: so-dora-001: ict-system cia+a integrity (dora canonical so)

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-003: Personal data accuracy and integrity (GDPR canonical SO)
nodes.rationale: Canonical GDPR security objective: Art. 5(1)(d) accuracy + Art. 16 rectification + Art. 5(1)(f) integrity; personal-data scope; semantic accuracy (workflow leg) + storage integrity.
nodes.norm_label: so-gdpr-003: personal data accuracy and integrity (gdpr canonical so)

nodes.label: NIST CSF DE.AE-08: Incidents Declared When Criteria Met
nodes.norm_label: nist csf de.ae-08: incidents declared when criteria met

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.PS-04: Log Records for Continuous Monitoring
nodes.rationale: Log records generated and made available for continuous monitoring and analysis; evidentiary loop for monitoring output.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ps-04: log records for continuous monitoring

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-04.3: Incident Response (Notification)
nodes.rationale: Covers AEV notification, severe-incident categorisation, voluntary reporting, OSS steward reporting extension.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-028: Simultaneous AEV Notification to CSIRT and ENISA
nodes.rationale: Art. 14(1) dual-channel notification via single reporting platform; 'simultaneously' read as same-timestamp (R1); maps to RS.MA-01 and RS.CO-04; AEV defined in Art. 3(42).
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-028: simultaneous aev notification to csirt and enisa

nodes.label: SR-DORA-011: Multi-Class Anomalous Activity Detection
nodes.rationale: Art. 10(1) promptly detect anomalous activities including network performance issues and ICT-related incidents, identify SPOFs. Three-class coverage: network, compute, performance.

nodes.label: SR-DORA-012: Multi-Layer Detection with Response Triggering
nodes.rationale: Art. 10(2) multiple layers of control, alert thresholds, trigger criteria, automatic alerts. Four-verb coordination: enable, define, trigger, initiate.
nodes.norm_label: sr-dora-012: multi-layer detection with response triggering

nodes.label: SR-DORA-030: Continuous Monitoring (Art. 8(1))
nodes.rationale: Continuously monitor and control security and functioning of ICT systems; minimise ICT risk impact through appropriate tools, policies, procedures.

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-008 — Incident Handling as Six-Action Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(b) + Art. 6(8): prevent, detect, analyse, contain, respond, recover. Operational substrate of Art. 23 reporting flow. NIST CSF: RS.MA-01, RS.AN-03.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-008 — incident handling as six-action lifecycle

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-048: Records of processing with supervisory-authority access and 250-employee carve-out
nodes.rationale: Art. 30(1)/(4)/(5) RoPA obligation with seven enumerated content items; mapped to NIST ID.AM-03 (data inventory) and GV.PO-02 (process enforcement).
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-048: records of processing with supervisory-authority access and 250-employee carve-out

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-050: Integrity-preserved RoPA records available to supervisory authority
nodes.rationale: Art. 30(3) + Art. 5(2) + Art. 31 set integrity and availability baseline for RoPA; mapped to NIST PR.PS-04, DE.AE-03, RS.AN-07 for log-grade generation, multi-source correlation, and integrity preservation.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-050: integrity-preserved ropa records available to supervisory authority

nodes.label: SR-CRA-027: Product Internal-Activity Recording with User Opt-Out
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part I (2)(l) + Annex II §8; record and monitor relevant internal activity with opt-out; feeds incident-declaration pipeline; operationalised through PR.PS-04 and DE.AE-08.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-027: product internal-activity recording with user opt-out

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(2) — Risk Enumeration
nodes.rationale: Five-event risk enumeration: accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure, unauthorised access. Inclusive OR per Berry COORD-S3.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33(1) — Breach Awareness
nodes.rationale: Cross-references back through the breach-awareness trigger to the Art. 32(2) five-event risk enumeration.

nodes.label: Req 1.4: Data integrity preserved against unauthorised modification (multi-reg aggregation)
nodes.rationale: Volere integrity requirement (section 15) converging GDPR Art. 5(1)(d)+(f)+Art.16+Art.19, CRA Annex I (2)(f)+(l), DORA Art. 9(2), AI Act Art. 15(3). Priority MUST, verification TEST.
nodes.norm_label: req 1.4: data integrity preserved against unauthorised modification (multi-reg aggregation)

nodes.label: Req 1.4.1: Personal-data accuracy and storage integrity
nodes.rationale: GDPR-specific: Art. 5(1)(d) accuracy + Art. 5(1)(f) integrity + Art. 16 rectification + Art. 19 cascade. NIST: PR.DS-01, PR.DS-10, PR.DS-12.
nodes.norm_label: req 1.4.1: personal-data accuracy and storage integrity

nodes.label: Req 1.4.2: Product-side technical integrity (universal-quantifier + corruption reporting)
nodes.rationale: CRA-specific: Annex I (2)(f) universal-quantifier protection of data+commands+programs+configuration; (2)(l) corruption reporting. NIST: PR.DS-01, PR.DS-10, PR.PS-04.
nodes.norm_label: req 1.4.2: product-side technical integrity (universal-quantifier + corruption reporting)

nodes.label: Req 1.4.3: ICT-system integrity cell of 4x3 CIA+A matrix
nodes.rationale: DORA-specific: Art. 9(2) high standards of CIA+A across at-rest/in-use/in-transit. NIST: PR.DS-01, PR.DS-02, PR.DS-10, PR.DS-12.
nodes.norm_label: req 1.4.3: ict-system integrity cell of 4x3 cia+a matrix

nodes.label: Req 1.4.4: High-risk AI system resilience (errors, faults, inconsistencies)
nodes.rationale: AI Act-specific: Art. 15(3) resilience via backup/fail-safe; R3 state-of-the-art standard; proportionate per Recital 66. NIST: PR.IR-03, PR.IR-04, PR.DS-11.
nodes.norm_label: req 1.4.4: high-risk ai system resilience (errors, faults, inconsistencies)

nodes.label: SO-D-01.4.AI_Act: AI Act Sub-SO for Data Integrity
nodes.rationale: High-risk AI system resilience to errors/faults/inconsistencies via technical redundancy (backup/fail-safe plans) per Art. 15(3). CSF anchors: PR.IR-03, PR.IR-04, PR.DS-11.
nodes.norm_label: so-d-01.4.ai_act: ai act sub-so for data integrity

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-015: AI Act Art. 15(3) resilience
nodes.rationale: AI Act security requirement: Art. 15(3) resilience to errors/faults/inconsistencies; R3 state-of-the-art; anchored to PR.IR-03, PR.IR-04, PR.DS-11.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 30(1): Records of processing activities (RoPA)
nodes.rationale: Seven content items: controller details, purposes, data-subject/data categories, recipients, third-country transfers, erasure time limits, Art. 32(1) security measures. 250-employee exception with disjunctive triggers.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 30(1): records of processing activities (ropa)

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 GV.PO-02: Cybersecurity processes and procedures established and enforced
nodes.rationale: Process-and-procedure discipline: maintaining, refreshing, making RoPA available on request is an enforced process with documented triggers, owners, review cadences.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 gv.po-02: cybersecurity processes and procedures established and enforced

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 ID.AM-03: Inventories of data and metadata maintained
nodes.rationale: Data-inventory discipline: each RoPA entry is an inventory record for designated data type with metadata for purpose, lawful basis, recipients, transfers, retention.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 id.am-03: inventories of data and metadata maintained

nodes.label: DORA Art. 24-25 - Digital Operational Resilience Testing
nodes.rationale: Chapter IV: sound and comprehensive testing programme as integral part of framework. 12 testing modalities in Art. 25(1). Art. 26 TLPT and Art. 27 advanced testing for significant entities.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 24-25 - digital operational resilience testing

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AT-01: Users informed and trained on cybersecurity topics
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-DORA-025. Anchors baseline awareness layer: phishing recognition, social-engineering resistance, password hygiene, incident-reporting reflexes.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.at-01: users informed and trained on cybersecurity topics

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AT-02: Workforce understand roles in cybersecurity objectives
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-DORA-025. Layers role-specific depth dimension demanded by OJ 'commensurate to the remit of their functions' qualifier.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.at-02: workforce understand roles in cybersecurity objectives

nodes.label: SR-DORA-025: Compulsory ICT security awareness and resilience training for staff
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(6) compulsory modules with complexity commensurate to function remit. Workforce-scale counterpart to Art. 5(4) management-body training. T4-vs-text gap on DORA-C26 mapping to patch management.
nodes.norm_label: sr-dora-025: compulsory ict security awareness and resilience training for staff

nodes.label: SR-CRA-006 — Pre-Market Elimination of Known Exploitable Vulnerabilities
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part I (2)(a): no known exploitable vulnerabilities at market placement. 'Known' is VAG+POLY S3 — constructive-knowledge baseline chosen (R2): knowledge a reasonable manufacturer exercising Annex VII §3 due diligence should have.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-006 — pre-market elimination of known exploitable vulnerabilities

nodes.label: SR-CRA-007 — Vulnerability and Component Identification with SBOM
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part II (1): identify and document vulnerabilities and components; SBOM in commonly used machine-readable format covering at least top-level dependencies. 'Top-level dependencies' is POLY-S2 (depth-1 vs full transitive closure).
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-007 — vulnerability and component identification with sbom

nodes.label: SR-CRA-008 — Machine-Readable SBOM Format
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part II (1) + Art. 3(39): SBOM format obligation. 'Commonly used and machine-readable' is POLY+VAG S3. Art. 13(24) authorises Commission implementing acts to specify format. Format names intentionally not introduced to honour tech-stack denylist.

nodes.label: Cross-Regulation Standards Encouragement Pattern
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 25 mirrors CRA Art. 27 (presumption of conformity via harmonised standards) and AI Act Art. 40 (conformity assessment via harmonised standards). The 'European and international standards and technical specifications' triplet is the standard cross-regulation formulation.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 25 — Member State Standards Encouragement
nodes.rationale: Encouragement-only (no binding entity obligation). Technology-neutrality clause is most distinctive phrase in Chapter IV. ENISA 'shall draw up advice and guidelines' is one of few mandatory ENISA provisions. Mirrors CRA Art. 27 and AI Act Art. 40 standardisation provisions.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 25 — member state standards encouragement

nodes.label: SR-CRA-107: User-facing lifecycle security instructions package
nodes.rationale: Annex II §8(a)-(f) + Art. 13(18): detailed instructions covering commissioning, data security, updates, decommissioning, auto-update opt-out, integrator info. Mapped to PR.AT-01 (partial fit).
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-107: user-facing lifecycle security instructions package

nodes.label: SR-CRA-018: Automatic security updates with user opt-out capability
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part I (2)(c) + Annex II §8(e): auto-update on by default, clear opt-out, postponement option, user informed how to disable. Mapped to PR.PS-01 and PR.DS-12. Key ambiguity: 'appropriate timeframe' is VAG-S3, anchored to vulnerability severity and risk assessment.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-018: automatic security updates with user opt-out capability

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-024: Privacy by Design
nodes.rationale: Appropriate technical and organisational measures designed to implement data-protection principles in an effective manner, integrated at means-determination and during processing.

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.PS-06: Secure Software Development Practices Integrated
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-039, 040, 041 for SDLC-integrated privacy by design/default and pseudonymisation.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ps-06: secure software development practices integrated

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 25(1): Privacy by Design
nodes.rationale: Requires implementation of appropriate technical and organisational measures both at determination of means and at processing itself, designed to implement data-protection principles.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 25(2): Privacy by Default
nodes.rationale: Only data necessary for each specific purpose processed; four AND-coordinated dimensions (amount, extent, period, accessibility) bounded to minimum.

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.PS-06: Secure SDLC practices integrated
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ps-06: secure sdlc practices integrated

nodes.label: SR-CRA-025: Secure-by-default configuration with reset capability
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part I (2)(b) secure-by-default floor with reset-to-original-state recovery path and tailor-made carve-out.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-025: secure-by-default configuration with reset capability

nodes.label: SR-CRA-064: Three-phase design, development, and production
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(1) umbrella duty mapping three coordinated verbs to three SDLC lifecycle phases; proportionality anchored in Art. 13(2) risk assessment.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-064: three-phase design, development, and production

nodes.label: SR-CRA-065: Lifecycle cybersecurity risk assessment including health-and-safety impact
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(2) six-phase lifecycle risk assessment with CRA-unique health-and-safety qualifier bridging cyber-physical harm.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-065: lifecycle cybersecurity risk assessment including health-and-safety impact

nodes.label: SR-CRA-022: Effective and regular security tests with evidence retention
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part II (3) testing duty with Annex VII §6 evidence and Annex VIII Part II (8) Module B periodic audits.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-022: effective and regular security tests with evidence retention

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-039: Privacy by Design Integrated at Means-and-Processing Determination
nodes.rationale: Art. 25(1) fires both at means-determination and during ongoing processing. 'State of the art' anchored to industry frameworks (ISO 27001, NIST SP 800-53, PCI-DSS, ISO 27701) as the reference set at design time.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-039: privacy by design integrated at means-and-processing determination

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-040: Pseudonymisation-by-Design with Separation of Identifying Information
nodes.rationale: Pseudonymisation is a design choice, not a runtime patch. The obligation only fires when embedded at means-determination through the SDLC. Preserves the Art. 34(3)(a) unintelligibility carve-out by maintaining separation of identifying information.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-040: pseudonymisation-by-design with separation of identifying information

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-041: Privacy by Default Across Four Coordinated Minimisation Dimensions
nodes.rationale: Art. 25(2) binds four AND-coordinated dimensions (amount, extent, period, accessibility) to what is necessary for each specific purpose, with default-deny accessibility.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-041: privacy by default across four coordinated minimisation dimensions

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-031: Processor erasure or return at end of processing services
nodes.rationale: Art. 28(3)(g) requires processor to delete or return all personal data at contract end; Art. 5(1)(e) storage limitation and Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation provide upstream justification. Mapped to NIST CSF PR.DS-10 and GV.SC-04.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-031: processor erasure or return at end of processing services

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-037: Controller-evidenced processor erasure on contract end
nodes.rationale: Controller-side audit-and-evidence obligation for processor contract-end erasure. Mapped to NIST CSF PR.DS-12 and GV.SC-04.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-037: controller-evidenced processor erasure on contract end

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-029: Basic cyber-hygiene practices baseline across workforce and systems
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(g) first clause: basic cyber hygiene practices. Mapped to NIST CSF PR.AT-01 and PR.PS-01.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-029: basic cyber-hygiene practices baseline across workforce and systems

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-043: Appropriate technical and organisational measures under Art. 24(1)
nodes.rationale: Art. 24(1) is the operational-responsibility centrepiece: controller must implement appropriate measures and demonstrate compliance. Mapped to NIST CSF GV.PO-01, GV.PO-02, GV.RM-04.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-043: appropriate technical and organisational measures under art. 24(1)

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-039: Risk-calibrated technical, operational and organisational measures baseline
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(1) chapeau: appropriate and proportionate measures. Dominant Berry VAG-S3 ambiguity of NIS2. Mapped to NIST CSF GV.RM-06 and ID.RA-06.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-039: risk-calibrated technical, operational and organisational measures baseline

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-009: All-hazards monitoring to surface adverse events
nodes.rationale: Detection dimension of Art. 21(2)(b) under all-hazards approach. Mapped to NIST CSF DE.CM-01 and DE.CM-09.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-009: all-hazards monitoring to surface adverse events

nodes.label: SO-NIS2-005: Incident handling capability
nodes.rationale: Security objective: prevention, detection, analysis, containment, response, recovery of incidents.

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-040: All-hazards methodology spanning cyber, physical and operational risks
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2) chapeau: all-hazards approach protecting NIS and physical environment. Mapped to NIST CSF GV.RM-06 and PR.IR-01.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-040: all-hazards methodology spanning cyber, physical and operational risks

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-041: Physical-environment protection ensures NIS substrate resilience
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2) chapeau second clause: physical environment of NIS. Out-of-scope for software-compliance track. Mapped to NIST CSF GV.RM-06.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-041: physical-environment protection ensures nis substrate resilience

nodes.label: SR-CRA-045: Non-Conformity Corrective Measures, Withdrawal, or Recall
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(21) immediate corrective action on non-conformity; covers product-side and process-side; 'know or have reason to believe' trigger; maps to RS.MI-01, RS.MI-02, GV.OV-02.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-045: non-conformity corrective measures, withdrawal, or recall

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28(1): Processor Selection
nodes.rationale: Controller must use only processors providing sufficient guarantees to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures ensuring GDPR compliance and data-subject rights protection. The sufficient-guarantees threshold.

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.SC-02: Suppliers Prioritized and Assessed Using SCRM
nodes.rationale: Due-diligence discipline for processor selection and cross-border transfer inventory.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.sc-02: suppliers prioritized and assessed using scrm

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.SC-03: Contracts Used to Implement SCRM
nodes.rationale: Vehicle for translating processor-side obligations into contractually binding form; eight sub-clauses map one-to-one to implementation measures.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.sc-03: contracts used to implement scrm

nodes.label: SR-CRA-050: Third-party component due diligence including non-commercial OSS
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(5) due-diligence duty explicitly includes non-commercial OSS; transfers assessment duty to integrating manufacturer without converting maintainer into manufacturer.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-050: third-party component due diligence including non-commercial oss

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-033: Processor Due Diligence with Documented Sufficient Guarantees
nodes.rationale: Art. 28(1) sufficient-guarantees threshold operationalised as documented due-diligence practice: written questionnaire, certifications review, security-measures audit, sub-processor inventory, and contractual Art. 28(3) clauses. Mapped to GV.SC-02 (due-diligence) and GV.SC-03 (contractual realisation).
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-033: processor due diligence with documented sufficient guarantees

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-055: Adequacy-Governed Cross-Border Transfer Inventory
nodes.rationale: Art. 44 umbrella principle; Art. 45(1) adequacy exemption; Art. 45(3) periodic review; Schrems II substantial-equivalence test.

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-058: Binding Corporate Rules for Intragroup Transfers
nodes.rationale: Art. 4(20) BCR definition; Art. 47(2) 14 mandatory content items (closed list); legally binding, enforceable rights, supervisory approval.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-058: binding corporate rules for intragroup transfers

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-060: Joint-Controller Role Allocation Through Binding Arrangement
nodes.rationale: Art. 26(1) transparent arrangement; CJEU IAB Europe C-604/22 extends joint-controller to parties with determinative influence even without processing.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-060: joint-controller role allocation through binding arrangement

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-011: Instruction-Bound Processing Under Least-Privilege
nodes.rationale: Chain-of-authority: controller to processor to authorised persons; documented instructions binding each link per Arts. 29, 32(4), 28(3)(a)/(b).

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-012: Confidentiality Undertakings for Authorised Personnel
nodes.rationale: Art. 28(3)(b) confidentiality ring around any natural person accessing personal data; independent of instruction obligation.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-012: confidentiality undertakings for authorised personnel

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-034: Eight-Element Processor Contract with Audit and Instruction Clauses
nodes.rationale: Art. 28(3)(a)-(h) closed AND-list: all eight sub-clauses mandatory in the processor contract; omitting any one puts both parties in non-compliance.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-034: eight-element processor contract with audit and instruction clauses

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-036: Sub-Processor Authorisation with Controller Change-Notification
nodes.rationale: Art. 28(2) requires prior specific or general written authorisation for sub-processors; in general authorisation case, processor must inform controller of changes giving opportunity to object.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-036: sub-processor authorisation with controller change-notification

nodes.label: SR-CRA-091: EU declaration accompanies or is web-accessible with product
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(20)/Annex II §6: full or simplified EU declaration with product, or internet address. Mapped to GV.OC-03.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-091: eu declaration accompanies or is web-accessible with product

nodes.label: SR-CRA-099: Commission implementing and delegated acts operationalisation
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(24)/(25), 14(9)/(10), 7(3)/(4), 30(6): Commission and ADCO implementing/delegated acts machinery for SBOM, dependency assessment, notification, Annex III amendments, labels. Mapped to GV.PO-02 and GV.OV-01.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-099: commission implementing and delegated acts operationalisation

nodes.label: SR-CRA-114: ENISA biennial report, EU vulnerability database, CSIRT helpdesk
nodes.rationale: Art. 16(3)/17(3)/(5)/(6): CSIRT-MSA notification, ENISA biennial report, EU vulnerability database (NIS 2 Art. 12(2)), CSIRT helpdesk. Mapped to RS.CO-04 and ID.IM-04.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-114: enisa biennial report, eu vulnerability database, csirt helpdesk

nodes.label: SR-CRA-034: Severe-incident CIA-of-sensitive-data categorisation test
nodes.rationale: Art. 14(5)(a) + NIS 2 Art. 6(2): incident is severe where it negatively affects or is capable of affecting CIA+authenticity of sensitive/important data or functions. Disjunctive-inclusion: any one CIA dimension triggers severity. Mapped to ID.RA-04 and RS.MA-03.

nodes.label: SO-CRA-058: Technical documentation + conformity assessment + EU declaration + CE marking
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(12), 31(1)/(2), 28(1)/(2)/(4), 30(1)/(3): before placing on market, manufacturer draws up tech docs, carries out conformity assessment, draws EU declaration, affixes CE marking. Sub-domain D-09.4.
nodes.norm_label: so-cra-058: technical documentation + conformity assessment + eu declaration + ce marking

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-031: Audit-Grade Records Integrity
nodes.rationale: Compliance records maintained with integrity and traceability sufficient for supervisory inspections. Source: Art. 30(3), 5(2), 31.

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-021: Disproportionate-Effort Public Communication Substitute
nodes.rationale: Art. 34(3)(c) narrow exception; public communication must achieve equally effective reach; high bar, not routine opt-out.

nodes.label: Berry Ambiguity Classification Framework
nodes.rationale: Provides the analytical taxonomy (VAG, POLY, COORD, SCOPE-Q) and severity levels (S2, S3) used across all clause analyses. Key sections: §5.1 (vague terms), §3.3.1 (polysemy), §5.4.7 (coordination/AND-OR), §5.5 (parallelism), §5.2.1 (scope limiters).

nodes.label: Open-List Drafting Convention (such as / at least / including)
nodes.rationale: Regulatory-drafting convention shared across CRA, NIS2, and DORA. DORA Art. 25(1) 12-modality list, CRA Annex I Part I §2(d), NIS2 Art. 21(2)(c) 'such as backup management' all use the same Berry §5.1 open-list signal. Not an artefact of any single regulation.
nodes.norm_label: open-list drafting convention (such as / at least / including)

nodes.label: Proportionality Overlay (Cross-Regulation)
nodes.rationale: DORA Art. 4 more elaborate than NIS2 Art. 1(2) and CRA Art. 1(2). DORA provides explicit CA-review (CL4-3) that NIS2 and CRA lack. NIS2 Art. 21(1) uses 'appropriate and proportionate' (2 qualifiers); DORA Art. 6(1) uses 3-attribute triad; GDPR Art. 24 uses 'appropriate' (1 qualifier).

nodes.label: State-of-the-Art (VAG-S3 Recurring Term)
nodes.rationale: Berry-classic vague term appearing in NIS2 Art. 21(1), GDPR Art. 25(1), GDPR Art. 32(1), CRA Annex I Part I (2)(e). Three readings: best practice (R1), published standards (R2), cutting-edge research (R3). R3 rejected by cost-of-implementation consideration. R1 vs R2 produce materially distinct obligations.

nodes.label: T3-vs-Text Gap Pattern
nodes.rationale: Recurring pattern where T3 taxonomy imposes distinctions not present in OJ text: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(h) split into 3 sub-domains (at-rest/in-transit/key-mgmt), Art. 21(2)(e) read as CI/CD pipeline, Art. 21(2)(j) read as audit logging, Art. 21(2)(g) read as role-specific training. Largest gap: 3 T3 clauses on 1 OJ sub-point.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13 — Security Objectives & Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split (SO + SR) generated from 01_SecurityObjectives.md and 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md. Covers SO-CRA-006 through SO-CRA-070 and SR-CRA-001 through SR-CRA-003. References D-01.1 through D-10.2 cross-regulation domain analyses.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-003 — Confidentiality of Data in Transit
nodes.rationale: Maps to NIST CSF PR.DS-02 and PR.IR-01. In-transit stratum is most frequently observed breach vector. SCOPE-Q-S2: whether protection covers internal east-west traffic or only external edges (answer: both, risk-assessment modulates primitive strength).
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-003 — confidentiality of data in transit

nodes.label: DORA Art. 21 — Single EU Hub Feasibility
nodes.rationale: Regulator-internal (ESAs/NCA institutional architecture, not entity-facing). 7 enumerated elements under 'at least' open qualifier. 'Single EU Hub' architecture undefined (centralised platform vs. API gateway vs. single standard).
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 21 — single eu hub feasibility

nodes.label: DORA Art. 25 — Digital Operational Resilience Testing
nodes.rationale: 12-modality open list (such as pattern) — identical structural pattern to CRA Annex I Part I §2(d). Art. 25(2) is sectoral carve-out for CSDs/CCPs (pre-deployment vulnerability assessments) — unique in Ch. IV. No other clause names specific entity types.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 25 — digital operational resilience testing

nodes.label: DORA Art. 4 — Proportionality Principle
nodes.rationale: Three distinct proportionality regimes: Ch. II default (self-implementing), Ch. III/IV/V Sec. I (deferred to chapter-specific clauses), CA-review (addressed to CAs). More elaborate than NIS2 Art. 1(2) and CRA Art. 1(2) — provides explicit CA-review that neither has. Propagates to every clause in Ch. II–V Sec. I.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 5 — Governance and Organisation
nodes.rationale: Management body 4-verb coordination (define, approve, oversee, be responsible for). 'Effective and prudent' dual qualifier (S3). Three lines of defence model per Art. 6(4) cross-reference. Art. 4 proportionality applies.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 6 — ICT Risk Management Framework
nodes.rationale: Three-attribute triad (sound, comprehensive, well-documented) is most demanding framework chapeau in 5-regulation corpus. 5-category open list (strategies, policies, procedures, protocols, tools). 'Minimise impact' resolved via Art. 6(8)(b) risk tolerance. Definitional anchor: DORA Art. 3(2) → NIS2 Art. 6(1).
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 6 — ict risk management framework

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(1) — Risk-Management Factors
nodes.rationale: Seven VAG/POLY instances identified (state-of-the-art, cost of implementation, appropriate to risks, exposure, size, likelihood/severity, societal/economic impact). R3 (risk-tiered) is dominant for proportionality function. Berry anchors at §5.1, §3.3.1, §5.4.7.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(b) — Incident Handling
nodes.rationale: Single phrase constitutes entire sub-point. Undefined; operational content delegated to standards and national implementation. T3 reads as real-time detection — OJ text contains no timeliness qualifier. Whether includes detection (vs. only response) is ambiguous (NIST SP 800-61 vs. EU ALTA-IR readings).

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(c) — Business Continuity and Crisis Management
nodes.rationale: 'Such as' opens illustrative list inside AND of business continuity and crisis management. Nesting admits ≥3 parse trees. Business continuity polysemy: service continuity vs. data continuity vs. organisational continuity — three senses imply different control sets.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 21(2)(c) — business continuity and crisis management

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(d) — Supply Chain Security
nodes.rationale: 'Direct' is a critical scope-limiter (S3): contractual Tier-1 vs. technical integration vs. operational dependency. Determines whether obligation reaches 1-hop, n-hop, or only contractual counterparties — central operational question of NIS2 supply-chain compliance.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(e) — Security in Development
nodes.rationale: Covers acquisition, development, maintenance (three coordinated lifecycle phases). T3 reads as CI/CD Pipeline Security — OJ text contains no pipeline/CI/CD words. T3-vs-text gap pattern same as GDPR C15/C17/C28 and CRA C03/C06.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(g) — Cyber Hygiene and Training
nodes.rationale: 'Basic cyber hygiene' is undefined technical compound (ENISA guidance gives list but regulation does not incorporate). T3 reads as role-specific training — OJ text contains neither 'role-specific' nor 'staff with security responsibilities'. AND requires both hygiene and training but content overlap is large.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 21(2)(g) — cyber hygiene and training

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(h) — Cryptography and Encryption
nodes.rationale: Cryptography ⊃ encryption (R1 dominant). 'Where appropriate' is a soft hedge making encryption discretionary. AND-with-hedge coordination (S3). T3 splits into at-rest/in-transit/key-management — no such distinction in OJ text (largest single T3-vs-text gap in NIS2 corpus).

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(i) — HR Security, Access Control, Asset Management
nodes.rationale: Three distinct security domains coordinated by AND (S3). Each independently a discipline (ISO 27001 A.6, A.5.15, A.5.9). Clause does not signal whether partial compliance (2 of 3) satisfies obligation. T3 reads as role-based access/need-to-know/least-privilege — OJ text mentions only 'access control policies'.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 21(2)(i) — hr security, access control, asset management

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(j) — MFA and Communications Security
nodes.rationale: Four distinct obligations coordinated via OR and AND in one sub-point. Parse tree admits ≥6 distinct obligation shapes. 'Where appropriate' closes entire sub-point, softening all four obligations (S3). T3 reads as Audit Logging — OJ text does not mention logging.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 21(2)(j) — mfa and communications security

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-032: Structured electronic access copy in commonly used format
nodes.rationale: Art. 15(1)/(3) grants data subject right to obtain copy in commonly used electronic form. Mapped to NIST CSF PR.DS-10 and PR.DS-12.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-032: structured electronic access copy in commonly used format

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-044: Continuous evidence-of-compliance with performance review
nodes.rationale: Art. 5(2), Art. 24(1), Art. 30(1) create accountability-and-evidence chain. Mapped to NIST CSF GV.PO-02 and GV.OV-03.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-044: continuous evidence-of-compliance with performance review

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-065: Plain-language transparent privacy notice design
nodes.rationale: Art. 12(1) requires concise, transparent, intelligible, easily accessible, clear, plain language. Mapped to NIST CSF GV.PO-02 and PR.AA-02.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-065: plain-language transparent privacy notice design

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-006: Strong authentication through MFA or continuous alternatives
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(j) requires MFA or continuous authentication where appropriate. Mapped to NIST CSF PR.AA-03 and PR.AA-05.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-006: strong authentication through mfa or continuous alternatives

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-007: Secured internal and emergency communications channels
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(j) second and third clauses: secured voice/video/text and emergency communications. Mapped to NIST CSF PR.DS-02 and PR.IR-03.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-007: secured internal and emergency communications channels

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-019: Business continuity, backup, recovery, and crisis triad
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(c): business continuity, backup management, disaster recovery, and crisis management. Mapped to NIST CSF RC.RP-04 and PR.DS-11.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-019: business continuity, backup, recovery, and crisis triad

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-025: Coordinated supply-chain risk assessments integrated into supplier decisions
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(3) sentence 2: take into account Art. 22(1) coordinated assessments. Mapped to NIST CSF ID.RA-02 and GV.SC-02.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-025: coordinated supply-chain risk assessments integrated into supplier decisions

nodes.label: SR-CRA-017 — Free-of-charge Update Dissemination with Advisory Messages
nodes.rationale: CRA Annex I Part II (8) + Part I (2)(c): security updates disseminated without delay, free of charge with advisory messages. Maps to PR.PS-02, RS.CO-03.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-017 — free-of-charge update dissemination with advisory messages

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RM-04
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF anchor for governance/risk management. Mapped to NIS2 sub-requirement (1.1.2) and DORA classification-driven cipher-strength overlay (SR-DORA-003).

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.DS-01
nodes.rationale: NIST Cybersecurity Framework anchor for data-at-rest protection. Primary CSF mapping for all four sub-requirements (1.1.1–1.1.4) and the high-level requirement 1.1.

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.DS-02
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF anchor for data-at-rest protection. Mapped to NIS2 sub-requirement (1.1.2) and DORA sub-requirement (1.1.4).

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.DS-10
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF anchor for data-at-rest protection. Mapped to GDPR sub-requirement (1.1.1) and DORA sub-requirement (1.1.4).

nodes.label: Requirement 1.1 — Data at Rest Protection (Multi-Reg)
nodes.rationale: Volere §15 integrity requirement. MUST priority, TEST verification. NIST CSF: PR.DS-01. Engages when ≥2 applicable regs overlap on same datastore. Fit criterion: AES-256+ with separated key custody, strictest applicable floor (CRA state-of-the-art).

nodes.label: Requirement 1.1.1 — Personal Data at Rest (GDPR)
nodes.rationale: GDPR-specific sub-requirement. MUST/TEST. NIST CSF: PR.DS-01, PR.DS-10. Depends on 1.3 (Key Management). Fit: AES-256+ on personal-data volumes, 5 Art. 32(1) preamble factors cited in risk assessment.

nodes.label: Requirement 1.1.2 — NIS Scope Data at Rest
nodes.rationale: NIS2-specific sub-requirement. MUST/TEST. NIST CSF: PR.DS-01, PR.DS-02, GV.RM-04. Documented cryptography policy per Art. 21(2)(h). 'Where appropriate' hedge admits narrower scope than GDPR.
nodes.norm_label: requirement 1.1.2 — nis scope data at rest

nodes.label: Requirement 1.1.3 — Product Data at Rest (CRA)
nodes.rationale: CRA-specific sub-requirement. MUST/TEST. NIST CSF: PR.DS-01. State-of-the-art encryption (AES-256 min or harmonised-standards equivalent). 'Render unintelligible' test per Annex I (2)(e). Strictest floor — discharges other regs.

nodes.label: Requirement 1.1.4 — Financial Entity ICT Data at Rest (DORA)
nodes.rationale: DORA-specific sub-requirement. MUST/TEST. NIST CSF: PR.DS-01. High-standards encryption + classification-driven cipher-strength overlay (Art. 9(4)(d) + SR-DORA-003). EBA/ESMA/EIOPA RTS-conformant under Art. 15.
nodes.norm_label: requirement 1.1.4 — financial entity ict data at rest (dora)

nodes.label: SO-CRA-002 (Canonical CRA SO)
nodes.rationale: Canonical security objective for CRA in D-01.1: State-of-the-art encryption of stored data (personal or other). Inherited by SO-D-01.1.CRA.

nodes.label: SO-NIS2-001 (Canonical NIS2 SO)
nodes.rationale: Canonical security objective for NIS2 in D-01.1: Cryptography policies covering CIA of stored/transmitted/processed data. Inherited by SO-D-01.1.NIS2.

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-001 (Security Requirement)
nodes.rationale: Source security requirement for NIS2 in D-01.1. Contains Art. 21(2)(h) verbatim text and CSF mapping (PR.DS-01, PR.DS-02, GV.RM-04).

nodes.label: SR-CRA-038 — Voluntary Third-party Vulnerability Reporting with CSIRT Bridge
nodes.rationale: CRA Art. 15(1)-(4): voluntary AEV/SI reporting by any person, CSIRT informs manufacturer, Art. 17(4) liability shield. Maps to RS.CO-03, GV.SC-01.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-038 — voluntary third-party vulnerability reporting with csirt bridge

nodes.label: SR-DORA-007 — Documented Patch and Update Governance
nodes.rationale: DORA Art. 9(4)(f) appropriate and comprehensive documented policies for patches and updates. Maps to PR.PS-02, ID.RA-01.
nodes.norm_label: sr-dora-007 — documented patch and update governance

nodes.label: SO-CRA-027: Severe Incident Definition
nodes.rationale: Incident is severe where it negatively affects CIA of sensitive/important data OR leads to malicious code execution; Art. 14(5)(a)+(b).

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 PR.AA-05: Access Permissions Managed per Least Privilege
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 pr.aa-05: access permissions managed per least privilege

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 PR.AA-06: Access Limited to Authorized Users, Services, Hardware
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 pr.aa-06: access limited to authorized users, services, hardware

nodes.label: SO-DORA-006: Security Objective (linked to Access Governance)
nodes.norm_label: so-dora-006: security objective (linked to access governance)

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 27: Representative in the Union
nodes.rationale: Art. 27(1) requires non-EU controller/processor to designate in writing a Union representative; Art. 27(2)(a) conjunctive exception for occasional, small-scale, low-risk processing.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 27: representative in the union

nodes.label: NIS 2 Directive (EU) 2022/2555
nodes.rationale: Parallel cybersecurity obligations for NSIEs: Art. 21(2)(a) inventory, (b) monitoring, (c) risk identification, (d) cryptography, (e) supply-chain, (f) policy review, (g) training. DORA financial entities retain joint obligations where also NSIEs.

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OC-02: Internal and External Stakeholders Understood
nodes.rationale: Mapped by SR-GDPR-038; stakeholder-recognition discipline for non-EU controller representative designation.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.oc-02: internal and external stakeholders understood

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RR-02: Cybersecurity risk roles established and enforced
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.rr-02: cybersecurity risk roles established and enforced

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RM-02: Risk Roles and Responsibilities Established
nodes.rationale: Risk roles, responsibilities, authorities, and accountabilities established and communicated; communication-and-understanding engine.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.rm-02: risk roles and responsibilities established

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RR-02: Risk Roles and Responsibilities
nodes.rationale: Roles, responsibilities, authorities, accountabilities established, communicated, understood, enforced. Anchors 3LoD structural separation.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.rr-02: risk roles and responsibilities

nodes.label: SR-DORA-010: Least-Privilege Physical and Logical Access Governance
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(4)(c) requires limiting access to what is required for legitimate and approved functions only. The 'legitimate AND approved' two-axis gating is the substantive burden. T4-vs-text gap noted: OJ text does not contain 'need-to-know' or 'least privilege' explicitly.
nodes.norm_label: sr-dora-010: least-privilege physical and logical access governance

nodes.label: SR-DORA-023 — ICT Change Management under Six-step Risk-based Process
nodes.rationale: DORA Art. 9(4)(e) documented policies for ICT change management: recorded, tested, assessed, approved, implemented, verified. Maps to PR.PS-01, PR.PS-02, PR.PS-06.
nodes.norm_label: sr-dora-023 — ict change management under six-step risk-based process

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32 — Security Objectives & Security Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split document covering Art. 32 security measures, Art. 28 processor contracts, Art. 25 privacy by design, Art. 30 records of processing, and Art. 32(2) risk enumeration.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 32 — security objectives & security rules

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-006: Authorised persons act on instructions + confidentiality
nodes.norm_label: so-gdpr-006: authorised persons act on instructions + confidentiality

nodes.label: Berry Ambiguity Framework
nodes.rationale: Analytical framework (§5.1 VAG, §5.4.7 COORD, §3.3.1 POLY, §5.7 temporal) used across all regulatory analyses to classify and severity-rank (S2/S3) linguistic ambiguities in EU regulatory text.

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-014 — Accuracy, Robustness, Cybersecurity Baseline
nodes.rationale: Art. 15(1): 3-way AND (accuracy AND robustness AND cybersecurity) — no partial compliance. Corner-stone substantive duty of high-risk AI title, on par with Art. 9 and Art. 10. Three S3 ambiguity features: VAG-3 on properties, POLY-S3 on accuracy/robustness decomposition, COORD-S2 on AND.

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-016 — AI-Specific Attack Vector Mitigation
nodes.rationale: Art. 15(4)-(5): 5-way AND of IR phases (prevent, detect, respond, resolve, control) × 6-way OR of attack types (data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples, confidentiality attacks, model flaws). S3 COORD axis; ≥30 distinct obligation shapes. AI-specific complement to CRA/NIS2 conventional cybersecurity.

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-021 — Post-Market Monitoring Feedback Loop
nodes.rationale: Art. 72(1)-(2): PMM system proportionate to AI technology and risks; actively and systematically collect, document, analyse. Feeds Art. 15(1) lifecycle consistency and Art. 73 reporting. Art. 74(1) extends Reg. 2019/1020 market-surveillance to AI. Borrows from MDR Art. 83 implicitly.

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-022 — Tiered Serious Incident Reporting
nodes.rationale: Art. 73(1)-(4): 3 timelines (15/10/2 days) × 2 attribution thresholds (awareness OR reasonable likelihood). Most temporally complex notification clause in AEGIS corpus. Cross-article POLY: Art. 73 vs Art. 55 boundary undefined.

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-023 — GPAI Model Evaluation for Systemic Risk
nodes.rationale: Art. 55(1)(a): standardised protocols + state of the art + systemic risks — second-most-consequential AI Act ambiguity. 'Systemic risks' borrowed from financial-services regulation (DORA Art. 4(50)); AI-Act use is broader. Parallel to but distinct from Title III high-risk obligations.
nodes.norm_label: sr-aiact-023 — gpai model evaluation for systemic risk

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-024 — GPAI Serious Incident Reporting to AI Office
nodes.rationale: Art. 55(1)(c): report to AI Office (EU-level) without undue delay; distinct from Art. 73 (MS market surveillance). Upstream companion to high-risk Art. 73. 'Without undue delay' is VAG-3; 'as appropriate' is POLY-3.
nodes.norm_label: sr-aiact-024 — gpai serious incident reporting to ai office

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-001 — Continuous Risk-Management Governance
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(1) umbrella provision: establish, implement, document, maintain risk management system across full lifecycle. Framework-agnostic (ISO 31000, NIST AI RMF, or bespoke). Mirrors GDPR Art. 32 and DORA Art. 6 continuous risk-treatment duty.

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-002 — Four-Step Risk Identification and Treatment
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(2)(a)-(d) closed cumulative list: identify/analyze, estimate/evaluate (incl. foreseeable misuse), evaluate PMM data, adopt measures. 'Reasonably foreseeable' recurs 4× with no OJ anchor — central AI Act ambiguity.
nodes.norm_label: sr-aiact-002 — four-step risk identification and treatment

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-017 — Quality Management System
nodes.rationale: Art. 17(1) QMS: 13-element closed list (a)-(m); sub-point (g) cross-refers to Art. 9 risk management system. Inspired by ISO 9001 but no specific standard mandated. Umbrella obligation examined first in conformity assessment.

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-018 — Secure Design Control and Verification (SDLC)
nodes.rationale: Art. 17(1)(c): techniques, procedures, systematic actions for design, design control, design verification. Operational bridge between Art. 17 QMS and Art. 9 risk management on one side, Art. 15 accuracy/robustness/cybersecurity on the other.
nodes.norm_label: sr-aiact-018 — secure design control and verification (sdlc)

nodes.label: CRA Art. 14 — Vulnerability Reporting
nodes.rationale: Referenced as cross-regulation parallel for 'becomes aware' awareness-trigger ambiguity (same Berry §5.7 pattern as GDPR Art. 33, NIS2 C30, DORA Art. 19, AI Act Art. 73).

nodes.label: DORA Art. 19 — Major ICT Incident Reporting
nodes.rationale: 3-tier reporting (initial/intermediate/final) with RTS-dependent time limits; sector-differentiated template (deliberate design choice vs NIS2 uniform 24h/72h/1-month); voluntary cyber-threat notification (Art. 19(2)) is CA-directed unlike NIS2 recipient-directed.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 19 — major ict incident reporting

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32 — Security Measures
nodes.rationale: 4-element closed list (pseudonymisation/encryption, CIA+R, restore-in-timely-manner, regular-testing); 'timely manner' is textbook Berry-flagged temporal vague phrase; R1 (RTO per activity) vs R2 (as-soon-as-practicable) yield distinct BCP/DRP scope.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 23 — Incident Reporting (24h/72h/1-month)
nodes.rationale: Uniform 24h/72h/1-month triple-tier template; DORA adopts sector-differentiated template that is more flexible but less predictable. NIS2 Art. 23(2) is recipient-directed (entity-to-recipient) vs DORA Art. 19(2) CA-directed.

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-009: Proportionate identity verification for rights requests
nodes.rationale: Art. 12(6) permits verification only to extent necessary. Full ID-document collection on any doubt rejected as disproportionate under Art. 5(1)(c). Graduated verification standard per request risk level.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-009: proportionate identity verification for rights requests

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33 — Security Objectives & Security Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split document covering breach notification to supervisory authority (Art. 33(1)), processor-to-controller notification (Art. 33(2)), notification content (Art. 33(3)), and breach detection.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 33 — security objectives & security rules

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 34 — Security Objectives & Security Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split document covering high-risk breach communication to data subjects (Art. 34(1)), content requirements (Art. 34(2)), and three exceptions (Art. 34(3)(a)-(c)).
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 34 — security objectives & security rules

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 4 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split (SO + SR) generated from 01_SecurityObjectives.md and 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md. The originals remain the authoritative aggregate indexes.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(2) — Accountability
nodes.rationale: Shifts the demonstration duty to the controller; every SR in this document references Art. 5(2) as the ex post accountability standard for demonstrating compliance.

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-047: Risk-change-triggered DPIA review with periodic cadence
nodes.rationale: Art. 35(11) requires DPIA review on material risk change; mapped to NIST ID.IM-04 and ID.RA-06 for contextual-change monitoring and risk-response-rerun.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-047: risk-change-triggered dpia review with periodic cadence

nodes.label: SO-CRA-034: Data Minimisation
nodes.rationale: Data limited to adequate, relevant, necessary for intended purpose; Annex I Part I (2)(g) + Art. 13(3) + Art. 3(23).

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 4(1): Personal Data Definition
nodes.rationale: Any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person. The material scope definition referenced by nearly all SRs. CJEU Breyer C-582/14 'means likely reasonably to be used' test for identifiability.

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-027: Controller Responsible for and Able to Demonstrate Compliance
nodes.rationale: Art. 5(2) accountability principle. Referenced throughout security_rationale fields as the ex-post demonstration standard against which all SRs must be evidenced.
nodes.norm_label: so-gdpr-027: controller responsible for and able to demonstrate compliance

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 21 - Basic Cybersecurity Measures
nodes.rationale: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 parallel baseline obligations for NSIEs. DORA financial entities retain as joint obligation where they also operate as NIS 2 entities.

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.DS-12: Data Risk Strategy
nodes.rationale: Data-handling rules tiered against impact assessment (RTO/RPO alignment with business-criticality). Ensures 4x3 matrix reflects entity's own criticality taxonomy.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ds-12: data risk strategy

nodes.label: SR-CRA-046: Product-Design Data Minimisation Adequate to Intended Purpose
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part I (2)(g) data minimisation borrowing GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) language at product-design level; maps to PR.DS-12 and ID.AM-03; anchored to Art. 3(23) intended purpose.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-046: product-design data minimisation adequate to intended purpose

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5 Security Rules Document
nodes.rationale: Per-article split of GDPR Art. 5 principles (lawfulness, fairness, transparency, purpose limitation, minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity/confidentiality, accountability) operationalised into Security Rules mapped to NIST CSF 2.0. Contains the full SR catalogue from SR-GDPR-001 through SR-GDPR-026.

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-013: Privacy-by-Default Across Collection, Retention, Exposure
nodes.rationale: Art. 25(2) four-dimensional AND-coordinated default: amount, extent, period, accessibility all minimised simultaneously.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-013: privacy-by-default across collection, retention, exposure

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-006: Rectification Workflow with Downstream Cascade Propagation
nodes.rationale: Four-stage workflow: request → verify (Art. 12(6)) → rectify → cascade to recipients (Art. 19). Supplementary statement mechanism for contested facts. Art. 19 cascade escape: 'impossible or disproportionate effort' is inclusive OR.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-006: rectification workflow with downstream cascade propagation

nodes.label: SO-AIACT-001 — AI Risk Management Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Umbrella security objective spanning Art. 9(1)+(2), Art. 15, Art. 72, Art. 73, Art. 55 — the continuous, iterative risk-management process across the full AI system lifecycle.

nodes.label: SO-CRA-028: User Notification + Machine-Readable Format + CSIRT Fallback
nodes.norm_label: so-cra-028: user notification + machine-readable format + csirt fallback

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9 — Security Objectives & Security Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split (SO + SR) generated from 01_SecurityObjectives.md and 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md. The originals remain the authoritative aggregate indexes.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 9 — security objectives & security rules

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 19 — Recipient Notification
nodes.rationale: Cascade notification obligation on controller; two escape clauses (impossible / disproportionate effort) per Berry §5.1; R1 vs R2 yield materially distinct cascade-notification policies.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 21 — Right to Object
nodes.rationale: Data subject right to object on grounds of particular situation; compelling legitimate grounds override; direct marketing absolute right; explicit attention requirement at first communication.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 30 — Records of processing activities
nodes.rationale: RoPA content, SA access, and 250-employee exception referenced in SR-GDPR-029, 044, 048, 050.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 30 — records of processing activities

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(1) — Data protection principles
nodes.rationale: Seven principles (lawfulness, purpose limitation, minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity/confidentiality, accountability) referenced across 12+ SRs as the foundational obligation set.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(14): Series-of-Production Conformity
nodes.rationale: Two limbs: procedural (conformity procedures) and informational (inform regulator of harmonised-standards changes). Referenced by SR-CRA-069.

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OV-01: Risk Management Strategy Outcomes Reviewed and Adjusted
nodes.rationale: Captures the strategy-outcomes-review dimension for series-production conformity. Referenced by SR-CRA-069.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.ov-01: risk management strategy outcomes reviewed and adjusted

nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-027: six documented lawfulness bases with necessity gating per purpose

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-029: Documented retention limits with erasure at purpose end
nodes.rationale: Binds Art. 5(1)(e) storage limitation, Art. 30(1)(f) retention documentation, and Art. 5(1)(c) minimisation into a chain mapped to PR.DS-12 and ID.AM-03.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-029: documented retention limits with erasure at purpose end

nodes.label: SR-CRA-069: Series-of-Production Conformity and Harmonised-Standards Monitoring
nodes.rationale: R2 reading for 'series of production': continuous production, capturing modern software-as-a-service delivery where every release is a new production event. Two limbs: procedural (conformity procedures) and informational (inform regulator of standards changes).
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-069: series-of-production conformity and harmonised-standards monitoring

nodes.norm_label: so-dora-003: risk identification and scenario management

nodes.norm_label: so-dora-005: resilience testing and adversarial verification

nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-DORA-005. Closes external-context feedback loop: supervisory guidance, ENISA reports, sectoral learnings, CTPP-concentration shifts feed scenario recalibration.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.im-04: risk management improvements informed by developments

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(1)(d): Regular Testing and Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Requires a process for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating the effectiveness of technical and organisational measures.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 32(1)(d): regular testing and evaluation

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.RA-01: Vulnerabilities in assets identified, validated, recorded
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.ra-01: vulnerabilities in assets identified, validated, recorded

nodes.rationale: Art. 35(1) requires DPIA prior to high-risk processing; Art. 35(7) specifies four content items; Art. 36(1) triggers prior consultation where residual risk remains high.
