nodes.label: GDPR Art. 35: Data Protection Impact Assessment
nodes.rationale: Art. 35(1) DPIA trigger for high-risk processing; Art. 35(7) four content items: systematic description, necessity/proportionality, risk assessment, measures envisaged.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 35: data protection impact assessment

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 35(11): DPIA Review on Risk Change
nodes.rationale: Controller must carry out review to assess whether processing is in accordance with DPIA at least when there is a change of the risk represented by processing operations.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 35(11): dpia review on risk change

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.RA-06: Risk Responses Chosen, Prioritized, Planned, Tracked
nodes.rationale: Risk-response layer for DPIA mitigation and prior-consultation trigger under Art. 35(7)(d) and Art. 36(1).
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.ra-06: risk responses chosen, prioritized, planned, tracked

nodes.label: SO-CRA-007: SBOM and component transparency
nodes.rationale: Security objective for software bill of materials and supply-chain transparency.

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-046: Four-element DPIA content with necessity and proportionality test
nodes.rationale: Art. 35(7)(a)-(d) four mandated DPIA elements with Art. 35(7)(b)-internal necessity reading (no less-intrusive alternative) distinct from Art. 6(1)(b) contract-necessity, mapped to ID.RA-05 and RS.AN-03.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-046: four-element dpia content with necessity and proportionality test

nodes.label: DORA Art. 24(1): Digital operational resilience testing
nodes.rationale: Chapter IV baseline requiring sound and comprehensive testing programme as integral part of framework.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 24(1): digital operational resilience testing

nodes.label: DORA Art. 7(2): Continuous risk identification
nodes.rationale: Requires continuous identification of all ICT risk sources and at-least-yearly scenario review.

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-023: Pre-Launch Supervisory Consultation on Residual High Risk
nodes.rationale: Art. 36(1) pre-launch gate: where DPIA identifies residual high risk after mitigation, consult before launching; 8-week supervisory window.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-023: pre-launch supervisory consultation on residual high risk

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(1)(d) — Periodic Testing of Security Measures
nodes.rationale: Requires a process for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating the effectiveness of technical and organisational measures; cadence anchored to risk-based factors in the Art. 32(1) preamble.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 32(1)(d) — periodic testing of security measures

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 35(11) — DPIA Review on Risk Change
nodes.rationale: Requires review to assess whether processing is performed in accordance with the DPIA at least when there is a change of the risk represented by processing operations.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 35(11) — dpia review on risk change

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(1)(f) — Appropriate Security
nodes.rationale: Supplies the underlying principle for the periodic testing obligation in Art. 32(1)(d); anchors the security measures requirement.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-079: Documented and Updated Cybersecurity Risk Assessment
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(3) s1 + Art. 13(4) s1; risk assessment as both documented activity and artefact in technical documentation; operationalised through GV.PO-02 and ID.RA-05.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-079: documented and updated cybersecurity risk assessment

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OV-01 — Strategy Outcomes Reviewed and Adjusted
nodes.rationale: CRA-specific CSF anchor: key-separation policy reviewed across support period under manufacturer's broader risk-management strategy.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.ov-01 — strategy outcomes reviewed and adjusted

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AA-04 — Identity Assertions Managed and Protected
nodes.rationale: DORA-specific CSF anchor: integrity of identity-assertion conveyance via signed tokens, mutual transport authentication, PKI chain-of-trust.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.aa-04 — identity assertions managed and protected

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AA-05 — Least Privilege Access Control
nodes.rationale: CRA-specific CSF anchor: distinct role-based credentials, distinct custodians for key-material and operational environments under least-privilege entitlements.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.aa-05 — least privilege access control

nodes.label: SO-CRA-004 — CRA Cryptographic Key Separation
nodes.rationale: Canonical CRA security objective: cryptographic keys managed with separation of roles (custodian ≠ consumer) per Annex I Part I (2)(d)+(e).

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-002 — GDPR Pseudonymisation/Encryption Key Separation
nodes.rationale: Canonical GDPR security objective: additional information (keys) kept separately with appropriate technical and organisational measures per Art. 4(5).

nodes.label: SR-CRA-004 — Cryptographic Key Separation from Operational Environment
nodes.rationale: CRA security rule operationalising Annex I (2)(d)+(e) + Art. 6(a) as key-separation duty. Maps to PR.DS-01, PR.AA-05, GV.OV-01. T2-vs-text gap: key management not explicitly in Annex I text.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-004 — cryptographic key separation from operational environment

nodes.label: Requirement 1.3 — Cryptographic Key Separation (Multi-reg Aggregation)
nodes.rationale: Volere requirement 1.3: product shall manage cryptographic keys with separation of roles. MUST priority, TEST verification. Engages when ≥2 applicable regs overlap on same key material.

nodes.label: Requirement 1.3.1 — Personal-data Key Separation (GDPR)
nodes.rationale: GDPR sub-requirement: additional information (key, mapping table, tokenisation seed) kept separately to prevent re-attribution per Art. 4(5) + Art. 34(3)(a).

nodes.label: Requirement 1.3.2 — Product-side Key Separation (CRA)
nodes.rationale: CRA sub-requirement: functional RBAC separation of key-material custodian from operational-environment custodian per Annex I (2)(d)+(e).

nodes.label: Requirement 1.3.3 — Financial-entity Key Protection (DORA)
nodes.rationale: DORA sub-requirement: 3-control AND with classification-driven cipher strength, HSM-anchored custodianship, split-knowledge, quorum-based recovery per Art. 9(4)(d).

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 4(12): Personal Data Breach Definition
nodes.rationale: Breach of security leading to accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to personal data transmitted, stored or otherwise processed. Five-event enumeration underlying the breach-notification chain.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 4(12): personal data breach definition

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33(1): 72-Hour Breach Notification
nodes.rationale: Controller must notify supervisory authority without undue delay and where feasible not later than 72 hours after becoming aware, unless unlikely to result in risk.

nodes.label: NIST CSF RS.MA-02: Incident Reports Triaged and Validated
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rs.ma-02: incident reports triaged and validated

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-016: 72-Hour Breach Notification to Supervisory Authority
nodes.rationale: Twin temporal anchor (without undue delay + 72 hours) with risk-based carve-out, directed to competent supervisory authority under Art. 55/56. 72 hours is the hard ceiling; 'where feasible' is a narrow technical-feasibility exception. Burden of demonstrating 'unlikely to result in a risk' rests with the controller per EDPB Guidelines 9/2022. Mapped to RS.CO-02, RS.CO-04, RS.MA-03.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-016: 72-hour breach notification to supervisory authority

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-017: Processor-to-Controller Breach Notification Without Undue Delay
nodes.rationale: Upstream trigger for the controller's Art. 33(1) 72-hour clock. Processor must notify controller as soon as aware; controller then has its own 72-hour window. Chosen reading: action on same operational shift or business day. Mapped to RS.CO-02 and RS.MA-02.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-017: processor-to-controller breach notification without undue delay

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-015: Post-Breach Containment, Mitigation, Remediation
nodes.rationale: Art. 33(3)(d) measures taken/proposed; Art. 34(3)(a)/(b) carve-outs; defence-in-depth after breach: containment, mitigation, remediation.

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-018: Structured Four-Element Breach Notification Content
nodes.rationale: Art. 33(3) four-element content: nature, contact, consequences, measures; phased-disclosure model under Art. 33(4).
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-018: structured four-element breach notification content

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-022: Downstream-Recipient Cascade for Rectification/Erasure
nodes.rationale: Art. 19 propagation to all known recipients; inclusive OR for impossible/disproportionate; prevents rectification right from becoming illusory.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-089: Public archives and substantial-modification conformity perimeter
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(10)/(11) cluster: manufacturer may maintain public software archives with user risk communication; substantial modifications shift conformity perimeter to modified version only. Mapped to NIST CSF PR.PS-02 and GV.OC-04.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-089: public archives and substantial-modification conformity perimeter

nodes.label: SR-CRA-090: Support-period end-date disclosed to users
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(19)/Annex II §7: end date of support period must be clearly specified at purchase; Art. 21 makes manufacturer-equivalents inherit the obligation. Mapped to GV.OC-04 and GV.PO-01.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-090: support-period end-date disclosed to users

nodes.label: SO-CRA-052: Presumption of conformity (harmonised standards / common specs / CSA certification)
nodes.rationale: Art. 27(1)/(2)/(5)/(8)/(9): product presumed conformant with Annex I where it conforms to harmonised standards, common specifications, or CSA certification at specified assurance level. Sub-domain D-09.1.
nodes.norm_label: so-cra-052: presumption of conformity (harmonised standards / common specs / csa certification)

nodes.label: SR-CRA-013: Support-period determination using eight-factor methodology
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(8) s.2/s.3 + Annex VII §4: eight-factor methodology for support period with 5-year minimum. Factors include user expectations, product nature, Union law, similar products, OS availability, component support, ADCO/Commission guidance. Mapped to ID.IM-02 and GV.OV-02.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-013: support-period determination using eight-factor methodology

nodes.label: SR-CRA-077: Presumption of conformity via harmonised standards or common specifications
nodes.rationale: Art. 27(1)/(2)/(5): rebuttable presumption of conformity where product conforms to harmonised standards (OJ-published) or common specifications. Coverage qualifier: presumption only to extent standards cover the requirements. Mapped to GV.OC-03 and GV.PO-02.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-077: presumption of conformity via harmonised standards or common specifications

nodes.label: SR-CRA-078: CSA certification presumption at substantial assurance level
nodes.rationale: Art. 27(8)/(9) + Art. 8(1): presumption where manufacturer holds EU certificate under CSA (Reg. 2019/881) at assurance level at least 'substantial'. As of mid-2025, no CSA scheme covers Annex IV critical products. Mapped to GV.OC-03 and GV.SC-04.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-078: csa certification presumption at substantial assurance level

nodes.label: SR-CRA-097: Class II conformity routes including CSA certification
nodes.rationale: Art. 32(3): Class II important products routed to Module B+C, Module H, or CSA certification at substantial. Certification is third option beyond notified-body routes. Mapped to GV.OC-03.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-097: class ii conformity routes including csa certification

nodes.label: SO-CRA-066: Conformity-assessment procedure selection (Module A / B+C / H / certification)
nodes.rationale: Art. 32(1)/(2)/(3)/(4)/(5): manufacturer designates CA procedure per product class. Module A default; B+C/H for Class I/II; certification for critical; FOSS simplified. Sub-domain D-09.4.
nodes.norm_label: so-cra-066: conformity-assessment procedure selection (module a / b+c / h / certification)

nodes.label: SO-CRA-071: Module A/B+C/H conformity-assessment regime
nodes.rationale: Art. 32(1) + Annex VIII Parts I-IV: manufacturer establishes and operates CA regime ensuring design, production, vulnerability-handling meet Annex I on continuing basis. Sub-domains D-10.3, D-09.4.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-095: Module A default self-declared conformity assessment
nodes.rationale: Art. 32(1) + Annex VIII Part I: Module A places sole responsibility on manufacturer for design, development, production, vulnerability-handling. Default route for non-Class I/II/critical products. Mapped to GV.PO-02 and GV.OC-03.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-095: module a default self-declared conformity assessment

nodes.label: SR-CRA-096: Class I notified-body conformity-assessment routes
nodes.rationale: Art. 32(2) + Annex VIII Parts II/III/IV: Class I products routed to Module B+C or H where harmonised standards not fully applied. Notified body performs EU-type examination. Mapped to GV.OC-03 and GV.SC-04.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-096: class i notified-body conformity-assessment routes

nodes.label: SR-CRA-098: Critical-product certification and FOSS simplified assessment
nodes.rationale: Art. 32(4)/(5): critical products (Annex IV) require CSA certification at substantial or higher, or B+C/H fallback. FOSS simplified: Module A if Annex VII docs are public. Mapped to GV.OC-03.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-098: critical-product certification and foss simplified assessment

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-029: Records of Processing Activities
nodes.rationale: Controllers and processors must maintain records of processing activities with supervisory-authority access.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 12(1) — Transparency Modalities
nodes.rationale: Six conjunctive form qualifiers with child-specific heightened readability. Oral provision requires identity proofing by other means.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(1)(a) — Transparency Principle
nodes.rationale: Anchors transparency as one of the principles relating to processing of personal data.

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-021: Sufficient Guarantees from Processors
nodes.rationale: Controller engages only processors providing sufficient guarantees to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures meeting GDPR requirements.

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-005: Proportionate Identity Verification for Rights Requests
nodes.rationale: Identity of data subjects making rights-exercise requests is verified using reasonable means proportionate to the risk of mis-identification, before action is taken. Sourced from Art. 12(6) and Art. 11(2).
nodes.norm_label: so-gdpr-005: proportionate identity verification for rights requests

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-010: Minimised Collection of Identity Verification Data
nodes.rationale: Art. 12(6) scope limitation through Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation: collect only what is necessary to confirm identity, not what would be ideal in a hypothetical stronger verification. The Art. 5(2) accountability burden shifts the demonstration duty to the controller.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-010: minimised collection of identity verification data

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.PS-06: Secure SDLC Practices
nodes.rationale: Lifecycle-spanning SDLC discipline: controls designed in at architecture time and continuously validated; captures privacy-by-design and pseudonymisation-by-design.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ps-06: secure sdlc practices

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-016: Lawful, Fair, Transparent Processing
nodes.rationale: Every processing operation anchored in specified purpose and traceable Art. 6(1) lawfulness basis.

nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-026: lawful, fair, and transparent processing

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-028: Heightened Handling for Special-Category Data

nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-028: heightened handling for special-category data

nodes.label: SO-NIS2-016: Security objective (coordinated supply-chain risk assessment)
nodes.norm_label: so-nis2-016: security objective (coordinated supply-chain risk assessment)

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-020: Direct supplier and service-provider security by contract
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(d) requires supply chain security including security-related aspects of relationships with direct suppliers. The 'direct' scope-limiter is the single most consequential scope-limiting term in Chapter IV.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-020: direct supplier and service-provider security by contract

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-021: Security-related contractual aspects of supplier relationships
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(d) second clause on security-related aspects of supplier relationships; the 'security-related' qualifier is read broadly (R3) per the literal adjective.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-021: security-related contractual aspects of supplier relationships

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-022: Per-supplier vulnerability intelligence for risk prioritisation
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(3) sentence 1 requires taking into account vulnerabilities specific to each direct supplier; operates as a PER-SUPPLIER obligation rather than a continuous baseline.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-022: per-supplier vulnerability intelligence for risk prioritisation

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-023: Supplier product, service, and process quality assessment
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(3) sentence 1 second clause requires assessment of overall quality of products and cybersecurity practices including secure development procedures; one of three coordinated assessment objects.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-023: supplier product, service, and process quality assessment

nodes.label: NIST CSF RS.AN-07: Incident Data and Metadata Collected with Integrity Preserved
nodes.rationale: Captures evidence-integrity discipline: chain of custody, provenance preservation, metadata collection making the notification defensible under supervisory scrutiny.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rs.an-07: incident data and metadata collected with integrity preserved

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33(1) — 72-Hour Breach Notification
nodes.rationale: Requires notification to supervisory authority without undue delay and where feasible not later than 72 hours after becoming aware; risk-based carve-out for breaches unlikely to result in risk.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33(2) — Processor-to-Controller Notification
nodes.rationale: Requires processor to notify controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a breach; establishes the upstream trigger for the controller's 72-hour clock.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33(3) — Breach Notification Content
nodes.rationale: Requires four-element content: nature of breach, contact details, likely consequences, measures taken or proposed; supports phased disclosure under Art. 33(4).

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 4(12) — Personal Data Breach Definition
nodes.rationale: Defines personal data breach as a breach of security leading to accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to personal data.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 4(12) — personal data breach definition

nodes.label: SO-CRA-049: OSS Steward Cybersecurity Policy
nodes.rationale: OSS steward puts in place verifiable cybersecurity policy fostering secure development and vulnerability handling; Art. 24(1) + Art. 3(14)/(48).

nodes.label: DORA Art. 6(1) - ICT Risk Management Framework
nodes.rationale: Sound, comprehensive, well-documented framework enabling quick, efficient, comprehensive ICT risk addressing. Top-of-stack governance artefact.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 6(1) - ict risk management framework

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AA-03: Authentication
nodes.rationale: Users, services, and hardware authenticated. NIST SP 800-63B AAL2/AAL3-aligned: FIDO2/WebAuthn, smartcard/PKI, certificate-based auth.

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-026: Appropriate Data-Protection Policies
nodes.rationale: Controller implements appropriate data-protection policies reviewed and updated in light of nature, scope, context, purposes, and risks.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-039: OSS Steward Actively-Exploited-Vulnerability Reporting Extension
nodes.rationale: Art. 24(3) extends Art. 14(1) to OSS stewards; 'involved in development' read broadly (R4); steward defined in Art. 3(14); maps to RS.MA-01 and GV.PO-01.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-039: oss steward actively-exploited-vulnerability reporting extension

nodes.label: SR-CRA-072: OSS Steward Verifiable Cybersecurity Policy and CVD Enablement
nodes.rationale: Art. 24(1) four sub-elements: verifiable documentation, voluntary-reporting enablement, nature-aware proportionality, remediation-practice coverage; maps to GV.PO-01 and GV.SC-01.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-072: oss steward verifiable cybersecurity policy and cvd enablement

nodes.label: SR-DORA-031: Information security policy covering CIA+A
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(4)(a) is the top-level policy instrument complementing Art. 6(1) framework and Art. 9(4)(b)-(j) operational policies. Four-way protection objective (availability, authenticity, integrity, confidentiality) across three asset types = twelve pairings in scope.
nodes.norm_label: sr-dora-031: information security policy covering cia+a

nodes.label: SO-CRA-018: Secure-by-Default Configuration
nodes.rationale: Product made available with secure-by-default configuration including reset capability; CRA sole authority per taxonomy §4.1 for D-03.4.

nodes.label: SO-CRA-042: Manufacturer-Equivalent Trigger
nodes.rationale: Importer/distributor placing under own name or substantially modifying is considered manufacturer; Art. 21 + Art. 3(30).

nodes.label: SO-DORA-004: Network/Infrastructure and Patch Governance
nodes.rationale: Sound network/infrastructure management + appropriate and comprehensive documented patch/update policies; Art. 9(4)(b)+(f).

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4) - Eight Mandatory Control Domains
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(4)(a)-(h) eight-item control list, each self-implementing under Art. 6(8) chapeau framework. The operational hinge of the protection-prevention architecture.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 9(4) - eight mandatory control domains

nodes.label: CRA Art. 3(23) - Intended Purpose Definition
nodes.rationale: Defines intended purpose as the lexical anchor for secure-by-default, data minimisation, and risk assessment scoping.

nodes.label: D-02.2 — Vulnerability Remediation Sub-Domain
nodes.rationale: Covers vulnerability remediation, support-period handling, and effective vulnerability management across the product lifecycle.

nodes.label: D-06.2 — SBOM / Supply Chain Transparency Sub-Domain
nodes.rationale: CRA sole authority per AEGIS taxonomy §4.1. Covers SBOM content, format, lifecycle retention, and MSA disclosure.
nodes.norm_label: d-06.2 — sbom / supply chain transparency sub-domain

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 GV.RM-06 — Standardized Risk Methodology
nodes.rationale: Anchors standardised risk-calibration methodology. Shared across SR-NIS2-039, SR-NIS2-040, SR-NIS2-041 for meta-methodology.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 gv.rm-06 — standardized risk methodology

nodes.label: SO-CRA-006: Vulnerability management
nodes.rationale: Security objective covering pre-market elimination, identification, and remediation of vulnerabilities.

nodes.label: SO-CRA-008 — Vulnerability Remediation
nodes.rationale: Vulnerabilities addressed and remediated without delay after awareness. Parent for SR-CRA-010.

nodes.label: SO-CRA-038 — SBOM Content and Format
nodes.rationale: SBOM in commonly used machine-readable format covering top-level dependencies; provided to MSA on reasoned request.

nodes.label: SO-NIS2-021 — Risk-Calibrated Measures
nodes.rationale: Linked objective for SR-NIS2-039. Covers the appropriate-and-proportionate measures baseline.

nodes.label: SO-NIS2-022 — All-Hazards and Physical Security
nodes.rationale: Linked objective for SR-NIS2-040, SR-NIS2-041. Covers all-hazards methodology and physical-environment protection.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-015: Migration-Only Remediation Carve-Out for Substantially Modified Versions
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(10) allows compliance for last-placed version only, with free-of-charge migration constraint; maps to PR.PS-02 and GV.SC-04; substantial modification defined by Art. 3(30) disjunctive test.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-015: migration-only remediation carve-out for substantially modified versions

nodes.label: SR-CRA-061: Manufacturer-Equivalent Status on Own-Name Placement or Substantial Modification
nodes.rationale: Art. 21 accountability transfer at supply-chain boundary; re-branding or substantial modification makes importer/distributor the manufacturer; maps to GV.SC-02 and GV.SC-04.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-061: manufacturer-equivalent status on own-name placement or substantial modification

nodes.label: SR-CRA-070: Substantial-Modification Compliance Scope Across Supply Chain
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(10)+21+22 architecture treating substantial modification as trigger for manufacturer-equivalent status; maps to PR.PS-02 and GV.SC-04.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-070: substantial-modification compliance scope across supply chain

nodes.label: SR-DORA-006: Network and Infrastructure Management with Automated Blast-Radius Isolation
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(4)(b) sound network/infrastructure management; 'may include' automated isolation is illustrative (R1); maps to PR.PS-01, PR.IR-01, PR.IR-03.
nodes.norm_label: sr-dora-006: network and infrastructure management with automated blast-radius isolation

nodes.label: SO-DORA-013: ICT Change Management Controls
nodes.rationale: Security objective: documented policies for ICT change management ensuring all changes recorded, tested, assessed, approved, implemented and verified in controlled manner.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-010 — Vulnerability Remediation Without Delay
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part II (2): address and remediate without delay. Triggered obligation. NIST CSF: PR.PS-02, ID.RA-06. Structurally identical to NIS2 Art. 21(4) and GDPR Art. 33 'without undue delay'.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-012 — Effective Vulnerability Handling Across Support Period
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(8) sentence 1: vulnerabilities including components handled effectively during support period. Frames entire post-market handling lifecycle. NIST CSF: ID.RA-06, PR.PS-02.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-012 — effective vulnerability handling across support period

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 4(11): Consent Definition
nodes.rationale: Any freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous indication of the data subject's wishes by a statement or clear affirmative action. Four conjunctive qualifiers - failure of any one defeats consent. CJEU Planet49 (C-673/17) held pre-ticked boxes do not constitute unambiguous consent.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(1)(a): Lawfulness, Fairness, Transparency
nodes.rationale: Gateway principle: every processing operation must satisfy all three conjunctive conditions. Relationship between them is multiplicative - failure of any one vitiates the obligation. Fairness as balance-of-power test; transparency anchored in Arts. 12-14.

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-032: Consent lifecycle — specific, informed, demonstrable, withdrawable
nodes.rationale: Consent to personal-data processing is freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous; withdrawal is as easy as giving; bundled consent must be clearly distinguishable; special-category consent is at the higher explicit standard.
nodes.norm_label: so-gdpr-032: consent lifecycle — specific, informed, demonstrable, withdrawable

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-051: Demonstrable consent with equally accessible withdrawal path
nodes.rationale: Art. 4(11) defines consent; Art. 7(1) shifts evidentiary burden to controller; Art. 7(3) requires withdrawal as easy as giving consent.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-051: demonstrable consent with equally accessible withdrawal path

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-052: Unbundled and non-conditional consent collection
nodes.rationale: Art. 7(2) requires clearly distinguishable consent presentation; Art. 7(4) prohibits conditioning contract performance on consent for unrelated processing.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-052: unbundled and non-conditional consent collection

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-053: Explicit elevated consent for special-category processing
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(2)(a) requires explicit consent above the Art. 4(11) baseline; the explicit qualifier is stronger and operates on top of the four-element test.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-053: explicit elevated consent for special-category processing

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-054: Verified consent for child and transfer-risk contexts
nodes.rationale: Art. 8(1)-(2) requires parental verification for child consent; Art. 49(1)(a) requires explicit risk-informed transfer consent.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-054: verified consent for child and transfer-risk contexts

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-012: Data Integrity and Downstream Propagation
nodes.norm_label: so-gdpr-012: data integrity and downstream propagation

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-057: Derogation-Based Transfer Fallback
nodes.rationale: Art. 49 derogations apply only absent adequacy (Art. 45) and appropriate safeguards (Art. 46); seven disjunctive grounds plus catch-all with four conjunctive qualifiers.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 45: Adequacy Decisions
nodes.rationale: Commission adequacy decisions exempt transfers from specific authorisation. Art. 45(3) requires periodic review at least every 4 years with power to amend, suspend or repeal.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 49: Derogations for Transfers
nodes.rationale: Seven disjunctive grounds plus catch-all for transfers in absence of adequacy and Art. 46 safeguards. Catch-all requires not repetitive, limited number, compelling legitimate interests, and suitable safeguards.

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-033: Cross-Border Transfer Conditions
nodes.rationale: Transfers only where Chapter V conditions met: adequacy → appropriate safeguards → derogations; catch-all with four conjunctive qualifiers.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 6(1): Lawfulness Bases (Six Bases)
nodes.rationale: Six lawfulness bases: consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public interest, legitimate interests; each with its own necessity qualifier.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 9(1): Special-Category Prohibition
nodes.rationale: Prohibits processing of nine enumerated special categories (racial/ethnic origin, political opinions, religious/philosophical beliefs, trade union membership, genetic data, biometric-for-unique-identification, health data, sex life/sexual orientation) unless Art. 9(2) exception applies. Each category independently triggers the prohibition.

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AA-02: Identities Proofed and Bound to Credentials
nodes.rationale: Identity-proofing leg binding asserted identity to credentials proportionate to interaction context.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.aa-02: identities proofed and bound to credentials

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 4 Security Rules Document
nodes.rationale: Per-article split of GDPR Art. 4 definitions and their operationalisation into Security Rules mapped to NIST CSF 2.0. Contains SRs covering pseudonymisation, accuracy, identity verification, instruction-bound processing, breach detection/notification, consent, special categories, processor due diligence, cross-border transfers, BCRs, and joint controllership.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 12(6) — Identity Verification for Rights Requests
nodes.rationale: Permits controller to request additional information to confirm identity where reasonable doubts exist; must be proportionate to risk of misidentification.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 12(6) — identity verification for rights requests

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 19 — Cascade Notification to Recipients
nodes.rationale: Requires communication of rectification or erasure to each recipient unless impossible or disproportionate effort; controller must inform data subject about recipients on request.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 19 — cascade notification to recipients

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 21 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering CIA baseline, timely restoration, and derogation-based transfer fallback.

nodes.label: CRA Annex I Part II (Vulnerability Handling Requirements)
nodes.rationale: Covers SBOM, vulnerability remediation, CVD policy, vulnerability sharing, secure update distribution, and dissemination requirements.
nodes.norm_label: cra annex i part ii (vulnerability handling requirements)

nodes.label: CRA Annex II (User-Facing Information Requirements)
nodes.rationale: Specifies information that must accompany products: manufacturer contact, SPOC, product identification, technical support, detailed instructions, SBOM accessibility.

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.AM-02: Software and System Inventories
nodes.rationale: Mapped to SR-CRA-052 for SBOM as the operational expression of software inventory maintenance.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.am-02: software and system inventories

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AA-01: Identity and Credential Management
nodes.rationale: Mapped to SR-CRA-023, SR-CRA-083 for authentication, identity management, and product identification.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.aa-01: identity and credential management

nodes.label: NIST CSF RS.CO-03: Information Sharing with Stakeholders
nodes.rationale: Mapped to SR-CRA-017, SR-CRA-021, SR-CRA-082 for advisory messages, vulnerability reporting channels, and information-sharing rules.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rs.co-03: information sharing with stakeholders

nodes.label: SR-CRA-019: Coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy publication
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part II (5) requires a CVD policy; Art. 13(8) sentence 6 lists it among appropriate policies; Art. 24(3) extends to OSS stewards.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-019: coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy publication

nodes.label: SR-CRA-021: Vulnerability contact address and single point of contact
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part II (6) requires a contact address for vulnerability reporting; Art. 13(17) requires a SPOC; Annex II §2 carries SPOC into user-facing information.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-021: vulnerability contact address and single point of contact

nodes.label: SR-CRA-023: Authentication identity and unique product identification
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part I (2)(d) requires authentication/identity/access-management; Art. 13(15) requires type/batch/serial number; Annex II §3 requires unique identification disclosure.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-023: authentication identity and unique product identification

nodes.label: SR-CRA-051: Component vulnerability reporting, remediation, and OSS sharing
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(6) sentence 1 requires reporting to component manufacturer and remediating per Annex I Part II; sentence 2 requires sharing code/documentation with OSS suppliers.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-051: component vulnerability reporting, remediation, and oss sharing

nodes.label: SR-CRA-052: Machine-readable SBOM covering top-level dependencies
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part II (1) requires SBOM in machine-readable format covering at least top-level dependencies; Art. 13(24) authorises Commission implementing acts on format.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-052: machine-readable sbom covering top-level dependencies

nodes.label: SR-CRA-071: User-facing and integrator-facing secure-use instructions
nodes.rationale: Annex II §8(a)-(f) requires detailed instructions covering commissioning, data security, updates, decommissioning, auto-update opt-off, and integrator compliance info; Art. 13(18) extends accessibility to support period.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-071: user-facing and integrator-facing secure-use instructions

nodes.label: SR-CRA-075: Manufacturer CVD policy and support-period documentation cluster
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(8) sentence 6 + Annex I Part II (5) + Art. 13(8) sentence 2 form the manufacturer's policies cluster: CVD policy + support-period methodology + documentary basis.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-075: manufacturer cvd policy and support-period documentation cluster

nodes.label: SR-CRA-082: Single point of contact for vulnerability reporting
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(17) requires a SPOC enabling direct and rapid communication including vulnerability reporting; Annex II §2 makes SPOC part of product-accompanying information.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-082: single point of contact for vulnerability reporting

nodes.label: SR-CRA-083: Bidirectional product and manufacturer identification
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(15) requires product identification (type/batch/serial); Art. 13(16) requires manufacturer contact info; Annex II §1/§3 carry both into user-facing information.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-083: bidirectional product and manufacturer identification

nodes.label: NIST CSF DE.CM-09: Computing hardware/software/runtime/data monitored
nodes.norm_label: nist csf de.cm-09: computing hardware/software/runtime/data monitored

nodes.label: NIST CSF DE.CM-01: Networks Monitored for Adverse Events
nodes.rationale: Network-layer monitoring surfacing unauthorised disclosure and exfiltration; most frequent breach vectors.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf de.cm-01: networks monitored for adverse events

nodes.label: NIST CSF DE.CM-03: Personnel Activity and Technology Usage Monitored
nodes.rationale: Personnel-activity and technology-usage monitoring addressing 'otherwise processed' events including alteration and internal unauthorised access.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf de.cm-03: personnel activity and technology usage monitored

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(1)(b) — Confidentiality of Processing Systems
nodes.rationale: Requires ability to ensure ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience; achieved only if monitoring is in place to detect personal data breaches.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 32(1)(b) — confidentiality of processing systems

nodes.label: DORA Art. 13(6): Staff ICT Security Training
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 13(6): staff ict security training

nodes.label: DORA Art. 5(2): Management Body ICT Risk Ownership
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 5(2): management body ict risk ownership

nodes.label: DORA Art. 5(4): Management Body ICT Risk Literacy
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 5(4): management body ict risk literacy

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 GV.RR-01: Leadership Accountable for Cybersecurity Risk
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 gv.rr-01: leadership accountable for cybersecurity risk

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 PR.AT-03: Senior Executives Understand Cybersecurity Roles
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 pr.at-03: senior executives understand cybersecurity roles

nodes.label: SO-DORA-014: Security Objective (linked to Management Body Literacy)
nodes.norm_label: so-dora-014: security objective (linked to management body literacy)

nodes.label: SO-DORA-015: Security Objective (linked to Staff Training)
nodes.norm_label: so-dora-015: security objective (linked to staff training)

nodes.label: SR-DORA-024: Management-body ICT-risk Literacy through Regular Training
nodes.rationale: Art. 5(4) requires management body to actively keep up to date with sufficient knowledge/skills, including specific training commensurate to ICT risk. This is the literacy underpinning of Art. 5(2) management-body responsibility.
nodes.norm_label: sr-dora-024: management-body ict-risk literacy through regular training

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(2): Accountability
nodes.rationale: Controller responsible for, and able to demonstrate, compliance with Art. 5(1) principles. The ex-post demonstration burden referenced in nearly every SR's security_rationale as the accountability anchor.

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OV-03: Performance Evaluation and Review
nodes.rationale: Captures evaluated-and-reviewed-correction dimension: controller's performance against objectives must be measured and adjusted, with adjustments materialising as refreshed policies, processes and procedures.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.ov-03: performance evaluation and review

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 24: Controller and Processor Responsibilities
nodes.rationale: Art. 24(1) appropriate measures to ensure and demonstrate compliance; Art. 24(2) proportionate data-protection policies; operational-responsibility centrepiece.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 24: controller and processor responsibilities

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 24(1) — Appropriate Measures
nodes.rationale: Requires controller to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures ensuring and demonstrating GDPR compliance, reviewed and updated where necessary.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 24(2) — Data-Protection Policies
nodes.rationale: Requires proportionate data-protection policies by the controller, anchored on the Art. 24(2) proportionality test.

nodes.label: EDPB Guidelines 07/2019 on Accountability
nodes.rationale: Provides operational guidance on accountability, continuous-evidentiary-trail reading, and materiality threshold for review triggers.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 25 — Data protection by design and by default
nodes.rationale: Dual obligation (by-design at means-determination and by-default at configuration) referenced in SR-GDPR-039, 040, 041.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 25 — data protection by design and by default

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(1): Design, Development, and Production per Annex I Part I
nodes.rationale: Umbrella duty: product designed, developed, and produced in accordance with Annex I Part I essential cybersecurity requirements. Referenced by SR-CRA-064.
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 13(1): design, development, and production per annex i part i

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(2): Cybersecurity Risk Assessment
nodes.rationale: Six-phase lifecycle propagation (planning through maintenance) with health-and-safety impact qualifier. Referenced by SR-CRA-065.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(3): Documented and Updated Risk Assessment
nodes.rationale: Three sentences: documented/updated, intended purpose + foreseeable use, Annex I Part I (2) applicability. Stored in Annex VII §3. Referenced by SR-CRA-066.
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 13(3): documented and updated risk assessment

nodes.label: SR-CRA-066: Documented, Updated Risk Assessment in Technical Documentation
nodes.rationale: R4 reading for 'updated as appropriate': material change in product/threat landscape/awareness of vulnerability. The assessment must indicate whether and how Annex I Part I (2) requirements apply — selective applicability, not all 13 sub-points for every product class.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-066: documented, updated risk assessment in technical documentation

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.PS-02: Software Maintained, Replaced, and Removed Commensurate with Risk
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF 2.0 subcategory anchoring lifecycle consequence of development-time decisions about component selection, dependency hygiene, and update channels.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ps-02: software maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk

nodes.label: Annex I Part II (2): Address and Remediate Vulnerabilities Without Delay
nodes.rationale: Requires address and remediate without delay, including security updates. Where technically feasible, updates provided separately from functionality updates. Referenced by SR-CRA-010, 015.
nodes.norm_label: annex i part ii (2): address and remediate vulnerabilities without delay

nodes.label: Annex I Part II (8): Disseminate Updates Without Delay, Free of Charge
nodes.rationale: Security updates disseminated without delay, free of charge (unless tailor-made), accompanied by advisory messages. Referenced by SR-CRA-017, 047.
nodes.norm_label: annex i part ii (8): disseminate updates without delay, free of charge

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(8): Support Period and Vulnerability Handling
nodes.rationale: Central provision: sentence 1 (handle vulnerabilities during support period), sentence 2 (eight-factor determination), sentence 3 (5-year minimum), sentence 6 (CVD policy). Referenced by SR-CRA-012, 013, 014, 019.
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 13(8): support period and vulnerability handling

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(9): Ten-Year Update Availability
nodes.rationale: Each security update remains available for minimum 10 years or remainder of support period, whichever is longer. Referenced by SR-CRA-016, 047.

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.IM-02: Improvement Processes for Risk Management Implemented
nodes.rationale: Captures the methodology-as-process leg for support-period determination. Referenced by SR-CRA-013.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.im-02: improvement processes for risk management implemented

nodes.label: SR-CRA-014: Five-Year Minimum Support Period with End-Date Disclosure
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(8) sentence 3 fixes a hard minimum of five years. Art. 13(19) requires the end date (month and year) to be clearly specified at the time of purchase. The 'at least' literal preserves manufacturer choice to extend beyond the floor.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-014: five-year minimum support period with end-date disclosure

nodes.label: SR-CRA-016: Ten-Year Update-Availability Tail Beyond Support Period
nodes.rationale: Creates a 10-year availability tail measured from the date of issue, layered on top of the support-period minimum. The 'whichever is longer' twin-anchor pattern means case-by-case per-update calculation.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-016: ten-year update-availability tail beyond support period

nodes.label: SR-CRA-047: Free, Timely Security-Update Dissemination Across Support Period
nodes.rationale: Combines secure distribution (Part II (7)), dissemination without delay free of charge (Part II (8)), and Annex II information accessibility (Art. 13(18)). The 10-year tail applies by extension: information accessible for support period or 10 years, whichever is longer.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-047: free, timely security-update dissemination across support period

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RM-04: Strategic Direction on Risk Identification and Response
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF 2.0 governance subcategory supplying the superstructure that converts ad-hoc algorithm choice into a defensible audit position.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.rm-04: strategic direction on risk identification and response

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AA-04: Identity assertions managed, protected, conveyed
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-DORA-002. Enforces integrity of identity-assertion conveyance via signed federated-identity tokens, mutual transport authentication, PKI chain-of-trust.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.aa-04: identity assertions managed, protected, conveyed

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AA-03: Users, services, hardware authenticated
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.aa-03: users, services, hardware authenticated

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33 — Breach Notification
nodes.rationale: 72-hour notification to supervisory authority. Processor notifies controller 'without undue delay'. Notification content: nature, DPO contact, likely consequences, measures taken. 'Without undue delay' and 'where feasible' are Berry-flagged temporal vagueness.

nodes.label: NIST CSF DE.CM-01: Networks monitored for potentially adverse events
nodes.norm_label: nist csf de.cm-01: networks monitored for potentially adverse events

nodes.label: NIST CSF RS.CO-04: Coordination with stakeholders consistent with applicable rules
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rs.co-04: coordination with stakeholders consistent with applicable rules

nodes.label: NIST CSF RS.CO-02: Incidents Reported Internally
nodes.rationale: Internal escalation and reporting dimension; gives cascade and notification obligations operational force.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rs.co-02: incidents reported internally

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-019: High-Risk Breach Communication to Data Subjects
nodes.rationale: Art. 34(1) higher threshold than Art. 33; clear and plain language; enables individual protective action such as account rotation and fraud-alert subscription.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-019: high-risk breach communication to data subjects

nodes.label: NIST CSF RS.CO-02: Incidents reported internally to appropriate stakeholders
nodes.rationale: Captures reporting dimension for Art. 19 cascade: routing correction events to internal stakeholders responsible for recipient notification.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rs.co-02: incidents reported internally to appropriate stakeholders

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33(3): Breach notification content (four elements)
nodes.rationale: Four-element content: (a) nature including categories/numbers, (b) DPO contact, (c) likely consequences, (d) measures taken or proposed. Phased disclosure under Art. 33(4).
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 33(3): breach notification content (four elements)

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28(3) — Processor contract requirements
nodes.rationale: Art. 28(3)(f) specifically requires processor-to-controller breach notification terms in the contract. SR-GDPR-017 references this as the contractual vehicle for the notification channel.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 4(12) — Definition of personal data breach
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 4(12) — definition of personal data breach

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 26 — Joint Controllers
nodes.rationale: Two or more controllers jointly determining purposes/means. Transparent arrangement for responsibilities. Essence made available to data subject. Data subject may exercise rights against each controller irrespective of arrangement terms.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 4(20) — BCR Definition
nodes.rationale: Defines binding corporate rules as personal data protection policies adhered to by a controller/processor for transfers within a group of undertakings to third countries.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 26(1) — Joint-Controller Arrangement
nodes.rationale: Requires transparent determination of respective responsibilities for compliance, data-subject rights, and Arts. 13/14 information duties. May designate a contact point (Recital 79). CJEU IAB Europe C-604/22 extends 'jointly determine' to parties with determinative influence.

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-036: Joint-Controller Governance
nodes.rationale: Security objective for joint-controller arrangements under Art. 26. Referenced by SR-GDPR-060.

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-017: Storage Limitation
nodes.rationale: No longer than necessary for purposes; longer retention only where lawful with Art. 89(1) safeguards. Source: Art. 5(1)(e), Art. 30(1)(f).

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-018: Erasure Without Undue Delay
nodes.rationale: Erased on data subject's request where Art. 17(1) grounds apply; operationally defined as making data inaccessible. Source: Art. 17, Art. 5(1)(c)/(e).

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(1)(b): Purpose Limitation
nodes.rationale: Purposes must be specified, explicit, and legitimate before processing begins; binds all Art. 5(1) principles.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(1)(c): Data Minimisation
nodes.rationale: Personal data must be adequate, relevant, and limited to what is necessary in relation to the purposes for which they are processed.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(1)(e): Storage Limitation
nodes.rationale: Personal data kept in identifiable form no longer than necessary for purposes; longer retention only for archiving, research, or statistical purposes with Art. 89(1) safeguards.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 19 — Communication of rectification or erasure to recipient
nodes.rationale: Requires cascade of rectification/erasure/restriction to each recipient unless impossible or disproportionate effort. Controller must inform data subject about recipients on request.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 19 — communication of rectification or erasure to recipient

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.SC-04: Suppliers Routinely Assessed Using Audits
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-031, 035, 037 for periodic third-party assessment and audit evidence.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.sc-04: suppliers routinely assessed using audits

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 17: Right to Erasure
nodes.rationale: Data subject right to erasure where Art. 17(1)(a)-(f) conditions apply; controller-side duties flow from Art. 5(1)(c) and Art. 5(1)(e).

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 19 — Cascade Notification to Recipients
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 19 — cascade notification to recipients

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-030: Right-to-erasure with cryptographic key-destruction deletion path
nodes.rationale: Adopts cryptographic-erasure reading of Art. 28(3)(g) 'deletes' as most defensible interpretation scaling across backups and replicas, mapped to PR.DS-10 and PR.DS-12.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-030: right-to-erasure with cryptographic key-destruction deletion path

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(2): CIA+A across data states
nodes.rationale: Core provision requiring high standards of availability, authenticity, integrity, confidentiality of data at rest, in use, or in transit.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 9(2): cia+a across data states

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-025: Purpose-Bound Data Minimisation with Compatibility Assessment
nodes.rationale: Operationalises Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation calibrated to purpose, with Art. 6(4) compatibility test as the procedural mechanism for any change of purpose.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-025: purpose-bound data minimisation with compatibility assessment

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 16 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering accuracy (Art. 5(1)(d)) and rectification right (Art. 16) with cascade notification (Art. 19).

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 19 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering cascade notification of rectification/erasure to recipients.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-01.1: Data Protection — Cryptography
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation sub-domain covering cryptography policies, encryption governance, and data protection at rest and in transit.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-02.1: Vulnerability Management
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation sub-domain covering vulnerability identification, handling, remediation, and coordinated disclosure.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-09.3: Governance — Asset Management
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation sub-domain covering authoritative asset inventories and their role as precondition for technical-control decisions.

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.AM-02: Software, Services, and Systems Inventories Maintained
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF 2.0 subcategory for software-side inventory: applications, services, libraries, firmware, cloud workloads linked to supply-chain provenance and access-control decisions.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.am-02: software, services, and systems inventories maintained

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AA-05: Access Permissions Managed per Least Privilege
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF 2.0 subcategory constraining what managed identities may do, translating least-privilege principle into entitlements created, reviewed, and revoked on defined cadence.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.aa-05: access permissions managed per least privilege

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AT-02: Workforce Understands Role-Specific Security Responsibilities
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF 2.0 subcategory binding HR-security lifecycle to workforce: joiners receive induction, movers get re-training, leavers complete off-boarding clearance.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.at-02: workforce understands role-specific security responsibilities

nodes.label: SO-NIS2-002: Vulnerability Handling and Disclosure in System Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Security objective for coordinated vulnerability handling and disclosure integrated into acquisition, development, and maintenance. Source: Art. 21(2)(e), Art. 21(3). Sub-domains D-02.1, D-02.3.
nodes.norm_label: so-nis2-002: vulnerability handling and disclosure in system lifecycle

nodes.label: SO-NIS2-003: Access Control, HR Security, and Asset Management
nodes.rationale: Security objective for access control policies, HR security, and asset management on least-privilege basis. Source: Art. 21(2)(i). Sub-domains D-03.1 through D-03.4.
nodes.norm_label: so-nis2-003: access control, hr security, and asset management

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-002: Vulnerability Handling and External Disclosure Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Requires vulnerability handling and disclosure integrated into acquisition, development, and maintenance lifecycle. Mapped to NIST CSF ID.RA-01, GV.SC-04. Sub-domains D-02.1, D-02.3. Continuous obligation.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-002: vulnerability handling and external disclosure lifecycle

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-003: Identity and Access-Control Policy Foundation
nodes.rationale: Requires HR security, access control policies, and asset management in cumulative form (literal AND). Mapped to NIST CSF PR.AA-01, PR.AA-05. Sub-domains D-03.1, D-03.3. Model-agnostic (RBAC/ABAC/MAC/DAC all permissible).
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-003: identity and access-control policy foundation

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-004: Workforce Identity Lifecycle as HR-Security Substrate
nodes.rationale: Covers joiner-mover-leaver lifecycle for workforce identity management. Mapped to NIST CSF PR.AT-02, PR.AA-01. Sub-domains D-08.2, D-03.1. Chosen reading is lifecycle-security per ISO 27001:2022 A.6.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-004: workforce identity lifecycle as hr-security substrate

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-005: Authoritative Hardware, Software, and Information-Asset Inventories
nodes.rationale: Requires cumulative asset inventories (hardware, software, information) per ISO 27001:2022 A.5.9. Mapped to NIST CSF ID.AM-01, ID.AM-02. Sub-domains D-09.3, D-03.3. Chosen reading is cumulative (R4).
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-005: authoritative hardware, software, and information-asset inventories

nodes.label: SO-NIS2-017: Security in acquisition, development, maintenance
nodes.rationale: Security objective: security integrated into NIS lifecycle including vulnerability handling and disclosure.
nodes.norm_label: so-nis2-017: security in acquisition, development, maintenance

nodes.label: Annex I Part I (2)(d): Authentication, Identity, or Access Management
nodes.rationale: Protection from unauthorised access by appropriate control mechanisms including authentication, identity, or access-management systems. 'Including but not limited to' keeps floor open. Referenced by SR-CRA-023.
nodes.norm_label: annex i part i (2)(d): authentication, identity, or access management

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.AM-01: Inventories of Hardware Maintained
nodes.rationale: Anchors the hardware-inventory dimension: Art. 13(15) type/batch/serial-number marking. Referenced by SR-CRA-023.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.am-01: inventories of hardware maintained

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AA-01: Identities and Credentials Managed
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.aa-01: identities and credentials managed

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 13 — Security Objectives & Security Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split generated from 01_SecurityObjectives.md and 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md; references SR-NIS2-001 for cryptography governance in sub-domain D-01.1.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 13 — security objectives & security rules

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 14 — Security Objectives & Security Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering SR-NIS2-001 (cryptography) and SR-NIS2-027 (secure-by-design in development); spans sub-domains D-01.1 and D-07.1.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 14 — security objectives & security rules

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21 — Security Objectives & Security Rules
nodes.rationale: Primary authoritative source defining 14 Security Objectives (SO-NIS2-001 through SO-NIS2-023) and multiple Security Rules across sub-domains D-01 through D-10; the parent document from which per-article splits are generated.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 21 — security objectives & security rules

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-014 — 24-Hour Derogation Notification for TSPs
nodes.rationale: Art. 23(4) ¶2: TSPs notify within 24h (derogating from 72h tier). eIDAS cross-reference via Art. 6(24). NIST CSF: RS.CO-04, RS.MA-03.

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-026: Security requirements embedded in NIS acquisition lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(e) first clause: security in acquisition. Mapped to NIST CSF PR.PS-06 and GV.SC-02.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-026: security requirements embedded in nis acquisition lifecycle

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-027: Secure-by-design controls integrated across NIS development
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(e) second clause: security in development. Mapped to NIST CSF PR.PS-06 and PR.PS-02.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-027: secure-by-design controls integrated across nis development

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-028: Maintenance-phase security with coordinated vulnerability disclosure
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(e) third clause: security in maintenance including vulnerability handling and disclosure. Mapped to NIST CSF PR.PS-02 and ID.RA-01.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-028: maintenance-phase security with coordinated vulnerability disclosure

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 29 — Processing Under Authority
nodes.rationale: Requires persons acting under controller or processor authority not to process data except on instructions, unless required by Union or Member State law.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(4) — Natural Persons Under Authority
nodes.rationale: Requires controller and processor to ensure natural persons acting under their authority do not process data except on instructions; reinforces the instruction-only rule.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 32(4) — natural persons under authority

nodes.label: SO-NIS2-018: Security objective (cyber hygiene and training)
nodes.norm_label: so-nis2-018: security objective (cyber hygiene and training)

nodes.label: Annex I Part I (2)(b): Secure-by-Default Configuration
nodes.rationale: Products made available with secure-by-default configuration including reset capability, unless otherwise agreed for tailor-made products. Referenced by SR-CRA-025.
nodes.norm_label: annex i part i (2)(b): secure-by-default configuration

nodes.label: Annex I Part I (2)(c): Security Updates, Auto-Updates, and Notification
nodes.rationale: Vulnerabilities addressed through security updates, including automatic updates as default with opt-out, notification of available updates, and postponement option. Referenced by SR-CRA-010, 017, 018.
nodes.norm_label: annex i part i (2)(c): security updates, auto-updates, and notification

nodes.label: Annex I Part I (2)(g): Data Minimisation (Adequate, Relevant, Necessary)
nodes.rationale: Process only data adequate, relevant, and limited to what is necessary in relation to intended purpose. Borrows GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) language at product-design level. Referenced by SR-CRA-046.
nodes.norm_label: annex i part i (2)(g): data minimisation (adequate, relevant, necessary)

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.PS-01: Configuration Management Practices Established, Documented, and Applied
nodes.rationale: Anchors the configuration-baseline dimension. Referenced by SR-CRA-018 (auto-update default) and SR-CRA-025 (secure-by-default).
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ps-01: configuration management practices established, documented, and applied

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-01.1: Data Protection (Confidentiality)
nodes.rationale: CRA sole authority per taxonomy §4.1; covers at-rest encryption, data minimisation, cross-state CIA protection.

nodes.label: SO-DORA-018: Continuous Monitoring + Info Security Policy
nodes.rationale: Security objective: continuous monitoring/control of ICT systems + information security policy defining rules to protect CIA+A of data, information assets and ICT assets.
nodes.norm_label: so-dora-018: continuous monitoring + info security policy

nodes.label: EBA Guidelines on ICT and Security Risk Management
nodes.rationale: Supervisory baseline for DORA obligations: risk-assessment approach, framework quality, monitoring coverage, asset-classification granularity.
nodes.norm_label: eba guidelines on ict and security risk management

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(2): Five-Event Risk Enumeration
nodes.rationale: Requires account of risks from accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to personal data. The five-event OR is inclusive.

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-011: High-Risk Breach Communication to Data Subjects
nodes.rationale: Higher threshold than Art. 33: communication required when breach is likely to result in a high risk to data subjects' rights and freedoms.
nodes.norm_label: so-gdpr-011: high-risk breach communication to data subjects

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 34(1): High-Risk Breach Communication to Data Subject
nodes.rationale: Controller must communicate breach to data subject without undue delay when likely to result in high risk to rights and freedoms.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 34(1): high-risk breach communication to data subject

nodes.label: SR-CRA-081: Systematic Always-Current Cybersecurity Record
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(7)/(14) always-current record duty connecting SDLC risk process to published regulatory landscape; operationalised through GV.OV-02 and ID.IM-04.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 DE.CM-03: Personnel activity and technology usage monitored
nodes.rationale: Addresses 'otherwise processed' events of Art. 32(2) list, including alteration and unauthorised access from inside trust boundary.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 de.cm-03: personnel activity and technology usage monitored

nodes.label: DORA Art. 10(2): Multi-layer Detection and Response Triggering
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 10(2): multi-layer detection and response triggering

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 DE.AE-02: Detected Events Analyzed for Attack Targets/Methods
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 de.ae-02: detected events analyzed for attack targets/methods

nodes.label: 01_SecurityObjectives.md (Aggregate Index)
nodes.rationale: Authoritative aggregate index from which per-article splits are generated.

nodes.label: 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md (Aggregate Index)
nodes.rationale: Authoritative aggregate index from which per-article splits are generated.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 11 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split generated from 01_SecurityObjectives.md and 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md; originals remain authoritative aggregate indexes.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 12 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split generated from 01_SecurityObjectives.md and 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md; originals remain authoritative aggregate indexes.

nodes.label: CRA Severe-Incident 24h/72h Notifications
nodes.rationale: Art. 14(4)(a)+(b) twin-trigger: 24h early warning then 72h incident notification for severe incidents. Structurally identical to AEV chain but higher-severity tier. CSIRT routes with priority.

nodes.label: CRA One-Month Severe-Incident Final Report
nodes.rationale: Art. 14(4)(c) closes the severe-incident reporting chain with an evidence-rich final report. Clock starts at 72h notification submission, not awareness. Supports ENISA biennial synthesis.

nodes.label: CRA User Notification with CSIRT Fallback
nodes.rationale: Art. 14(8) requires manufacturer to inform impacted users of vulnerability/incident and mitigation measures, in structured machine-readable format where appropriate. CSIRT fallback if manufacturer fails to notify timely.
nodes.norm_label: cra user notification with csirt fallback

nodes.label: CRA Intermediate Status Report on CSIRT Request
nodes.rationale: Art. 14(6) bridges the gap between 24h/72h notifications and 14d/1-month final reports. CSIRT-driven cadence; manufacturer duty is contingent on CSIRT request.
nodes.norm_label: cra intermediate status report on csirt request

nodes.label: CRA OSS Steward AEV Reporting Extension
nodes.rationale: Art. 24(3) extends Art. 14(1) AEV notification to OSS stewards (Art. 3(14) legal persons) to the extent involved in product development. Steward treated as manufacturer for triggering condition. Proportionality preserved by Recital 18.
nodes.norm_label: cra oss steward aev reporting extension

nodes.label: CRA OSS Steward Severe-Incident Reporting
nodes.rationale: Art. 24(3) extends Art. 14(3)/(8) to OSS stewards where severe incidents affect steward's NIS for product development. Closes symmetric gap with Art. 14(1)-only extension.

nodes.label: CRA Bidirectional Product and Manufacturer Identification
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(15)/(16) + Annex II §1/§3 establish bidirectional identification: every unit traceable, every unit traceable back to manufacturer. Enables routing of Art. 14 reports and supply-chain attribution.
nodes.norm_label: cra bidirectional product and manufacturer identification

nodes.label: CRA Commission Implementing and Delegated Acts
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(24)/(25), 14(9)/(10), 7(3)/(4), 30(6) establish Commission/ADCO acts machinery. Several acts scheduled for adoption by 11 Dec 2025; compliance duty attaches upon publication.
nodes.norm_label: cra commission implementing and delegated acts

nodes.label: CRA ENISA Single Reporting Platform
nodes.rationale: Art. 16(1)/(4): ENISA establishes single reporting platform for Art. 14/15 notifications with appropriate and proportionate security measures. Inter-institutional surface auditable by manufacturers and CSA-EU.

nodes.label: DORA ICT Incident Management Process
nodes.rationale: Art. 17(1): define, establish, implement ICT-related incident management to detect, manage, notify. Chapter III chapeau with Art. 18 classification and Art. 19 reporting. Cross-notification with GDPR Art. 33.

nodes.label: DORA ICT Third-Party Risk Management
nodes.rationale: Art. 28(1): manage ICT third-party risk with four-factor proportionality (nature, scale, complexity, importance). Parallel to GDPR Art. 28 and NIS 2 Art. 21 supply-chain duties. EBA Guidelines baseline.

nodes.label: DORA Continuous Monitoring and Control
nodes.rationale: Art. 8(1)/9(1): continuously monitor and control security and functioning of ICT systems. Real-time security-operations substrate. Pairs with Art. 17 incident management and Chapter IV testing.

nodes.label: AI Act Article 9 (Risk Management for High-Risk AI)
nodes.rationale: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. Art. 9 risk-management duty for high-risk AI systems where AI components in scope. Art. 4(2) provider-deployer literacy duties intersect with DORA training obligations.
nodes.norm_label: ai act article 9 (risk management for high-risk ai)

nodes.label: CRA Article 13 (Conformity Assessment & Vulnerability Handling)
nodes.rationale: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847. Downstream fact-feeding layer for product vendors feeding DORA entities. Art. 13(5) vulnerability handling, Art. 13(11) patch governance, Art. 13 conformity-assessment for digital products.

nodes.label: NIS 2 Article 21 (Basic Cybersecurity Governance)
nodes.rationale: Directive (EU) 2022/2555. Parallel regime for non-financial NSIEs. DORA financial entities retain joint obligation where they also operate as NIS 2 entities. Art. 21(2)(a)-(g) supply parallel baselines.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4)(d): Strong Authentication & Key Protection
nodes.rationale: Requires strong authentication mechanisms based on relevant standards and dedicated control systems, plus protection measures of cryptographic keys whereby data is encrypted based on approved data classification and ICT risk assessment.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 9(4)(d): strong authentication & key protection

nodes.label: DORA Article 9 (Security of Processing)
nodes.rationale: Chapter II Section II operational resilience architecture. Art. 9(2) cross-state CIA+A, Art. 9(4)(a)-(j) eight mandatory control domains. Core of DORA protection-prevention framework.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 32 (Security of Processing)
nodes.rationale: Risk-based security measures for personal data processing. Art. 32(1)(a)-(d) four sub-letters as floor of expected measures. Art. 32(2) five-event risk enumeration. Co-exists with DORA Art. 9 for financial entities.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 4(5): Pseudonymisation Definition
nodes.rationale: Processing of personal data in such a manner that it can no longer be attributed to a specific data subject without additional information, provided such additional information is kept separately and subject to appropriate technical and organisational measures. The de-attribution requirement is the operational test.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 34(3): Three exceptions to data-subject notification
nodes.rationale: (a) Encryption/unintelligibility, (b) subsequent measures neutralising high risk, (c) disproportionate effort with public communication substitute.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 34(3): three exceptions to data-subject notification

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 PR.IR-03: Resilience in normal and adverse situations
nodes.rationale: Resilience dimension: key-escrow recovery, key rotation without service degradation, recovery to known-good state. Art. 34(3)(b) subsequent-measures path.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 pr.ir-03: resilience in normal and adverse situations

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-020: Cryptographic and mitigation carve-outs for data-subject notification
nodes.rationale: Two paths to eliminate data-subject notification duty: cryptographic protection at time of breach (Art. 34(3)(a)) or subsequent mitigation neutralising high risk (Art. 34(3)(b)). Mapped to PR.DS-01 and PR.IR-03.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-020: cryptographic and mitigation carve-outs for data-subject notification

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9 (Protection Policies)
nodes.rationale: Core operational resilience architecture: Art. 9(2) CIA+A cross-state protection and Art. 9(4)(a)-(h) eight-item control list including info security policy, network mgmt, access control, authentication, change mgmt, and patch policies.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 12 (Backup and Recovery)
nodes.rationale: Backup policies specifying scope and minimum frequency based on criticality/confidentiality, plus restoration and recovery procedures and methods.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 PR.AA (Access Control)
nodes.rationale: Authentication (PR.AA-03, PR.AA-04) and least-privilege access (PR.AA-05, PR.AA-06) subcategories covering human, service, and machine identities.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 PR.DS (Data Security)
nodes.rationale: Data-at-rest (PR.DS-01), data-in-transit (PR.DS-02), data-in-use (PR.DS-10), backup (PR.DS-11), and risk-strategy-aligned data management (PR.DS-12) subcategories.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 21 Analysis (D-01.3)
nodes.rationale: Per-article split of DORA Security Rules mapped to NIST CSF 2.0, covering asset inventory, continuous monitoring, and information security policy obligations.

nodes.label: NIST CSF RC.RP-01: Recovery portion of IR plan executed
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rc.rp-01: recovery portion of ir plan executed

nodes.label: GDPR Article 34 — Communication of personal data breach to data subject
nodes.rationale: Art. 34(1) high-risk trigger, Art. 34(2) content requirement, Art. 34(3)(a) encryption exception, Art. 34(3)(b) subsequent-measures exception, Art. 34(3)(c) disproportionate-effort exception. Higher threshold than Art. 33.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 34 — communication of personal data breach to data subject

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.SC-04: Suppliers and Third Parties Routinely Assessed
nodes.rationale: Anchors supply-chain coordination and third-party assessment dimensions.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.sc-04: suppliers and third parties routinely assessed

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.PS-01: Configuration management practices
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ps-01: configuration management practices

nodes.label: SO-CRA-010: Effective vulnerability handling
nodes.rationale: Security objective for the post-market vulnerability handling lifecycle across the support period.

nodes.label: CRA (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847)
nodes.rationale: Upstream supply-side obligations: Art. 13 vulnerability handling, secure-by-default, conformity assessment for digital products.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4): Eight mandatory control domains
nodes.rationale: Chapeau of eight self-implementing control items (a)-(h) under Art. 6(8) framework.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 9(4): eight mandatory control domains

nodes.label: SR-CRA-076: Cessation-of-Operations Notification to MSAs and Users
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(23) lifecycle-end counterpart to placing-on-market duty; operationalised through GV.OC-04 and GV.OV-02.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-076: cessation-of-operations notification to msas and users

nodes.label: SR-CRA-020: Public Disclosure of Fixed Vulnerabilities with Delay Exception
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part II (4) + Art. 16(2) + Art. 14(9); share and publicly disclose fixed vulnerabilities; duly justified delay exception where risks of publication outweigh benefits; operationalised through RS.CO-03 and GV.SC-04.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-020: public disclosure of fixed vulnerabilities with delay exception

nodes.label: DORA Art. 5 (Management Body)
nodes.rationale: Establishes management body responsibility (Art. 5(2)) and literacy/training obligation (Art. 5(4)) as the top-of-pyramid governance rules of DORA.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 PR.AT (Awareness/Training)
nodes.rationale: User training (PR.AT-01), workforce role understanding (PR.AT-02), and senior executive literacy (PR.AT-03) subcategories.

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-024: Supplier secure-development procedures assessed per criticality
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(3) sentence 1: supplier secure development procedures. Mapped to NIST CSF GV.SC-02 and PR.PS-06.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-024: supplier secure-development procedures assessed per criticality

nodes.label: SO-CRA-023: AEV Notification to CSIRT and ENISA
nodes.norm_label: so-cra-023: aev notification to csirt and enisa

nodes.label: SO-CRA-025: Severe-Incident Notification to CSIRT and ENISA
nodes.norm_label: so-cra-025: severe-incident notification to csirt and enisa

nodes.label: NIST CSF RS.AN-07: Incident Data Integrity and Provenance Preserved
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rs.an-07: incident data integrity and provenance preserved

nodes.label: NIST CSF RS.MA-01: Incident Management Plan Executed in Coordination
nodes.rationale: Anchors third-party-coordination leg for AEV and severe-incident notification.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rs.ma-01: incident management plan executed in coordination

nodes.label: SR-CRA-029: Twenty-Four-Hour AEV Early-Warning Notification
nodes.rationale: Art. 14(2)(a); early warning within 24h of awareness; twin-trigger: without undue delay + hard 24h ceiling; operationalised through RS.MA-02 and RS.CO-02.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-030: AEV Tiered Seventy-Two-Hour and Fourteen-Day Notifications
nodes.rationale: Art. 14(2)(b)+(c); progressive disclosure: 72h vulnerability notification + 14d final report after corrective measure available; operationalised through RS.AN-03, RS.AN-07, RS.CO-02.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-030: aev tiered seventy-two-hour and fourteen-day notifications

nodes.label: SR-CRA-031: Simultaneous Severe-Incident Notification to CSIRT and ENISA
nodes.rationale: Art. 14(3) + Art. 14(5)(a)/(b); severe incident defined by disjunctive tests: CIA of sensitive/important data OR malicious code; operationalised through RS.MA-01 and RS.AN-03.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-031: simultaneous severe-incident notification to csirt and enisa

nodes.label: CRA Severe-Incident CIA Categorisation Test
nodes.rationale: Art. 14(5)(a) test A: incident is severe if it negatively affects or is capable of affecting CIA of sensitive/important data or functions. Four dimensions inherited from NIS 2 via Art. 3(43). Disjunctive-inclusion: any one CIA dimension triggers severity.

nodes.label: CRA Severe-Incident Malicious-Code Categorisation Test
nodes.rationale: Art. 14(5)(b) test B: incident is severe where it led or is capable of leading to introduction/execution of malicious code in product or user NIS. Complements test A; either test satisfied means severe.

nodes.label: DORA Cross-State CIA+A Protection Matrix
