nodes.rationale: Art. 9(2): 4-way AND of CIA+A × 3-way OR of data states (at-rest/in-use/in-transit) yielding 4×3 protection matrix. Risk-tiered controls per entity criticality taxonomy.

nodes.label: DORA Continuous ICT Risk-Source Identification
nodes.rationale: Art. 7(2)/8(2): continuous identification of all ICT risk sources with inter-entity awareness. Propagates obligation across financial sector value chain. CRA Art. 13(5) feeds downstream.

nodes.label: DORA Annual Risk-Scenario Register Refresh
nodes.rationale: Art. 7(2) sentence 2: review risk scenarios at least yearly. Hard numeric anchor closes temporal ambiguity. Findings must feed strategy adjustment, not just documentation.

nodes.label: DORA Network and Infrastructure Management
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(4)(b): sound network/infrastructure management structure. 'May include' automated isolation mechanisms (illustrative, not standalone). Zero-trust segmentation, blast-radius containment.

nodes.label: DORA Documented Patch and Update Governance
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(4)(f): appropriate and comprehensive documented policies for patches/updates. Governance instrument (policy) not operational cadence. Full asset estate scope. NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(e) parallel.
nodes.norm_label: dora documented patch and update governance

nodes.label: DORA Multi-Modality Resilience Testing Programme
nodes.rationale: Art. 24(1)/25(1): sound and comprehensive testing programme as integral part of ICT risk-management framework. 12-way open list of modalities. Art. 26 TLPT and Art. 27 advanced testing impose higher tiers.

nodes.label: DORA ICT Risk Management Framework
nodes.rationale: Art. 6(1)/(2): sound, comprehensive, well-documented ICT risk management framework. Top-of-stack governance artefact operationalised by Art. 7, 9, Chapter III. Parallels NIS 2 Art. 21 and AI Act Art. 9.

nodes.label: DORA ICT Asset Inventory and Classification
nodes.rationale: Art. 7(1): identify, classify, document all ICT-supported business functions, information assets, ICT assets, dependencies. Inventory-onboarding substrate for all downstream obligations. Parallel to GDPR Art. 30.
nodes.norm_label: dora ict asset inventory and classification

nodes.label: DORA Information Security Policy
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(4)(a): develop and document information security policy defining rules to protect CIA+A of data, information assets, ICT assets. Top-level policy instrument complementing Art. 6(1) framework.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 11(1): ICT Business Continuity Policy
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 11(1): ict business continuity policy

nodes.label: DORA Art. 11(2)-(3): BC Implementation and Audit Review
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 11(2)-(3): bc implementation and audit review

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 RC.RP-04: Critical Functions Restored via Recovery Plan
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 rc.rp-04: critical functions restored via recovery plan

nodes.label: NIST CSF DE.AE-03: Multi-Source Event Correlation
nodes.rationale: Captures multi-source correlation discipline: RoPA maintained across multiple systems must be collectable and correlatable into single supervisory-authority-presentable view.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf de.ae-03: multi-source event correlation

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.AM-03: Data Inventories and Metadata
nodes.rationale: Captures data-inventory discipline: each RoPA entry is operationally an inventory record for a designated data type with metadata for purpose, lawful basis, recipients, transfers and retention.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.am-03: data inventories and metadata

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.PS-04: Log Record Generation
nodes.rationale: Captures record-generation discipline: each RoPA entry generated and made available as log-grade record material with continuous monitoring and analysis.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ps-04: log record generation

nodes.label: NIST CSF RS.AN-07: Incident Data Integrity and Provenance
nodes.rationale: Captures integrity-and-provenance discipline: records relied on by supervisory authority must be tamper-evident and provenance-preserving.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rs.an-07: incident data integrity and provenance

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 30(1) — Records of Processing Activities
nodes.rationale: Seven enumerated content items for RoPA: controller details, purposes, data-subject/personal-data categories, recipients, third-country transfers, erasure time limits, security measures.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 30(1) — records of processing activities

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 30(5) — 250-Employee Exception
nodes.rationale: Disjunctive trigger: if any of (risk, not-occasional, special-category, criminal-conviction) applies, the small-organisation exception does not apply and RoPA must still be maintained.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 31 — Supervisory Authority Cooperation
nodes.rationale: Requires cooperation with supervisory authority on request, including on inspection. Sets the availability baseline for RoPA records.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(21): Non-Conformity Corrective Measures
nodes.rationale: Covers product-side and process-side non-conformity. 'Know or have reason to believe' trigger. Choice of remedy (fix/withdraw/recall) governed by proportionality. Referenced by SR-CRA-045.

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OV-02: Risk Management Strategy Reviewed and Adjusted
nodes.rationale: Anchors strategy-review and re-baselining dimensions for cessation, always-current record, and corrective measures.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.ov-02: risk management strategy reviewed and adjusted

nodes.label: NIST CSF RS.MI-01: Incidents Contained
nodes.rationale: Short-term containment runbook: isolating affected systems, revoking credentials, blocking exfiltration paths.

nodes.label: NIST CSF RS.MI-02: Incidents Mitigated
nodes.rationale: Mid-term mitigation: re-encrypting data, resetting credentials, patching exploited vulnerability.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 5(2) - Management Body Responsibility
nodes.rationale: Top-of-pyramid governance rule: management body shall define, approve, oversee and be responsible for all arrangements related to ICT risk management framework. Establishes personal liability.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(4): Instruction-Bound Processing by Natural Persons
nodes.rationale: Requires controller and processor to ensure natural persons acting under their authority do not process data except on instructions.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 32(4): instruction-bound processing by natural persons

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-022: Processor Contract Compliance
nodes.rationale: Processor relationships must be governed by contracts containing the eight mandatory Art. 28(3) sub-clauses.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 DE.CM-06: External service provider activities monitored
nodes.rationale: Day-to-day monitoring counterpart complementing periodic audit: adverse events at processor surface observable to controller in real time.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 de.cm-06: external service provider activities monitored

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28(3): Eight Mandatory Processor Contract Clauses
nodes.rationale: Closed AND-list of eight sub-clauses: documented instructions, confidentiality, Art. 32 measures, sub-processor conditions, data-subject rights assistance, Arts. 32-36 assistance, return/deletion, audits.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 28(3): eight mandatory processor contract clauses

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 29: Processing Under Authority
nodes.rationale: Processor and persons under controller/processor authority shall not process data except on instructions from the controller, unless required by Union or Member State law.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 6(4) - Control Function Independence
nodes.rationale: Appropriate level of independence per three lines of defence model or internal risk management and control model. Banking-supervision standard (Basel Committee).

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.AM-05: Assets prioritized by classification, criticality, impact
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-DORA-029. Closes prioritisation loop: OJ 'classify' verb operationalised through classification, criticality, resource weight, mission-impact scoring.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.am-05: assets prioritized by classification, criticality, impact

nodes.label: SO-DORA-017: Three Lines of Defence + Asset Identification
nodes.rationale: ICT risk oversight assigned to control function with appropriate independence per three-lines-of-defence; ICT assets identified, classified and adequately documented.
nodes.norm_label: so-dora-017: three lines of defence + asset identification

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 9: Risk Management for High-Risk AI
nodes.rationale: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 risk-management duty for high-risk AI systems; parallels DORA Art. 6(1) framework where AI components are in scope.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 9: risk management for high-risk ai

nodes.label: CRA: Cyber Resilience Act (EU) 2024/2847
nodes.rationale: Conformity-of-products duties where DORA policy covers protection of digital products. Art. 13(5) vulnerability handling supplies downstream fact-feeding for product vendors feeding DORA entities.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 6(1): Sound & Comprehensive ICT Risk Framework
nodes.rationale: Top-of-stack governance artefact requiring sound, comprehensive, well-documented framework enabling quick, efficient, comprehensive ICT risk addressing. Operationalised by Art. 7, Art. 9, and Chapter III.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 6(1): sound & comprehensive ict risk framework

nodes.label: DORA Art. 7(2): Continuous Risk Identification & Scenario Review
nodes.rationale: Sentence 1: continuous identification of all ICT risk sources with inter-entity awareness. Sentence 2: review risk scenarios at least yearly. Hard numeric anchor closes temporal ambiguity.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 7(2): continuous risk identification & scenario review

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(2): ICT Security Policies & CIA+A
nodes.rationale: Core operational resilience provision requiring design, procurement, and implementation of ICT security ensuring CIA+A across at-rest/in-use/in-transit. Recital 49: continuity of service under normal and adverse conditions.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 9(2): ict security policies & cia+a

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4)(a): Information Security Policy
nodes.rationale: Top-level policy instrument in the eight-item control list of Art. 9(4), complementing the Art. 6(1) framework and operational policies at Art. 9(4)(b)–(j).

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5: Data Processing Principles
nodes.rationale: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 principles relating to processing of personal data; co-exists with DORA Art. 9(4)(a) information security policy.

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 21: Basic Cybersecurity Governance
nodes.rationale: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 parallel baseline for non-financial NSIEs. Art. 21(2)(a) cross-state, (c) risk identification, (d) cryptography, (f) policy review. DORA financial entities retain joint obligation where also NIS 2 entities.

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OC-01: Organizational Mission Informs Risk Mgmt
nodes.rationale: Supplies mission-alignment layer: OJ 'quickly, efficiently and comprehensively' maps onto mission-driven risk-management prioritisation.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.oc-01: organizational mission informs risk mgmt

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OV-02: Risk Mgmt Strategy Reviewed & Adjusted
nodes.rationale: Anchors strategic layer requiring strategy adjustment when scenario-review findings diverge from entity's risk-appetite statement.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.ov-02: risk mgmt strategy reviewed & adjusted

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.PO-01: Organizational Cybersecurity Policy
nodes.rationale: Captures policy-document discipline: every controller has a communicated, current, enforced cybersecurity-and-data-protection policy anchored on Art. 24(2) proportionality test.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.po-01: organizational cybersecurity policy

nodes.label: DORA Art. 5(2): Management body responsibility
nodes.rationale: Top-of-pyramid governance rule: define, approve, oversee, be responsible for all ICT risk management arrangements.

nodes.label: Annex I Part II (5): Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure Policy
nodes.rationale: Requires manufacturers to put in place and enforce a CVD policy. Referenced by SR-CRA-019.
nodes.norm_label: annex i part ii (5): coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(10): Substantial Modification Compliance Scope
nodes.rationale: Permits compliance with remediation requirement only for last-placed version, provided users have free access and no additional costs. Referenced by SR-CRA-015.
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 13(10): substantial modification compliance scope

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.PO-01: Organisational Cybersecurity Policy Established, Communicated, and Enforced
nodes.rationale: Captures the policy-establishment and enforcement leg. Referenced by SR-CRA-014 (support-period policy) and SR-CRA-019 (CVD policy).
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.po-01: organisational cybersecurity policy established, communicated, and enforced

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-035: Documented risk-analysis methodology with proportional scope and cadence
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(a) first clause: policies on risk analysis. Methodology-agnostic; OJ does not prescribe qualitative, quantitative, or hybrid approach.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-035: documented risk-analysis methodology with proportional scope and cadence

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-036: Information-system-security policy governs NIS configuration and operation
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(a) second clause: policies on information system security. Read as requiring a distinct policy from risk analysis per the literal AND conjunction.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-036: information-system-security policy governs nis configuration and operation

nodes.label: CRA Art. 3(30) - Substantial Modification Definition
nodes.rationale: Defines substantial modification through a disjunctive test covering compliance impact OR intended-purpose modification; referenced by SR-CRA-015, SR-CRA-045, SR-CRA-070.

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OC-04: Stakeholder Communication of Critical Objectives
nodes.rationale: Mapped to SR-CRA-014, SR-CRA-047, SR-CRA-076, SR-CRA-083 for communicating critical commitments and capabilities to stakeholders.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.oc-04: stakeholder communication of critical objectives

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.PS-02: Software Maintenance and Replacement
nodes.rationale: Mapped to SR-CRA-015, SR-CRA-016, SR-CRA-017, SR-CRA-047, SR-CRA-070 for software lifecycle management.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ps-02: software maintenance and replacement

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(1)(a): Pseudonymisation and Encryption
nodes.rationale: Names pseudonymisation and encryption as illustrative appropriate technical measures under the Art. 32(1) risk-based preamble.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 34(3)(a): Unintelligibility Exception
nodes.rationale: Communication not required if measures render personal data unintelligible to any person not authorised to access it, such as encryption.

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.IR-03: Resilience in Normal and Adverse Situations
nodes.rationale: Key-escrow recovery, key rotation, recovery to known-good state; supports Art. 34(3)(a) carve-out and Art. 34(3)(b) subsequent measures.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ir-03: resilience in normal and adverse situations

nodes.label: DORA Art. 10 (Detection)
nodes.rationale: Detection substrate: Art. 10(1) anomalous activity detection and SPOF identification; Art. 10(2) multi-layer detection with threshold-driven response triggering.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 11 (Business Continuity)
nodes.rationale: Comprehensive ICT business continuity policy (Art. 11(1)), implementation arrangements with five objectives (Art. 11(2)), and independent internal audit review (Art. 11(3)).

nodes.label: DORA Art. 17 (Incident Management)
nodes.rationale: Chapter III chapeau: define, establish and implement ICT-related incident management process to detect, manage and notify incidents. Operationalised by Art. 18 classification and Art. 19 reporting.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33 - Personal Data Breach Notification
nodes.rationale: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 cross-notification interface with DORA Art. 19. Composite supervisory exposure when incident involves personal data.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 33 - personal data breach notification

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 DE.CM (Continuous Monitoring)
nodes.rationale: Network monitoring (DE.CM-01) and compute/hardware monitoring (DE.CM-09) for detecting potentially adverse events.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 PR.IR (Identity Mgmt/Resilience)
nodes.rationale: Network protection (PR.IR-01), resilience mechanisms (PR.IR-03), and resource capacity (PR.IR-04) subcategories.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 RS/RC (Response & Recovery)
nodes.rationale: Incident management execution (RS.MA-01), root-cause analysis (RS.AN-03), recovery execution (RC.RP-01, RC.RP-03, RC.RP-04).

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(1)(d) — Testing and evaluating security
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 32(1)(d) — testing and evaluating security

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 34(3) — Exceptions to data-subject notification
nodes.rationale: Art. 34(3)(a) provides a carve-out where data is rendered unintelligible; Art. 34(3)(b) provides a carve-out where subsequent measures ensure the high risk is no longer likely to materialise. The (b) threshold is harder: controller must demonstrate mitigation actually neutralises the risk, not merely that it was attempted.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 34(3) — exceptions to data-subject notification

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33(1): 72-hour breach notification to supervisory authority
nodes.rationale: Controller must notify supervisory authority without undue delay and where feasible not later than 72 hours after becoming aware, unless unlikely to result in risk. Twin temporal anchor with risk-based carve-out.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 33(1): 72-hour breach notification to supervisory authority

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33(2): Processor-to-controller breach notification
nodes.rationale: Processor must notify controller without undue delay after becoming aware of personal data breach. Upstream trigger for controller's 72-hour clock.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 RS.MA-03 — Incidents categorized, prioritized, and scoped
nodes.rationale: Anchors the triage that establishes whether the Art. 4(12) breach definition is met and whether the risk threshold engages the notification duty.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 rs.ma-03 — incidents categorized, prioritized, and scoped

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.SC-01: Supply Chain Risk Management Programme
nodes.rationale: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management programme established and agreed; mapped by SR-CRA-038/050/072.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.sc-01: supply chain risk management programme

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-06.2: Supply Chain (SBOM)
nodes.rationale: CRA sole authority per taxonomy §4.1; covers SBOM format, content, and on-request provision.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 PR.PS (Protective Technology)
nodes.rationale: Configuration management (PR.PS-01), software maintenance (PR.PS-02), logging (PR.PS-04), and secure SDLC (PR.PS-06) subcategories.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(e): Security in acquisition, development, and maintenance
nodes.rationale: Three coordinated lifecycle phases forming the substantive limb of Art. 21(2)(e), with the process limb being the separate vulnerability handling and disclosure obligation.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 21(2)(e): security in acquisition, development, and maintenance

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-07.1: Secure Development
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation sub-domain covering secure-by-design controls, secure coding, and development lifecycle security.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 44: General Transfer Principle
nodes.rationale: Umbrella principle for cross-border transfers: any transfer to third country shall take place only if Chapter V conditions complied with, and level of protection guaranteed by GDPR not undermined. Schrems II essential-equivalence test.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 47(2) — 14 Mandatory BCR Content Items
nodes.rationale: Closed list of 14 mandatory items (Recital 108): group structure, transfer categories, legal binding force, principles, data-subject rights, controller responsibility, DPO, complaint mechanism, supervisory cooperation, training, audit, change reporting, cooperation procedure. All must be present for approval.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 47(2) — 14 mandatory bcr content items

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-034: Binding Corporate Rules
nodes.rationale: Security objective for intragroup transfer mechanisms under Art. 47. Referenced by SR-GDPR-058.

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-015: Data Minimisation
nodes.rationale: Adequate, relevant, necessary in relation to purposes; further processing compatible per Art. 6(4) test. Source: Art. 5(1)(c), Art. 6(4).

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 6(1): Lawfulness of Processing
nodes.rationale: Six lawfulness bases (a)-(f); bases (b)-(d) carry 'necessary' qualifiers; (e) requires Union/Member State law; (f) requires balancing test per Recital 47/49.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 9(1): Special Categories Prohibition
nodes.rationale: Nine conjunctive special categories each independently trigger prohibition; ten Art. 9(2) exceptions provide the only lawful processing paths.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 35 — Data protection impact assessment
nodes.rationale: Art. 35(1) high-risk DPIA trigger; Art. 35(7) DPIA content (systematic description, necessity/proportionality, risk assessment, mitigation measures). Supplies evidence base for Art. 36 consultation.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 35 — data protection impact assessment

nodes.label: GDPR Article 36 — Prior consultation
nodes.rationale: Art. 36(1) prior consultation where DPIA indicates residual high risk; Art. 36(2) 8-week supervisory response obligation. Pre-launch gate distinct from post-launch incident reporting.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 5 — Principles relating to processing of personal data
nodes.rationale: Art. 5(1)(a) lawfulness/fairness/transparency; Art. 5(1)(b) purpose limitation; Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation; Art. 5(1)(f) integrity/confidentiality; Art. 5(2) accountability. Gateway principles for all processing.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 5 — principles relating to processing of personal data

nodes.label: GDPR Article 6 — Lawfulness of processing
nodes.rationale: Art. 6(1)(a) consent; Art. 6(4) compatibility test for further processing with five conjunctive factors. Supplies the lawfulness basis for Art. 5(1)(a) obligation.

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OC-03: Legal/Regulatory Requirements Understood and Managed
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-027, SR-GDPR-028 as the regulatory-translation layer for GDPR obligations into cybersecurity governance.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.oc-03: legal/regulatory requirements understood and managed

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.IM-04: Risk Management Improvements from Context
nodes.rationale: Captures forward-looking-improvement discipline: DPIA review triggered by contextual changes — threat-intelligence shifts, incidents, technology evolution.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.im-04: risk management improvements from context

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.RA-01: Vulnerability Identification and Recording
nodes.rationale: Captures asset-level vulnerability-recording discipline: DPIA's systematic-description requirement is operationally the same as vulnerability-recording posture for data, processing and supporting assets.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.ra-01: vulnerability identification and recording

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.RA-05: Inherent Risk Understanding
nodes.rationale: Captures inherent-risk understanding: threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods and impacts assembled into coherent inherent-risk picture before designing measures. Also captures structured-risk-assessment spine of DPIA necessity/proportionality and risks-to-data-subjects.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.ra-05: inherent risk understanding

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.RA-06: Risk Response Selection and Tracking
nodes.rationale: Captures risk-response layer: choose, prioritise, plan and track measures addressing identified risks. Also captures risk-response-rerun when material change in risk detected.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.ra-06: risk response selection and tracking

nodes.label: NIST CSF RS.AN-03: Root Cause Analysis
nodes.rationale: Captures measures-envisaged discipline: documentation of safeguards and security measures as structured analysis of what each measure addresses and how it traces to specific identified risk.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rs.an-03: root cause analysis

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-013: DPIA and prior consultation objective
nodes.norm_label: so-gdpr-013: dpia and prior consultation objective

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 35(1) — DPIA Trigger
nodes.rationale: Requires DPIA prior to processing likely to result in high risk, in particular using new technologies. Open-textured threshold with EDPB nine-criteria list as operational anchor.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 35(11) — DPIA Review
nodes.rationale: Requires review where necessary, at least when there is a change of the risk represented by processing operations. Material change in risk is primary trigger supplemented by periodic review.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 35(7) — DPIA Content
nodes.rationale: Four mandated content items: systematic description, necessity/proportionality assessment, risks-to-data-subjects assessment, measures-envisaged including safeguards and security measures.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 36(1) — Prior Consultation
nodes.rationale: Requires prior consultation with supervisory authority where DPIA indicates processing would result in high risk in absence of mitigation measures.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 4(1) — Personal Data Definition
nodes.rationale: Supplies the personal-data definition on which the DPIA scope rests.

nodes.label: EDPB Guidelines 4/2019 on DPIA
nodes.rationale: Provides nine-criteria list as operational anchor for high-risk threshold and interpretation of 'new technologies' as not widely deployed at time of assessment.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 12(5) — Manifestly Unfounded or Excessive Requests
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 12(5) — manifestly unfounded or excessive requests

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-038: Information Duties and Rights-Exercise Support
nodes.rationale: Controller provides transparent, concise, intelligible, easily accessible information in clear and plain language; supports exercise of data-subject rights; verifies identity on reasonable doubt; responds within one month; acts free of charge except in defined exceptions.
nodes.norm_label: so-gdpr-038: information duties and rights-exercise support

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-066: One-Month SLA on Data-Subject Rights Requests
nodes.rationale: Art. 12(3) sets 1-month hard ceiling; extension to 3 months requires demonstrated complexity. 'Without undue delay' is a directional qualifier, not a separate deadline per EDPB Guidelines on Art. 12.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-066: one-month sla on data-subject rights requests

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-067: Anti-Abuse Controls for Manifestly Unfounded Rights Requests
nodes.rationale: Art. 12(5) allows fee or refusal for manifestly unfounded/excessive requests. Controller bears the burden of demonstrating the character. Refusal cannot rest on general suspicion; the demonstrative burden is not satisfied by the controller's general suspicion.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-067: anti-abuse controls for manifestly unfounded rights requests

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 24 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering controller responsibility, appropriate measures, and evidence-of-compliance.

nodes.label: EDPB Guidelines 07/2020 on processor obligations
nodes.rationale: Referenced for sufficient-guarantees factors, sub-processor authorisation, and audit expectations across SR-GDPR-033, 035, 036.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28 — Processing by a processor
nodes.rationale: Processor obligations (selection, authorisation, contract, sub-processors, erasure, audit) referenced across SR-GDPR-030 through SR-GDPR-037.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 28 — processing by a processor

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 4(7)/(8) — Controller/Processor definitions
nodes.rationale: Defines controller (determines purposes and means) and processor (processes on behalf of controller), anchoring the chain-of-authority pattern.

nodes.label: SO-NIS2-013: Security objective (business continuity and crisis management)
nodes.norm_label: so-nis2-013: security objective (business continuity and crisis management)

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 PR.DS-11: Backups Created, Protected, Maintained, Tested

nodes.rationale: Prior specific or general written authorisation required; general authorisation requires notification of changes giving controller opportunity to object.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28(3): Processor Contract Mandatory Clauses
nodes.rationale: Eight sub-clauses (a)-(h) form a closed AND-list; all mandatory; contract must stipulate each; includes instructions, confidentiality, Art. 32 measures, sub-processor conditions, DSR assistance, audit access, return/deletion.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 28(3): processor contract mandatory clauses

nodes.label: CRA Article 13 (Manufacturer Obligations)
nodes.rationale: The central article governing manufacturer obligations for products with digital elements, spanning design through end-of-life.

nodes.label: D-01.2 — Data in Transit Encryption Sub-Domain
nodes.rationale: Single-control sub-domain: in-transit is cheapest of three encryption sub-domains. All 3 regulation pairs verified as SAME. Modern TLS typically satisfies all without additional investment.
nodes.norm_label: d-01.2 — data in transit encryption sub-domain

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.DS-02: Data-in-Transit Protected
nodes.rationale: Authenticated-transport encryption for transit. Prevents classical confidentiality-without-integrity gap.

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.IR-01: Networks Protected from Unauthorized Access
nodes.rationale: Logical-access dimension complementing in-transit confidentiality; closes lateral-movement gap.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ir-01: networks protected from unauthorized access

nodes.label: SO-CRA-003 — In-Transit Confidentiality (CRA)
nodes.rationale: CRA security objective specifically for data-in-transit confidentiality. Parent for SR-CRA-003.

nodes.label: Requirement 1.2 — Data in Transit Protection (Multi-Reg)
nodes.rationale: MUST priority, TEST verification. TLS 1.3+ on all channels, mTLS where both endpoints authenticate, certificate validation fail-closed, network segmentation documented. Strictest floor (CRA) discharges GDPR and DORA.

nodes.label: Requirement 1.2.1 — Personal Data in Transit (GDPR)
nodes.rationale: TLS 1.3+ on channels carrying personal data; five-event Art. 32(2) risk enumeration addressed by technical measures. NIST CSF: PR.DS-02, PR.IR-01.

nodes.label: Requirement 1.2.2 — Product Data in Transit (CRA)
nodes.rationale: State-of-the-art symmetric encryption (TLS 1.3 AES-256-GCM), Annex I (2)(e) render-unintelligible test, (2)(j) attack-surface limitation. Both internal east-west and external edges covered.

nodes.label: Requirement 1.2.3 — Financial Entity ICT Data in Transit (DORA)
nodes.rationale: High-standards in-transit cryptography with EBA/ESMA/EIOPA RTS conformance. mTLS architecture + zone-trust + peer-peer authentication documented.
nodes.norm_label: requirement 1.2.3 — financial entity ict data in transit (dora)

nodes.label: D-01.2 CRA Sub-SO (Product Data in Transit)
nodes.rationale: State-of-the-art encryption + attack-surface limitation (Annex I (2)(e)+(j)). Stricter than GDPR; meeting CRA discharges GDPR on in-transit channel.
nodes.norm_label: d-01.2 cra sub-so (product data in transit)

nodes.label: D-01.2 DORA Sub-SO (Financial Entity ICT Data in Transit)
nodes.rationale: CIA+A at high standards across all data states including in transit (Art. 9(2)). Entity-level transport-security governance: zone trust, mTLS, peer-peer authentication.
nodes.norm_label: d-01.2 dora sub-so (financial entity ict data in transit)

nodes.label: D-01.2 GDPR Sub-SO (Personal Data in Transit)
nodes.rationale: Personal data transmitted across networks remains confidential and unaltered, anchored to Art. 32(2) five-event risk enumeration. CSF anchors: PR.DS-02, PR.IR-01.
nodes.norm_label: d-01.2 gdpr sub-so (personal data in transit)

nodes.label: D-01.2 High-Level Security Objective (Data in Transit Encryption)
nodes.rationale: Common obligation across GDPR, CRA, DORA: in-transit cryptographic confidentiality and integrity. Engages when ≥2 applicable regulations overlap on same channel. All 3 pairs verified as SAME by CRDA-deep.
nodes.norm_label: d-01.2 high-level security objective (data in transit encryption)

nodes.label: DORA Regulation (EU) 2022/2554
nodes.rationale: EU Digital Operational Resilience Act. Art. 9(2) requires high standards of CIA+A across data states including in transit.

nodes.label: GDPR Regulation (EU) 2016/679
nodes.rationale: EU General Data Protection Regulation. Art. 32(1)(b)+(2) covers security of processing including in-transit personal data.

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.PS-01: Configuration Management Practices Established
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-041 for by-default configuration discipline across four minimisation dimensions.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ps-01: configuration management practices established

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 34(1) — High-Risk Breach Communication to Data Subject
nodes.rationale: Requires communication to data subject without undue delay when breach is likely to result in high risk; higher threshold than Art. 33 supervisory notification.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 34(1) — high-risk breach communication to data subject

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 34(3) — Data-Subject Notification Exceptions
nodes.rationale: Provides three exceptions: (a) cryptographic protection rendering data unintelligible, (b) subsequent measures ensuring high risk no longer likely to materialise, (c) disproportionate effort with public communication substitute.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(5): Due Diligence on Third-Party Components
nodes.rationale: Express inclusion of non-commercial OSS in due-diligence scope. The OSS community's non-commercial posture transfers the duty to assess to the integrating manufacturer. Referenced by SR-CRA-050.
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 13(5): due diligence on third-party components

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(6): Component Vulnerability Reporting and Remediation

nodes.norm_label: cra art. 13(6): component vulnerability reporting and remediation

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OV-03: Cybersecurity Performance Evaluated

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RM-04: Strategic direction on risk response
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.rm-04: strategic direction on risk response

nodes.label: GDPR Arts. 44–49 — Cross-border transfer regime
nodes.rationale: Chapter V transfer conditions: adequacy (Art. 45), appropriate safeguards (Art. 46), BCR (Art. 47), and derogations (Art. 49) as fallback.

nodes.label: Annex I Part I (2)(l): Recording and Monitoring with User Opt-Out

nodes.norm_label: annex i part i (2)(l): recording and monitoring with user opt-out

nodes.label: NIST CSF DE.AE-08: Incidents Declared When Adverse Events Meet Criteria

nodes.label: DORA Article 6 (ICT Risk Management Framework)
nodes.rationale: Top-of-stack governance: Art. 6(1) sound/comprehensive/well-documented framework, Art. 6(4) three-lines-of-defence independence, Art. 6(8) chapeau obligation. Operationalised by Art. 7, Art. 9, Chapter III.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(1): Security of Processing
nodes.rationale: Risk-based preamble with five factors; four sub-letters (a)-(d) as floor of expected measures; operationalises Art. 5(1)(f).

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 ID.RA-04: Threat Impacts and Likelihoods Identified and Prioritized
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 id.ra-04: threat impacts and likelihoods identified and prioritized

nodes.label: TIBER-EU Framework (ESAs Joint Committee)
nodes.rationale: Referenced in Art. 26(11) as the defining framework for TLPT. Incorporates ISO/IEC 33069 and threat-intelligence-led methodology. ECB-led methodology is the dominant reading.

nodes.label: Annex I Part II (1): SBOM in Machine-Readable Format
nodes.rationale: Requires SBOM in commonly used and machine-readable format covering at least top-level dependencies. Referenced by SR-CRA-009, 012, 052.
nodes.norm_label: annex i part ii (1): sbom in machine-readable format

nodes.label: SR-CRA-009: SBOM Lifecycle Retention and Market-Surveillance Disclosure

nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-009: sbom lifecycle retention and market-surveillance disclosure

nodes.rationale: CRA Art. 3(47) imports GDPR Art. 4(1) notion of personal data, extending the at-rest encryption obligation to any non-personal data stored alongside.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 4(1) — definition of personal data

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 PR.DS-10: Data-in-use protected
nodes.rationale: Closes the in-use dimension historically under-protected by financial entities through confidential-computing enclaves and memory-encryption primitives.

nodes.rationale: Art. 24(3) extends Art. 14(3)/(8) to stewards where severe incidents affect steward's NIS for product development. Closes symmetric gap with Art. 14(1) extension in SR-CRA-039.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-032: Severe-Incident 24-Hour and 72-Hour Notifications
nodes.rationale: Art. 14(4)(a)/(b) require SI early warning 24h + incident notification 72h with progressively richer content. Mapped to RS.MA-02 and RS.MA-03.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-033: One-Month Severe-Incident Final Report
nodes.rationale: Art. 14(4)(c) requires final report within 1 month of 72h notification, with detailed description, root cause, and mitigation measures. Mapped to RS.AN-06 and RS.AN-08.

nodes.rationale: Provides the dominant EU supervisory baseline where the underlying service is outsourcing, including proportionality assessment under Art. 4.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28 — Controller-Processor Contract Requirements
nodes.rationale: Parallels but does not replace DORA third-party contractual requirements for personal-data processing.

nodes.label: SR-DORA-021: Minimum Contractual Elements for ICT Third-Party Arrangements
nodes.rationale: Converts a written contract into an enforceable supply-chain control. Closes both the formal-allocation axis and the operational-performance axis of the third-party regime.

nodes.label: SR-DORA-022: Unrestricted Audit Rights Over Critical ICT Third-Party Providers
nodes.rationale: Converts a paper audit-right into a live detection-and-verification capability. Closes the gap between formal right and effective use that has historically caused post-incident forensics to stall at the supplier boundary.
nodes.norm_label: sr-dora-022: unrestricted audit rights over critical ict third-party providers

nodes.label: DORA Art. 28(1) - ICT Third-Party Risk
nodes.rationale: Foundational third-party risk-governance rule with four-factor proportionality. Contractual minimum elements at Art. 30(1)-(2) and audit rights at Art. 30(3)(e) operationalise it.

nodes.label: ICT Third-Party Risk Under Four-Factor Proportionality
nodes.rationale: Art. 28(1) requires managing ICT third-party risk considering nature/scale/complexity/importance of dependencies and contractual risks. The 'critical or important' distinction propagates to 18 of 38 DORA clauses.
nodes.norm_label: ict third-party risk under four-factor proportionality

nodes.label: AI-Specific Attack Taxonomy (Art. 15(4)–(5))
nodes.rationale: Six AI-specific attack categories: data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples/model evasion, confidentiality attacks, model flaws. No analog in GDPR/NIS2/CRA/DORA. Layered overlay, not substitution.

nodes.label: CRA R2 Constructive-Knowledge Baseline
nodes.rationale: Strictest knowledge-test floor: inquiry-resistant standard capturing non-CVE-listed weaknesses. Materially more demanding than AI Act 'reasonably foreseeable'. Applies to manufacturer regardless of downstream entity cadence.

nodes.label: CVD (Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure)
nodes.source_location: NIS2 Art. 12(1), CRA Annex I Part II (4)–(6)
nodes.rationale: NIS2 provides institutional pathway (CSIRT-coordinated); CRA provides substantive content (manufacturer CVD policy). NIS2 entity using CRA product has both layers.

nodes.label: D-04.3 Incident Reporting (Referenced Sub-domain)
nodes.rationale: D-02.1 does not generate recipient asymmetry; the identification process is inward-looking. Recipient fragmentation (GDPR Art. 33→SA, NIS2 Art. 23(4)→CSIRT, CRA Art. 14→CSIRT+ENISA, DORA Art. 19→CA, AI Act Art. 73→MSA) is D-04.3's concern.

nodes.label: DORA Lex Specialis Principle
nodes.rationale: For pure-financial entities, DORA absorbs NIS2 identification obligation. High-level SO does not aggregate across lex-specialis boundary. Cross-sector entities stack-merge.

nodes.label: DORA Temporal Floor (continuous + at-least-yearly)
nodes.rationale: Strictest temporal floor of the five regulators. A DORA-cadenced programme discharges GDPR 'regularly', NIS2 silent baseline, CRA R2, and AI Act 'known AND reasonably foreseeable' on the same asset.

nodes.label: 5×5 Scope-Overlap Matrix
nodes.rationale: Gating condition for high-level SO engagement. Y = scope overlap on single artefact; Conditional = disjoint in baseline, Y on integrated-stack. NIS2↔DORA conditional (lex specialis for pure-financial).

nodes.label: CRDA — Cross-Regulation Domain Analysis
nodes.rationale: Static cross-regulation analysis with 10 pairwise comparisons. Initial classifications: 8 COMPLEMENTARY + 2 DIFFERENT PERSPECTIVE. All corrected to SAME after OJ-text analysis.

nodes.label: CRDA-deep — OJ-text-verified Pairwise Analysis
nodes.rationale: Deep per-pair analysis with verbatim OJ text, scope/trigger/threshold/recipient/content comparisons. All 10 pairs verified as SAME. Corrected CRDA initial classifications.

nodes.label: Requirement 2.1 — Multi-reg Vulnerability Identification
nodes.rationale: Volere audit requirement (section 15). MUST priority, TEST verification. Engages conditionally when ≥2 regs overlap on same asset. NIST CSF: ID.RA-01, ID.RA-03, ID.AM-02, PR.PS-02, GV.OV-02.

nodes.label: Requirement 2.1.1 — Periodic Testing + DPIA Review
nodes.rationale: GDPR-specific: Art. 32(1)(d) periodic testing + Art. 35(11) DPIA review. VAG 'regularly' discharged by DORA-cadenced programme. NIST CSF: ID.RA-01, PR.PS-02, ID.RA-05, ID.IM-02.

nodes.label: Requirement 2.1.2 — Vulnerability Handling + Disclosure
nodes.rationale: NIS 2-specific: Art. 21(2)(e) CVD lifecycle. Silent temporal anchor. NIST CSF: ID.RA-01, GV.SC-04.

nodes.label: Requirement 2.1.3 — SBOM-backed Product Identification
nodes.rationale: CRA-specific: Annex I Part I (2)(a) + Part II (1) + Art. 13(3)/(7)/(8). R2 constructive-knowledge baseline. NIST CSF: ID.RA-01, ID.AM-02, PR.PS-02.

nodes.label: Requirement 2.1.4 — Continuous ICT-risk + Annual Review
nodes.rationale: DORA-specific: Art. 7(2) + Art. 8(2). Strictest temporal floor. NIST CSF: ID.RA-01, ID.RA-03, ID.RA-05, ID.IM-04, PR.PS-02, GV.OV-02.

nodes.label: Requirement 2.1.5 — AI Risk-identification + Attack Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: AI Act-specific: Art. 9(2) 4-step cycle + Art. 15(4)–(5) attack taxonomy. NIST CSF: ID.RA-03, ID.RA-04, ID.RA-06, PR.PS-06, RS.MI-01, RS.MA-03, GV.RM-01, GV.RM-06.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-02.3: Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure

nodes.label: SR-CRA-073: OSS steward cooperation with market surveillance authorities
nodes.rationale: Request-triggered: no standing reporting or audit obligation; cooperation fires only upon reasoned MSA request with specific operational cause
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-073: oss steward cooperation with market surveillance authorities

nodes.label: Req 2.3: CVD ecosystem maintained (Volere immunity)
nodes.rationale: MUST priority, TEST verification; conditional scope_overlap — HL engages only on integrated manufacturer-as-NIS-2-entity stack

nodes.label: Req 2.3.1: Manufacturer-side CVD policy, public disclosure, SPOC
nodes.rationale: CRA-only manufacturer activates this sub-SO; depends on 2.1.3 identification pipeline and 2.2.1 security-update availability

nodes.label: Req 2.3.2: Entity-side vulnerability handling and disclosure
nodes.rationale: NIS-2-only essential entity activates without manufacturer-side CVD architecture; Art. 21(2)(e) silent on temporal anchoring
nodes.norm_label: req 2.3.2: entity-side vulnerability handling and disclosure

nodes.label: CRA Art. 14(5)(a) — Severe-incident categorisation test
nodes.rationale: Defines severity as negative impact (or capability of negative impact) on availability, authenticity, integrity, or confidentiality of sensitive or important data or functions. Four CIA dimensions inherited from NIS 2 via CRA Art. 3(43) incident cross-reference.

nodes.label: CRA Article 32: Conformity assessment routes
nodes.rationale: Class I (Module A), Class II (B+C/H/CSA), critical products (B+C/H/CSA at substantial).

nodes.label: CRA Art. 32(3) — Class II conformity assessment routes
nodes.rationale: Routes Class II important products (Annex III Class II) to Module B+C, Module H, or CSA certification at substantial assurance level. The certification path is the third option in addition to two notified-body routes from Art. 32(2).
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 32(3) — class ii conformity assessment routes

nodes.label: CRA Article 27: Presumption of conformity
nodes.rationale: Three presumption routes: harmonised standards, common specifications, CSA certification at substantial level.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 27 — Presumption of conformity framework
nodes.rationale: Multi-paragraph framework: Art. 27(1) harmonised standards presumption, Art. 27(2) common specifications via implementing acts, Art. 27(5) presumption via common specs, Art. 27(8) CSA certification presumption, Art. 27(9) delegated acts for CSA schemes. All presumptions are rebuttable and coverage-limited.
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 27 — presumption of conformity framework

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 6(6) — Incident definition (cross-referenced by CRA Art. 3(43))
nodes.rationale: Supplies the four security dimensions (availability, authenticity, integrity, confidentiality) inherited by CRA's incident definition. Authenticity is the NIS-2/CRA-unique addition over classical CIA triad. OJ-corrective note: CRA Art. 3(43) imports from NIS 2 Art. 6(6), not Art. 6(2).
nodes.norm_label: nis 2 art. 6(6) — incident definition (cross-referenced by cra art. 3(43))

nodes.label: CRA Article 15: Voluntary reporting by any person
nodes.rationale: Voluntary AEV and severe-incident reporting; CSIRT bridges to manufacturer; liability shield.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 PR.PS-02: Software Maintained, Replaced, and Removed Commensurate with Risk

nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 pr.ps-06: secure software development practices integrated and monitored

nodes.label: DORA Art. 17(1): ICT-Related Incident Management Process

nodes.label: DORA Art. 24(1): Digital Operational Resilience Testing Programme

nodes.norm_label: dora art. 24(1): digital operational resilience testing programme

nodes.label: DORA Art. 7(2): Continuous ICT Risk Identification and Annual Scenario Review
nodes.rationale: Sentence 1 requires continuous identification of all ICT risk sources with inter-entity awareness; sentence 2 requires at-least-yearly risk-scenario review; forms temporal and methodological chassis per Art. 6(8)(a).
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 7(2): continuous ict risk identification and annual scenario review

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4): Eight Mandatory ICT Security Control Domains
nodes.rationale: Chapeau establishes eight mandatory control categories including network management (b), access control (c), change management (e), and patch governance (f); anchors structural dimension of ICT security controls.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 9(4): eight mandatory ict security control domains

nodes.label: Cyber Resilience Act (EU) 2024/2847

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 9(2) — Post-Market Monitoring
nodes.rationale: Post-market-monitoring duties for high-risk AI systems where AI components are in scope alongside DORA Art. 8(1) monitoring

nodes.rationale: Adopts 'means likely reasonably to be used' test for identifiability; brings pseudonymous data into scope where re-identification is operationally feasible

nodes.rationale: DORA SR-DORA-030 maps here; continuous monitoring and control of ICT systems

nodes.rationale: Requires ICT BC policy as integral part of overall BC policy; 'may be adopted as dedicated specific policy' permits either form-factor; sits alongside Art. 12 backup obligations.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 11(1): comprehensive ict business continuity policy

nodes.label: DORA Art. 5 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Largest article split; contains SO-DORA-014 and SO-DORA-016 definitions plus SRs covering CIA+A protection, authentication, key protection, risk identification, scenario refresh, network management, patch governance, resilience testing, TLPT, access control, detection, BC, backup, incident management, training, and governance.

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-003: Risk-Measure Validation Through Targeted Testing
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(6)-(7) verification layer; testing ensures consistency for intended purpose; real-world conditions per Art. 60; 'most appropriate AND targeted' is VAG on both modifiers.
nodes.norm_label: sr-aiact-003: risk-measure validation through targeted testing

nodes.label: Berry Ambiguity Framework (VAG, POLY, COORD, S2/S3)
nodes.rationale: Analytical framework used throughout D-02.1.md to classify linguistic ambiguities: VAG (vague), POLY (polysemous), COORD (coordination), with severity levels S2/S3. References Berry §3.3.1, §5.1, §5.4.7, §5.5, §5.6, §5.7.
nodes.norm_label: berry ambiguity framework (vag, poly, coord, s2/s3)

nodes.label: DORA-D22 — 'critical or important function' (S3 tautology)
nodes.rationale: Recurring definitional anchor across CL8-3, CL9-2, CL9-4, CL11-1, CL11-2, CL11-3, CL12-3, CL12-4, CL13-1, CL16-2. Identified as S3 tautological definition (Berry classic).

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 6(1) — 'network and information system' cross-ref
nodes.rationale: DORA Art. 3(2) cross-references NIS 2 Art. 6(1) for the definition of 'network and information system'. Recurs as definitional anchor in CL9-1, CL9-3, CL9-4, CL10-2, CL12-1, CL16-2.
nodes.norm_label: nis 2 art. 6(1) — 'network and information system' cross-ref

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 55(1)(a) — GPAI model evaluation for systemic risk (SR-AIACT-023)
nodes.rationale: Second-most-consequential AI Act ambiguity: triple VAG-3 (standardised protocols + state of the art + systemic risks). 'Systemic risks' borrowed from financial-services regulation (DORA Art. 4(50)). Maps to NIST CSF GV.RM-06, ID.RA-04, PR.PS-06.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 55(1)(a) — gpai model evaluation for systemic risk (sr-aiact-023)

nodes.label: DORA Art. 10(1) — Detection mechanisms
nodes.rationale: Promptly detect anomalous activities, ICT network performance issues, ICT-related incidents, material SPOFs. Regularly tested per Art. 25. RTS-pending via Art. 15(c).

nodes.label: DORA Art. 11(1)+(2) — ICT Business Continuity Policy + 5 objectives
nodes.rationale: Comprehensive BCP with 5 cumulative objectives (continuity, quick response, activation, impact estimation, communication). Cross-refs Art. 8, 12, 14, 19. RTS-pending via Art. 15(d).
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 11(1)+(2) — ict business continuity policy + 5 objectives

nodes.label: DORA Art. 12(1)+(2) — Backup policies chapeau
nodes.rationale: Backup policies specifying scope and minimum frequency based on criticality/confidentiality. Non-jeopardise condition for backup activation. Periodic testing required.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 13(1)-(3) — Threat-intel + post-incident reviews + lessons propagation
nodes.rationale: Learn-and-evolve cycle: gather vulnerability/cyber-threat info, post-incident reviews after major incidents, lessons incorporated continuously into ICT risk assessment. Non-microenterprise communication carve-out.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 13(1)-(3) — threat-intel + post-incident reviews + lessons propagation

nodes.label: DORA Art. 14(1) — Crisis communication plans
nodes.rationale: Responsible disclosure of major ICT-related incidents or vulnerabilities to clients, counterparts, and public. 'Responsible' is Berry-flagged vague term.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 15 — ESAs RTS Mandate (7 subject areas)
nodes.rationale: Meta-procedural RTS mandate: ESAs (Joint Committee + ENISA) develop common draft RTS for 7 subject areas mapping to Art. 9-11-6 elements. Deadline 17 Jan 2024; Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1774 adopted.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 15 — esas rts mandate (7 subject areas)

nodes.label: DORA Art. 16(1)+(3) — Simplified framework for small entities
nodes.rationale: Structurally parallel to Art. 9(4) hinge but at lower operational granularity. Omits access control, change management, and patches as standalone control families. Deliberate regulatory choice for small entities.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 16(1)+(3) — simplified framework for small entities

nodes.label: DORA Art. 8(4)+(5)+(6) — Critical-asset mapping + inventory + TPP dependencies
nodes.rationale: Covers identification of information/ICT assets, criticality mapping, TPP interconnections, and periodic inventory updates. Contains 4 ambiguity instances (VAG, POLY) with Berry anchors.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 8(4)+(5)+(6) — critical-asset mapping + inventory + tpp dependencies

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(2) — Design/procure/implement ICT security
nodes.rationale: Three coordinated verbs (design, procure, implement) + 4 data-security dimensions × 3 data states. RTS-pending via Art. 15(a).

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4) — THE HINGE (6 control families)
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(4) is identified as the operational core of DORA's ICT risk-management framework, establishing six mandatory control families: info-security policy, network/infrastructure, access control, authentication+encryption, change management, patches/updates. The 6-way AND in 9(4)(e) and hendiadys in 9(4)(f) are operationally consequential.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 9(4) — the hinge (6 control families)

nodes.label: T3-vs-text gaps (C14, C15, C16, C17, C26, C27, C28)
nodes.rationale: Catalogues inconsistencies between v0.1 T3 mapping and OJ text. Major distortions: C14 (need-to-know/least privilege imposed), C16 (MFA imposed), C28 (role-specific training imposed). All are T3-imposed mapping artefacts, not OJ-text artefacts.
nodes.norm_label: t3-vs-text gaps (c14, c15, c16, c17, c26, c27, c28)

nodes.rationale: Art. 72(1)-(2) PMM system as ex-post assurance loop complementing ex-ante conformity assessment; proportionate to AI technology and risks.

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 15(1) — Accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity baseline (SR-AIACT-014)
nodes.rationale: 3-way AND fusing accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity into one continuous lifecycle-wide duty. No partial compliance. Maps to NIST CSF PR.PS-06, PR.IR-03, ID.RA-04. Cross-regulation: references CRA C07, NIS 2 C01 for cybersecurity definitional gap.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 15(1) — accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity baseline (sr-aiact-014)

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 15(3) — Resilience against errors/faults/drift (SR-AIACT-015)
nodes.rationale: Resilience backstop to Art. 15(1). 3-way OR of failure modes (errors, faults, inconsistencies). 2-way OR for means (backup OR fail-safe). Maps to NIST CSF PR.IR-03, PR.IR-04, PR.DS-11.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 15(3) — resilience against errors/faults/drift (sr-aiact-015)

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 15(4)-(5) — AI-specific attack vector mitigation (SR-AIACT-016)
nodes.rationale: 5-way AND of IR phases (prevent, detect, respond, resolve, control) × 6-way OR of attack types (data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples, confidentiality attacks, model flaws). Cross-regulation: parallel to CRA Annex I, NIS 2. Maps to NIST CSF ID.RA-04, PR.PS-06, RS.MI-01, RS.MA-03.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 15(4)-(5) — ai-specific attack vector mitigation (sr-aiact-016)

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 17(1) — Quality Management System (SR-AIACT-017)
nodes.rationale: Umbrella QMS obligation with 13-element closed list (a)-(m). Sub-point (g) cross-refers to Art. 9 risk management. Inspired by ISO 9001 but no specific standard mandated. Maps to NIST CSF GV.PO-01, GV.RM-01, GV.RM-04.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 17(1) — quality management system (sr-aiact-017)

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 17(1)(c) — Design, design control, design verification (SR-AIACT-018)
nodes.rationale: SDLC anchor of QMS. Twin 3-way AND: (design, design control, design verification) × (techniques, procedures, systematic actions). Operational bridge between Art. 17 QMS and Art. 15 properties. Maps to NIST CSF PR.PS-06, PR.PS-01.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 17(1)(c) — design, design control, design verification (sr-aiact-018)

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 26(1) — Deployer measures aligned with instructions for use (SR-AIACT-019)
nodes.rationale: Deployer-side mirror of provider QMS. 'Technical and organisational measures' uses same AND/OR pattern as GDPR Art. 5(1)(f) and NIS 2 Art. 21(1). Maps to NIST CSF GV.PO-01, GV.OC-03, PR.AT-01.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 26(1) — deployer measures aligned with instructions for use (sr-aiact-019)

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 73(1)-(4) — Tiered serious incident reporting (SR-AIACT-022)
nodes.rationale: Most temporally complex notification clause: 3 timelines (15/10/2 days) × 2 attribution thresholds. Cross-regulation: references NIS 2 C30, DORA Art. 19 for parallel reporting obligations. Maps to NIST CSF RS.CO-02, RS.CO-04, RS.MA-03, RS.MA-01.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 73(1)-(4) — tiered serious incident reporting (sr-aiact-022)

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 55(1)(c) — GPAI serious incident reporting to AI Office (SR-AIACT-024)
nodes.rationale: Upstream companion to Art. 73. Recipient: AI Office (EU-level) vs. national MSAs. 'Without undue delay' is VAG-3 (Berry classic). Cross-article boundary with Art. 73 undefined. Maps to NIST CSF RS.CO-02, RS.MA-03, RS.AN-03.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 55(1)(c) — gpai serious incident reporting to ai office (sr-aiact-024)

nodes.label: Cross-state CIA+A Protection Matrix

nodes.label: Classification-Driven Cryptographic-Key Protection

nodes.label: Network and Infrastructure Management with Blast-Radius Isolation

nodes.label: Documented Patch and Update Governance

nodes.label: Art. 13(9): 10-Year Update Availability
nodes.rationale: Security updates remain available after issuance for at least 10 years or remainder of support period, whichever is longer.

nodes.label: Art. 3(39): SBOM Definition

nodes.label: SO-CRA-045: Design/Development/Production per Annex I

nodes.label: CRA Annex I Part I (2)(d): Protection from unauthorised access + reporting
nodes.rationale: Product-side access boundary with 'possible unauthorised access reported' (R1 inclusive: any successful + any detected-but-failed). Strictest visibility floor across four regulators. Reporting dimension is CRA-specific, not mirrored in GDPR/NIS2/DORA.
nodes.norm_label: cra annex i part i (2)(d): protection from unauthorised access + reporting

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4)(c): Access limited to legitimate and approved functions and activities only
nodes.rationale: Strictest authorisation floor across four regulators. Literal 'only' qualifier (Berry §5.3.1) closes off any access not strictly tied to legitimate and approved function. T4-vs-text gap: T4 imports need-to-know/least-privilege not in OJ literal.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 9(4)(c): access limited to legitimate and approved functions and activities only

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 29: Instructions-only processing
nodes.rationale: Chain of authority controller→processor→authorised persons. 'Instructions' polysemy (R1 documented in contract with operational instructions recorded contemporaneously). Staff-side/processor-boundary surface. Only exception: Union or Member State law.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(i): HR security, access control policies and asset management
nodes.rationale: Three distinct security domains coordinated by AND in single sub-point. Model-agnostic (OJ text contains no RBAC/ABAC/MAC/DAC). T3-vs-text gap: T3 imports role-based/need-to-know/least-privilege not in OJ. Literal AND requires all three (partial compliance rejected).
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 21(2)(i): hr security, access control policies and asset management

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering processor obligations, sub-processor authorisation, and data-subject rights cascade

nodes.label: Requirement 3.3: Multi-boundary authorisation architecture (high-level)
nodes.rationale: Volere requirement 15/access. MUST priority, TEST verification. One authorisation-surface register per boundary with explicit boundary hand-off protocols. DORA 'only' qualifier is binding floor; CRA 'possible unauthorised access' is binding visibility floor.

nodes.label: Requirement 3.3.1: Personal-data-scope chain of authority
nodes.rationale: GDPR-specific sub-requirement. Documented instructions register + Art. 28(3)(a)/(b) processor contract + confidentiality-undertaking register. Boundary hand-off to NIS2 workforce-side and CRA product-side documented as controlled interfaces.

nodes.label: Requirement 3.3.2: Entity-side access-control policy (model-agnostic)
nodes.rationale: NIS2-specific sub-requirement. Model-agnostic (OJ does not impose RBAC/ABAC/MAC/DAC). Literal AND of AC + HR-security + asset-management all three required. T3-vs-text gap preserved as model-agnostic.

nodes.label: Requirement 3.3.3: Product-side authenticated-and-authorised boundary + reporting
nodes.rationale: CRA-specific sub-requirement. R1 inclusive reading on 'possible' (any successful + any detected-but-failed). Attack-surface-reduction evidence. Reporting dimension is CRA-specific strictest visibility floor.

nodes.label: Requirement 3.3.4: Financial-entity ICT-asset access (legitimate and approved only)
nodes.rationale: DORA-specific sub-requirement. Literal 'only' qualifier (Berry §5.3.1) closing off any access not strictly tied to legitimate and approved function. Multi-party authorisation for privileged grants. DORA absorbs NIS2 via lex specialis for pure-financial entities.
nodes.norm_label: requirement 3.3.4: financial-entity ict-asset access (legitimate and approved only)

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 21(1) — Objection Grounds Ambiguity
nodes.rationale: 'Compelling legitimate grounds' is stronger than Art. 6(1)(f) legitimate interests. The 'overriding' test for compelling grounds is undefined. R1 (strictly necessary) vs R2 (materially more weighty) yield materially distinct balance-tests.

nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.at-02 — workforce security awareness

nodes.label: CRA Annex I Part I (2)(d) — Identity/Access Management
nodes.rationale: Requires protection from unauthorised access by appropriate control mechanisms including authentication, identity, or access-management systems. 'Including but not limited to' keeps floor open. 'Verifiable manner' is the strictest knowledge-test floor.
nodes.norm_label: cra annex i part i (2)(d) — identity/access management

nodes.label: CRA Art. 7 — Important Products Classification
nodes.rationale: Two criteria (A or B) define important products. 'Core functionality' is the single most consequential classification term. 3-tier classification: Default (Art. 6), Important (Art. 7), Critical (Art. 8).

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4) — The Hinge (6 sub-points)
nodes.rationale: The operational core of DORA's protection regime. 6 sub-points (a)-(f) with 15 ambiguity instances. Sub-point (d) is the identity-lifecycle anchor for D-03.1.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4)(d) — Strong Authentication + Key Protection
nodes.rationale: 3-control AND: strong authentication + cryptographic key protection + risk-based encryption. Identity-lifecycle is one dimension. PR.AA-03 + PR.AA-04 anchors. OJ text does NOT contain 'multi-factor' — T4-vs-text gap P0-flagged.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 9(4)(d) — strong authentication + key protection

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 12(6) — Identity Verification
nodes.rationale: Permits controller to request additional information to confirm data-subject identity when reasonable doubts exist. Anchored to PR.AA-03 + PR.AA-02. VAG/S3 ambiguity on 'reasonable doubts' and 'additional information'.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(1) — Risk Management Core Obligation
nodes.rationale: 'Appropriate and proportionate' is the dominant VAG trigger of NIS2. Propagates to all 10 sub-points of Art. 21(2)(a)-(j). COORD/S3: three distinct security domains in Art. 21(2)(i) coordinated by AND.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 21(1) — risk management core obligation

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(i) — HR Security + Access Control + Asset Mgmt
nodes.rationale: Three distinct security domains coordinated by AND. COORD/S3 ambiguity: clause does not signal whether partial compliance (2 of 3) satisfies the obligation. T3-vs-text gap: OJ text contains no 'role-based', 'need-to-know', or 'least privilege' phrases.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 21(2)(i) — hr security + access control + asset mgmt

nodes.label: CRA↔DORA Pairwise Relationship
nodes.rationale: CRDA initial: COMPLEMENTARY. CRDA-deep verified: SAME. CRA is product-facing; DORA is financial-entity-facing. Obligations stack without contradiction.

nodes.label: GDPR↔CRA Pairwise Relationship
nodes.rationale: CRDA initial: DIFFERENT-PERSPECTIVE. CRDA-deep verified: SAME. Scope-disjoint test: Conditional (Y when CRA product hosts data-subject rights endpoints).

nodes.label: GDPR↔DORA Pairwise Relationship
nodes.rationale: CRDA initial: COMPLEMENTARY. CRDA-deep verified: SAME. Scope-disjoint test: Conditional (Y when DORA financial entity is also controller).

nodes.label: GDPR↔NIS2 Pairwise Relationship
nodes.rationale: CRDA initial: DIFFERENT-PERSPECTIVE. CRDA-deep verified: SAME. Scope-disjoint test: N (data subjects vs workforce are distinct identity objects). No contradiction.

nodes.label: NIS2↔CRA Pairwise Relationship
nodes.rationale: CRDA initial: COMPLEMENTARY. CRDA-deep verified: SAME. Product-to-entity layering. NIS2 governs entity; CRA governs product.

nodes.label: NIS2↔DORA Pairwise Relationship
nodes.rationale: CRDA initial: COMPLEMENTARY. CRDA-deep verified: SAME. DORA is lex specialis for pure-financial entities. For cross-sector, NIS2 layers on DORA.

nodes.label: Requirement 3.1 — Multi-boundary Identity Architecture
nodes.rationale: Volere requirement derived from SO-D-03.1.HL. MUST priority, TEST verification. NIST CSF: PR.AA-01 through PR.AA-06, ID.AM-01, PR.AT-02, PR.DS-12, DE.CM-09.

nodes.label: Requirement 3.1.1 — Data-subject Identity Verification
nodes.rationale: GDPR-specific sub-requirement. Graduated verification standard at rights-exercise endpoint. Art. 5(1)(c) minimisation register. Boundary hand-off to D-03.2 and CRA leg documented.

nodes.label: Requirement 3.1.2 — Workforce JML Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: NIS2-specific sub-requirement. Joiner-mover-leaver register with risk-tiered verification cadences. For pure-financial entities, DORA absorbs via lex specialis.

nodes.label: Requirement 3.1.3 — Product-side Identity Management
nodes.rationale: CRA-specific sub-requirement. Verifiable manner throughout operational lifetime. Type/batch/serial unique identification. SBOM-correlated identity register. Strictest knowledge-test floor.

nodes.label: Requirement 3.1.4 — Financial-entity Identity Assertion
nodes.rationale: DORA-specific sub-requirement. Assertion-conveyance integrity (signed tokens, mutual transport auth, PKI chain-of-trust). AAL2/AAL3 per NIST SP 800-63B. Strictest assertion-conveyance floor.

nodes.label: DORA Clause C19: Art. 9(4)(f) patches and updates
nodes.rationale: Source clause with T4-vs-text gap: T4 maps to D-07.2 Secure Coding but OJ text is patches and updates.
nodes.norm_label: dora clause c19: art. 9(4)(f) patches and updates

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.PS-02 – Software Maintenance
nodes.rationale: Software maintained, replaced, removed commensurate with risk. Supplies the risk-proportionality axis for change decisions.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 24–26 — Resilience Testing & TLPT
nodes.rationale: Primary source articles for SR-DORA-008 and SR-DORA-009. Art. 24(1) requires a sound and comprehensive testing programme; Art. 25(1) lists 12 testing modalities; Art. 26(1) mandates TLPT at least every 3 years.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 7 — ICT Risk Identification
nodes.rationale: Primary source article for SR-DORA-004 and SR-DORA-005. Art. 7(2) requires continuous identification of all sources of ICT risk and at-least-yearly review of risk scenarios.

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OV-02 — Risk management strategy reviewed
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-DORA-005 and SR-DORA-008. Anchors the strategic layer by requiring strategy adjustment when scenario-review findings diverge from the entity's risk-appetite statement.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.ov-02 — risk management strategy reviewed

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.RA-04 — Impacts and likelihoods identified
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-DORA-009. Supplies the threat-likelihood-impact framing that TLPT's threat-intelligence-led methodology depends on.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.ra-04 — impacts and likelihoods identified

nodes.label: TIBER-EU Framework
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-DORA-009. Art. 26(11) defines TLPT by reference to the TIBER-EU framework or equivalent, which incorporates ISO/IEC 33069 and threat-intelligence-led methodology.

nodes.label: 01_SecurityObjectives.md (Parent Aggregate)
nodes.rationale: Parent document from which SO-DORA-014 and SO-DORA-016 are extracted. Remains the authoritative aggregate index.

nodes.label: 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md (Parent Aggregate)
nodes.rationale: Parent document from which SR-DORA-001 through SR-DORA-012 are extracted. Remains the authoritative aggregate index.

nodes.label: DORA Clause C13: Art. 9(4)(b) network/infrastructure management
nodes.rationale: Source clause with T4 mapping mismatch: T4 maps to D-02.2 Patch Management but OJ text is network/infrastructure management.
nodes.norm_label: dora clause c13: art. 9(4)(b) network/infrastructure management

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.PS-01 – Configuration Management
nodes.rationale: Configuration management practices established, documented, applied to assets. Anchors golden baselines, drift detection, configuration-as-code for the 'controlled manner' qualifier.

nodes.label: Pair: CRA ↔ DORA (D-03.2)
nodes.rationale: Verified SAME. CRA product-side permissive; DORA financial-entity demanding. Layered: DORA deployer-side + CRA product-side.

nodes.label: Pair: GDPR ↔ CRA (D-03.2)
nodes.rationale: Verified SAME. Neither has explicit MFA mandate. GDPR staff-side instructions; CRA product-side 'may include'. Compatible but weak as MFA source.

nodes.label: Pair: GDPR ↔ DORA (D-03.2)
nodes.rationale: Verified SAME. DORA provides stronger authentication floor; GDPR provides staff-side legal authority and confidentiality layer. DORA gap: OJ says 'strong authentication' not 'multi-factor'.

nodes.label: Pair: GDPR ↔ NIS2 (D-03.2)
nodes.rationale: Verified SAME after OJ-text analysis (corrected from COMPLEMENTARY). GDPR supplies authorisation/confidentiality wrapper; NIS2 supplies explicit MFA mechanism. Conditional scope overlap.

nodes.label: Pair: NIS2 ↔ CRA (D-03.2)
nodes.rationale: Verified SAME. NIS2 explicit MFA entity-level; CRA permissive product-level 'may include authentication'. Compatible: NIS2 MFA exceeds CRA baseline.

nodes.label: Pair: NIS2 ↔ DORA (D-03.2)
nodes.rationale: Verified SAME. DORA strong-authentication is strictest floor; NIS2 'where appropriate' is risk-anchored. Lex specialis: DORA absorbs NIS2 for pure-financial entities.

nodes.label: Req 3.2: Layered Authentication Architecture (Volere)
nodes.rationale: Volere requirement: authentication mechanism of sufficient strength for risk in scope, calibrated by strictest applicable floor. MUST priority, TEST verification.

nodes.label: Req 3.2.2: NIS2 MFA or Continuous Authentication
nodes.rationale: NIS2-specific sub-requirement. Art. 21(2)(j) first clause. DORA floor discharges 'where appropriate' test when DORA applies on same party.
nodes.norm_label: req 3.2.2: nis2 mfa or continuous authentication

nodes.label: Req 3.2.4: DORA Strong Authentication
nodes.rationale: DORA-specific sub-requirement. Art. 9(4)(d). T4-vs-text gap P0-flagged. Chosen reading: mechanism-agnostic R5 with R3 MFA as dominant EU supervisory reading.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(2) — CIA+A cross-state protection
nodes.rationale: Core provision requiring high standards of availability, authenticity, integrity, confidentiality of data whether at rest, in use or in transit. Sits at core of Chapter II Section II operational resilience architecture.

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 21 — Parallel security requirements for NSIEs
nodes.rationale: Supplies parallel cross-state formulation, patch-governance, supply-chain, and policy-review requirements to which DORA-fall-back NSIEs are subject. Reinforces vocabulary and provides joint obligations where entities operate under both regimes.
nodes.norm_label: nis 2 art. 21 — parallel security requirements for nsies

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 11 — Processing Not Requiring Identification
nodes.rationale: Art. 11(2) preserves data-subject rights where the data subject provides additional information enabling identification, anchoring the reciprocal obligation in rights-exercise workflows.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 11 — processing not requiring identification

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 19 — Communication of Rectification to Recipients
nodes.rationale: Requires controller to communicate rectification or erasure to each recipient, unless impossible or disproportionate effort. Establishes the downstream-integrity obligation.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 19 — communication of rectification to recipients

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-09.4: Governance and Documentation
nodes.rationale: Covers transparency, notice design, SLA management, and anti-abuse governance processes.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 12 — Transparent Information and Rights Exercise
nodes.rationale: Covers transparency modalities (12(1)), one-month response deadline (12(3)), identity verification on reasonable doubt (12(4)/(6)), and anti-abuse for manifestly unfounded requests (12(5)).
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 12 — transparent information and rights exercise

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(1)(c): Data minimisation principle
nodes.rationale: Personal data adequate, relevant, limited to what is necessary; referenced by SR-031, SR-025, SR-010.

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.DS-12 — Data managed consistent with risk strategy
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-DORA-001. Supplies the risk-strategy calibration: data-handling rules are tiered against impact assessment (RTO/RPO alignment with business-criticality).
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ds-12 — data managed consistent with risk strategy

nodes.label: DORA Art. 24(1) — Digital operational resilience testing programme
nodes.rationale: Requires sound and comprehensive testing programme as integral part of ICT risk-management framework. Art. 24(7) RTS mandate is principal pending source of measurability.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 24(1) — digital operational resilience testing programme

nodes.label: CRA-CL29: Art. 13(8) sentence 3 — 5-year minimum
nodes.rationale: Hard minimum of five years for support period, or expected use time if shorter.

nodes.label: DORA Clause C09: Art. 9(2) CIA+A 4-way AND + data states
nodes.rationale: Source clause carrying S3 ambiguity on 'high standards' (VAG), 4-way AND of CIA+A (COORD), and 3-way OR of data states (COORD).
nodes.norm_label: dora clause c09: art. 9(2) cia+a 4-way and + data states

nodes.label: DORA Clause C15: Art. 9(4)(d) strong auth + key protection + encryption
nodes.rationale: Source clause carrying S3 on 'strong authentication' (VAG), 'relevant standards' (VAG/POLY), and 3-control AND (COORD).
nodes.norm_label: dora clause c15: art. 9(4)(d) strong auth + key protection + encryption

nodes.label: DORA Art. 15 — RTS Mandate to ESAs
nodes.rationale: Pending RTS mandate expected to specify further the 'relevant standards' and close measurability gaps. Art. 15(2)-(3) may harden the measurability of 'high standards' via technical standards adopted by the ESAs Joint Committee.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 15 — rts mandate to esas

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9 — ICT Security Controls
nodes.rationale: Primary source article for SR-DORA-001 through SR-DORA-003, SR-DORA-006, SR-DORA-007, SR-DORA-010. Art. 9(2) provides the CIA+A cross-state obligation; Art. 9(4) provides the eight-item control list.

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AA-04 — Identity assertions managed
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-DORA-002. Enforces integrity of identity-assertion conveyance via signed federated-identity tokens, mutual transport authentication, and PKI chain-of-trust.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.aa-04 — identity assertions managed

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.IR-03 — Resilience mechanisms
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-DORA-006. Supplies resilience layer (redundant paths, failover, automated isolation mechanisms triggered on detected compromise).

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RM-04: Strategic direction on risk established and communicated
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.rm-04: strategic direction on risk established and communicated

nodes.label: DORA Art. 15 — ESAs RTS mandate
nodes.rationale: Pending RTS mandate to ESAs expected to specify relevant standards, harden measurability of high standards, and close VAG ambiguities in Art. 9(2) and Art. 9(4)(d)

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 24(1): Appropriate measures and demonstrability
nodes.rationale: Controller's overarching obligation to implement and demonstrate appropriate measures; referenced by SR-043, SR-044.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 24(1): appropriate measures and demonstrability

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.RA-05 — Risk understanding for response decisions
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-DORA-005. Forces each scenario into a structured likelihood-by-impact matrix, converting narrative description into quantified risk inputs.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.ra-05 — risk understanding for response decisions

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 6(6): Incident Definition (imported by CRA Art. 3(44))
nodes.norm_label: nis 2 art. 6(6): incident definition (imported by cra art. 3(44))

nodes.label: CRA Annex I Part I (2)(d) — Unauthorised Access Controls
nodes.rationale: Requires protection from unauthorised access by appropriate control mechanisms including but not limited to authentication, identity, or access-management systems. Permissive — authentication is one of several admitted mechanisms.
nodes.norm_label: cra annex i part i (2)(d) — unauthorised access controls

nodes.label: CRA ↔ DORA Pair Analysis (Complementary)
nodes.rationale: CRA product-side controls and DORA financial-entity-side controls are layered. DORA requires governance depth that CRA's product-side text does not reach.

nodes.label: GDPR ↔ CRA Pair Analysis (Complementary)
nodes.rationale: CRA names authentication as one of several control families (permissive); GDPR does not mandate MFA. Compatible but weak as MFA source; should not derive hard MFA requirement without NIS2 or DORA.

nodes.label: GDPR ↔ DORA Pair Analysis (Complementary)
nodes.rationale: DORA provides stronger authentication floor; GDPR provides staff-side legal authority and confidentiality layer. OJ says 'strong authentication' not expressly 'multi-factor'.

nodes.label: GDPR ↔ NIS2 Pair Analysis (Complementary)
