nodes.rationale: GDPR supplies authority/confidentiality duties; NIS2 supplies explicit MFA/continuous-authentication mechanism. Classified COMPLEMENTARY after OJ-text verification.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(1) — Risk-Management Core Obligation Ambiguity
nodes.rationale: Dominant VAG trigger of NIS2. 'Appropriate and proportionate' qualifier propagates to all 10 sub-points of Art. 21(2)(a)–(j) and to Art. 21(3) and Art. 21(4). Three materially distinct readings (independent, hierarchical, compound).
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 21(1) — risk-management core obligation ambiguity

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(j) — MFA + Secured Comms + Emergency Comms
nodes.rationale: Contains four coordinated obligations (MFA OR continuous auth + secured voice/video/text + emergency comms) with 'where appropriate' hedge. Parse tree admits ≥6 distinct obligation shapes. T3-vs-text gap: T3 reads as Audit Logging but OJ text does not mention logging.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 21(2)(j) — mfa + secured comms + emergency comms

nodes.label: NIS2 ↔ CRA Pair Analysis (Complementary)
nodes.rationale: NIS2 is explicit MFA/continuous-authentication source; CRA is broader and permissive. Product can support entity's NIS2 duties but CRA clause alone does not impose same MFA threshold.

nodes.label: NIS2 ↔ DORA Pair Analysis (Complementary)
nodes.rationale: Both regulate authentication; NIS2 is risk-anchored, DORA is strong-authentication-anchored. Financial entity within retained NIS2 scope can satisfy both with one architectural design.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28(3)(b) — Processor Confidentiality
nodes.rationale: Requires processor contract to ensure authorised persons committed to confidentiality or under statutory obligation. No explicit MFA mandate.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(j) — MFA/Continuous Auth + Secured Comms
nodes.rationale: Explicit MFA or continuous authentication solutions, secured voice/video/text communications and secured emergency communication systems, where appropriate. The explicit MFA source in the EU regulatory landscape.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 21(2)(j) — mfa/continuous auth + secured comms

nodes.label: DORA Art. 5(2) — Management body responsibility
nodes.rationale: Top-of-pyramid governance rule: management body shall define, approve, oversee and be responsible for implementation of all arrangements related to ICT risk management framework. Establishes personal liability.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 5 — Management Body Responsibilities
nodes.rationale: The article under analysis. Art. 5(2) establishes the four-verb coordination (define/approve/oversee/be responsible) for the ICT risk management framework. Art. 5(4) requires management body training commensurate to ICT risk.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-05.4: Data Lifecycle — Portability/Access
nodes.rationale: Data lifecycle portability and access sub-domain covering structured electronic format delivery and data portability.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 6(1): Lawfulness Bases
nodes.rationale: Six alternative lawfulness bases: consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public interest, legitimate interests. Each carries specific necessity qualifiers.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(2) — Accountability / Demonstrability
nodes.rationale: Controller responsible for and able to demonstrate compliance with Art. 5(1) principles. Ex-post demonstration standard referenced throughout all SRs. Foundation for SO-GDPR-027.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 37: DPO Designation
nodes.rationale: Mandatory DPO where processing is by public authority, core activities involve large-scale systematic monitoring, or large-scale special-category/criminal-conviction data.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 6 Security Rules Document
nodes.rationale: Per-article split of Security Objectives and Security Rules for GDPR Art. 6, covering lawfulness bases, sub-processor authorisation, DPIA content, and consent.

nodes.label: Req 3.4: Two-layer default posture high-level requirement
nodes.rationale: Volere requirement derived from SO-D-03.4.HL; MUST priority, TEST verification. Two-layer default posture with explicit layer hand-offs at controller-data-side and product-configuration-side interface.
nodes.norm_label: req 3.4: two-layer default posture high-level requirement

nodes.label: Req 3.4.1: Data-centric by-default on processing systems
nodes.rationale: Four Art. 25(2) dimensions minimised independently and AND-coordinated per EDPB Guidelines 04/2019. Opt-in gate closes accessibility dimension. MUST priority, TEST verification.
nodes.norm_label: req 3.4.1: data-centric by-default on processing systems

nodes.label: Req 3.4.2: Product-centric secure-by-default configuration
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part I (2)(b)+(c) multi-leg product default: secure-by-default + reset + tailor-made carve-out + auto-update default + opt-out + postponement. MUST priority, TEST verification.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(2) — Five-Event Risk Enumeration
nodes.rationale: Accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure, or access to personal data transmitted, stored or otherwise processed.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(2): Accountability principle
nodes.rationale: Controller must be able to demonstrate compliance; referenced as the ex-post demonstration anchor in nearly all SRs.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5 Security Rules (D-03.1)
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering the six Art. 5(1) principles operationalised through SRs 001-030, spanning CIA, pseudonymisation, accuracy, breach response, minimisation, lawfulness, retention, and erasure.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 7: Conditions for Consent
nodes.rationale: Demonstrability (7(1)), unbundling (7(2)), withdrawal (7(3)), and non-conditionality (7(4)) requirements for valid consent.

nodes.label: CRD Art. 91: Fit-and-Proper Requirements
nodes.rationale: Co-exists with Art. 5(4) management-body training and Art. 5(2) governance obligations. Provides the personal-capacity threshold framework.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split generated from 01_SecurityObjectives.md and 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md covering DORA Chapter II Section II operational resilience architecture

nodes.label: DORA Art. 5(2): Management Body Accountability
nodes.rationale: Four-verb coordination: define, approve, oversee, be responsible for all ICT risk management arrangements. Accountability link for evidence trail to competent authorities.

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-059: Third-Country Legal-Request Recognition Filter
nodes.rationale: Art. 48 filter: third-country judgments requiring transfer/disclosure recognised only via international agreement (e.g. MLAT). Canonical example: CLOUD Act conflict. Mapped to GV.OC-03 and GV.SC-03.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 4 Security Rules (D-03.1)
nodes.rationale: Per-article split of SecurityObjectives and SecurityRules for GDPR Art. 4, covering consent, special categories, processor due diligence, pseudonymisation, DPIA, cross-border transfers, BCRs, and joint controllership.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 49 Security Rules (D-03.1)
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering Art. 49 derogations, child/transfer consent, and third-country legal-request recognition filter.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 8: Child Consent
nodes.rationale: Age threshold (default 16, MS may lower to 13) and reasonable verification of parental responsibility for information-society services.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 9: Special Categories
nodes.rationale: Prohibition on processing nine special categories unless one of ten Art. 9(2) exceptions applies. Explicit consent (9(2)(a)) is stronger than Art. 4(11) specific consent.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 49: Transfer Derogations
nodes.rationale: Seven disjunctive derogation grounds plus catch-all for transfers in absence of adequacy and Art. 46 safeguards. Explicit consent (49(1)(a)) requires risk-informed acknowledgement.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4)(d) — Strong authentication and key protection
nodes.rationale: Part of eight-item control list in Art. 9(4)(a)-(h). Art. 15 ESAs RTS mandate expected to specify 'relevant standards'.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 9(4)(d) — strong authentication and key protection

nodes.label: DORA Art. 15 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split generated from 01_SecurityObjectives.md and 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md. Contains SR-DORA-001, 002, 003, 006, 007.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5 — Principles of Processing
nodes.rationale: Six principles including transparency (5(1)(a)), data minimisation (5(1)(c)), accuracy (5(1)(d)), integrity and confidentiality (5(1)(f)), and accountability (5(2)).

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 4(5) — Pseudonymisation Definition
nodes.rationale: Processing such that data can no longer be attributed without additional information kept separately under appropriate measures.

nodes.label: CRA-CL129: Annex I Part I (1) chapeau
nodes.rationale: Appropriate level of cybersecurity based on risks across life cycle. Propagates qualifier into all 13 sub-points.
nodes.norm_label: cra-cl129: annex i part i (1) chapeau

nodes.label: CRA-CL134: Annex I Part I (2)(e) confidentiality + encryption
nodes.rationale: Stored, transmitted, or otherwise processed data protected in confidentiality by state-of-the-art mechanisms.
nodes.norm_label: cra-cl134: annex i part i (2)(e) confidentiality + encryption

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 21(2): Parallel Baseline Obligations for NSIEs
nodes.norm_label: nis 2 art. 21(2): parallel baseline obligations for nsies

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 29 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering instruction-bound processing and confidentiality undertakings for authorised personnel

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5 Compliance Requirements (D-03.3)
nodes.rationale: Comprehensive mapping of GDPR security requirements (SR-GDPR-007 through SR-GDPR-022) to NIST CSF 2.0 subcategories, covering periodic testing, DPIA review, identity verification, instruction-bound processing, privacy-by-default, breach detection/notification/containment, and downstream cascade obligations.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 6(1): ICT Risk Management Framework Obligation
nodes.rationale: Requires sound, comprehensive, well-documented framework enabling quick, efficient, comprehensive ICT risk addressing. Top-of-stack governance artefact.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 6(1): ict risk management framework obligation

nodes.label: DORA Art. 6(4): Control Function Independence
nodes.rationale: Assigns ICT risk management/oversight to control function with appropriate independence per 3LoD or alternative model.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 8(2): ICT Asset Identification and Dependencies
nodes.rationale: Identify ICT-supported business functions, ICT assets, third-party provider assets, and dependencies. Note: OJ-corrective audit flagged Art. 7(2)→Art. 8(2) misattribution in source.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 8(2): ict asset identification and dependencies

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-061: Essence Disclosure of Joint-Controller Arrangement
nodes.rationale: Art. 26(2) requires essence of joint-controller arrangement made available to data subject. Mapped to NIST GV.PO-01 and GV.OV-03. Sub-domain D-09.2.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-061: essence disclosure of joint-controller arrangement

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-06.3: Supply Chain
nodes.rationale: Supply chain sub-domain covering processor contracts, auditability, and joint-controller contractual arrangements.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-09.2: Governance — Documentation
nodes.rationale: Governance documentation sub-domain covering joint-controller arrangements, DPIA review, and organisational policy.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-01.3: Data Protection (in use / crypto)
nodes.norm_label: sub-domain d-01.3: data protection (in use / crypto)

nodes.label: DORA Article 5: Management body responsibilities
nodes.rationale: Art. 5(2) management body oversight and accountability; Art. 5(4) management-body training. Provides the accountability link for all SR evidence trails.

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RM-06: Standardised Risk Calculation Method
nodes.rationale: Anchors the standardised risk-calibration methodology for the Art. 21(1) chapeau: documented method to calculate, document, categorise and prioritise risks against four proportionality factors.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.rm-06: standardised risk calculation method

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.SC-02: Supplier Risk Management Process
nodes.rationale: Most frequently referenced NIST CSF subcategory (6 SRs). Anchors the assessment discipline for supplier identification, prioritisation, and evaluation across the supply-chain security domain.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.sc-02: supplier risk management process

nodes.label: ISO 22301 (Business Continuity Management Systems)
nodes.rationale: Recognised methodological anchor for the business continuity dimension of the Art. 21(2)(c) BC/DR/CM triad.

nodes.label: ISO 22361 (Crisis Management)
nodes.rationale: Recognised methodological anchor for the crisis management dimension of the Art. 21(2)(c) BC/DR/CM triad.

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.PS-02: Software Maintenance, Replacement, and Removal
nodes.rationale: Anchors the lifecycle consequence dimension: development-time decisions determine maintenance burden. Closes the loop between external vulnerability disclosure and internal remediation.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ps-02: software maintenance, replacement, and removal

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.PS-06: Secure Software Development Practices
nodes.rationale: Anchors the design-time control set (threat modelling, secure coding, code review, security testing) for the NIS lifecycle SRs (acquisition, development).
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ps-06: secure software development practices

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) — Data Minimisation
nodes.rationale: Personal data adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary in relation to the purposes.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 6(4) — Compatibility Test
nodes.rationale: Five factors for further processing beyond original purposes: link, context, nature, consequences, safeguards.

nodes.label: NIS2 Article 22 (Cooperation Group Coordinated Assessments)
nodes.rationale: Institutional counterpart to Art. 21(2)(d) supply-chain security. Enables Cooperation Group to carry out coordinated assessments of critical ICT supply chains, taking into account technical and non-technical risk factors. Entity obligation triggered only when assessment exists.

nodes.label: CER Directive (EU) 2022/2557
nodes.rationale: Parallel regulation reinforcing operational-continuity objective. Art. 12 (emergency communication) and Art. 13 (crisis management) provide cross-regulation harmonisation context for NIS2 BC/DR/CM obligations.

nodes.label: NIS2 Directive Article 21 (Risk Management Measures)
nodes.rationale: The parent regulatory provision from which all SRs in this fragment derive. Contains the chapeau (Art. 21(1)), sub-points (a)-(g) in Art. 21(2), supplier assessment in Art. 21(3), and corrective measures in Art. 21(4).

nodes.label: NIS2 Recital 56 (Proportionality Factors)
nodes.rationale: Operationalises the Art. 21(1) appropriate-and-proportionate qualifier with four named factors: degree of exposure, entity size, likelihood/severity of incidents, societal and economic impact. Governs methodology discretion across all SRs.

nodes.label: CRA-CL143: Annex I Part II (1) SBOM + vulnerability identification
nodes.rationale: Identify and document vulnerabilities and components, including SBOM in commonly used machine-readable format covering top-level dependencies.
nodes.norm_label: cra-cl143: annex i part ii (1) sbom + vulnerability identification

nodes.label: CRA (EU) 2024/2847
nodes.rationale: Cyber Resilience Act providing upstream vulnerability-handling and secure-by-default flows feeding DORA entities.

nodes.label: GDPR (EU) 2016/679
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation interface for personal-data processing, staff awareness duties, and breach notification.

nodes.label: 01_SecurityObjectives.md (parent aggregate index)
nodes.rationale: The parent document from which this per-article split was generated. Remains the authoritative aggregate index.

nodes.label: 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md (parent aggregate index)
nodes.rationale: The parent document from which this per-article split was generated. Remains the authoritative aggregate index.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(1)(d) — Accuracy Principle
nodes.rationale: Requires personal data to be accurate and kept up to date; every reasonable step to erase/rectify inaccurate data without delay. Foundation for SR-GDPR-005, 006.

nodes.label: SO-CRA-051: Vulnerability disclosure and coordinated response
nodes.rationale: Linked objective for SR-CRA-075, 076 — CVD policy and cessation notification.
nodes.norm_label: so-cra-051: vulnerability disclosure and coordinated response

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 39(1) — DPO Tasks
nodes.rationale: Five mandatory tasks: inform/advise, monitor compliance, DPIA advice, cooperate with authority, contact point.

nodes.label: DORA Article 6: ICT risk management framework
nodes.rationale: Chapeau obligation requiring sound, comprehensive, well-documented ICT risk management framework. Art. 6(1) sets top-of-stack governance; Art. 6(4) requires 3LoD independence; Art. 6(8) chapeau links to all downstream obligations.
nodes.norm_label: dora article 6: ict risk management framework

nodes.label: DORA Article 9: Protection and prevention
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(2) cross-state CIA+A protection; Art. 9(4)(a)-(h) eight mandatory control domains including information security policy, network management, access control, authentication, change management, patch management.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 GV.OC-01: Organizational mission informs risk management
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 gv.oc-01: organizational mission informs risk management

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 GV.RM-02: Risk roles and responsibilities established
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 gv.rm-02: risk roles and responsibilities established

nodes.label: CRA Annex I Part I (1) — Chapeau
nodes.rationale: Requires appropriate level of cybersecurity based on risks across life cycle. Referenced as CRA-CL129. D-03.1 CL7-1 Instance 1 notes same pattern as CRA Annex I Part I (1) chapeau 'appropriate'.
nodes.norm_label: cra annex i part i (1) — chapeau

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(8) — Support Period Determination
nodes.rationale: Sentence 1: handle vulnerabilities effectively during support period. Sentence 2: 8-factor determination. Sentence 3: 5-year minimum. Sentence 5: documentation of factors. Sentence 6: CVD policy.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 15 RTS — Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1774
nodes.rationale: Adopted by Commission 31 May 2024. Supplements DORA with RTS for Art. 15(a)–(g). Resolves many S3 instances flagged in D-03.1 analysis. Deadline was 17 January 2024.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 6(1) — ICT Risk Management Framework
nodes.rationale: The overarching framework referenced by Art. 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14. Art. 6(5) requires a report on review of the framework. Art. 6(8) sets the DOR strategy.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 6(1) — ict risk management framework

nodes.label: DORA-D08 — ICT-Related Incident
nodes.rationale: S3 regress. Cross-referenced to NIS 2 Art. 6(6). Referenced in CL9-2, CL9-4, CL10-1, CL10-2, CL11-1, CL11-2, CL11-3, CL12-4, CL13-1, CL14-1, CL16-1.

nodes.label: DORA-D10 — Major ICT-Related Incident
nodes.rationale: S3 — 'high adverse impact'. Referenced in CL11-4, CL13-1, CL14-1, CL16-1, CL21-1.

nodes.label: DORA-D22 — Critical or Important Function
nodes.rationale: S3 tautological definition. Referenced in CL8-3, CL9-2, CL9-4, CL11-1, CL11-2, CL11-3, CL12-3, CL12-4, CL13-1, CL13-2, CL16-2. The 'considered critical' threshold in Art. 8(4) propagates from this tautology.

nodes.label: DORA-D60 — Microenterprise
nodes.rationale: S2 — 'fewer than 10 persons' per pilot §2.12. Carve-out in CL8-2, CL11-2, CL11-3, CL11-4, CL12-2, CL13-1, CL13-2, CL16-1, CL16-2.

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 6(1) — Network and Information System
nodes.rationale: Definitional anchor for DORA Art. 3(2). Covers 'ICT systems'; 'protocols' and 'tools' are open-ended. Referenced in CL7-1, CL9-1, CL9-3, CL9-4, CL10-2, CL12-1, CL16-2.
nodes.norm_label: nis 2 art. 6(1) — network and information system

nodes.label: CL10-1 — Art. 10(1) Detection Mechanisms
nodes.rationale: Requires mechanisms to promptly detect anomalous activities including ICT network performance issues and ICT-related incidents, and to identify potential material single points of failure. Detection mechanisms must be regularly tested per Art. 25.

nodes.label: CL10-2 — Art. 10(2)+(3) Multi-Layer Controls
nodes.rationale: Requires multiple layers of control, alert thresholds and criteria to trigger incident response, automatic alert mechanisms, and sufficient resources for monitoring user activity and ICT anomalies.

nodes.label: CL11-1 — Art. 11(1)+(2) BCP + 5 Objectives
nodes.rationale: Requires a comprehensive ICT business continuity policy with five cumulative objectives: continuity of CIFs, quick response to incidents, activation without delay, impact estimation, and communication/crisis management.

nodes.label: CL11-2 — Art. 11(3)+(4)+(5) Recovery + BIA
nodes.rationale: Requires ICT response and recovery plans (with independent internal audit for non-microenterprises), BCP for outsourced CIFs, and business impact analysis using quantitative and qualitative criteria.

nodes.label: CL11-3 — Art. 11(6)–(9) BCP Testing + Crisis Mgmt
nodes.rationale: Requires at-least-yearly testing of BCPs and recovery plans, cyber-attack and switchover scenarios for non-microenterprises, crisis management function, readily accessible records, and CSD reporting.
nodes.norm_label: cl11-3 — art. 11(6)–(9) bcp testing + crisis mgmt

nodes.label: CL11-4 — Art. 11(10)+(11) Cost Reporting + ESA Guidelines
nodes.rationale: Non-microenterprises must report aggregated annual costs and losses from major ICT-related incidents upon CA request. ESAs to develop common guidelines by 17 July 2024.
nodes.norm_label: cl11-4 — art. 11(10)+(11) cost reporting + esa guidelines

nodes.label: CL12-1 — Art. 12(1)+(2) Backup Policies
nodes.rationale: Requires backup policies specifying scope and minimum frequency based on criticality/confidentiality, restoration procedures, and backup systems that do not jeopardise security or data CIA.

nodes.label: CL12-2 — Art. 12(3)+(4) Restoration + Redundant Capacities
nodes.rationale: Requires physically and logically segregated restoration systems, timely restoration, and redundant ICT capacities for non-microenterprises (microenterprises assess need based on risk profile).

nodes.label: CL12-3 — Art. 12(5) CSD Secondary Processing Site
nodes.rationale: CSD-specific: maintain at least one secondary processing site at geographical distance with distinct risk profile, capable of ensuring continuity of CIFs, immediately accessible to staff.
nodes.norm_label: cl12-3 — art. 12(5) csd secondary processing site

nodes.label: CL12-4 — Art. 12(6)+(7) RTO/RPO + Data Integrity
nodes.rationale: Requires recovery time and recovery point objectives for each function considering criticality and market efficiency impact, plus multiple checks and reconciliations for data integrity.

nodes.label: CL13-1 — Art. 13(1)–(3) Threat Intel + Post-Incident Reviews
nodes.rationale: Requires capabilities to gather vulnerability/cyber-threat information, post-incident reviews after major ICT-related incidents, and continuous incorporation of lessons into ICT risk assessment.
nodes.norm_label: cl13-1 — art. 13(1)–(3) threat intel + post-incident reviews

nodes.label: CL13-2 — Art. 13(4)–(7) Effectiveness + Training + Tech
nodes.rationale: Requires monitoring effectiveness of DOR strategy, yearly senior ICT staff reporting to management body, compulsory ICT security awareness training, and continuous monitoring of technological developments (non-microenterprises).

nodes.label: CL14-1 — Art. 14(1) Crisis Communication Plans
nodes.rationale: Requires crisis communication plans enabling responsible disclosure of major ICT-related incidents or vulnerabilities to clients, counterparts, and the public.

nodes.label: CL15-1 — Art. 15 ESAs RTS Mandate
nodes.rationale: Mandates ESAs (Joint Committee + ENISA) to develop common draft RTS for 7 subject areas (Art. 9(2), 9(4)(c), 10(1), 10(2), 11(1), 11(3), 11(6), 6(5)). Deadline 17 Jan 2024. Adopted as Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1774.

nodes.label: CL16-1 — Art. 16(1)+(2) Simplified Framework Scope
nodes.rationale: Exempts five entity categories (small investment firms, exempted PIs, CRD-exempted, EMD-exempted, small IORPs) from Art. 5-15. Requires documented and periodically reviewed ICT risk management framework with continuous improvement.

nodes.label: CL16-2 — Art. 16(1)(a)–(h) Simplified Obligations
nodes.rationale: Structurally parallel to Art. 9(4) hinge but at lower granularity. Omits access control, change management, and patches as standalone control families. Deliberate regulatory choice: small entities exempted from most operationally demanding controls.

nodes.label: CL21-1 — Art. 21(1)+(2) Single EU Hub Feasibility
nodes.rationale: Mandates ESAs to prepare joint report assessing feasibility of a single EU Hub for major ICT-related incident reporting. Regulator-internal scope, not directly entity-facing.
nodes.norm_label: cl21-1 — art. 21(1)+(2) single eu hub feasibility

nodes.label: CL7-1 — Art. 7 ICT Systems Baseline
nodes.rationale: Establishes the baseline requirement for financial entities to use and maintain updated ICT systems, protocols and tools that are appropriate, reliable, sufficiently capacitated, and technologically resilient.

nodes.label: CL8-1 — Art. 8(1)+(2) Identification
nodes.rationale: Requires identification, classification and documentation of all ICT-supported business functions, information assets, ICT assets, and continuous identification of ICT risk sources including bidirectional exposure to/from other financial entities.

nodes.label: CL8-2 — Art. 8(3)+(7) Major-Change + Legacy ICT
nodes.rationale: Applies to non-microenterprises. Requires risk assessment upon each major change and specific ICT risk assessment on all legacy ICT systems at least yearly.

nodes.label: CL8-3 — Art. 8(4)+(5)+(6) Critical-Asset Mapping
nodes.rationale: Requires mapping of critical assets, links and interdependencies, identification of TPP interconnections supporting critical or important functions, and periodic inventory updates.

nodes.label: CL9-2 — Art. 9(2) Design/Procure/Implement
nodes.rationale: Requires design, procurement and implementation of ICT security policies, procedures, protocols and tools ensuring resilience, continuity, availability and data security (availability, authenticity, integrity, confidentiality) at rest, in use, or in transit.

nodes.label: CL9-3 — Art. 9(3)(a)–(d) Data Security Baseline
nodes.rationale: Four cumulative data-security objectives: secure transfer, minimise corruption/loss/unauthorised access, prevent availability/authenticity/integrity/confidentiality breaches, protect from data management risks.

nodes.label: CL9-4 — Art. 9(4)(a)–(f) THE HINGE
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(4) is identified as the operational core of DORA, establishing six mandatory control families: info-security policy, network/infrastructure, access control, authentication+encryption, change management, patches/updates. The 6-way AND in 9(4)(e) and hendiadys in 9(4)(f) are operationally consequential.

nodes.label: T3-vs-Text Gaps (§5)
nodes.rationale: Catalogues inconsistencies between v0.1 T3 mapping (C14-C17, C26-C28) and OJ text. Major distortions: C14 imposed need-to-know/least-privilege not in OJ; C16 imposed MFA not in OJ; C28 imposed role-specific training not in OJ. T3 omitted 19 clauses added in v0.2.

nodes.label: SO-CRA-048: User and integrator information and instructions
nodes.rationale: Linked objective for SR-CRA-071, 107 — Annex II §8 detailed instructions package.
nodes.norm_label: so-cra-048: user and integrator information and instructions

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 15 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split generated from 01_SecurityObjectives.md and 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md covering access rights, data portability, identity verification, cascade notification, and joint-controller essence disclosure.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 26 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering joint-controller arrangements, role allocation, essence disclosure, and minimised identity verification data collection.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(1): Security of processing measures
nodes.rationale: Four-element list (pseudonymisation/encryption, CIA+R, restoration, testing); referenced by SR-035, SR-039, SR-040.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 32(1): security of processing measures

nodes.label: NIST CSF DE.CM-09 – Compute Monitoring
nodes.rationale: Computing hardware, software, runtime environments, data monitored. Extends coverage to compute layer (endpoints, servers, file integrity).

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OC-01 – Mission Alignment
nodes.rationale: Organizational mission understood and informs cybersecurity risk management. Maps the 'quickly, efficiently, comprehensively' adverb triplet to mission-driven prioritisation.

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OC-03 – Legal/Regulatory Alignment
nodes.rationale: Legal, regulatory, contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity understood and managed. Closes the multi-regulation alignment loop (GDPR, NIS2, CRA, contractual).

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.PO-01 – Cybersecurity Policy
nodes.rationale: Organizational cybersecurity policy established, communicated, enforced. Anchors the policy-substrate dimension ensuring framework is enforceable rather than aspirational. Shared by both SR-DORA-027 and SR-DORA-031.

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RM-02 – Risk Role Communication
nodes.rationale: Risk roles, responsibilities, authorities, accountabilities established and communicated. Ensures role allocation is exercisable rather than theoretical.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.rm-02 – risk role communication

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RR-02 – Risk Roles and Responsibilities
nodes.rationale: Roles, responsibilities, authorities, accountabilities for cybersecurity risk management established, communicated, understood, enforced. Anchors structural separation between 3LoD lines.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.rr-02 – risk roles and responsibilities

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.AM-02 – Software/Services Inventory
nodes.rationale: Inventories of software, services, systems maintained. Software/services/systems layer with own change-detection cadence.

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.AM-03 – Data Inventory
nodes.rationale: Inventories of data and corresponding metadata maintained. Data layer with own lifecycle and ownership chain.

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.AM-05 – Asset Prioritisation
nodes.rationale: Assets prioritized based on classification, criticality, resources, mission impact. Closes the prioritisation loop ensuring inventory is priority-ordered substrate for downstream controls.

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AT-01 – User Cybersecurity Training
nodes.rationale: All users informed and trained on cybersecurity topics (phishing, social engineering). Anchors the baseline awareness layer closing the human-factor gap.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.at-01 – user cybersecurity training

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AT-02 – Workforce Role Understanding
nodes.rationale: All workforce members understand roles and responsibilities in achieving cybersecurity objectives. Layers role-specific depth for security-critical functions.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.at-02 – workforce role understanding

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.DS-12 – Data Management
nodes.rationale: Data managed consistent with risk strategy to protect CIA. Translates the four-way protection objective into risk-strategy-aligned data-governance regime.

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.PS-04 – Log Records
nodes.rationale: Log records generated and made available for continuous monitoring and analysis. Closes the evidentiary loop for incident-response consumption under Art. 17.

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.PS-06 – Secure SDLC
nodes.rationale: Secure software development practices integrated and monitored throughout SDLC. Closes the tested/assessed/approved stages to secure-development practices.

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.AM-01 — Hardware Inventory
nodes.rationale: CRA-specific anchor. Type/batch/serial marking backing the SBOM-correlated identity register.

nodes.label: AI Act (EU) 2024/1689
nodes.rationale: Cross-referenced for Art. 4(2) provider-deployer literacy duties (training intersection), Art. 9 risk-management duty (framework intersection), Art. 9(2) post-market-monitoring (monitoring intersection).

nodes.label: DORA Art. 13(6) – ICT Security Awareness Training
nodes.rationale: Requires ICT security awareness programmes and digital operational resilience training as compulsory modules, with complexity commensurate to staff function remit.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 13(6) – ict security awareness training

nodes.label: DORA Art. 6(1) – ICT Risk Management Framework
nodes.rationale: Requires sound, comprehensive, well-documented ICT risk management framework enabling quick, efficient, comprehensive ICT risk addressing. Art. 6(2) specifies strategies, policies, procedures, protocols, tools.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 6(1) – ict risk management framework

nodes.label: DORA Art. 6(4) – Control Function Independence
nodes.rationale: Requires assignment of ICT risk management/oversight to a control function with appropriate independence per three-lines-of-defence or alternative internal risk management model.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 7(1) – Asset Identification and Classification
nodes.rationale: Requires identification, classification, adequate documentation of all ICT-supported business functions, roles, information assets, ICT assets, and their dependencies in relation to ICT risk.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 7(1) – asset identification and classification

nodes.label: DORA Art. 8(1) – Continuous Monitoring and Control
nodes.rationale: Requires continuous monitoring and control of security and functioning of ICT systems, minimising ICT risk impact through appropriate security tools, policies, procedures.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 8(1) – continuous monitoring and control

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4)(a) – Information Security Policy
nodes.rationale: Requires development and documentation of information security policy defining rules to protect availability, authenticity, integrity, confidentiality of data, information assets, ICT assets including customer assets.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4)(e) – ICT Change Management
nodes.rationale: Requires documented policies, procedures, controls for ICT change management based on risk-assessment approach; all changes recorded, tested, assessed, approved, implemented, verified in controlled manner.

nodes.label: CL10-3 — Art. 10(4) DRSP Additional
nodes.rationale: Sector-specific obligation for Data Reporting Service Providers to effectively check trade reports for completeness, identify omissions and obvious errors, and request re-transmission.

nodes.label: CL14-2 — Art. 14(2)+(3) Communication Policies + Spokesperson
nodes.rationale: Requires internal and external communication policies differentiating staff involved in ICT risk management from those needing information, and at least one person tasked with public and media function.

nodes.label: CL9-1 — Art. 9(1) Continuous Monitoring
nodes.rationale: Requires continuous monitoring and control of security and functioning of ICT systems, with minimisation of ICT risk impact through appropriate security tools, policies and procedures.

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.PO-02 — Cybersecurity Processes and Procedures Established
nodes.rationale: Controls documented consent-flow process: separation of consent UIs, plain-language labelling, prohibition of conditioning. Referenced by SR-GDPR-052.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.po-02 — cybersecurity processes and procedures established

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33(1): 72-Hour Breach Notification Obligation
nodes.rationale: Requires the controller to notify the supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach, unless unlikely to result in risk to rights and freedoms of natural persons.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 9(2)(a) — Explicit Consent for Special Categories
nodes.rationale: Lifts Art. 9(1) prohibition via explicit consent (stronger than Art. 4(11) specific). EDPB 05/2020 §3.4: requires express statement, not bundled. Referenced by SR-GDPR-053.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 9(2)(a) — explicit consent for special categories

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 44 — General Cross-Border Transfer Principle
nodes.rationale: Umbrella principle: transfers only if Chapter V conditions met and GDPR protection level not undermined. Referenced by SR-GDPR-055.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 44 — general cross-border transfer principle

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 45(1) — Adequacy-Based Transfer
nodes.rationale: Exempts transfers covered by Commission adequacy decision from specific authorisation. Referenced by SR-GDPR-055.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 45(3) — Periodic Review of Adequacy
nodes.rationale: Commission must review adequacy at least every 4 years; may amend, suspend, or repeal. Referenced by SR-GDPR-055.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 45(3) — periodic review of adequacy

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 47(2) — BCR Mandatory Content (14 Items)
nodes.rationale: Closed list of 14 mandatory BCR content items; all must be present for approval. Referenced by SR-GDPR-058.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 47(2) — bcr mandatory content (14 items)

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 49(1)(a) — Explicit Transfer Consent
nodes.rationale: Derogation requiring explicit consent after being informed of transfer risks. Referenced by SR-GDPR-054 and SR-GDPR-057.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 4(7) — Controller Definition
nodes.rationale: Defines controller as entity determining purposes and means, alone or jointly. Referenced by SR-GDPR-060.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 7(1) — Demonstrability of Consent
nodes.rationale: Shifts evidentiary burden onto controller to demonstrate data subject consent. Referenced by SR-GDPR-051.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 7(2) — Clearly Distinguishable Consent Request
nodes.rationale: Requires consent request to be clearly distinguishable from other matters in written declarations. Referenced by SR-GDPR-052.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 7(2) — clearly distinguishable consent request

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 7(3) — Right to Withdraw Consent
nodes.rationale: Withdrawal must be as easy as giving consent; controller must cease processing upon withdrawal. Referenced by SR-GDPR-051.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 7(3) — right to withdraw consent

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 7(4) — No Conditioning on Consent
nodes.rationale: Contract performance must not be conditional on consent for processing not necessary to the contract. Referenced by SR-GDPR-052.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 7(4) — no conditioning on consent

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 8(1) — Age Threshold for Child Consent
nodes.rationale: Default age 16, Member States may lower to 13. Governs only consent, not other Art. 6 bases. Referenced by SR-GDPR-054.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 8(1) — age threshold for child consent

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 8(2) — Reasonable Verification of Parental Responsibility
nodes.rationale: Process obligation (not outcome guarantee) to verify parental responsibility using available technology. Referenced by SR-GDPR-054.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 8(2) — reasonable verification of parental responsibility

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OC-03 — Legal/Regulatory Requirements Understood and Managed
nodes.rationale: Broad regulatory-compliance frame used across SR-GDPR-051, 054, 055, 057. Captures the controller's obligation to understand and manage legal-basis conditions.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.oc-03 — legal/regulatory requirements understood and managed

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RR-02 — Roles/Responsibilities/Accountabilities Established
nodes.rationale: Controls explicit allocation of joint-controller roles. Referenced by SR-GDPR-060.

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.SC-01 — SCRM Program/Strategy Established
nodes.rationale: Group-level SCRM programme within which BCRs sit. Referenced by SR-GDPR-058.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.sc-01 — scrm program/strategy established

nodes.label: D-04.1 Incident Detection & Triage (Unified View)
nodes.author: SubDomains merge (Executor sub-agent)
nodes.rationale: Unified view merging sub-domain definition, domain analysis, deep analysis, and ambiguity sections. Generated by reorg_by_domain_md.py. Covers cross-regulation analysis of detection-and-triage across GDPR, NIS2, CRA, DORA with 6 pairwise verifications (3 COMPLEMENTARY + 3 DIFFERENT-PERSPECTIVE, 0 emergent tensions).

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OV-02: Strategy Review
nodes.rationale: Organizational cybersecurity risk management strategy is reviewed and adjusted to address changes in risk landscape. Shared across SR-DORA-005 and SR-DORA-008 as the strategic-review anchor.

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AA-06: Physical and Logical Access Limitation
nodes.rationale: Access to physical and logical assets limited to authorized users, services, and hardware. Enforces the physical-and-logical twin layer preventing physical-bypass of logical controls.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.aa-06: physical and logical access limitation

nodes.label: DORA Art. 24(1): Resilience Testing Programme
nodes.rationale: Establish, maintain and review sound and comprehensive digital operational resilience testing programme. Chapter IV dedicated to testing with Art. 26 TLPT and Art. 27 advanced testing.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4): Protection Controls (8 Domains)
nodes.rationale: Eight mandatory control domains including network management (b), access control (c), change management (e), and patch governance (f). Anchors the structural dimension of ICT security controls.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13: Vulnerability Handling and Secure Updates
nodes.rationale: Downstream fact-feeding layer for product vendors feeding DORA entities. Supplies vulnerability handling, secure-by-default, and secure-update flows.
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 13: vulnerability handling and secure updates

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.SC-02: Supply chain risk management process
nodes.rationale: Suppliers and other third parties are known, prioritized, and assessed using a cybersecurity supply chain risk management process. Recurring mapping across SR-CRA-061, SR-CRA-062, SR-CRA-008, SR-CRA-050.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.sc-02: supply chain risk management process

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.SC-04: Supplier contractual obligation assessment
nodes.rationale: Suppliers and other third parties are routinely assessed using audits, test results, or other forms of evaluation to confirm they are meeting their contractual obligations. Recurring mapping across SR-CRA-061, SR-CRA-062, SR-CRA-070, SR-CRA-015.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.sc-04: supplier contractual obligation assessment

nodes.label: Manufacturer-Equivalent Status (CRA Arts. 21/22)
nodes.rationale: Accountability transfer mechanism: importer/distributor (Art. 21) or third-party modifier (Art. 22) becomes manufacturer of record upon own-name placement or substantial modification, assuming Arts. 13 and 14 obligations.

nodes.label: Substantial Modification (CRA Art. 3(30))
nodes.rationale: Defined as a modification after market placement where the manufacturer has not considered it in conformity assessment, affecting Annex I compliance OR modifying intended purpose. Central trigger concept across Arts. 21, 22, and 13(10).

nodes.label: SO-CRA-043: Third-party substantial modification = manufacturer (part or whole)
nodes.rationale: Security objective: natural/legal person other than manufacturer/importer/distributor carrying out substantial modification is considered manufacturer for affected part or whole product.
nodes.norm_label: so-cra-043: third-party substantial modification = manufacturer (part or whole)

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-03.3: Access Control
nodes.rationale: Access control sub-domain. Locus for least-privilege physical and logical access governance.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-062: Third-party substantial modification triggers manufacturer status
nodes.rationale: Closes a critical loophole: an integrator or third-party modifier not in the supply chain contract cannot escape manufacturer obligations by literal definitional exclusion. Mapped to GV.SC-02 and GV.SC-04.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-062: third-party substantial modification triggers manufacturer status

nodes.label: CRA Art. 3 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split generated from 01_SecurityObjectives.md and 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md; covers SOs and SRs spanning incident response, supply chain, data minimisation, OSS stewardship, and manufacturer-equivalent triggers.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 21 — Security Objectives & Security Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering cross-state CIA+A protection, cryptographic key protection, risk identification, network management, patch governance, resilience testing, and access control.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 21 — security objectives & security rules

nodes.label: Business Continuity, Backup, Recovery, and Crisis Triad
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(c) requires BC/DR/CM as a coherent triad; the 'such as' opens an illustrative list inside an AND of business continuity and crisis management. Mapped to NIST CSF RC.RP-04 and PR.DS-11.
nodes.norm_label: business continuity, backup, recovery, and crisis triad

nodes.label: Direct Supplier and Service-Provider Security by Contract
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(d) supply chain security mandate. The 'direct' scope-limiter is the single most consequential scope-limiting term in Chapter IV, determining whether the obligation reaches Tier-1 contractual, n-hop technically integrated, or operationally dependent counterparties.
nodes.norm_label: direct supplier and service-provider security by contract

nodes.label: Security-Related Contractual Aspects of Supplier Relationships
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(d) second clause on security-related aspects of supplier relationships. The 'security-related' qualifier admits cybersecurity-only, information-security broader, and any-security-implication readings; R3 chosen per literal text.
nodes.norm_label: security-related contractual aspects of supplier relationships

nodes.label: Per-Supplier Vulnerability Intelligence for Risk Prioritisation
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(3) sentence 1 requires per-supplier vulnerability assessment. Operates as PER-SUPPLIER obligation type rather than continuous baseline. Article 6(15) vulnerability definition anchors substantive scope.
nodes.norm_label: per-supplier vulnerability intelligence for risk prioritisation

nodes.label: Supplier Product, Service, and Process Quality Assessment
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(3) sentence 1 second clause on overall quality of products and cybersecurity practices. One of three coordinated assessment objects in the Article 21(3) supplier-assessment architecture.
nodes.norm_label: supplier product, service, and process quality assessment

nodes.label: Supplier Secure-Development Procedures Assessed per Criticality
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(3) sentence 1 third assessment object. Cross-links to Art. 21(2)(e) security-in-development. The externally-assessable interpretation is chosen since the obligation is on the entity to assess rather than on the supplier to self-certify.
nodes.norm_label: supplier secure-development procedures assessed per criticality

nodes.label: Coordinated Supply-Chain Risk Assessments Integrated into Supplier Decisions
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(3) sentence 2 entity-side propagation hook for Art. 22(1) Cooperation Group coordinated assessments. The 'take into account' verb admits passive-consideration or active-integration readings; passive chosen since no specific decision mechanism is prescribed.
nodes.norm_label: coordinated supply-chain risk assessments integrated into supplier decisions

nodes.label: Security Requirements Embedded in NIS Acquisition Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(e) first clause - security in acquisition. First of three coordinated lifecycle phases. Broad-cumulative interpretation covers both procurement process and product security.
nodes.norm_label: security requirements embedded in nis acquisition lifecycle

nodes.label: Secure-by-Design Controls Integrated Across NIS Development
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(e) second clause - security in development. Applies whether in-house or outsourced. Design-time decisions determine maintenance-time residual-risk profile.
nodes.norm_label: secure-by-design controls integrated across nis development

nodes.label: Maintenance-Phase Security with Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(e) third clause - security in maintenance including vulnerability handling and disclosure. Two-distinct-activities reading chosen (internal triage + external communication). Institutional anchor for external disclosure is Art. 12(1) CSIRT.
nodes.norm_label: maintenance-phase security with coordinated vulnerability disclosure

nodes.label: Basic Cyber-Hygiene Practices Baseline
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(g) first clause. Entity-discretionary interpretation under Recital 56 proportionality since OJ does not enumerate hygiene practices. Cultural reading dominant under Recital 50.

nodes.label: Documented Risk-Analysis Methodology with Proportional Scope and Cadence
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(a) first clause - policies on risk analysis. Methodology-agnostic: OJ does not prescribe qualitative, quantitative or hybrid. Entity-discretionary hybrid reading chosen per Recital 56.
nodes.norm_label: documented risk-analysis methodology with proportional scope and cadence

nodes.label: Information-System-Security Policy Governing NIS Configuration and Operation
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(a) second clause - policies on information system security. Two-distinct-policies reading dominant (one for risk analysis, one for IS security). Broader cyber-plus-operational reading chosen per all-hazards approach.
nodes.norm_label: information-system-security policy governing nis configuration and operation

nodes.label: Policy Framework for Assessing Cybersecurity Risk-Management Measure Effectiveness
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(f) - policies and procedures to assess effectiveness. Outcome-effectiveness reading chosen (assessment object is 'cybersecurity risk-management measures' not specific controls). Structurally distinct from Art. 21(4) corrective measures.
nodes.norm_label: policy framework for assessing cybersecurity risk-management measure effectiveness

nodes.label: Scheduled Procedures Operationalising Cybersecurity Effectiveness Measurement
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(f) procedural limb. Captures the procedural half of the 'policies and procedures' AND coordination. Structurally lighter than SR-NIS2-037 because substantive ambiguity lives in the policy half.
nodes.norm_label: scheduled procedures operationalising cybersecurity effectiveness measurement

nodes.label: Risk-Calibrated Technical, Operational and Organisational Measures Baseline
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(1) sentence 1 chapeau - the meta-clause that propagates to every Art. 21(2) sub-point. Compound-qualifier reading of 'appropriate and proportionate' chosen because sentence 2 explicitly operationalises with four named factors. Dominant Berry VAG-S3 ambiguity of the Directive.
nodes.norm_label: risk-calibrated technical, operational and organisational measures baseline

nodes.label: All-Hazards Methodology Spanning Cyber, Physical and Operational Risks
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2) chapeau - meta-methodology clause converting cybersecurity-only default into all-hazards reading. Broadest inclusive reading chosen because chapeau explicitly extends to 'the physical environment of those systems'.
nodes.norm_label: all-hazards methodology spanning cyber, physical and operational risks

nodes.label: Physical-Environment Protection Ensuring NIS Substrate Resilience
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2) chapeau second clause extending all-hazards to physical environment. Structurally a carve-out flag: in-scope for Art. 21 but out-of-scope for software-compliance track. Narrow reading chosen ('of those systems' anchors to NIS).
nodes.norm_label: physical-environment protection ensuring nis substrate resilience

nodes.label: Root-Cause Corrective Measures Triggered by Non-Compliance Findings
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(4) triggered-response instrument. Trigger is entity's own finding of non-compliance. Reasonable-time reading of 'without undue delay' chosen (no numeric deadline in OJ). Root-cause-remediation reading per ISO 27001:2022 corrective-action concept.
nodes.norm_label: root-cause corrective measures triggered by non-compliance findings

nodes.label: Documented Cryptography and Encryption Governance Baseline
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(h) cryptography and where-appropriate encryption. Hierarchical AND-with-hedge: cryptography always required, encryption additionally where risk assessment indicates. Two compounding S3 ambiguities drive materially different compliance obligations.
nodes.norm_label: documented cryptography and encryption governance baseline

nodes.label: Incident Handling as a Six-Action Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(b) + Art. 6(8) six-action definition (prevent, detect, analyse, contain, respond, recover). Process reading chosen per 'actions and procedures' anchor. Operational substrate of Art. 23 reporting flow and Art. 21(2)(c) BC hook.
nodes.norm_label: incident handling as a six-action lifecycle

nodes.label: 24-Hour Derogation Notification for Trust Service Providers
nodes.rationale: Art. 23(4) paragraph 2 TSP derogation from 72h tier. Applies to eIDAS-defined trust service providers. Twin-trigger pattern identical to SR-NIS2-010. Annex I/QTSP designation reflected in ESSENTIAL_ENTITY role.
nodes.norm_label: 24-hour derogation notification for trust service providers

nodes.label: D-04.2 High-Level Requirement: Multi-Layer Containment
nodes.rationale: Volere immunity requirement. Multi-layer containment architecture with one measure catalogue per layer and explicit layer hand-offs. DORA BC arrangements are operative ceiling when both DORA and NIS2 apply. Priority MUST, verification TEST.

nodes.label: D-04.2 NIS2 Sub-Requirement: Entity-Level Contain Phase
nodes.rationale: Entity-level response plan documents 'contain' action with isolation procedures, system-segregation runbooks, blast-radius limitation. NIS2 plan hosts GDPR TOMs and CRA evidence under explicit cross-references. DORA BC absorbs NIS2 contain for financial-services subset via lex specialis.
nodes.norm_label: d-04.2 nis2 sub-requirement: entity-level contain phase

nodes.label: D-04.2 High-Level SecurityObjective: Multi-Layer Containment Architecture
nodes.rationale: Common containment-and-mitigation duty across GDPR, NIS2, CRA, DORA. Does NOT collapse four containment layers into single measure type. Engages when >=2 applicable regs target overlapping containment layers on same party. 0 emergent tensions (6 pairs verified non-SAME).
nodes.norm_label: d-04.2 high-level securityobjective: multi-layer containment architecture

nodes.label: D-04.2 NIS2 Sub-SO: Entity-Level Contain Phase
nodes.rationale: NIS2 containment is entity-level incident-handling 'contain' phase within 6-action lifecycle. Entity response plan is the procedural wrapper hosting GDPR TOMs and CRA product-resilience evidence. Appropriate-and-proportionate qualifier operationalises containment depth.
nodes.norm_label: d-04.2 nis2 sub-so: entity-level contain phase

nodes.label: DORA Art. 30(1)+(2): Minimum contractual elements
nodes.rationale: Requires rights and obligations clearly allocated in writing with at least nine minimum elements. OJ-corrective note: audit rights and exit strategies are in Art. 30(3)(e)(i) and (f) (CIF-only), not Art. 30(2).

nodes.label: DORA Art. 30(3)(e): Unrestricted audit rights
nodes.rationale: Grants unrestricted access, inspection, and audit rights with narrow exception for alternative assurance levels when other clients' rights are affected.

nodes.label: DORA Article 10: Anomalous activity detection
nodes.rationale: Chapter II Section II detection substrate that Chapter III operationalises into incident-management process. Dual objective per Recital 54: cyber-threat + operational-performance anomaly detection.

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 14(1) — Human Oversight Design by Provider
nodes.rationale: Umbrella provision for human-oversight duty. Requires high-risk AI systems designed to be effectively overseen by natural persons with appropriate human-machine interface tools. Bridges technical-design to human-factors obligations.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 14(1) — human oversight design by provider

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 14(4) — Five Cumulative Oversight Abilities
nodes.rationale: Five-element AND-coordinated list: (a) properly understand, (b) remain aware of automation bias, (c) correctly interpret, (d) decide, (e) intervene. Operationalises the Art. 14(1) umbrella duty. 'As appropriate and proportionate' soft hedge modifies entire list.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 14(4) — five cumulative oversight abilities

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 26(2) — Deployer Oversight Assignment
nodes.rationale: Deployer-side mirror of Art. 14(1). Requires assignment of oversight to natural persons with necessary competence, training, authority, and support. Personnel-qualification anchor of deployer's AI-governance framework.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 26(2) — deployer oversight assignment

nodes.label: SO-CRA-074: ENISA Biennial Report, EU Vuln DB, CSIRT Helpdesk
nodes.norm_label: so-cra-074: enisa biennial report, eu vuln db, csirt helpdesk

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5: Principles for processing personal data
nodes.rationale: Six principles: lawfulness/fairness/transparency (a/b), purpose limitation (b), data minimisation (c), accuracy (d), storage limitation (e), integrity/confidentiality (f). Art. 5(2) accountability: controller responsible and able to demonstrate compliance.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 5: principles for processing personal data

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 16: Right to rectification
nodes.rationale: Data subject right to obtain rectification without undue delay. Supplementary statement mechanism for contested facts. Art. 19 cascade to recipients.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 28(1): ICT Third-Party Risk
nodes.rationale: Manage ICT third-party risk under four-factor proportionality. Foundational third-party risk-governance rule with contractual minimum elements at Art. 30(1)-(2).

nodes.label: Pre-launch supervisory consultation on residual high risk
nodes.rationale: Art. 36(1) pre-launch gate: where DPIA identifies residual high risk after mitigation, controller must consult supervisory authority before launching. Operationalised via GV.OC-03 and ID.RA-06.
nodes.norm_label: pre-launch supervisory consultation on residual high risk

nodes.label: Pre-launch DPIA with risk treatment and prior-consultation trigger
nodes.rationale: Art. 35(1) DPIA trigger for high-risk processing; Art. 35(7) four content items; Art. 36(1) prior consultation where residual risk remains high. Operationalised via ID.RA-01, ID.RA-05, ID.RA-06.
nodes.norm_label: pre-launch dpia with risk treatment and prior-consultation trigger

nodes.label: Four-element DPIA content with necessity and proportionality test
nodes.rationale: Art. 35(7)(a)-(d) four mandated elements; necessity means no less-intrusive alternative; proportionality means benefits justify intrusiveness. Operationalised via ID.RA-05 and RS.AN-03.
nodes.norm_label: four-element dpia content with necessity and proportionality test

nodes.label: Risk-change-triggered DPIA review with periodic cadence
nodes.rationale: Art. 35(11) review on material risk change; supplemented by periodic (annual) review; contextual changes (threat intel, incidents, tech evolution) feed improvement. Operationalised via ID.IM-04 and ID.RA-06.
nodes.norm_label: risk-change-triggered dpia review with periodic cadence

nodes.label: SO-DORA-009: Crisis Communication for Responsible Disclosure
nodes.rationale: Security objective: crisis communication plans enable responsible disclosure of major ICT-related incidents or vulnerabilities to clients, counterparts, and (as appropriate) the public. Sub-domain D-04.3.
nodes.norm_label: so-dora-009: crisis communication for responsible disclosure

nodes.label: SR-DORA-018: Standing Crisis Communication Plans
nodes.rationale: Art. 14(1) standing-planning counterpart to triggered Art. 19 reporting. Plans must be in place before any incident. Maps to NIST RS.CO-03 and RS.CO-04. Co-exists with NIS 2 Art. 23 and CRA Art. 14.

nodes.label: SR-DORA-017: Major ICT Incident Notification to Supervisor and Clients
nodes.rationale: Art. 19(1)+(3) dual notification duty. OJ-corrective note flags material gap: SR drops the 'impact on financial interests of clients' trigger condition from Art. 19(3). Maps to NIST RS.CO-02 and RS.CO-04. Parallel to GDPR Art. 33 and NIS 2 Art. 23.
nodes.norm_label: sr-dora-017: major ict incident notification to supervisor and clients

nodes.label: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2956
nodes.rationale: Partially addresses reporting templates in Annex I to IV. EBA/ESMA/EIOPA RTS under Art. 18(3) for criteria combination and materiality thresholds. Pending technical standards may close the 'high standards' VAG regress.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 18 — Incident Classification
nodes.rationale: Per-article split for Art. 18 classification criteria. No standalone SO row; covered via SRs that reference Art. 18 as the classification trigger for Art. 19 reporting.

nodes.label: Appropriate technical and organisational measures under Art. 24(1)
nodes.rationale: Art. 24(1) operational-responsibility centrepiece; review triggered by material change of risk supplemented by annual periodic review. Operationalised via GV.PO-01, GV.PO-02, GV.RM-04.
nodes.norm_label: appropriate technical and organisational measures under art. 24(1)

nodes.label: Continuous evidence-of-compliance with performance review
nodes.rationale: Art. 5(2) accountability + Art. 24(1) demonstrability + Art. 30(1) RoPA as evidence instrument; continuous-evidentiary-trail reading. Operationalised via GV.PO-02 and GV.OV-03.

nodes.label: Policies on risk analysis + IS security (SO-NIS2-022)
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(a) security objective: policies on risk analysis and information system security documenting entity's approach to identifying, assessing, treating risks.
nodes.norm_label: policies on risk analysis + is security (so-nis2-022)

nodes.label: Policies to assess effectiveness of risk-management measures (SO-NIS2-023)
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(f) security objective: policies and procedures to assess effectiveness of cybersecurity risk-management measures with results feeding back into cycle.
nodes.norm_label: policies to assess effectiveness of risk-management measures (so-nis2-023)

nodes.label: D-04 Incident Response Index
nodes.rationale: Top-level index for D-04 Incident Response domain, listing 4 sub-subdomains (D-04.1 through D-04.4), 4 merged files, 108 article copies, and 203 ambiguity sections.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split of CRA Art. 13 containing 30+ Security Objectives (SO-CRA-006 through SO-CRA-070) and Security Rules (SR-CRA-001 through SR-CRA-008+). References D-04.1 in related_documents. Covers design/development/production, vulnerability handling, SBOM, CVD, support period, and conformity assessment.

nodes.label: Lawful, fair, and transparent processing on documented Art. 6 basis
nodes.rationale: Art. 5(1)(a) gateway principle: three conjunctive conditions (lawful, fair, transparent) multiplicative; failure of any one vitiates the obligation. Operationalised via GV.OC-03 and GV.PO-01.
nodes.norm_label: lawful, fair, and transparent processing on documented art. 6 basis

nodes.label: Six documented lawfulness bases with necessity gating per purpose
nodes.rationale: Art. 6(1)(a)-(f) six bases each with own qualifiers; necessity gating for (b)-(d), balancing test for (f). Operationalised via GV.OC-03 and GV.PO-02.
nodes.norm_label: six documented lawfulness bases with necessity gating per purpose

nodes.label: Heightened handling for nine special-category personal-data classes
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(1) prohibition with ten Art. 9(2) exceptions; nine categories independently trigger; explicit consent sits above Art. 4(11) baseline. Operationalised via GV.OC-03 and PR.DS-12.
nodes.norm_label: heightened handling for nine special-category personal-data classes

nodes.label: MFA or continuous auth + secured comms + secured emergency (SO-NIS2-004)
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(j) security objective: MFA or continuous authentication where appropriate, secured voice/video/text, secured emergency communication systems.
nodes.norm_label: mfa or continuous auth + secured comms + secured emergency (so-nis2-004)

nodes.label: Strong authentication through MFA or continuous alternatives
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(j) MFA or continuous authentication where appropriate; mechanism-agnostic; FIDO2/WebAuthn as dominant state-of-the-art; SMS-OTP rejected for new deployments. Operationalised via PR.AA-03 and PR.AA-05.
nodes.norm_label: strong authentication through mfa or continuous alternatives

nodes.label: Secured internal and emergency communications channels
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(j) secured voice/video/text + emergency communication systems; distinct from data-in-transit mandate; resilience in adverse conditions. Operationalised via PR.DS-02 and PR.IR-03.
nodes.norm_label: secured internal and emergency communications channels

nodes.label: CRA Art. 21 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split document covering manufacturer-equivalent trigger (own name/trademark or substantial modification) with SOs and SRs mapped to NIST CSF 2.0.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 22 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split document covering third-party substantial modification triggering manufacturer status, closing the loophole for non-supply-chain modifiers.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split (SO + SR) generated from 01_SecurityObjectives.md and 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md. The originals remain the authoritative aggregate indexes.

nodes.label: SO-NIS2-011: Recipient Notification of Significant Incidents and Threats
nodes.rationale: Art. 23(1) para 1 + Art. 23(2). User-facing twin of CSIRT-side notification. 'Where appropriate' + 'without undue delay' softer than CSIRT-side hard ceilings.
nodes.norm_label: so-nis2-011: recipient notification of significant incidents and threats

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-016: Recipient Notification of Significant Service-Affecting Incidents
nodes.rationale: Maps to NIST CSF RS.CO-03, RS.CO-04. User-facing notification flow. 'Where appropriate' + 'without undue delay' softer than CSIRT-side. Recipient channel separated from regulator-side flow.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-016: recipient notification of significant service-affecting incidents

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-017: Proactive Threat and Remedy Communication to Recipients
nodes.rationale: Maps to NIST CSF RS.CO-03, RS.MI-01. Upstream twin of incident notification - communicates about threat before it materialises. Extends containment perimeter to recipient side.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-017: proactive threat and remedy communication to recipients

nodes.label: DORA Art. 14(1): Crisis Communication Plans
nodes.rationale: Standing-planning counterpart to triggered Art. 19 reporting. Plans must be in place before any incident. Chapter II Section 2 framework. Risk-proportional per EBA Guidelines with 'as appropriate' calibration for public dimension.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 19(1): Major Incident Reporting to Competent Authority
nodes.rationale: Hard duty to notify relevant competent authority of any major ICT-related incident. Trigger is moment of classification as 'major', not moment of awareness. Operates in parallel with GDPR Art. 33 and NIS 2 Art. 23.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 19(1): major incident reporting to competent authority

nodes.label: DORA Art. 19(3): Client Notification of Major Incidents
nodes.rationale: OJ-corrective note: OJ conditions client notification on 'AND HAS AN IMPACT ON THE FINANCIAL INTERESTS OF CLIENTS' — the SR drops this trigger condition, converting conditional to unconditional. Operates on separate clock: 'without undue delay as soon as they become aware'.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 19(3): client notification of major incidents

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28/30/33 — Processor/Records/Breach
nodes.rationale: Parallel data-protection obligations: processor controls (Art. 28), records of processing (Art. 30), breach notification (Art. 33) creating composite supervisory exposure with DORA.

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 23: Incident Notification
nodes.rationale: Directive (EU) 2022/2555. Parallel incident-notification workflow. Art. 23(4) 24-hour early warning analogous to potential DORA early-warning mini-notification. Co-exists with DORA Art. 19 reporting.

nodes.label: Records of processing with supervisory-authority access and 250-employee carve-out
nodes.rationale: Art. 30(1) seven content items; Art. 30(4) supervisory access; Art. 30(5) 250-employee exception with disjunctive risk/special-category/criminal-conviction trigger. Operationalised via ID.AM-03 and GV.PO-02.
nodes.norm_label: records of processing with supervisory-authority access and 250-employee carve-out

nodes.label: Integrity-preserved RoPA records available to supervisory authority
nodes.rationale: Art. 30(3) in writing/electronic form; Art. 5(2) accountability; Art. 31 cooperation; records must be tamper-evident and provenance-preserving. Operationalised via PR.PS-04, DE.AE-03, RS.AN-07.
nodes.norm_label: integrity-preserved ropa records available to supervisory authority

nodes.label: SO-AIACT-002: Testing for Risk Management
nodes.rationale: Testing including real-world conditions for risk management measures (Art. 9(6)-(7)).

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RM-02: Risk Role Communication
nodes.rationale: Risk roles, responsibilities, authorities, and accountabilities established and communicated. Ensures role allocation is communicated across the entity and understood by all three lines.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.rm-02: risk role communication

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AT-01: Cybersecurity Awareness Training
nodes.rationale: All users informed and trained on cybersecurity topics. Anchors the baseline awareness layer closing the human-factor gap.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.at-01: cybersecurity awareness training

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AT-02: Role-Specific Cybersecurity Understanding
nodes.rationale: All workforce members understand their roles and responsibilities in achieving cybersecurity objectives. Layers the role-specific depth dimension demanded by 'commensurate to the remit of their functions'.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.at-02: role-specific cybersecurity understanding

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4)(d): Cryptographic Key Protection
nodes.rationale: Ties encryption to approved data classification and ICT risk assessment. 'Approved' qualifier binding under Art. 5(2) management body oversight. Recital 53 grounds in precautionary principle for sensitive financial data.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 13(6): Staff Training
nodes.rationale: Compulsory ICT security awareness and resilience training modules. Workforce-scale counterpart to Art. 5(4) management-body training.

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 21: Basic Cybersecurity Measures
nodes.rationale: Parallel baseline obligations on NSIEs outside DORA. Referenced across multiple SRs as cross-regulatory parallel for risk identification, incident handling, business continuity, and training.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 3(2) — Definition: Network and Information System
nodes.rationale: Every ICT-related clause in Ch. II Sec. II inherits from DORA Art. 3(2) → NIS 2 Art. 6(1). The foundational definitional anchor for the entire regulation.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 3(2) — definition: network and information system

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 6(1) — Network and Information System (definition)
nodes.rationale: Upstream definition that DORA Art. 3(2) inherits from. The cross-regulation definitional anchor for all ICT-related obligations in the DORA corpus.
nodes.norm_label: nis 2 art. 6(1) — network and information system (definition)

nodes.label: SO-NIS2-012: Cross-MS Notification and SPOC Forwarding
nodes.rationale: Art. 23(6)/(8)/(10)/(7). Cross-border notification when incident concerns 2+ Member States. SPOC forwarding under Art. 23(8). CER cross-sharing under Art. 23(10).
nodes.norm_label: so-nis2-012: cross-ms notification and spoc forwarding

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-018: Cross-Border Notification Across Member States and ENISA
nodes.rationale: Maps to NIST CSF RS.CO-04, GV.SC-05. Multi-stakeholder coordination: affected MS SPOCs, ENISA, EU-CyCLONe. SPOC forwarding under Art. 23(8) on CSIRT request.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-018: cross-border notification across member states and enisa

nodes.label: CRDA-Deep D-04.4: Cross-Regulation Deep Analysis (6 Pairs Verified)
nodes.rationale: Verified 5 of 6 pairs as SAME (4 COMPLEMENTARY + 1 DIFFERENT-PERSPECTIVE) and corrected 1 pair (NIS2↔DORA from EQUAL to COMPLEMENTARY). No SCOPE-DISJOINT, no CONTRADICTORY. Scope-disjoint test applied to all pairs.
nodes.norm_label: crda-deep d-04.4: cross-regulation deep analysis (6 pairs verified)

nodes.label: CRDA Domain D-04.4: Cross-Regulation Domain Analysis
nodes.rationale: Initial CRDA classification: NIS2↔DORA as EQUAL (later corrected). All other pairs COMPLEMENTARY or DIFFERENT-PERSPECTIVE. AI Act out-of-scope per AEGIS taxonomy §4.1.
nodes.norm_label: crda domain d-04.4: cross-regulation domain analysis

nodes.label: Cross-Regulation 'Appropriate and Proportionate' Qualifier Pattern
nodes.source_location: NIS2 Art. 21(1), GDPR Art. 32(1), DORA Art. 6(1)
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 21(1) uses 'appropriate and proportionate' (2 qualifiers, S3 ambiguity on independent vs compound). DORA Art. 6(1) uses 'sound, comprehensive and well-documented' (3 attributes, most demanding). GDPR Art. 24 uses 'appropriate' (1 qualifier). DORA's triad is the most demanding framework-quality specification.

nodes.label: Cross-Regulation Training Polysemy Pattern
nodes.rationale: Three regulations share the same POLY pattern for 'training': GDPR Art. 39 (DPO training), NIS2 Art. 20(2) (management body training), CRA Annex I Part II §2(c) (security update procedures including training).

nodes.label: Cross-Regulation 'Without Undue Delay' Temporal Pattern
nodes.source_location: GDPR Art. 34(1), DORA Art. 19(3), NIS2 CL35
nodes.rationale: Same temporal trigger phrase appears in GDPR Art. 34(1) (breach communication), DORA Art. 19(3) (client notification), and NIS2 CL35. DORA adds twin trigger 'without undue delay as soon as they become aware of it' with S3 ambiguity on primary vs clock-start reading.

nodes.label: NIS2 Essential and Important Entity Classification
nodes.rationale: Single most important scope-defining layer of NIS2. Three layers of indeterminacy: essential vs important (different supervisory regimes), size thresholds, sectoral coverage (Annex I/II). Member-State discretion (Art. 3(1)(e),(g)) adds further ambiguity. Prerequisite for all Art. 20-25 obligations.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 essential and important entity classification

nodes.label: Q6=b Split – T2-C24 Mapping Error Resolution
nodes.rationale: T2-C24 mis-attributed Art. 13(5) due-diligence to Art. 13(13) 10-year retention. v0.2 split resolves: CRA-CL23a (Art. 13(5) due diligence) + CRA-CL38 (Art. 13(13) 10-year retention). Net: 3 T3 clauses → 36 v0.2 clauses.
nodes.norm_label: q6=b split – t2-c24 mapping error resolution

nodes.label: T3-vs-Text Gap Pattern (Mapping Inconsistencies)
nodes.source_location: Multiple sections (NIS2 C11, C15, C16-C18, C20, C22, C29; CRA C03/C06)
nodes.rationale: Recurring pattern where T3 mapping imposes readings not present in OJ text: CI/CD pipeline (NIS2 C11), role-specific training (NIS2 C15), at-rest/in-transit/key-management split (NIS2 C16-C18), RBAC/least-privilege (NIS2 C20), audit logging (NIS2 C22), real-time detection (NIS2 C29). Flagged as mapping-layer inconsistencies, not text ambiguities.

nodes.label: CRA Article 13 – Manufacturer Obligations
nodes.rationale: Operational core of manufacturer's risk-assessment duty; 6-phase lifecycle propagation; support-period architecture (5-year minimum + 10-year update tail); supply-chain due-diligence; corrective measures. 36 v0.2 clauses identified.

nodes.label: CRA Article 21 – Importer/Distributor as Manufacturer
nodes.rationale: Importer or distributor becomes manufacturer when placing product under its name/trademark or carrying out substantial modification. Two S3 ambiguities: 'under its name or trademark' and 'substantial modification'.

nodes.label: CRA-CL27 – Art. 13(8) Vulnerability Handling During Support
nodes.rationale: 'Handled effectively' is S3 ambiguous (patch vs mitigate vs either). 'Including its components' is S2 scope question (direct vs transitive). Inherits Art. 3(20) support period definition.
nodes.norm_label: cra-cl27 – art. 13(8) vulnerability handling during support

nodes.label: CRA-CL46 – Art. 13(21) Corrective Measures
nodes.rationale: 'Immediately take' is S2 (without delay vs 24h vs as soon as discovered). 'Corrective measures' is S2 with 5 readings (fix, update docs, withdraw, recall, any combination). Literal reading is R5 (any combination per 'as appropriate').

nodes.label: DORA Article 6 – ICT Risk Management Framework
nodes.rationale: Framework chapeau requires 'sound, comprehensive and well-documented' (most demanding 3-attribute triad in 5-regulation corpus). Art. 6(8) 8-point digital operational resilience strategy (open list). Art. 6(9) multi-vendor strategy. Art. 6(10) outsourcing with full responsibility retention.
nodes.norm_label: dora article 6 – ict risk management framework

nodes.label: DORA CL19-3 – Art. 19(3) Client Notification
nodes.rationale: Twin temporal trigger 'without undue delay as soon as they become aware' (S3). 'Financial interests' undefined (S3). 'Potentially affected' and 'where applicable' hedges (S2). Same awareness trigger as NIS2 CL35.

nodes.label: DORA CL6-5 – Art. 6(8)+(9)+(10) Resilience Strategy, Multi-Vendor, Outsourcing
nodes.rationale: 8-point strategy (open list, S3). Risk tolerance vs risk appetite (S3, EBA-aligned). KPIs vs KRMs (S3). Multi-vendor strategy 'holistic' (S3). Outsourcing with 'fully responsible' (S3, strict/joint-and-several reading).
nodes.norm_label: dora cl6-5 – art. 6(8)+(9)+(10) resilience strategy, multi-vendor, outsourcing

nodes.label: GDPR Article 34 – Communication of Personal Data Breach to Data Subject
nodes.rationale: Obligation on controller to communicate breach to data subject without undue delay when high risk; three exceptions (encryption, subsequent measures, disproportionate effort).
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 34 – communication of personal data breach to data subject

nodes.label: GDPR Article 35 – Data Protection Impact Assessment
