nodes.rationale: Mandatory DPIA for high-risk processing including new technologies, profiling, large-scale special categories, systematic monitoring. Contains 11 paragraphs with systematic description, necessity/proportionality assessment, risk assessment, and mitigation measures.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 35 – data protection impact assessment

nodes.label: NIS2 Article 20 – Management Body Liability and Training
nodes.rationale: Only direct personal-liability provision in NIS2 Chapter IV. Two-tier training obligation (mandatory for members, encouraged for employees). Classification of essential/important entities is prerequisite for all obligations.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 article 20 – management body liability and training

nodes.label: NIS2 Article 21 – Risk Management Measures
nodes.rationale: Core obligation: appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures. 10 sub-points (a)-(j) covering policies, incident handling, business continuity, supply chain, security in development, effectiveness assessment, cyber hygiene, cryptography, HR security, MFA/communications. Dominant VAG trigger propagating to all sub-points.

nodes.label: NIS2-C08 – Art. 21(2)(d) Supply Chain Security
nodes.rationale: 'Direct suppliers or service providers' is S3 SCOPE-Q: contractual (Tier-1) vs technical (API-connected) vs operational (single-points-of-failure). Determines whether obligation reaches 1-hop, n-hop, or only contractual counterparties.

nodes.label: NIS2-C16 – Art. 21(2)(h) Cryptography and Encryption
nodes.rationale: 'Where appropriate' soft hedge makes encryption discretionary. Cryptography vs encryption is subordination relation. T3 splits into at-rest/in-transit/key-management but OJ text contains no such distinction (T3-vs-text gap).

nodes.label: NIS2-C21 – Art. 21(2)(j) MFA and Communications Security
nodes.rationale: Four distinct obligations coordinated via OR and AND in one sub-point. 'Where appropriate' closes entire sub-point. Parse tree admits ≥6 distinct obligation shapes. MFA polysemy: SMS-OTP vs TOTP vs hardware token vs passkeys.
nodes.norm_label: nis2-c21 – art. 21(2)(j) mfa and communications security

nodes.label: NIS2-CL07 – Art. 21(1) Risk Management Core Obligation
nodes.rationale: Dominant VAG trigger of NIS2. 'Appropriate and proportionate' propagates to all 10 sub-points. 'Technical, operational and organisational measures' is S2 POLY (distinct categories vs cumulative vs open list). 'Manage the risks' is S2 (identify-assess-mitigate vs treat vs continuous monitoring).
nodes.norm_label: nis2-cl07 – art. 21(1) risk management core obligation

nodes.label: NIS2-CL11 – Art. 21(2)(b) Incident Handling
nodes.rationale: Defined in Art. 6(8) as 6-action list (prevent, detect, analyse, contain, respond, recover) but 'aiming to' makes it illustrative. S2 POLY: process (NIST SP 800-61) vs team (CSIRT/SOC) vs capability (tooling).

nodes.label: DORA Article 17: ICT-related incident management
nodes.rationale: Chapter III chapeau establishing the process obligation that Art. 18 classification and Art. 19 reporting operationalise. Cross-references NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(b) and GDPR Art. 33.

nodes.label: Privacy-by-default across collection, retention, and exposure
nodes.rationale: Art. 25(2) four-dimension AND-coordinated default (amount, extent, period, accessibility) operationalised via PR.PS-01 and PR.DS-12; relaxation requires affirmative data-subject intervention.
nodes.norm_label: privacy-by-default across collection, retention, and exposure

nodes.label: Downstream-recipient cascade for rectification and erasure
nodes.rationale: Art. 19 downstream-integrity obligation: corrections must propagate to all known recipients or controller must demonstrate impossibility/disproportionate effort. Operationalised via RS.CO-02 and PR.DS-12.
nodes.norm_label: downstream-recipient cascade for rectification and erasure

nodes.label: Purpose-bound data minimisation with compatibility assessment
nodes.rationale: Art. 5(1)(c) minimisation calibrated to purpose; Art. 6(4) compatibility test for further processing. Operationalised via PR.DS-12 and ID.AM-03.
nodes.norm_label: purpose-bound data minimisation with compatibility assessment

nodes.label: Structured electronic access copy in commonly used format
nodes.rationale: Art. 15(1)/(3) data-subject access right; commonly used electronic form read as structured-interoperable (JSON, CSV, XML). Operationalised via PR.DS-10 and PR.DS-12.
nodes.norm_label: structured electronic access copy in commonly used format

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28(3)(a)-(h) — Processor Contract Mandatory Clauses
nodes.rationale: Eight mandatory sub-clauses forming a closed AND-list: instructions, confidentiality, Art. 32 measures, sub-processor conditions, rights assistance, Arts. 32-36 assistance, return/deletion, audits.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 28(3)(a)-(h) — processor contract mandatory clauses

nodes.label: Written EU representative for non-EU controllers and processors
nodes.rationale: Art. 27(1) designation in writing; Art. 27(2)(a) conjunctive exception (occasional AND small-scale AND low-risk). Operationalised via GV.OC-02 and GV.RR-02.
nodes.norm_label: written eu representative for non-eu controllers and processors

nodes.label: Plain-language transparent privacy notice design
nodes.rationale: Art. 12(1) six conjunctive form qualifiers (concise, transparent, intelligible, easily accessible, clear, plain); child-specific heightened standard; identity-proofing for oral provision. Operationalised via GV.PO-02 and PR.AA-02.

nodes.label: Supply chain security (SO-NIS2-014)
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(d) security objective: supply chain security managed across direct supplier and service-provider relationships.

nodes.label: Management body approval and liability (SO-NIS2-021)
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 20(1) security objective: management body approves, oversees, and bears liability for Art. 21 cybersecurity risk-management measures.

nodes.label: CRA Substantial Modification (Art. 3(30), Art. 13(10), Art. 21-22)
nodes.rationale: Substantial modification triggers manufacturer-equivalent obligations. Compliance with Annex I Part II(2) only required for last-placed version if users have free access. Series-of-production conformity maintained.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 11 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split document covering ICT business continuity policy, implementation arrangements with independent audit, and risk-calibrated backup with verified restoration.

nodes.label: DORA Article 19 – Incident Reporting to Clients
nodes.rationale: Client notification without undue delay upon awareness of major ICT-related incident impacting financial interests. Cyber-threat sub-paragraph with 'where applicable' and 'potentially affected' hedges. Outsourcing of reporting with full responsibility retention.
nodes.norm_label: dora article 19 – incident reporting to clients

nodes.label: DORA CL5-1: Art. 5(1) Internal Governance Framework Ambiguity
nodes.rationale: 3 ambiguity instances: 'internal governance and control framework' (S3, three-lines-of-defence vs any model), 'effective and prudent' (S3, distinct vs hendiadys), 'high level of digital operational resilience' (S2, propagated from DORA-D01 definition).
nodes.norm_label: dora cl5-1: art. 5(1) internal governance framework ambiguity

nodes.label: NIS2-CL12: Art. 21(2)(c) Business Continuity Ambiguity Analysis
nodes.rationale: 5 ambiguity instances: 'business continuity' polysemy (S2), 'such as' nested coordination (S3), 'crisis management' polysemy (S2), 'backup management' polysemy (S2), 'disaster recovery' polysemy (S2). R4 (cumulative) is dominant reading for BC.
nodes.norm_label: nis2-cl12: art. 21(2)(c) business continuity ambiguity analysis

nodes.label: Req 4.4: Multi-Layer Recovery Architecture (Volere Immunity)
nodes.rationale: High-level Volere requirement (section 15, immunity subtype). MUST priority, TEST verification. Depends on 4.1 (detection) and 4.2 (containment). NIST CSF: RC.RP-01, RC.RP-03, RC.RP-04, PR.DS-11, PR.DS-12, PR.IR-03, PR.IR-04.

nodes.label: Req 4.4.1: Personal-Data Availability Restored in Timely Manner
nodes.rationale: GDPR-specific sub-requirement. NIST CSF: PR.IR-04, PR.DS-11, RC.RP-04. Depends on 4.2.1 (containment) and 4.1.1 (awareness trigger).
nodes.norm_label: req 4.4.1: personal-data availability restored in timely manner

nodes.label: Req 4.4.2: Entity-Level BC + Backup + DR + CM Triad
nodes.rationale: NIS2-specific sub-requirement. NIST CSF: RC.RP-04, PR.DS-11. ISO 22301 (BCMS) and ISO 22361 (crisis management) as methodological anchors. On DORA+NIS2 parties, DORA absorbs NIS2 BC/DR/CM for ICT subset via lex specialis.
nodes.norm_label: req 4.4.2: entity-level bc + backup + dr + cm triad

nodes.label: Req 4.4.3: Product-Internal Availability Preserved Also After Incident
nodes.rationale: CRA-specific sub-requirement. NIST CSF: PR.IR-03, PR.DS-12. Annex VII §2 technical documentation + §6 test-reports as evidence base. Layered-not-substituted caveat preserved.
nodes.norm_label: req 4.4.3: product-internal availability preserved also after incident

nodes.label: Req 4.4.4: Comprehensive ICT BC Policy + OJ-Corrected Art. 11(2)(a)-(e)
nodes.rationale: DORA-specific sub-requirement. NIST CSF: RC.RP-01, RC.RP-03, RC.RP-04, PR.IR-03, PR.IR-04, PR.DS-11. OJ-corrected Art. 11(2)(a)-(e) objective list: (a) continuity-of-critical-functions, (b) response-and-resolution, (c) plan-activation, (d) impact-and-loss-estimation, (e) communication-and-CA-reporting.
nodes.norm_label: req 4.4.4: comprehensive ict bc policy + oj-corrected art. 11(2)(a)-(e)

nodes.label: SO-CRA-021: Product Availability Post-Incident (CRA Annex I Part I (2)(h))
nodes.norm_label: so-cra-021: product availability post-incident (cra annex i part i (2)(h))

nodes.label: DORA Art. 14 — Crisis Communication Plans
nodes.rationale: Per-article split document covering Art. 14(1) standing crisis communication plans for responsible disclosure of major ICT-related incidents. Generated from aggregate SecurityObjectives and SecurityRules indexes.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 17 — Incident Management Process
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering Art. 17(1) end-to-end ICT-related incident management process. Contains multiple SRs spanning detection, management, notification, and supporting controls.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 19 — Incident Reporting
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering Art. 19(1) supervisor notification and Art. 19(3) client notification of major ICT-related incidents.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 21 — Cross-Domain Security Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering multiple SRs spanning data protection, risk identification, network management, and monitoring. Broadest cross-domain coverage in the D-04.3 article set.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 27 — Requirements for Testers (TLPT)
nodes.rationale: NEW in v0.2 (T3 omitted entirely). Five sub-requirements for external testers, internal-tester additional conditions, and data processing in contracts.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 7 — ICT Systems, Protocols and Tools
nodes.rationale: 4 baseline requirements: appropriateness (Art. 4 proportionality), reliability, sufficient capacity, technological resilience. The entry point for the Ch. II Sec. II operational requirements.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 7 — ict systems, protocols and tools

nodes.label: DORA-D08 — 'ICT-Related Incident' (S3 regress)
nodes.rationale: S3 regress definition. Inherited by detection, response, and reporting clauses throughout Ch. II and Ch. III.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-06.3: Supply Chain (Processor Management)
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation domain for processor contracts, sub-processor authorisation, and auditability.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-10.3: Monitoring & Audit
nodes.rationale: Sub-domain covering periodic security measure evaluation and audit.

nodes.label: Req 4.3: Multi-Recipient Notification Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Volere audit requirement: unified pipeline generating per-regulation submissions from single event record; parallel-clock binding principle; 5 distinct recipient classes with 5 distinct timeline patterns.

nodes.label: Req 4.3.1: GDPR 72h DPA Notification
nodes.rationale: Sub-requirement for GDPR-specific DPA notification with 'where feasible' softening and 'unlikely risk' carve-out; Art. 33(3) content template is GDPR-unique.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 6 — Security Objectives & Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering definitions (NIS, security of NIS, incident handling, trust service) that anchor Art. 21 obligations.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 17 — Right to Erasure
nodes.rationale: Data-subject trigger for erasure; controller-side duties flow from Art. 5(1)(c)/(e); processor-side mirror in Art. 28(3)(g).

nodes.label: GDPR Article 7 — Conditions for Consent
nodes.rationale: Art. 7(1) demonstrability; Art. 7(2) bundled consent; Art. 7(3) withdrawal; Art. 7(4) conditional consent. Central to SR-GDPR-051, 052.

nodes.label: NIST SP 800-63: Digital identity guidelines
nodes.rationale: EBA Guidelines specify supervisory expectation that financial entities operate authentication mechanisms aligned with NIST SP 800-63 or equivalent.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 55 — Competent Supervisory Authority
nodes.rationale: Determines which SA is competent for breach notification. Referenced by SR-GDPR-016.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 56 — Cooperation Between Authorities (One-Stop-Shop)
nodes.rationale: One-stop-shop mechanism determining lead authority. Referenced by SR-GDPR-016 in Art. 56 context.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 19: Incident reporting
nodes.rationale: Art. 19(1) report major incidents to CA. Art. 19(3) inform clients without undue delay. Art. 19(4) intermediate report at 72 hours.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 4 — Definitions
nodes.rationale: Art. 4(7)/(8) controller/processor definitions; Art. 4(12) personal data breach definition (destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure, access); Art. 4(22) supervisory authority.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(1)(c) — Timely Restore of Availability
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 32(1)(c) — timely restore of availability

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(1)(f) — Integrity and Confidentiality
nodes.rationale: Establishes integrity and confidentiality as a processing principle requiring appropriate security including protection against unauthorised processing and accidental loss, destruction or damage.

nodes.label: SO-CRA-020 — Product Internal Activity Recording
nodes.rationale: Per-regulation SO for CRA: recording and monitoring of product internal activity with user opt-out, corruption reporting. Product with digital elements; manufacturer perspective. Anchors: DE.CM-09 + PR.PS-04.

nodes.label: Req 4.1 — Multi-Layer Detection Architecture (High-Level)
nodes.rationale: Volere audit requirement (MUST, TEST). Derives from SO-D-04.1.HL. Specifies one detection pipeline per layer with explicit hand-offs. NIST CSF: DE.CM-01, DE.CM-09, DE.AE-02, PR.PS-04, RS.MA-01/02/03, ID.RA-04. Applicable when ≥2 regs overlap on same party.

nodes.label: Req 4.1.1 — GDPR Data-Flow Breach Detection
nodes.rationale: Detects personal-data breaches at controller data-flow boundary covering 5 Art. 4(12) breach types. Documents 'becoming aware' moment per EDPB Guidelines 9/2022 §3.4. Depends on 4.1.2 (controller-NSIE) and 4.1.3 (integrated manufacturer-controller).

nodes.label: Req 4.1.2 — NIS2 Entity-Level All-Hazards Detection
nodes.rationale: Entity-wide monitoring covering cybersecurity, operational, and physical-environment hazards. Six-action detect leg per Art. 6(8). Risk-tiered depth per Art. 21(1) 'appropriate and proportionate'. DORA Art. 10 satisfies ICT-hazard subset; NIS2 chapeau extends to physical/operational.

nodes.label: Req 4.1.3 — CRA Product-Internal Recording
nodes.rationale: Intra-product recording of state changes (access/modification of data, services, functions) with user opt-out. Feeds deployer's entity-level pipeline as a feed, not a substitute. Corruption/unauthorised-modification reporting per Annex I Part II (6).

nodes.label: Req 4.1.4 — DORA Multi-Class Anomalous-Activity Detection
nodes.rationale: Multi-layer detection with explicit alert thresholds, auto-alert to ICT-incident-response staff, and SPOF identification. Art. 17(1) detect/manage/notify 3-way. DORA detection feeds GDPR 'becoming aware' for personal-data subset. Lex specialis: DORA absorbs NIS2 ICT-hazard detection for pure-financial entities.

nodes.label: 01_SecurityObjectives.md (Aggregate SO Index)
nodes.rationale: Authoritative aggregate index from which per-article SO splits are generated; the GDPR Art. 5 document is a per-article split derived from this parent.

nodes.label: 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md (Aggregate SR Index)
nodes.rationale: Authoritative aggregate index from which per-article SR splits are generated; the GDPR Art. 5 document is a per-article split derived from this parent.

nodes.label: NIST CSF RC.RP-04: Service Restoration
nodes.rationale: Critical mission functions and services restored through recovery plan implementation. Anchors the service-restoration layer with documented RTOs.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 12(1): Backup and Recovery
nodes.rationale: Backup policies based on criticality/confidentiality and restoration/recovery procedures. Operationalises Art. 11 BC policy with specific backup obligations.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 11(2)+(3): BC arrangements and audit review
nodes.rationale: Five-objective BC list (a)-(e) plus independent internal audit review for non-microenterprises. OJ-corrective note flags mislabelling of objectives (c)/(d)/(e).
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 11(2)+(3): bc arrangements and audit review

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 4(12): Personal Data Breach Definition
nodes.rationale: Defines a personal data breach as a breach of security leading to accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to personal data.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 4(12): personal data breach definition

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-01.1: Data Protection — Confidentiality at Rest
nodes.norm_label: sub-domain d-01.1: data protection — confidentiality at rest

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-01.2: Data Protection — Confidentiality in Transit
nodes.norm_label: sub-domain d-01.2: data protection — confidentiality in transit

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-10.1: Monitoring and Audit — Event Detection
nodes.norm_label: sub-domain d-10.1: monitoring and audit — event detection

nodes.label: GDPR Article 28(3) (Processor Contract Requirements)
nodes.rationale: The eight mandatory sub-clauses (a)-(h) form a closed AND-list. Art. 28(3)(a) documented instructions, (b) confidentiality, (c) Art. 32 measures, (d) sub-processor conditions, (e) data-subject rights assistance, (f) Arts. 32-36 assistance, (g) return/deletion, (h) audits. Omitting any one creates non-compliance.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 29 (Processing Under Authority)
nodes.rationale: Requires that persons acting under the authority of the controller or processor do not process data except on instructions, unless required by Union or Member State law. Establishes the instruction-only rule at the access-control layer.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 30 (Records of Processing Activities)
nodes.rationale: Art. 30(1) enumerates seven content items for the RoPA; Art. 30(4) requires availability to supervisory authority; Art. 30(5) provides the 250-employee exception with disjunctive risk/special-category/criminal-conviction triggers.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 4(12) (Personal Data Breach Definition)
nodes.rationale: Defines a personal data breach as a breach of security leading to accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to personal data transmitted, stored or otherwise processed. This five-event enumeration anchors the threat-modelling scope.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 5(2) (Accountability)
nodes.rationale: The accountability principle requires the controller to be able to demonstrate compliance. Every SR in this document references Art. 5(2) as the ex post demonstration standard for the documented evidence chain.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(1)(b) — Ongoing CIA and Resilience
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 32(1)(b) — ongoing cia and resilience

nodes.label: SO-CRA-039: Importer Pre-Market Compliance and Corrective Measures
nodes.rationale: Importer places only compliant products, performs pre-market checks, informs MSA of significant risk, takes corrective measures, retains documentation 10 years.
nodes.norm_label: so-cra-039: importer pre-market compliance and corrective measures

nodes.label: SO-CRA-040: Distributor Due Care, Pre-Market Checks, and Corrective Measures
nodes.rationale: Distributor acts with due care, verifies CE/docs/upstream compliance before making available, takes corrective measures on non-conformity.
nodes.norm_label: so-cra-040: distributor due care, pre-market checks, and corrective measures

nodes.label: SR-CRA-054: Importer Pre-Market Documentary Verification Gate
nodes.rationale: Art. 19(1)/(2) four pre-market checks (conformity assessment, tech docs, CE marking, manufacturer ID); mapped to GV.SC-02 (supplier assessment) and GV.SC-04 (contractual-obligation confirmation).
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-054: importer pre-market documentary verification gate

nodes.label: SR-CRA-055: Importer Non-Conformity and Vulnerability Escalation Pathway
nodes.rationale: Art. 19(3)/(5) pre-placement hold and post-placement vulnerability escalation; mapped to RS.MI-01 (containment) and RS.CO-04 (cross-border coordination).
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-055: importer non-conformity and vulnerability escalation pathway

nodes.label: SR-CRA-057: Distributor Due-Care and Pre-Market Verification
nodes.rationale: Art. 20(1)/(2) distributor due-care and three pre-market checks (CE, Annex II docs, upstream compliance); mapped to GV.SC-04; procedurally lighter than importer verification.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-057: distributor due-care and pre-market verification

nodes.label: SR-CRA-058: Distributor Non-Conformity and Corrective-Measures Escalation
nodes.rationale: Art. 20(3)/(4) distributor-side analogue of importer Art. 19(3)/(5); mapped to RS.MI-01 and RS.CO-04; corrective-measure set mirrors Art. 13(21).
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-058: distributor non-conformity and corrective-measures escalation

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 3(49): Serious Incident Definition
nodes.rationale: Defines 'serious incident' via three sub-categories (a)/(b)/(c) with distinct severity thresholds. VAG-3 ambiguity on interaction between sub-categories.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 3(49): serious incident definition

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 55: GPAI Provider Obligations
nodes.rationale: Title IV, Chapter V: obligations of GPAI model providers with systemic risk. Art. 55(1)(a) model evaluation; Art. 55(1)(c) incident reporting.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 55: gpai provider obligations

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 64: AI Office
nodes.rationale: Establishes the AI Office as EU-level body. Recipient of GPAI serious incident reports under Art. 55(1)(c).

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 73: Serious Incident Reporting
nodes.rationale: Art. 73(1)-(4) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689: tiered reporting with 15/10/2-day timelines and awareness/reasonable-likelihood triggers.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 73: serious incident reporting

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 99: Penalties
nodes.rationale: Recital 92 sets the penalty envelope. Art. 99 provides the enforcement mechanism for Art. 73 reporting obligations.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 14: Vulnerability and Incident Reporting
nodes.rationale: Three-tier temporal pattern: 24h early warning, 72h notification, 14d/1m final report. Parallel structure to AI Act Art. 73 but with different recipients (CSIRT + ENISA).
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 14: vulnerability and incident reporting

nodes.label: SR-CRA-056: Importer 10-Year Retention of Conformity Documentation
nodes.rationale: Art. 19(6) parallels manufacturer's Art. 13(13). Importer remains audit point after manufacturer may cease operations.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-056: importer 10-year retention of conformity documentation

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 8: Child consent in information society services
nodes.rationale: Art. 8(1) age threshold 16 (Member States may lower to 13). Art. 8(2) reasonable verification of parental responsibility. Available-technology standard is a rolling baseline.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 8: child consent in information society services

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 9: Special categories of personal data
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(1) prohibits processing of nine special categories. Art. 9(2) lists ten exceptions. Art. 9(2)(a) explicit consent is stronger than Art. 4(11) specific consent. Art. 10 covers criminal-conviction data separately.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 9: special categories of personal data

nodes.label: Continuous breach detection enabling the 72-hour clock
nodes.rationale: Art. 32(1)(b) monitoring is the regulatory foundation for the entire incident-response chain; no detection, no awareness, no notification. Operationalised via DE.CM-01, DE.CM-09, RS.MA-02.
nodes.norm_label: continuous breach detection enabling the 72-hour clock

nodes.label: Post-breach containment, mitigation, and remediation runbooks
nodes.rationale: Art. 33(3)(d) measures-taken-or-proposed obligation operationalised as defence-in-depth: short-term containment (RS.MI-01), mid-term mitigation (RS.MI-02), long-term remediation (PR.DS-01).
nodes.norm_label: post-breach containment, mitigation, and remediation runbooks

nodes.label: 72-hour breach notification to the supervisory authority
nodes.rationale: Art. 33(1) twin temporal anchor (without undue delay + 72 hours) with risk-based carve-out, directed to competent supervisory authority per Art. 4(22). Operationalised via RS.MA-03, RS.CO-02, RS.CO-04.
nodes.norm_label: 72-hour breach notification to the supervisory authority

nodes.label: Processor-to-controller breach notification without undue delay
nodes.rationale: Art. 33(2) upstream trigger for controller's 72-hour clock; processor must notify as soon as aware, distinct from controller's own window. Operationalised via RS.MA-02 and RS.CO-02.
nodes.norm_label: processor-to-controller breach notification without undue delay

nodes.label: Structured four-element breach notification content
nodes.rationale: Art. 33(3)(a)-(d) four-element content requirement (nature, contact, consequences, measures) with phased-disclosure under Art. 33(4). Operationalised via RS.AN-03, RS.AN-07, RS.CO-02.

nodes.label: High-risk breach communication to affected data subjects
nodes.rationale: Art. 34(1) higher threshold than Art. 33; clear and plain language requirement per Art. 34(2). Operationalised via RS.CO-03 and RS.CO-04.
nodes.norm_label: high-risk breach communication to affected data subjects

nodes.label: Cryptographic and mitigation carve-outs for data-subject notification
nodes.rationale: Art. 34(3)(a) encryption/unintelligibility and (b) subsequent-measures exceptions eliminate data-subject notification duty despite high-risk breach. Operationalised via PR.DS-01 and PR.IR-03.
nodes.norm_label: cryptographic and mitigation carve-outs for data-subject notification

nodes.label: Disproportionate-effort public-communication substitute for notification
nodes.rationale: Art. 34(3)(c) narrow exception where direct notification involves disproportionate effort; substitute must achieve equally effective notice. Operationalised via RS.CO-03.

nodes.label: Timely availability restoration after physical or technical incident
nodes.rationale: Art. 32(1)(c) recovery-and-restore obligation with RTO defined per processing activity. Operationalised via PR.IR-04, PR.DS-11, RC.RP-04.
nodes.norm_label: timely availability restoration after physical or technical incident

nodes.label: Five-event threat model with monitoring and event analysis
nodes.rationale: Art. 32(2) five-event OR enumeration (destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure, unauthorised access); inclusive reading; anchors breach-awareness trigger. Operationalised via DE.CM-01, DE.CM-03, DE.AE-02.
nodes.norm_label: five-event threat model with monitoring and event analysis

nodes.label: Cryptography policies and procedures (SO-NIS2-001)
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(h) security objective: policies and procedures for cryptography and where appropriate encryption, covering CIA of stored/transmitted/processed data.

nodes.label: Incident handling capability (SO-NIS2-005)
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(b) security objective: prevention, detection, analysis, containment, response, recovery of incidents including significant-impact events.

nodes.label: BC, backup, DR, crisis management (SO-NIS2-013)
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(c) security objective: business continuity, backup management, disaster recovery, crisis management ensuring availability and integrity restoration.

nodes.label: All-hazards monitoring to surface adverse events
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(b) detection dimension + Art. 21(2) chapeau all-hazards (cybersecurity, operational, physical); network + host/data tier monitoring. Operationalised via DE.CM-01 and DE.CM-09.
nodes.norm_label: all-hazards monitoring to surface adverse events

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 24 — Responsibility of the Controller
nodes.rationale: Art. 24(1) appropriate technical and organisational measures with demonstrability, Art. 24(2) proportionate data-protection policies. The operational-responsibility centrepiece tying controller obligation to demonstrability.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 24 — responsibility of the controller

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-10.3: Monitoring and Audit — Testing and Evaluation
nodes.norm_label: sub-domain d-10.3: monitoring and audit — testing and evaluation

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(1)(d) — Regular Testing and Evaluation
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 32(1)(d) — regular testing and evaluation

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 9(2): Post-Market Monitoring
nodes.rationale: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. Post-market-monitoring duties for high-risk AI systems. Co-exists with DORA Art. 9(1) monitoring where AI components are in scope.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(1): Protection and Prevention (Monitoring)
nodes.rationale: OJ-corrective note (v0.2 audit, material): the 'monitor' obligation actually lives under Art. 9(1), not Art. 8(1) which is the chapeau for Identification. Art. 9(1) requires financial entities to continuously monitor and control the security and functioning of ICT systems.

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(b): Basic Cybersecurity Monitoring
nodes.rationale: Directive (EU) 2022/2555. Parallel baseline for monitoring and incident-handling obligations on NSIEs outside DORA. Co-exists with DORA Art. 9(1) monitoring and Art. 17(1) incident management.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 RS.MA-02: Incident Reports Triaged and Validated
nodes.rationale: Closes the detection chain by triaging and validating detected events into declared incidents, supplying the documented awareness moment.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 rs.ma-02: incident reports triaged and validated

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 26: Joint controllers
nodes.rationale: Art. 26(1) transparent determination of responsibilities. CJEU IAB Europe (C-604/22) extends to parties with determinative influence. Recital 79 contact point designation.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-06.4: Supply Chain — Cross-border
nodes.rationale: Sub-domain covering cross-border notification and EU representative obligations.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-09.1: Governance & Documentation
nodes.rationale: Sub-domain covering lawfulness bases, consent documentation, DPO designation, and regulatory compliance management.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-07.1: Secure Development (Privacy by Design)
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation domain for privacy by design integration in SDLC.
nodes.norm_label: sub-domain d-07.1: secure development (privacy by design)

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 25: Data protection by design and by default
nodes.rationale: Art. 25(1) cites pseudonymisation as canonical by-design technique. Art. 25(2) requires by-default limits. Pseudonymisation is a design choice, not a runtime patch.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 25: data protection by design and by default

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 25 — Data protection by design and by default
nodes.rationale: Art. 25(1) design-time counterpart; Art. 25(2) requires default configuration to minimise on four dimensions: amount, extent, period, accessibility.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 25 — data protection by design and by default

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 GV.PO-02: Cybersecurity Processes Established
nodes.rationale: Captures the process-and-procedure discipline for maintaining and enforcing documented procedures.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 gv.po-02: cybersecurity processes established

nodes.label: CRA-CL130: Annex I Part I (2)(a) no known exploitable vulnerabilities
nodes.norm_label: cra-cl130: annex i part i (2)(a) no known exploitable vulnerabilities

nodes.label: CRA-CL18: Art. 13(3) sentence 1 risk assessment documented
nodes.norm_label: cra-cl18: art. 13(3) sentence 1 risk assessment documented

nodes.label: CRA-CL26: Art. 13(7) systematically document cybersecurity aspects
nodes.norm_label: cra-cl26: art. 13(7) systematically document cybersecurity aspects

nodes.label: CRA-CL39: Art. 3(39) SBOM definition
nodes.rationale: Formal record containing details and supply-chain relationships of components in software elements of the product.

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.AM-02: Software/system inventories maintained
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.am-02: software/system inventories maintained

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 72: Post-Market Monitoring
nodes.rationale: Art. 72(1)-(2): PMM system proportionate to AI technology and risks. Ex-post assurance loop complementing ex-ante conformity assessment.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-04.2: Incident Response — Response
nodes.rationale: Response sub-domain within Incident Response. Covers ICT response plans and crisis management.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 11 — Security Objectives & Security Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split generated from 01_SecurityObjectives.md and 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md covering BC policy, response/recovery plans, and backup obligations.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 11 — security objectives & security rules

nodes.label: DORA Art. 12 — Security Objectives & Security Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering backup policies, restoration/recovery procedures, and risk-calibrated backup with verified restoration capability.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 12 — security objectives & security rules

nodes.label: DORA Art. 6 (ICT Risk Management Framework)
nodes.rationale: DORA article establishing the top-of-stack governance requirement for a sound, comprehensive, well-documented ICT risk management framework with three-lines-of-defence independence.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 GV.PO/GV.RM (Governance Policy/Risk Mgmt) Controls
nodes.rationale: Group of NIST CSF 2.0 governance controls (GV.PO-01, GV.OC-01, GV.RM-02, GV.RM-04, GV.OV-02, GV.RR-02) providing the operational mapping target for DORA governance and framework obligations.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 gv.po/gv.rm (governance policy/risk mgmt) controls

nodes.label: DORA Art. 5 Security Rules Document
nodes.rationale: Per-article split of DORA Art. 5 covering management body responsibilities, CIA+A protection, authentication, key protection, risk identification, and scenario review.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9: ICT security measures
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(4) chapeau: eight mandatory control domains. Art. 9(4)(a) info security policy, (b) network mgmt, (c) access control, (d) cryptographic keys, (f) patches.

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RM-01: Risk Management Objectives
nodes.rationale: Risk management objectives established and agreed by stakeholders. Anchors the 4-verb coordination of Art. 9(1).
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.rm-01: risk management objectives

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 34: Communication of personal data breach to data subject
nodes.rationale: Art. 34(1) high-risk notification duty. Art. 34(3)(a) carve-out when data rendered unintelligible (e.g., encryption). Operational standard: competent adversary without key cannot recover plaintext.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 34: communication of personal data breach to data subject

nodes.label: DORA Art. 24-25: Digital operational resilience testing programme
nodes.rationale: Art. 24(1) requires sound and comprehensive testing programme as integral part of ICT risk-management framework. Art. 25(1) lists 12 testing modalities. Chapter IV dedicated to testing programme.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 24-25: digital operational resilience testing programme

nodes.label: DORA Art. 7(2): Continuous ICT risk identification and scenario review
nodes.rationale: Sentence 1: continuous identification of all ICT risk sources. Sentence 2: review risk scenarios at least yearly. Forms the temporal and methodological chassis of the ICT risk-management framework.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 7(2): continuous ict risk identification and scenario review

nodes.label: Role: FINANCIAL_ENTITY
nodes.rationale: Primary obligated role under DORA. Subject to Art. 10 detection, Art. 14 crisis communication, Art. 17 incident management, Art. 19 reporting.

nodes.label: DORA Article 14: Crisis communication plans
nodes.rationale: Standing-planning counterpart to triggered Art. 19 reporting. Co-exists with NIS 2 Art. 23 and CRA Art. 14. EBA Guidelines frame as risk-proportional.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 39 — Staff Awareness Duties
nodes.rationale: Regulation (EU) 2016/679. Co-exists with DORA Art. 13(6) workforce training for personal-data processing contexts.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-08.1: Human Factors — Awareness
nodes.rationale: Awareness sub-domain within Human Factors. OJ-literal locus for Art. 13(6) training programmes.

nodes.label: Documented retention limits with erasure at purpose end
nodes.rationale: Art. 5(1)(e) storage limitation chain: minimisation at collection, retention-period setting, RoPA documentation. Operationalised via PR.DS-12 and ID.AM-03.
nodes.norm_label: documented retention limits with erasure at purpose end

nodes.label: Right-to-erasure with cryptographic key-destruction deletion path
nodes.rationale: Art. 17 erasure right operationalised via cryptographic key destruction as most defensible interpretation; scales across backups and replicas. Operationalised via PR.DS-10 and PR.DS-12.
nodes.norm_label: right-to-erasure with cryptographic key-destruction deletion path

nodes.label: Processor erasure or return at end of processing services
nodes.rationale: Art. 28(3)(g) processor-side mirror obligation at contract-end; controller chooses deletion or return; backups in scope unless legal retention applies. Operationalised via PR.DS-10 and GV.SC-04.
nodes.norm_label: processor erasure or return at end of processing services

nodes.label: Processor due diligence with documented sufficient guarantees
nodes.rationale: Art. 28(1) sufficient-guarantees threshold operationalised as documented due-diligence practice: questionnaire, certifications review, security audit, sub-processor inventory. Operationalised via GV.SC-02 and GV.SC-03.
nodes.norm_label: processor due diligence with documented sufficient guarantees

nodes.label: Eight-element processor contract with audit and instruction clauses
nodes.rationale: Art. 28(3)(a)-(h) closed AND-list: all eight sub-clauses mandatory; omitting any one puts both parties in non-compliance. Operationalised via GV.SC-03.
nodes.norm_label: eight-element processor contract with audit and instruction clauses

nodes.label: Processor auditability with continuous external-activity monitoring
nodes.rationale: Art. 28(3)(c) substantive standard + Art. 28(3)(h) evidentiary/audit-access standard; controller's principal levers into processor security. Operationalised via GV.SC-03, GV.SC-04, DE.CM-06.
nodes.norm_label: processor auditability with continuous external-activity monitoring

nodes.label: Sub-processor authorisation with controller change-notification
nodes.rationale: Art. 28(2) prior specific or general written authorisation; general authorisation requires notification of changes giving controller opportunity to object. Operationalised via GV.SC-02 and GV.SC-03.

nodes.label: Controller-evidenced processor erasure on contract end
nodes.rationale: Controller-side audit-and-evidence obligation: verify processor honoured contract-end erasure-or-return duty; cryptographic-erasure reading preserved. Operationalised via PR.DS-12 and GV.SC-04.
nodes.norm_label: controller-evidenced processor erasure on contract end

nodes.label: Privacy by design integrated at means-and-processing determination
nodes.rationale: Art. 25(1) fires both at means-determination and during processing; state-of-the-art read as industry-framework (ISO 27001, NIST SP 800-53). Operationalised via PR.PS-06 and PR.DS-12.
nodes.norm_label: privacy by design integrated at means-and-processing determination

nodes.label: Pseudonymisation-by-design with separation of identifying information
nodes.rationale: Art. 25(1) canonical by-design technique; Art. 4(5) de-attribution with separate additional information; Art. 34(3)(a) unintelligibility carve-out preserved. Operationalised via PR.PS-06 and PR.DS-01.
nodes.norm_label: pseudonymisation-by-design with separation of identifying information

nodes.label: Privacy by default across four coordinated minimisation dimensions
nodes.rationale: Art. 25(2) four AND-coordinated dimensions (amount, extent, period, accessibility); each independently bounded; trade-off reading rejected. Operationalised via PR.PS-01 and PR.PS-06.
nodes.norm_label: privacy by default across four coordinated minimisation dimensions

nodes.label: Vulnerability handling and disclosure in system lifecycle (SO-NIS2-002)
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(e) security objective: vulnerabilities identified, handled, disclosed through coordinated process integrated into acquisition/development/maintenance lifecycle.
nodes.norm_label: vulnerability handling and disclosure in system lifecycle (so-nis2-002)

nodes.label: Security in acquisition, development, maintenance (SO-NIS2-017)
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(e) security objective: security integrated into acquisition, development, maintenance including vulnerability handling and disclosure.

nodes.label: Vulnerability handling and external disclosure lifecycle
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(e) two coordinated limbs: security-in-lifecycle (process) and vulnerability handling/disclosure (substantive); CSIRT coordinator under Art. 12(1). Operationalised via ID.RA-01 and GV.SC-04.
nodes.norm_label: vulnerability handling and external disclosure lifecycle

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33 — Breach Notification to Supervisory Authority
nodes.rationale: 72-hour notification clock from awareness. Four-element content requirement. Processor-to-controller notification chain.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 33 — breach notification to supervisory authority

nodes.label: 5-Track Timeline Divergence
nodes.rationale: Emergent tension: 5 regulations with different timelines (GDPR 72h, NIS2 24h/72h/1m, CRA 24h/72h/14d+1m, DORA without-undue-delay, AI Act 15d/10d/2d) create up to 6 distinct deadlines for a single event. No regulation specifies the binding-procedure principle for resolving simultaneous triggers.

nodes.label: AI Office
nodes.rationale: Distinct recipient for GPAI systemic-risk serious incident reports under Art. 55. Separate clock from MSA pathway. One of two recipient classes in AI Act notification (MSA for high-risk, AI Office for GPAI).

nodes.label: AI Act Serious Incident (Art. 3(49))
nodes.rationale: Three sub-categories: (a) death; (b) serious harm to health; (c) serious infringement of fundamental rights. Gating classification test before timeline selection in the 4-trigger x 4-timeline matrix.

nodes.label: Becoming Aware Trigger (Cross-Regulation)
nodes.rationale: The awareness trigger is polysemous across all 5 regulations (actual vs constructive knowledge). Same pattern in NIS2 Art. 23(4)(a)(b), CRA Art. 14, GDPR Art. 33(1), DORA Art. 19, AI Act Art. 73. National implementations diverging on when awareness attaches.

nodes.label: Binding-Procedure Principle
nodes.rationale: Operational rule for resolving simultaneous multi-regulation triggers: the strictest timeline binds per recipient, but parallel recipients each get their own deadline. No single regulation specifies this principle; Phase 2 must define it.

nodes.label: CSIRT (Computer Security Incident Response Team)
nodes.rationale: Primary notification recipient for NIS2 significant incidents and CRA AEV/severe incidents. Member-State-determined as single-entry-point or with CA forwarding. Also receives CRA notifications simultaneously with ENISA.

nodes.label: Supervisory Authority / DPA
nodes.rationale: GDPR notification recipient for personal data breach reporting (72h, where feasible). Distinct from CSIRT, MSA, AI Office, and competent authority. The 'where feasible' qualifier is unique to GDPR among the 5 regulations.

nodes.label: Market Surveillance Authority (MSA)
nodes.rationale: Recipient for AI Act high-risk AI serious incident reports (Art. 73) and CRA manufacturer cooperation (Art. 13(22)). MS-determined routing channel; may go to multiple MSAs when incident spans jurisdictions.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 Mapping (RS Domain)
nodes.rationale: Mapping dominated by RS.CO-04 (incident info shared with stakeholders) and RS.MA-01/02/03 (incident management). CSF surface is consistent — no cross-mapping conflict. Conflict is purely at timeline and recipient level, which is a regulatory-orchestration concern not a CSF construct.

nodes.label: Recipient Fragmentation (5 Distinct Classes)
nodes.rationale: 5 regulations notify to 5 distinct recipient classes (DPA, CSIRT, MSA, competent authority, AI Office) with overlapping but non-identical event triggers. Non-pairwise additivity is the routing complexity — no single regulation specifies how to route an event satisfying multiple triggers simultaneously.

nodes.label: Twin-Trigger Temporal Pattern
nodes.rationale: Recurring pattern across NIS2, CRA, and GDPR: 'without undue delay AND in any event within X hours' — the soft trigger plus hard ceiling conjunction. Identified as the dominant temporal coordination pattern in the corpus.

nodes.label: AI Act Article 73 (Serious Incident Reporting)
nodes.rationale: Most temporally complex notification clause in the AEGIS corpus. 4-trigger x 4-timeline matrix: 15d default, 10d death, 2d widespread infringement, 15d causal-link-anchor. Exceeds any other regulator's single-clock pattern.

nodes.label: NIS2 Twin-Trigger Notification (24h/72h/1m)
nodes.rationale: MUST-priority audit requirement mandating 3-tier temporal discipline for significant incident notification to CSIRT or competent authority, with the 'in any event' ceiling as NIS2-unique binding rule overriding GDPR 'where feasible' softening.

nodes.label: AI Act 4-Trigger x 4-Timeline Serious Incident Reporting
nodes.rationale: MUST-priority requirement described as the most temporally complex notification clause in the AEGIS corpus; 4-trigger x 4-timeline matrix (15d/10d/2d/causal-link) plus separate GPAI Art. 55 pathway to AI Office.
nodes.norm_label: ai act 4-trigger x 4-timeline serious incident reporting

nodes.label: DORA Art. 12 — Backup and Restoration
nodes.rationale: Art. 12(1) backup policies based on criticality/confidentiality plus restoration and recovery procedures.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 13 — Training and Post-Incident Review
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(6) compulsory ICT security awareness and digital operational resilience training.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 13 — training and post-incident review

nodes.label: DORA Art. 21 Security Rules Document
nodes.rationale: Per-article split of DORA Art. 21 containing SRs for change management, training, risk framework, three-lines-of-defence, asset inventory, monitoring, and information security policy.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 24: Digital operational resilience testing
nodes.rationale: Art. 24(1) sound and comprehensive testing programme as integral part of framework. Art. 24(7) RTS mandate pending.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 24: digital operational resilience testing

nodes.label: SO-NIS2-006: 24h Early Warning + 72h Incident Notification
nodes.rationale: Twin-trigger notification: 24h early warning (Art. 23(4)(a)) + 72h incident notification (Art. 23(4)(b)). 'Without undue delay' is primary trigger; 24h/72h are hard ceilings. Significant-incident test via Art. 23(3) test A or B.

nodes.label: SO-NIS2-007: Final Incident Report (1 Month)
nodes.rationale: Art. 23(4)(d) final report not later than 1 month after 72h notification. Four-part structure: description, root cause, mitigation measures, cross-border impact.

nodes.label: SO-NIS2-009: TSP 24h Notification Derogation
nodes.rationale: Art. 23(4) para 2 derogation for trust service providers. 24h regardless of 72h/1m tier structure. Applies to eIDAS-defined TSPs per Art. 6(24) cross-reference.

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-010: 24-Hour Early-Warning Notification
nodes.rationale: Maps to NIST CSF RS.CO-04, RS.MA-02. Twin-trigger: 'without undue delay' primary + 24h hard ceiling. 'Becoming aware' - literal OJ reading (actual awareness) vs dominant CJEU reading (constructive awareness).

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-011: 72-Hour Incident Notification with Initial Assessment
nodes.rationale: Maps to NIST CSF RS.CO-04, RS.MA-03. Updates 24h early warning with severity, impact, IoCs. 'Where available' hedge on IoC inclusion - best-effort, not exhaustive.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-011: 72-hour incident notification with initial assessment

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-012: One-Month Final Report
nodes.rationale: Maps to NIST CSF RS.CO-04, RC.RP-06. 1-month clock runs from 72h notification submission. Four-part structure: description, root cause, mitigation, cross-border impact.

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-044: Notification Routing Between Competent Authorities and CSIRTs
nodes.rationale: Maps to NIST CSF RS.CO-04, GV.OC-03. Authority-side obligation (not entity-side). CA forwards to CSIRT 'upon receipt' - immediate reading. MS-determined routing architecture.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-044: notification routing between competent authorities and csirts

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-045: Good-Faith Notification Liability Shield
nodes.rationale: Maps to NIST CSF GV.OC-03. Art. 23(1) para 1 fourth sentence. Legal-incentive instrument preventing chilling effect. Shield is relative-to-non-notifying-baseline, not absolute. Does not protect from liability for underlying incident.

nodes.label: CRA-CL139: Annex I Part I (2)(j) limit attack surfaces
nodes.norm_label: cra-cl139: annex i part i (2)(j) limit attack surfaces

nodes.label: CRA-CL14: Art. 13(1) design/development/production duty
nodes.rationale: Umbrella design-and-development duty on manufacturers, executed in three sequenced phases (designed, developed, produced).

nodes.label: DORA-D10 — 'Major ICT-Related Incident' (S3 regress)
nodes.rationale: S3 regress — inherits from Art. 3(22) 'critical or important function' (DORA-D22 tautology). The 'high adverse impact' threshold is undefined at OJ level; materiality thresholds delegated to Art. 18(3) RTS.

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 12(1) — Automatic Recording of Events (Logs)
nodes.rationale: Requires high-risk AI systems to technically allow automatic recording of events over the lifetime of the system. Log-generation substrate for post-market monitoring. Mirrors DORA Art. 12 and NIS 2 Art. 21 log-retention duties.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 12(1) — automatic recording of events (logs)

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 19(1) — Six-Month Minimum Log Retention
nodes.rationale: Only hard numeric anchor for retention duration across the AI Act. Escape clause defers to GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), NIS 2 incident-log retention, and DORA Art. 12. T5 mapping error: AIA-C11 references non-existent Art. 12(4); substance is in Art. 19(1).
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 19(1) — six-month minimum log retention

nodes.label: DORA Art. 10 — Detection
nodes.rationale: Detection mechanisms for anomalous activities and SPOFs, multi-layer controls, alert thresholds, sufficient monitoring resources, and DRSP-specific trade report checking. 4 paragraphs.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 11 — Response and Recovery
nodes.rationale: Establishes comprehensive ICT BCP with 5 enumerated aims, recovery plans, BIA, BCP testing (yearly), crisis management function, records, CSD reporting, and cost reporting. 11 paragraphs covering the full response-recovery lifecycle.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 12 — Backup Policies and Restoration
nodes.rationale: Backup policies, physically/logically segregated restoration, redundant ICT capacities, CSD secondary processing site, RTO/RPO objectives, and data integrity checks. 7 paragraphs establishing the recovery infrastructure requirements.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 12 — backup policies and restoration

nodes.label: DORA Art. 13 — Learning and Evolving
nodes.rationale: Closes the loop with Learn-Evolve: threat-intel capability, post-incident reviews, lessons propagation into risk assessment, effectiveness monitoring, training, and technology monitoring. 7 paragraphs.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 14 — Communication
nodes.rationale: Crisis communication plans, responsible disclosure of major incidents/vulnerabilities, internal/external communication policies, and designated public/media function person. 3 paragraphs.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 17 — ICT-Related Incident Management Process
nodes.rationale: Define/establish/implement incident management process, recording, early warning indicators, classification procedures, roles, communication plans, senior management escalation, and response procedures. 3 paragraphs with 6 sub-points.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 17 — ict-related incident management process

nodes.label: DORA Art. 18 — Classification of ICT-Related Incidents and Cyber Threats
nodes.rationale: 6 multiplicative criteria for classifying incidents + 3 for cyber threats. Delegates combination rule and materiality thresholds to ESA RTS (Art. 18(3)). Deadline 17 January 2024.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 18 — classification of ict-related incidents and cyber threats

nodes.label: DORA Art. 25 — Testing of ICT Tools and Systems
nodes.rationale: Open list of 12 test modalities (vulnerability assessments through penetration testing). CSD/CCP pre-deployment requirement. Microenterprise exception.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 25 — testing of ict tools and systems

nodes.label: DORA Art. 8 — Identification
nodes.rationale: Identify/classify/document ICT-supported business functions, continuous risk-source identification, major-change risk assessment, legacy ICT assessment, critical-asset mapping, inventory, and TPP dependency mapping. 7 paragraphs.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-09.3: Governance — Documentation
nodes.rationale: Documentation sub-domain within Governance. Locus for asset inventory and classification obligations.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 7(1): ICT asset identification and classification
nodes.rationale: Inventory-onboarding substrate for every downstream obligation. OJ-corrective note flags potential misattribution to Art. 8(1).
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 7(1): ict asset identification and classification

nodes.label: CRA Support Period (Art. 13(8)-(9))
nodes.rationale: Minimum 5 years or expected use time if shorter. Security updates available for at least 10 years after issuance or remainder of support period. End-date must be communicated at purchase (month + year).

nodes.label: CRA Art. 33 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering vulnerability remediation (Annex I Part II (2)) and AEV notification obligations; no standalone SO row but covered via SRs.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 6 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering secure-by-default configuration, cryptographic key separation, update dissemination, and cross-referenced AEV/severe-incident rules.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 30 (Contractual Arrangements)
nodes.rationale: DORA article governing minimum contractual elements, audit rights, and exit strategies for ICT third-party service provider arrangements.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 GV.SC (Supply Chain) Controls
nodes.rationale: Group of NIST CSF 2.0 supply chain governance controls (GV.SC-01 through GV.SC-04) providing the operational mapping target for DORA third-party risk obligations.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 28 Security Rules Document
nodes.rationale: Per-article split of DORA Art. 28 covering third-party risk management, standards compliance, contractual elements, and audit rights.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 32 Security Rules Document
nodes.rationale: Per-article split of DORA Art. 32 covering BC implementation arrangements and third-party standards compliance.

nodes.label: DORA-D29 — ICT Concentration Risk
nodes.rationale: Definitional anchor for 'high concentration of sensitive information' in Art. 21(2)(b). Same Berry pattern as the Single EU Hub risk assessment.

nodes.label: DORA Proportionality Formulation (Art. 4)
nodes.rationale: Five-factor proportionality: size + risk profile + nature + scale + complexity of services/activities/operations. Berry pattern (5-way AND). Applied to Art. 20 time limits and sectoral specificities.

nodes.label: Responsibility Non-Delegation Principle
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation principle: a financial entity cannot outsource its reporting compliance by outsourcing the reporting process. Consistent across DORA Art. 19(5), Art. 26(3), Art. 22(1); GDPR Art. 28(4); NIS 2 Art. 21(1).

nodes.label: Single EU Hub (DORA Art. 21 concept)
nodes.rationale: Architectural concept for centralised incident reporting. Three readings: centralised platform, API gateway, or single standard. Structurally analogous to NIS 2 SPOC (Art. 12) and CER Directive critical-entity framework but at higher integration level.

nodes.label: DORA Ch. III Deep Analysis (Art. 20-21, Art. 19(5))
nodes.rationale: Layer 1 catalogue of DORA Articles 20, 21, and 19(5) covering RTS/ITS mandates, Single EU Hub feasibility, and outsourcing responsibility non-delegation principle.
nodes.norm_label: dora ch. iii deep analysis (art. 20-21, art. 19(5))

nodes.label: DORA Art. 19(5) — Outsourcing + Responsibility Clause
nodes.rationale: Permits outsourcing of reporting obligations to third-party service providers while the financial entity remains fully responsible. Embodies the responsibility non-delegation principle consistent across Ch. III, Ch. IV, and Art. 22(1).

nodes.label: DORA Art. 20 — ESAs RTS/ITS Mandate
nodes.rationale: Pure RTS+ITS delegation of Ch. III. Mandates ESAs to develop common draft RTS (report content, time limits, cyber-threat notification) and ITS (standard forms, templates, procedures). Deadline: 17 July 2024.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 21 — Single EU Hub Feasibility Mandate
nodes.rationale: Meta-procedural mandate on ESAs (not entity-facing) to assess feasibility of centralising incident reporting through a single EU Hub. 7 required elements (a)-(g). Deadline: 17 January 2025. Report published Q1 2025.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 21 — single eu hub feasibility mandate

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28(4) — Processor Obligations
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation consistency: processor obligations do not discharge controller obligations. Same pattern as DORA Art. 19(5) responsibility non-delegation.

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 12 — Single Point of Contact (SPOC)
nodes.rationale: Structural analogue to DORA Single EU Hub concept, but at a lower integration level. Referenced as cross-regulation comparison point.
nodes.norm_label: nis 2 art. 12 — single point of contact (spoc)

nodes.label: Reg. (EU) 2024/2956 — DORA Implementing Regulation
nodes.rationale: Substantially implements Art. 20 mandates: Annex II (report content + time limits), Annex III (cyber-threat notification), Annex IV (standard forms/templates/procedures). Adopted as of mid-2025.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 5(2): Management body oversight and accountability
nodes.rationale: Provides the accountability link for all SRs: management body must present documented evidence trail to competent authorities. The 'approved' qualifier in Art. 9(4)(d) is binding under this article.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 5(2): management body oversight and accountability

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4): Mandatory ICT security control domains
nodes.rationale: Chapeau establishing eight mandatory control domains. Art. 9(4)(b) network management, (c) access control, (d) cryptographic keys, (f) patches and updates are all sub-paragraphs of this article.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 9(4): mandatory ict security control domains

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 21(2): Parallel obligations for NSIEs
nodes.rationale: Supplies parallel regime for non-financial NSIEs. DORA financial entities retain joint obligation where they also operate as NIS 2 entities. Referenced across multiple SRs for cross-regulatory alignment.
nodes.norm_label: nis 2 art. 21(2): parallel obligations for nsies

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-07.4: Secure Development — Change Management
nodes.rationale: Change management sub-domain within Secure Development. Locus for Art. 9(4)(e) six-step change management process.
nodes.norm_label: sub-domain d-07.4: secure development — change management

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-10.1: Monitoring & Audit
nodes.rationale: Monitoring sub-domain. Locus for continuous risk identification and audit obligations.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 13 — Security Objectives & Security Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering ICT security awareness training, risk identification, patch governance, change management, and asset inventory.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 13 — security objectives & security rules

nodes.label: SO-NIS2-008: Ongoing incident progress report + closing final report
nodes.rationale: Covers Art. 23(4)(e). Sub-domain D-04.3.
nodes.norm_label: so-nis2-008: ongoing incident progress report + closing final report

nodes.label: SO-NIS2-010: Intermediate report on CSIRT/CA request
nodes.rationale: Covers Art. 23(4)(c). Sub-domain D-04.3.
nodes.norm_label: so-nis2-010: intermediate report on csirt/ca request

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-013: Progress and closing reports for ongoing incidents
nodes.rationale: Art. 23(4)(e) ongoing incident progress + closing report. Mapped to NIST CSF RS.CO-04 and RC.RP-06.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-013: progress and closing reports for ongoing incidents

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-015: On-demand intermediate status reports to the CSIRT
nodes.rationale: Art. 23(4)(c) intermediate report on CSIRT request. Mapped to NIST CSF RS.CO-04 and RS.AN-07.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-015: on-demand intermediate status reports to the csirt

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.SC-05: Response and recovery planning and testing with suppliers
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF 2.0 subcategory for third-party-response discipline in cross-border notification.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.sc-05: response and recovery planning and testing with suppliers

nodes.label: NIST CSF RC.RP-06: End of incident recovery declared and after-action review completed
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF 2.0 subcategory for recovery-completion discipline in final report and ongoing incident closure.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rc.rp-06: end of incident recovery declared and after-action review completed

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 19 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering NIS2 Article 19 with the liability-shield rule SR-NIS2-045 for good-faith incident notification.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 23 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering NIS2 Article 23 incident notification architecture: 24h early warning, 72h notification, 1-month final report, TSP derogation, cross-border notification, and recipient notification.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 33 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering NIS2 Article 33 with the liability-shield rule SR-NIS2-045 cross-referenced from Art. 23(1) ¶1.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13 — Security Objectives & Security Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split (SO + SR) generated from 01_SecurityObjectives.md and 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md. Covers manufacturer obligations for products with digital elements across 10+ domains (D-02 through D-10). Status: DRAFT.
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 13 — security objectives & security rules

nodes.label: CRA Annex I Part II — Vulnerability Handling Requirements
nodes.rationale: Essential requirements for vulnerability handling: identify/document (Part II(1)), effective/regular tests (Part II(3)), public disclosure (Part II(4)), CVD policy (Part II(5)), sharing (Part II(6)), secure update distribution (Part II(7)), dissemination (Part II(8)).
nodes.norm_label: cra annex i part ii — vulnerability handling requirements

nodes.label: CRA Annex VII — Technical Documentation Requirements
nodes.rationale: Technical documentation content: SBOM (§2(b)), risk-assessment documentation (§3), support-period info (§4), test reports (§6), SBOM on MSA request (§8).
nodes.norm_label: cra annex vii — technical documentation requirements

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21 — Security Objectives & Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split generated from 01_SecurityObjectives.md and 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md; originals remain authoritative aggregate indexes.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 9 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split (SO + SR) generated from 01_SecurityObjectives.md and 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md covering GDPR Article 9 special-category data processing, consent, lawfulness bases, and related obligations.

nodes.label: ISO/IEC 27001: Information security management
nodes.rationale: Functions as a reference framework (not technology selection) for the EU-acceptable floor of information security standards under DORA Art. 28(5).

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.RA-02: Threat and vulnerability information collected
nodes.rationale: Threat and vulnerability information from internal and external sources collected and used to support risk identification; closes threat-intelligence loop for due diligence.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.ra-02: threat and vulnerability information collected

nodes.label: DORA Art. 28(5): ICT third-party standards compliance
nodes.rationale: Central DORA ambiguity: OJ text does not name a specific standard. ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2, NIST CSF, CIS Controls, and ENISA guidance are all plausible reference points. EBA RTS under Art. 28(9) expected to refine.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 28(5): ict third-party standards compliance

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 25(1) — Privacy by Design
nodes.rationale: Requires controller to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures (pseudonymisation, minimisation) both at determination of means and at processing itself, considering state of the art, cost, nature, scope, context, purposes, and risks.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 6(1)(a)-(f) — Six Lawfulness Bases
nodes.rationale: Six bases: consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public interest, legitimate interests; each carries its own qualifiers and necessity gating.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 9(1) — Special-Category Data Prohibition
nodes.rationale: Nine conjunctive categories each independently triggering prohibition; processing only permitted under one of ten Art. 9(2) exceptions.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-06.3: Supply Chain — Cross-Border Transfers
nodes.norm_label: sub-domain d-06.3: supply chain — cross-border transfers

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-05.1: Data Lifecycle (Minimisation)
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation domain for data minimisation, purpose limitation, and compatibility.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-09.1: Governance (Accountability & Lawfulness)
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation domain for controller accountability, lawfulness bases, and governance documentation.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 49(1) — Derogations for Transfers
nodes.rationale: Seven disjunctive grounds plus catch-all. Applies only absent adequacy decision (Art. 45(3)) and Art. 46 appropriate safeguards.

nodes.label: GDPR-NIS2 Timeline Contradiction
nodes.rationale: GDPR 72h has 'where feasible' softening; NIS2 72h has 'in any event' hard ceiling. On confirmed same-party overlap, NIS2's 72h is the operative binding deadline. Baseline is scope-disjoint; contradiction only on confirmed overlap.

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 73 — Serious Incident Reporting (15/10/2 day timelines)
nodes.rationale: Most temporally complex notification clause in the AEGIS corpus. Three numerical timelines (15/2/10 days) × two attribution thresholds (awareness OR reasonable likelihood). Cross-regulation parallel to DORA Art. 19 and NIS 2 Art. 23.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 73 — serious incident reporting (15/10/2 day timelines)

nodes.label: DORA Article 19 (Incident Reporting)
nodes.rationale: Parallel CA + client notification tracks. Art. 19(3) client notification conditional on financial-interest impact (OJ-corrective note). Temporal anchor delegated to RTS. DORA 'without undue delay' is functionally shorter than GDPR 72h in practice.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 20 — Harmonisation of Reporting Content and Templates
nodes.rationale: Pure RTS/ITS delegation — content, time limits, and templates wholly dependent on ESAs Joint Committee output. Deadline 17 July 2024. Adopted as Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2956.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 20 — harmonisation of reporting content and templates

nodes.label: DORA Art. 23 — Ch. III Extension to Payment-Sector Entities
nodes.rationale: Extends entire Ch. III to operational/security payment-related incidents for CIs, PIs, AISPs, EMIs. DORA↔PSD2 integration point. Supersedes PSD2 Art. 96(1) reporting architecture for these entity types.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 23 — ch. iii extension to payment-sector entities

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33 — Breach Notification (72h)
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation parallel for notification timelines. Same awareness-trigger ambiguity pattern ('becomes aware'). DORA's sector-differentiated approach vs GDPR's uniform 72h.

nodes.label: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2956 — DORA Reporting Templates
nodes.rationale: Adopted 18 July 2024. Contains Annex I–IV templates for reporting. Partially addresses Art. 20 RTS/ITS mandate. Per-tier time limits layered with sectoral differentiation.

nodes.label: NIS2 Article 23 (Reporting Obligations)
nodes.rationale: Second-most-consequential article in NIS2 for software-compliance. Defines 3-tier incident-reporting architecture (24h/72h/1m) running parallel to GDPR Art. 33/34 and CRA Art. 14. 22 atomic clauses (CL26-CL47).

nodes.label: DORA Major ICT Incident CA + Client Notification
nodes.rationale: MUST-priority requirement with parallel CA + client tracks; temporal anchor delegated to EBA/ESMA/EIOPA RTS under Art. 18(3); DORA 'without undue delay' is the operative ceiling over GDPR 'where feasible' in multi-reg overlap.
nodes.norm_label: dora major ict incident ca + client notification

nodes.label: NIST CSF DE.AE-03: Event Data Collected and Correlated from Multiple Sources
nodes.rationale: Multi-source correlation for RoPA across systems. Mapped by SR-GDPR-050.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf de.ae-03: event data collected and correlated from multiple sources

nodes.label: DORA-D22 — 'Critical or Important Function' (tautological definition)
nodes.rationale: S3 regress — tautological definition flagged at pilot file §2.7. Propagates to every clause referencing 'critical or important functions'. The criticality threshold is undefined (entity-determined per literal reading).

nodes.label: CRA Annex I Part I §1 — Product Design/Development/Production
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation comparison: 3 verbs (design, develop, produce) describing processes not qualities. DORA's triad describes qualities of an artifact (the framework itself) — a different kind of obligation.
nodes.norm_label: cra annex i part i §1 — product design/development/production

nodes.label: DORA Art. 16 — Simplified ICT Risk Management Framework
nodes.rationale: Structurally parallel to Art. 9(4) hinge but at lower operational granularity. Exempts 5 entity categories from Arts 5-15. Deliberate regulatory choice: small entities exempted from most operationally demanding controls (access control, change management, patches as standalone families).
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 16 — simplified ict risk management framework

nodes.label: DORA Art. 24 — General Requirements for Digital Operational Resilience Testing
nodes.rationale: Testing programme as integral part of Art. 6 framework. Risk-based approach, independence, remediation, yearly cadence. 6 paragraphs.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 24 — general requirements for digital operational resilience testing

nodes.label: DORA Art. 26 — TLPT (Threat-Led Penetration Testing)
nodes.rationale: Mandates TLPT on hard 3-year cadence, anchored to TIBER-EU framework (non-binding). Binding-to-non-binding definitional regress pattern same as CRA Annex I → ISO standards.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 6(1) — ICT Risk Management Framework (3-attribute triad)
nodes.rationale: The framework-level chapeau requiring 'sound, comprehensive and well-documented' — identified as the most demanding framework chapeau in the 5-regulation corpus. Sets the bar for every Ch. II–V Sec. I clause.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 6(1) — ict risk management framework (3-attribute triad)

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 21(1) — Appropriate and Proportionate Measures
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation comparison: uses 'appropriate and proportionate' (2 qualifiers) vs DORA's 3-attribute triad. DORA's triad is the most demanding framework-quality specification in the corpus.
nodes.norm_label: nis 2 art. 21(1) — appropriate and proportionate measures

nodes.label: TIBER-EU — ECB Threat Intelligence-Based EU Framework
nodes.rationale: Non-binding ECB framework that DORA Art. 26(11) references for TLPT. Binding-to-non-binding definitional regress pattern — same as CRA Annex I → ISO standards.
nodes.norm_label: tiber-eu — ecb threat intelligence-based eu framework

nodes.label: Instruction-bound processing under least-privilege authorisation
nodes.rationale: Operationalises GDPR Arts. 29, 32(4), 28(3)(a)/(b) chain-of-authority pattern via NIST CSF PR.AA-05 and PR.AA-06, binding natural persons to documented instructions with Union/Member State law as sole exception.

nodes.label: Confidentiality undertakings for authorised personnel
nodes.rationale: Creates a confidentiality ring around any natural person accessing personal data via Art. 28(3)(b), independent of the instruction obligation; operationalised through PR.AA-05 and PR.AT-02.

nodes.label: DPO-driven GDPR awareness and role-specific training
nodes.rationale: Art. 39(1)(a)/(b) DPO as internal awareness catalyst; split into general-population (annual) and role-specific (quarterly/event-triggered) training. Operationalised via PR.AT-01 and PR.AT-02.
nodes.norm_label: dpo-driven gdpr awareness and role-specific training

nodes.label: Access control policies + HR security + asset management (SO-NIS2-003)
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(i) security objective: access control limited to authorised users on least-privilege basis, covering HR security and asset management.
nodes.norm_label: access control policies + hr security + asset management (so-nis2-003)

nodes.label: Basic cyber hygiene practices (SO-NIS2-018)
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(g) security objective: basic cyber hygiene practices covering all users of NIS with access to entity systems.

nodes.label: Identity and access-control policy foundation
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(i) three-domain AND (HR security + access control + asset management); model-agnostic; least-privilege principle. Operationalised via PR.AA-01 and PR.AA-05.

nodes.label: Workforce identity lifecycle as HR-security substrate
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(i) HR-security dimension: joiner-mover-leaver lifecycle per ISO 27001:2022 A.6; role-based access transitions. Operationalised via PR.AT-02 and PR.AA-01.
nodes.norm_label: workforce identity lifecycle as hr-security substrate

nodes.label: Authoritative hardware, software, and information-asset inventories
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(i) asset-management dimension: cumulative (hardware + software + information) per ISO 27001:2022 A.5.9; living artefact. Operationalised via ID.AM-01 and ID.AM-02.
nodes.norm_label: authoritative hardware, software, and information-asset inventories

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 34(3): Exceptions to data-subject notification
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 34(3): exceptions to data-subject notification

nodes.label: Actively Exploited Vulnerability (CRA Art. 14)
nodes.rationale: CRA-specific notification trigger for manufacturer awareness of actively exploited vulnerabilities. Dual-track with severe incident. 14-day final report tier is CRA-unique and tighter than NIS2's 1-month.

nodes.label: CRA-DORA Scope-Disjoint Baseline
nodes.rationale: Clearest P0 case: CRA duties on manufacturer, DORA on financial entity. In common case, a bank using a CRA-regulated product is not the manufacturer. CRDA's unconditional 'contradictory' is scope-incorrect for baseline; should be supply-chain notification hand-off.

nodes.label: CRA Severe Incident (Art. 14(5))
nodes.rationale: Defined via two tests: (a) negatively affects CIA of sensitive/important data or functions; (b) led or capable of leading to malicious code introduction/execution. Same definitional regress pattern as NIS2 significant incident.

nodes.label: Definitional Regress Pattern
nodes.rationale: Three regulations, three different threshold terms (significant incident, severe incident, major ICT-related incident), zero cross-referenced definitions. Each uses vaguer terms than the term it defines. Art. 23(11) implementing acts expected to address but not yet published as of mid-2025.

nodes.label: DORA Major ICT-Related Incident (Art. 18)
nodes.rationale: Classification per Art. 18 criteria; temporal anchor delegated to EBA/ESMA/EIOPA RTS. DORA is lex specialis for financial entities, absorbing NIS2 ICT-hazard notification obligation.

nodes.label: NIS2 Significant Incident (Art. 23(3))
nodes.rationale: Defined via two tests: (a) severe operational disruption or financial loss; (b) considerable material or non-material damage to other persons. Suffers from definitional regress — uses vaguer terms (severe, considerable) than the term it defines.

nodes.label: CRA Article 14 (Reporting Obligations of Manufacturers)
nodes.rationale: Defines dual-track reporting architecture: AEV (24h/72h/14d) and severe incident (24h/72h/1m). 18 atomic clauses (CL51-CL68). 'Simultaneously' to CSIRT+ENISA is CRA-unique. Machine-readable user notification format is CRA-unique.

nodes.label: CRA AEV Three-Tier + SI Parallel Pathway Notification
nodes.rationale: MUST-priority requirement for dual-pathway discipline: AEV 24h/72h/14d and SI 24h/72h/1m, with the 14-day AEV final tier being CRA-unique and tighter than NIS2/DORA tiers.
nodes.norm_label: cra aev three-tier + si parallel pathway notification

nodes.label: CRA-CL135: Annex I Part I (2)(f) integrity + corruption reporting
nodes.norm_label: cra-cl135: annex i part i (2)(f) integrity + corruption reporting

nodes.label: CRA-CL141: Annex I Part I (2)(l) logging + monitoring
nodes.norm_label: cra-cl141: annex i part i (2)(l) logging + monitoring

nodes.label: CRA-CL21: Art. 13(4) sentence 1 include risk assessment in technical documentation
