nodes.norm_label: cra-cl21: art. 13(4) sentence 1 include risk assessment in technical documentation

nodes.label: CRA-CL22: Art. 13(4) sentence 2 AI Act carve-out
nodes.norm_label: cra-cl22: art. 13(4) sentence 2 ai act carve-out

nodes.label: CRA-CL48: Art. 13(23) cessation of operations notification
nodes.norm_label: cra-cl48: art. 13(23) cessation of operations notification

nodes.label: CRA-CL50: Art. 13(25) Union-wide dependency assessment by ADCO
nodes.norm_label: cra-cl50: art. 13(25) union-wide dependency assessment by adco

nodes.label: DORA Art. 10: Detection and incident management
nodes.rationale: Art. 10(1) establishes detection substrate; Art. 10(2) specifies operational shape (multiple layers, thresholds, triggers, automatic alerts). Chapter II Section II establishes detection that Chapter III operationalises into incident-management.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 10: detection and incident management

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 12: Transparent Information and Rights
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 12: transparent information and rights

nodes.label: Role: MANUFACTURER
nodes.rationale: Primary obligated role under CRA Art. 14 reporting chain. Also the role to which OSS stewards are equated for Art. 14(1) triggering.

nodes.label: CRA Article 14: Vulnerability handling and incident reporting
nodes.rationale: Core CRA article establishing the tiered reporting architecture: 24h/72h/14d/1m for severe incidents, AEV notification, user notification, CSIRT coordination, and implementing acts.
nodes.norm_label: cra article 14: vulnerability handling and incident reporting

nodes.label: Role: OSS_STEWARD
nodes.rationale: Defined in CRA Art. 3(14) as legal persons systematically providing support on sustained basis. Exception per Orchestrator brief — not in strict enum. Subject to Art. 24(3) extensions.

nodes.label: CRA Article 24: OSS steward obligations
nodes.rationale: Extends Art. 14(1) and Art. 14(3)/(8) to OSS stewards. Proportionality preserved by Recital 18. Steward not subject to manufacturer obligations beyond enumerated extensions.

nodes.label: GDPR Arts. 44-45: Cross-border transfer framework
nodes.rationale: Art. 44 umbrella principle. Art. 45(1) adequacy exemption. Art. 45(3) periodic review at least every 4 years. Schrems II essential-equivalence test as operational standard.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 47: Binding Corporate Rules
nodes.rationale: Art. 47(1) supervisory approval under consistency mechanism. Art. 47(2) 14 mandatory content items (closed list). Must be legally binding, confer enforceable rights, applied by every group member.

nodes.label: ENISA — EU Agency for Cybersecurity
nodes.rationale: Consulted by ESAs in developing RTS under Art. 15 and Art. 16(3). Also consulted in Art. 19(7) cross-MS assessment and Art. 21(2) single EU Hub feasibility.

nodes.label: ESAs Joint Committee (EBA + ESMA + EIOPA)
nodes.rationale: The body mandated to develop draft RTS under Art. 15 and Art. 20, in consultation with ENISA. Also responsible for cross-MS assessment under Art. 19(7) and yearly aggregated reports under Art. 22(2).

nodes.label: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1774 — DORA RTS for Art. 15(a)–(g)
nodes.rationale: Adopted by Commission on 31 May 2024 on basis of ESA Joint Committee draft. Supplements DORA with RTS for Art. 15(a)–(g). Resolves many S3 instances flagged in the analysis.
nodes.norm_label: delegated regulation (eu) 2024/1774 — dora rts for art. 15(a)–(g)

nodes.label: DORA Art. 21 — Centralisation of Reporting (Single EU Hub Feasibility)
nodes.rationale: Feasibility-report mandate on centralisation (single EU Hub). Joint ESA report in consultation with ECB, ENISA. 7 enumerated elements. Deadline 17 January 2025 (passed; report published Q1 2025).
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 21 — centralisation of reporting (single eu hub feasibility)

nodes.label: DORA Art. 22 — Supervisory Feedback

nodes.label: D-05.1 Data Minimisation
nodes.author: SubDomains merge (Executor sub-agent)
nodes.rationale: Unified view combining sub-domain definition, domain analysis, deep analysis, and ambiguity. Three participating regulations (GDPR, CRA, AI Act) each impose data minimisation on a distinct data class at a distinct trigger. NIS2 and DORA are out-of-scope per AEGIS taxonomy §4.1.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 6: Lawfulness of processing
nodes.rationale: Six lawfulness bases: consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public interest, legitimate interests. Bases (b)-(d) carry necessity qualifiers; (e) requires Union/MS law; (f) requires balancing test.

nodes.label: D-05.1 Data Lifecycle sub-domain
nodes.rationale: Data lifecycle sub-domain covering lawfulness bases, consent, special categories, and data governance practices across GDPR and AI Act.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 12 (Transparent Information and Communication)
nodes.rationale: Art. 12(6) permits identity verification where reasonable doubts exist; proportionate to risk of misidentification, not arbitrary document collection.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5 (Principles for Processing)
nodes.rationale: Foundational principles (lawfulness, purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity/confidentiality, accountability) referenced across multiple SRs as cross-cutting obligations.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 6 – Lawfulness of processing
nodes.rationale: Art. 6(1)(a)-(f) six lawfulness bases; Art. 6(4) compatibility test for further processing. Bases (b)-(f) carry 'necessary' qualifiers; (f) requires balancing test.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 9 – Processing of special categories of personal data
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(1) prohibition of nine special categories; Art. 9(2) ten exceptions. Art. 9(2)(a) explicit consent above Art. 4(11) baseline. Categories are conjunctive, each independently triggering prohibition.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 9 – processing of special categories of personal data

nodes.label: D-09.1 Governance-Documentation sub-domain
nodes.rationale: Governance and documentation sub-domain covering legal-basis documentation, consent records, DPO designation, and regulatory compliance processes.

nodes.label: EDPB Guidelines 02/2019 on Art. 6(1)(b)
nodes.rationale: Interprets necessary in Art. 6(1)(b) contract-necessity strictly; expansive reading treating any commercial reliance as satisfying necessity is rejected.

nodes.label: EDPB Guidelines 05/2020 on Consent
nodes.rationale: Interprets Art. 4(11) consent qualifiers as conjunctive (all four must be present simultaneously); §3.4 interprets explicit as additional layer on top of specific; §3.1 each element assessed independently.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 9: Special categories of personal data
nodes.rationale: General prohibition on processing special-category personal data. AI Act Art. 10(5) creates the exceptional gateway that deliberately crosses into this GDPR territory for bias detection and correction.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 9: special categories of personal data

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(13): 10-year documentation retention
nodes.rationale: Technical documentation and EU declaration at disposal of MSAs for 10 years or support period whichever longer; shared by SR-CRA-084, 086, 091.

nodes.label: CRA-CL14: Art. 13(1) design/develop/produce per Annex I Part I
nodes.rationale: Umbrella design-and-development duty on manufacturers across three sequenced phases.
nodes.norm_label: cra-cl14: art. 13(1) design/develop/produce per annex i part i

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 39(2) — DPO due regard to risk
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 39(2) — dpo due regard to risk

nodes.label: 3-Way Special-Category Emergent Tension
nodes.rationale: GDPR Art. 9(1) prohibits + AI Act Art. 10(5) creates exception + CRA silent on special-category. Non-pairwise observation: AI Act's exception enables a processing class neither GDPR nor CRA explicitly contemplates. Codified as gateway-clause architecture.

nodes.label: CRA ↔ AI Act Pair (COMPLEMENTARY)
nodes.rationale: Different lifecycle stages: CRA = runtime product data, AI Act = training pipeline data. Sequential not concurrent. AI Act quality criteria sharpen CRA runtime minimisation when same dataset flows through both.

nodes.label: GDPR ↔ AI Act Pair (SCOPE-DISJOINT + Carve-out)
nodes.rationale: CORRECTED from CONTRADICTORY to SCOPE-DISJOINT with explicit Art. 10(5) carve-out. Exception-permission pattern, not prohibition-vs-prohibition. Single overlap point: high-risk AI provider training with bias-detection needs that cannot be met by non-special-category data.

nodes.label: GDPR ↔ CRA Pair (COMPLEMENTARY)
nodes.rationale: Verbatim operative-language match: 'adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary'. Controller-driven purpose vs manufacturer-design intended purpose. Stricter operational interpretation binds on shared data stream. Art. 6(4) compatibility test is residual GDPR-only requirement.

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-004 — Special Category Gateway
nodes.rationale: Art. 10(5) exceptional special-category processing. CSF: PR.DS-12, PR.DS-01, GV.OC-03. `strictly necessary` and `appropriate safeguards` are Berry-classic vague terms. 6 sub-conditions AND-coordinated.

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-005 — Dataset Quality Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Art. 10(3) 4-criterion quality: relevant, sufficiently representative, free of errors, complete. CSF: PR.DS-12, PR.DS-01. Hedge-AND coordination problem: chosen strict reading binds hedge only to last two criteria.

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-006 — Exceptional Special-Category Processing
nodes.rationale: Art. 10(5) gateway into GDPR Art. 9(1). CSF: PR.DS-12, PR.DS-01, GV.OC-03. Pseudonymisation, differential-privacy, federated-learning as state-of-the-art privacy-preserving measures. Cross-regulation scope ambiguity with GDPR Art. 9(2) bases applying in parallel.

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 10(5) — Special Category Gateway
nodes.rationale: 6 cumulative conditions (a)–(f) all required: bias detection cannot be achieved by other data + strict necessity + safeguards + enhanced governance + documentation + post-correction deletion. Creates a conditional exception to GDPR Art. 9(1). The single point where data minimisation is relaxed by one of the three regulations.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 10(5) — special category gateway

nodes.label: CRA Annex I Part I (2)(g) — Product Data Minimisation
nodes.rationale: Verbatim: 'the processing of only the data that are adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary in relation to the intended purpose of the product.' Manufacturer-design driven, product data scope (personal or other). Tied to Art. 3(23) intended purpose.
nodes.norm_label: cra annex i part i (2)(g) — product data minimisation

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 9(1) — Special Category Prohibition
nodes.rationale: Prohibits processing of special-category personal data absent Art. 9(2) basis. AI Act Art. 10(5) creates a conditional exception (gateway) into this prohibition for bias detection/correction in high-risk AI systems.

nodes.label: Req 5.1 — Multi-class Data Minimisation
nodes.rationale: Volere requirement (section 15, privacy subtype, MUST priority, TEST verification). Derives from SO-D-05.1.HL. NIST CSF: PR.DS-12, ID.AM-03, GV.OC-03, GV.PO-01, PR.PS-06, PR.DS-01. Applicable to GDPR, CRA, AI_ACT with conditional scope overlap.

nodes.label: Req 5.1.1 — Personal-data Minimisation
nodes.rationale: GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) + Art. 6(4) compatibility + Art. 9(1) prohibition + Art. 25 by-design/by-default + Art. 35 DPIA. Derives from SO-D-05.1.GDPR. Dependencies on 5.1.2 and 5.1.3 for cross-regulation interactions.

nodes.label: Req 5.1.2 — Product-data Minimisation
nodes.rationale: CRA Annex I Part I (2)(g) + Art. 3(23) intended purpose + Art. 13(2) risk assessment. Derives from SO-D-05.1.CRA. INSPECT verification. Dependencies on 5.1.1 and 5.1.3.

nodes.label: Req 5.1.3 — Training-data Quality
nodes.rationale: AI Act Art. 10(1)/(2)/(3) quality criteria + Art. 10(5) 6-cumulative-condition gateway. Derives from SO-D-05.1.AIACT. TEST verification. Dependencies on 5.1.1 and 5.1.2.

nodes.label: SO-D-05.1.AIACT (AI Act Sub-SO)
nodes.rationale: High-risk AI training-data quality per Art. 10(1)/(2)/(3) with Art. 10(5) 6-cumulative-condition special-category gateway. Inherits from SO-AIACT-003, SO-AIACT-004. CSF anchors: ID.AM-03, PR.DS-12, PR.PS-06, PR.DS-01, GV.OC-03. Operates upstream on training pipeline.

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-019: Deployer measures aligned with provider instructions for use
nodes.rationale: Art. 26(1) requires deployers to take appropriate technical and organisational measures to use systems per provider instructions. Deployer-side mirror of provider QMS obligation under Art. 17. Inherits cross-regulation reading from GDPR Art. 5(1)(f) and NIS 2 Art. 21(1).
nodes.norm_label: sr-aiact-019: deployer measures aligned with provider instructions for use

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 34: Communication of Breach to Data Subject
nodes.rationale: Art. 34(1) high-risk notification duty. Art. 34(3)(a) exemption when data rendered unintelligible. Two conditions: measures applied to affected data, key unavailable to unauthorised parties.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 34: communication of breach to data subject

nodes.label: Req 5.3.1: GDPR Personal-Data Erasure
nodes.rationale: MUST: Erase personal data on Art. 17(1) request (6 grounds); processor deletes/returns per Art. 28(3)(g); cryptographic key destruction as deletion path. NIST CSF: PR.DS-10, PR.DS-12, GV.SC-04.

nodes.label: Req 5.3.2: CRA Manufacturer-Side Removal
nodes.rationale: MUST: User can securely and easily remove all data and settings via discoverable UI affordance, with Annex II 8(d) decommissioning instructions. NIST CSF: PR.DS-10, PR.DS-12.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-048: CRA Terminal Deletion
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part I (2)(m) first limb: secure permanent removal of all data. VAG+COORD-S2 (secure AND easy) + POLY-VAG-S2 (permanent = recovery-infeasible). Mapped to PR.DS-10, PR.DS-12.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-049: CRA Secure Cross-Product Transfer
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part I (2)(m) second limb: secure transfer to other products/systems. Mapped to PR.DS-02, PR.DS-12.

nodes.label: Berry & Kamsties (2000) — Legal text ambiguity framework
nodes.rationale: Analytical framework used throughout: §3.3.1 (polysemy, universal quantifiers), §5.1 (vague terms), §5.4.7 (AND/OR structure), §5.7 (temporal operators). S2/S3 severity classification.
nodes.norm_label: berry & kamsties (2000) — legal text ambiguity framework

nodes.label: DORA Art. 19(4) — Three-tier reporting (initial/intermediate/final)
nodes.rationale: None of the time limits live in OJ. The OJ text references an RTS (Art. 20(a)(ii)) that was not in force at adoption. As of mid-2025, Reg. (EU) 2024/2956 Annex II partially fills the gap. Structurally identical to NIS 2 Art. 23(4) in spirit but sector-differentiated.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 19(7) — ESAs/ECB cross-MS assessment + notification
nodes.rationale: Relevance assessment delegated to ESAs/ECB. Criteria live in Art. 18(3)(b) RTS. OJ-level cross-MS relevance is framework-only.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 19(7) — esas/ecb cross-ms assessment + notification

nodes.label: DORA Art. 19(8) — ESMA + host-MS transmission (CSD carve-out)
nodes.rationale: Three trigger conditions AND'd: CSD cross-border activity, likely severe consequences for host MS markets, cooperation arrangements exist. 'likely' and 'severe consequences' both undefined (Berry cluster).
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 19(8) — esma + host-ms transmission (csd carve-out)

nodes.label: DORA Art. 5(1) — Internal governance and control framework
nodes.rationale: Three materially distinct readings of 'internal governance and control framework': three lines of defence, two lines of defence, or any recognised internal-control model. R3 is the literal reading per Art. 6(4) option.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 5(1) — internal governance and control framework

nodes.label: EDPB Guidelines 5/2020 on storage limitation
nodes.rationale: Disambiguation source for R1 reading of 'deletes' as cryptographic erasure (key destruction). Also referenced for pseudonymised data still being personal data.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28(3)(g) — Data return or deletion (processor-side obligation)
nodes.rationale: Berry-flagged POLY-S3 on 'deletes' with three operational senses: physical destruction, logical deletion, cryptographic erasure. GDPR does not specify which. R1 (cryptographic erasure) vs R3 (physical destruction) yield materially distinct deletion-engineering requirements.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 28(3)(g) — data return or deletion (processor-side obligation)

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 23 — Incident reporting (24h/72h/1-month)
nodes.rationale: Uniform template for incident reporting. DORA Art. 19(4) is structurally identical in spirit but sector-differentiated rather than uniform. NIS 2 Art. 23(2) is recipient-directed; DORA Art. 19(2) is CA-directed.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(10): Substantial-modification last-version compliance
nodes.rationale: Carve-out allowing Annex I Part II(2) compliance for last-placed version where user-migration conditions met; shared by SR-CRA-070 and SR-CRA-089.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 21: Manufacturer-equivalent trigger
nodes.rationale: Importer/distributor placing under own name or substantial modifier inherits manufacturer obligations; shared by SR-CRA-070, 090, 092.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 34 – Communication of personal data breach to data subject
nodes.rationale: Art. 34(1) high-risk trigger; Art. 34(2) content requirement; Art. 34(3)(a) encryption exception; Art. 34(3)(b) subsequent-measures exception; Art. 34(3)(c) disproportionate-effort exception. Higher threshold than Art. 33.

nodes.norm_label: sub-domain d-04.3 – breach response and notification

nodes.label: SO-AIACT-005: Automatic event logging and traceability
nodes.rationale: High-risk AI systems technically allow automatic recording of events over lifetime with traceability appropriate to intended purpose. Art. 12(1)+(2).
nodes.norm_label: so-aiact-005: automatic event logging and traceability

nodes.label: SO-AIACT-006: Provider log retention 6-month floor
nodes.rationale: Providers keep logs for period appropriate to intended purpose, minimum 6 months, unless provided otherwise in Union or national law. Art. 19(1).

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-007: Lifetime automatic logging of high-risk AI system events
nodes.rationale: Art. 12(1)-(2) requires automatic recording of events over system lifetime with traceability appropriate to intended purpose. Forms the log-generation substrate for post-market monitoring. Mirrors DORA Art. 12 and NIS 2 Art. 21 log-retention duties.
nodes.norm_label: sr-aiact-007: lifetime automatic logging of high-risk ai system events

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-008: Six-month minimum log retention aligned with intended purpose
nodes.rationale: Art. 19(1) requires 6-month minimum log retention. Only hard numeric anchor for retention duration across the AI Act. Escape clause defers to GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), NIS 2, and DORA Art. 12. T5 mapping error: AIA-C11 references non-existent Art. 12(4).
nodes.norm_label: sr-aiact-008: six-month minimum log retention aligned with intended purpose

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-009: Provider-side log-retention responsibility across hosting models
nodes.rationale: Art. 19(1) sentence 1 allocates log retention responsibility to provider. 'Under their control' qualifier is the responsibility-allocation hinge, covering physical, legal, and technical control across hybrid and multi-cloud deployments.
nodes.norm_label: sr-aiact-009: provider-side log-retention responsibility across hosting models

nodes.label: AI Act (Regulation)
nodes.rationale: Addresses training-data-quality specifically. Provider-driven trigger. Art. 10(1)/(2)/(3) + Art. 10(5) special-category gateway.

nodes.label: Three Data-Class Layering Principle
nodes.rationale: Personal data (GDPR, controller-driven, collection from data subjects) + Product data (CRA, manufacturer-design, runtime capture) + Training data (AI Act, provider-driven, upstream pipeline). Layered not collapsed. Policy and evidence layers must remain class-segregated for compliance demonstration.

nodes.label: NIS2 & DORA (Out-of-Scope)
nodes.rationale: Out-of-scope for D-05.1 per AEGIS taxonomy §4.1 — both are operational-resilience / incident-reporting focused, not data-lifecycle.

nodes.label: D-05 Data Lifecycle (Index)
nodes.rationale: Parent domain containing 4 sub-subdomains (D-05.1 through D-05.4), 4 merged files, 38 article copies, and 75 ambiguity sections.

nodes.label: Req 5.3: Stacked Erasure Architecture Requirement
nodes.rationale: MUST: Product shall render user's personal data inaccessible via stacked GDPR Art. 17 + CRA (2)(m) erasure architecture with layer-segregated hand-offs. NIST CSF: PR.DS-10, PR.DS-12, GV.SC-04.

nodes.label: SO-CRA-036: User Data Removal
nodes.rationale: User of product with digital elements can securely and easily remove all data and settings on permanent basis; secure cross-product transfer. Manufacturer-bound architectural obligation.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 15 (Access Right)
nodes.rationale: Art. 15(1) access right, Art. 15(3) companion copy in commonly used electronic form. The operational companion to Art. 20 portability — supplies the read-only copy at the data subject's request. VAG-S3 ambiguity on 'commonly used electronic form' resolved via EDPB Guidelines 06/2020.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 20 (Portability Right)
nodes.rationale: Sole authority for D-05.4. Art. 20(1) portability right, Art. 20(2) format + cross-controller transmission, Art. 20(3) conditions (consent/contract + automated means), Art. 20(4) exclusions (no public-interest-task or legitimate-interest).

nodes.label: EDPB Guidelines 06/2020 on Data Portability
nodes.rationale: Interprets the parallel Art. 20 phrase 'commonly used electronic form'. Supports the structured-interoperable reading (JSON, CSV, XML) and rejects print-ready rendering and controller-proprietary formats as defeating the portability purpose.

nodes.label: Volere Requirement 5.4.1 (GDPR Sub-Requirement)
nodes.rationale: MUST priority, TEST verification. Derives from SO-D-05.4.GDPR with source SR-GDPR-032. Specifies Art. 20(1) export, Art. 15(3) companion copy, Art. 12(3) ≤1-month service-level, Art. 12(5) free of charge, Art. 20(2) sentence 2 cross-controller transmission.

nodes.label: GDPR Sub-SO SO-D-05.4.GDPR
nodes.rationale: Sole sub-SO capturing the full regulatory surface of D-05.4; activates when GDPR is in applicable_regs. Inherits from SO-GDPR-020 with source SR-GDPR-032.

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 19(1): Log retention >=6 months for high-risk AI systems
nodes.rationale: Providers retain Art. 12(1) logs for period appropriate to intended purpose, at least six months, unless Union/national law provides otherwise. Floor-within-ceiling with GDPR Art. 5(1)(e).
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 19(1): log retention >=6 months for high-risk ai systems

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(9): 10-year update-availability tail
nodes.rationale: Security updates remain available minimum 10 years or remainder of support period, whichever is longer (twin-anchor R2 reading). Applies to update artefacts (firmware, patches, advisories), NOT personal data.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28: Processor
nodes.rationale: Art. 28(1) requires sufficient guarantees. Art. 28(2) requires sub-processor authorisation. Art. 28(3) enumerates mandatory contract clauses. 'Sufficient guarantees' is qualitative.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 89(1): Safeguards for archiving/research/statistical processing
nodes.rationale: Pseudonymisation, aggregation, access limitation as appropriate technical and organisational measures for longer retention in public interest, scientific/historical research, or statistical purposes.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 89(1): safeguards for archiving/research/statistical processing

nodes.label: AI Act Article 10: Data and data governance for high-risk AI systems
nodes.rationale: Art. 10(1) quality criteria; Art. 10(2) eight-element data-governance closed list; Art. 10(3) relevance/representativeness/completeness; Art. 10(5) special-category exception with 6 cumulative conditions.
nodes.norm_label: ai act article 10: data and data governance for high-risk ai systems

nodes.label: D-05.2 Retention & Archiving sub-domain
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation sub-domain covering retention/archiving across GDPR (ceiling), CRA (floor for update artefacts), and AI Act (floor for AI logs). 3-axis layering rule with separation architecture where regimes overlap.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 17 – Right to erasure (right to be forgotten)
nodes.rationale: Art. 17(1)(a)-(f) erasure conditions; controller-side duties flow from Art. 5(1)(c)/(e); Art. 28(3)(g) processor mirror. 'Deletes' carries POLY-S3 with three operational senses.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 17 – right to erasure (right to be forgotten)

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 19 – Communication of rectification or erasure to recipient
nodes.rationale: Art. 19 cascade notification to recipients; 'impossible' OR 'disproportionate effort' as inclusive disjunction; Art. 15(4) caps to known recipients.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 19 – communication of rectification or erasure to recipient

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(1) – Principles of processing
nodes.rationale: Art. 5(1)(a) lawfulness/fairness/transparency; (b) purpose limitation; (c) data minimisation; (e) storage limitation; (f) integrity/confidentiality. Art. 5(2) accountability. Gateway principles for all processing.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-05.3 – Erasure and data subject rights
nodes.norm_label: sub-domain d-05.3 – erasure and data subject rights

nodes.label: GDPR Article 13 — Information to be provided when personal data are collected
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 13 — information to be provided when personal data are collected

nodes.label: GDPR Article 14 — Information to be provided when personal data are not obtained from the data subject
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 14 — information to be provided when personal data are not obtained from the data subject

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-068: Collection-time data-disclosure with documented source triggers
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(1) requires collection-time information; Art. 14(1)/(2) extends to third-party-source data with a one-month ceiling. Operationalised via data inventory (ID.AM-03) and risk-strategy data management (PR.DS-12).
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-068: collection-time data-disclosure with documented source triggers

nodes.label: CRA Annex I Part I (2)(m) Second Limb
nodes.rationale: Manufacturer-side architectural obligation for secure cross-product transfer (confidentiality + integrity + destination-authentication). NOT a portability right. The architectural substrate that makes Art. 20 cross-controller transmission operationally feasible when data resides in a CRA-classified product.
nodes.norm_label: cra annex i part i (2)(m) second limb

nodes.label: GDPR Article 20: Data Portability
nodes.rationale: Art. 20(1) structured, commonly used, machine-readable format; Art. 20(2) cross-controller transmission; Art. 20(3) qualifying conditions (consent/contract + automated); Art. 20(4) exclusions.

nodes.label: D-05.4 Data Portability Sub-Domain
nodes.rationale: Single-regulator sub-domain where GDPR is the sole authority per AEGIS taxonomy §4.1; NIS 2, CRA, DORA, AI Act are out-of-scope at the regulatory layer. 0 pairwise cells, 0 emergent tensions by construction.

nodes.label: Volere Requirement 5.4 (High-Level)
nodes.rationale: MUST priority, TEST verification. Derives from SO-D-05.4.HL. Applicable when GDPR in applicable_regs AND portability-eligible personal data exists. NIST CSF: PR.DS-10, PR.DS-12.

nodes.label: High-Level Security Objective SO-D-05.4.HL
nodes.rationale: Emitted for traceability per the activation model; redundant in the single-regulator case but describes the common portability duty with the CRA architectural anchor noted in the Objective text.

nodes.label: D-09.2 DPIA sub-domain
nodes.rationale: Data Protection Impact Assessment sub-domain covering DPIA content, review on material change, and risk-profile assessment.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 28 — General principles (10 paragraphs, 6 umbrella cards)
nodes.rationale: Longest single article in DORA. Five operational blocks: principles+strategy, register, pre-contract, security+audit, termination+exit. Block (4) cross-references Art. 29 for concentration risk.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 28 — general principles (10 paragraphs, 6 umbrella cards)

nodes.label: DORA Art. 29 — Preliminary assessment of ICT concentration risk
nodes.rationale: NEW in v0.2; not in T3. Entity-level preliminary ICT concentration risk assessment. 2 paragraphs, 2 atomic clauses.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 29 — preliminary assessment of ict concentration risk

nodes.label: DORA Art. 28 chapeau+(1)+(2) — Umbrella principles + strategy
nodes.rationale: Integral component of Art. 6 framework; full responsibility; proportionality; multi-vendor strategy; management body review. R1 vs R2 admit materially distinct compliance populations.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 28 chapeau+(1)+(2) — umbrella principles + strategy

nodes.label: DORA Art. 28(3) — Register of information + reporting
nodes.rationale: Register at entity/sub-consolidated/consolidated levels; yearly reporting; advance notification of planned critical/important arrangements. 'appropriately documented' is Berry-classic.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 28(3) — register of information + reporting

nodes.label: DORA Art. 29(1) — Concentration-risk preliminary assessment
nodes.rationale: Non-substitutable CTPP OR multiple contracts with same/closely-connected CTPP. NEW in v0.2; not in T3.

nodes.label: CJEU IAB Europe (C-604/22)
nodes.rationale: Interpreted 'jointly determine' to include parties with determinative influence on purposes or means even where they do not themselves process data. Extends joint-controller status to industry-association-managed consent frameworks.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 4(7)/(8) — Controller and processor definitions
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 4(7)/(8) — controller and processor definitions

nodes.label: GDPR Arts. 44-45: Cross-Border Transfer Principles and Adequacy
nodes.rationale: Art. 44 umbrella principle. Art. 45(1) adequacy exemption. Art. 45(3) periodic review at least every four years. Schrems II substantial-equivalence test is operational anchor.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr arts. 44-45: cross-border transfer principles and adequacy

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 29 (Processing Under Authority)
nodes.rationale: Binds natural persons acting under controller/processor authority to instruction-only processing; Union or Member State law is the sole exception.

nodes.label: EDPB Guidelines 3/2018 on DPO
nodes.rationale: §3.1: core activities are primary revenue-driving business activities excluding supporting/ancillary functions. and/or in nature/scope/purposes interpreted as inclusive-OR. No universal large-scale threshold fixed.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28(3)(a)/(b) — Processor contract terms
nodes.rationale: Requires processor contract to stipulate processing only on documented instructions and confidentiality commitment from authorised persons.

nodes.label: Annex II §8: Detailed instructions (a)–(f)
nodes.rationale: User-facing instructions covering commissioning, data security, updates, decommissioning, auto-update opt-out, and integrator information; shared by SR-CRA-071 and SR-CRA-107.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 30 — Key contractual provisions (15 sub-elements)
nodes.rationale: Contract-architecture 'coração'. 9 sub-elements in Art. 30(2) for all ICT services; 6 in Art. 30(3) for critical/important functions. 15 atomic clauses total.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 30 — key contractual provisions (15 sub-elements)

nodes.label: DORA Art. 30(1) — Written contract + format
nodes.rationale: Contract in one written document; SLAs included; paper or downloadable durable format. Part of the 15 key contractual provisions.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 30(2)(d) — Data access / recovery / return
nodes.rationale: Data access, recovery, return in easily accessible format; insolvency/resolution/discontinuation triggers. S3 severity.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 30(2)(d) — data access / recovery / return

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33: Breach Notification to Supervisory Authority
nodes.rationale: Art. 33(1) creates 72-hour notification clock from awareness. Art. 33(2) requires processor-to-controller notification without undue delay. Awareness requires detection capability.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 33: breach notification to supervisory authority

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 25 (Privacy by Design and by Default)
nodes.rationale: Art. 25(1) by-design and Art. 25(2) by-default form the upstream obligation chain for SR-039, SR-040, SR-041. Art. 25(1) fires at means-determination and during processing; Art. 25(2) is its operational manifestation at configuration time.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 25 (privacy by design and by default)

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33(2) — Processor-to-controller breach notification
nodes.rationale: Processor must notify controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 30 — Records of processing activities
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 30 — records of processing activities

nodes.label: GDPR Article 5(2): Accountability
nodes.rationale: The controller must be responsible for, and able to demonstrate, compliance with Art. 5(1) principles. Serves as the ex-post demonstration anchor for nearly all SRs in this document set.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 7: Conditions for Consent
nodes.rationale: Art. 7(1) demonstrability, Art. 7(2) bundled consent distinguishability, Art. 7(3) withdrawal as easy as giving, Art. 7(4) conditional consent prohibition.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 31 — Cooperation with supervisory authority
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 31 — cooperation with supervisory authority

nodes.label: Pre-Market CE Marking and EU Declaration Chain
nodes.rationale: The four sequential gates (technical documentation → conformity assessment → EU declaration → CE marking) must all be cleared before first placement. Art. 28(4) attributes sole compliance responsibility to the declaration drafter. Art. 30(1) specifies affixing requirements.
nodes.norm_label: pre-market ce marking and eu declaration chain

nodes.label: Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure Policy
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part II(5) requires the manufacturer to publish and promote a CVD policy. The SPOC (Art. 13(17)) is the operational entry point; the CVD policy defines the coordination workflow. Analogous to ISO/IEC 29147/30111.

nodes.label: Manufacturer-Equivalent Status (Art. 21/22)
nodes.rationale: Art. 21 (importer/distributor placing under own name) and Art. 22 (third-party substantial modifier) trigger manufacturer-equivalent status, inheriting the full Art. 13 obligation set including corrective measures, support-period display, and CVD policy.

nodes.label: Cybersecurity Risk Assessment (Art. 13(2)-(4))
nodes.rationale: The risk assessment is both a documented activity (Art. 13(3)) and an artefact in the technical documentation (Art. 13(4)). It selects which Annex I Part I requirements apply and must be updated during the support period. May be consolidated with other Union-acts assessments (Art. 13(4) s.2).

nodes.label: Substantial Modification Trigger (Art. 13(10) + Art. 21 + Art. 22)
nodes.rationale: The Art. 13(10)+21+22 architecture treats substantial modification as the boundary between normal-version-update and manufacturer-equivalent liability transfer. Art. 3(30) defines the term; the Art. 13(10) carve-out allows last-placed-version compliance subject to user-migration choice.

nodes.label: Support Period and Retention Window
nodes.rationale: The support period is the temporal anchor for documentation retention (Art. 13(13): 10 years or support period, whichever longer), risk-assessment updates (Art. 13(3)), corrective measures (Art. 13(21)), and end-date disclosure (Art. 13(19)). It defines the manufacturer's continuing obligation window.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 30 (Records of Processing Activities)
nodes.rationale: Art. 30(1) seven content items, Art. 30(3) form requirement, Art. 30(4) supervisory access, Art. 30(5) 250-employee exception form the RoPA obligation chain for SR-044, SR-048, SR-050.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(2) (Accountability)
nodes.rationale: Art. 5(2) is the cross-cutting accountability anchor referenced by nearly all SRs as the ex-post demonstration standard against which compliance is assessed on the day of any supervisory inspection.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 35(1): DPIA trigger for high-risk processing
nodes.rationale: DPIA required where processing likely to result in high risk, in particular using new technologies; open-textured trigger with EDPB Guidelines 4/2019 nine-criteria list as operational anchor.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 35(1): dpia trigger for high-risk processing

nodes.label: GDPR Arts. 35-36 – DPIA and prior consultation
nodes.rationale: Art. 35(1) high-risk DPIA trigger; Art. 35(7) DPIA content; Art. 36(1) prior consultation on residual high risk; Art. 36(2) 8-week supervisory response. Pre-launch gate.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr arts. 35-36 – dpia and prior consultation

nodes.label: EU Charter Art. 7 (Right to private life)
nodes.rationale: Relevant to how recipient-list request interacts with confidentiality obligations (e.g. trade-secret-protected recipients).
nodes.norm_label: eu charter art. 7 (right to private life)

nodes.label: EDPB Guidelines 5/2019
nodes.rationale: Pending revision; relevant to whether 'recipient' includes processors (Art. 28) and joint controllers (Art. 26) or only independent third-party controllers.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 11(2) — Identification-exemption (cross)
nodes.rationale: Preserves the identification precondition for the data-subject rights endpoint.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 15(4) — Third-party-rights limit
nodes.rationale: Caps the disclosure obligation to recipients known to the controller; the controller is not required to investigate recipients beyond its own records.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 18 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split (SO + SR) generated from 01_SecurityObjectives.md and 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md. The originals remain the authoritative aggregate indexes.

nodes.label: D-06.2 Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) — Unified Sub-domain Document
nodes.author: SubDomains merge (Executor sub-agent)
nodes.rationale: Unified view merging sub-domain definition, domain analysis, deep analysis, and relevant ambiguity for the SBOM sub-domain. CRA is sole authority per AEGIS taxonomy §4.1.
nodes.norm_label: d-06.2 software bill of materials (sbom) — unified sub-domain document

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OV-02: Risk management strategy reviewed and adjusted to address changes
nodes.rationale: Shared by SR-CRA-066 (update dimension of risk assessment) and SR-CRA-076 (cessation as risk-landscape change). Captures the strategy-review-and-adjustment dimension.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.ov-02: risk management strategy reviewed and adjusted to address changes

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.PO-02: Cybersecurity processes and procedures established, communicated, and enforced
nodes.rationale: Shared by five SRs (064, 066, 069, 075, 079). The most broadly-referenced CSF subcategory in this document, anchoring the process-and-procedure implementation layer across all lifecycle phases.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.po-02: cybersecurity processes and procedures established, communicated, and enforced

nodes.label: GDPR Article 24: Responsibility of the controller
nodes.rationale: Source article for SR-GDPR-043 (Art. 24(1), (2)), SR-GDPR-044 (Art. 24(1)). Operational-responsibility centrepiece tying controller obligation to demonstrability.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 24: responsibility of the controller

nodes.label: GDPR Article 30: Records of processing activities
nodes.rationale: Source article for SR-GDPR-044 (Art. 30(1)), SR-GDPR-048 (Art. 30(1), (4), (5)), SR-GDPR-050 (Art. 30(3)). RoPA content, access, and integrity.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 30: records of processing activities

nodes.label: GDPR Article 5: Principles relating to processing
nodes.rationale: Art. 5(1)(a)-(f) principles and Art. 5(2) accountability. Referenced across nearly all SRs as the accountability anchor for ex-post demonstration.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 5: principles relating to processing

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OV-03: Cybersecurity performance evaluated and reviewed
nodes.rationale: Evaluated-and-reviewed-correction dimension converting raw evidence into accountability. Adjustments materialise as refreshed policies and procedures.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.ov-03: cybersecurity performance evaluated and reviewed

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.PO-01: Organizational cybersecurity policy established and enforced
nodes.rationale: Policy-document discipline anchored on Art. 24(2) proportionality test. Without it, controller cannot demonstrate existence or enforcement of posture.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.po-01: organizational cybersecurity policy established and enforced

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(5) — Vulnerability Handling (referenced)
nodes.rationale: Supplies downstream fact-feeding layer for product vendors feeding DORA entities.

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OC-01: Mission understood and informs risk management
nodes.rationale: Supplies the mission-alignment layer: cybersecurity investment proportionate to entity's critical objectives and services.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.oc-01: mission understood and informs risk management

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OV-02: Risk Strategy Review & Adjustment
nodes.rationale: Anchors strategic layer: strategy adjustment when scenario-review findings diverge from risk-appetite statement, ensuring review produces governance change rather than documentation churn.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.ov-02: risk strategy review & adjustment

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RM-02: Risk roles established and communicated
nodes.rationale: Layers the communication-and-understanding engine ensuring role allocation is communicated across entity and understood by all three lines so escalation pathways are exercisable.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.rm-02: risk roles established and communicated

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RR-02: Risk management roles established and enforced
nodes.rationale: Anchors structural separation between operational management (first line), risk-and-compliance oversight (second line), and internal audit (third line).
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.rr-02: risk management roles established and enforced

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.AM-04: Supplier and third-party inventories maintained
nodes.rationale: Anchors the upstream inventory that GV.SC-02 cannot operate without. The proportionality judgement is only as defensible as the inventory on which it is computed.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.am-04: supplier and third-party inventories maintained

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 21(2) — Parallel Baseline Obligations
nodes.rationale: Supplies parallel cross-state formulation (21(2)(a)), cryptography regime (21(2)(d)), incident-handling (21(2)(b)-(c)), and policy review cadence (21(2)(f)) to which DORA-fall-back NSIEs are subject.

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AA-05: Access managed per least privilege
nodes.rationale: Establishes permission-tier discipline: function-aligned entitlements, RBAC/ABAC, just-in-time elevation, separation-of-duties enforcement, and privileged-access management with session recording.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.aa-05: access managed per least privilege

nodes.label: NIST CSF RC.RP-01: Recovery executed after incident response
nodes.rationale: Anchors the recovery-execution dimension: BC policy must specify criteria for recovery transition from incident-response to recovery-mode with documented decision points and RTOs.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rc.rp-01: recovery executed after incident response

nodes.label: NIST CSF RS.MA-01: Incident plan executed with third-party coordination
nodes.rationale: Establishes process-execution layer covering pre-incident planning and post-declaration execution with third-party coordination for CTPPs, competent authorities, and client-communication channels.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rs.ma-01: incident plan executed with third-party coordination

nodes.label: DORA Art. 21 — Security Objectives & Rules (CIA+A, Risk, Network)
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 21 — security objectives & rules (cia+a, risk, network)

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-01.1: Data protection at rest
nodes.norm_label: sub-domain d-01.1: data protection at rest

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-01.2: Data protection in transit
nodes.norm_label: sub-domain d-01.2: data protection in transit

nodes.label: NIS2-CL20 — Art. 21(3) s1 Supply-chain risk assessment
nodes.rationale: Covers vulnerabilities, overall quality, and secure development procedures of direct suppliers; R4 composite reading chosen for 'overall quality'; R2 supplier-SDLC reading for 'secure development procedures'
nodes.norm_label: nis2-cl20 — art. 21(3) s1 supply-chain risk assessment

nodes.label: NIS2-C05 — Art. 21(2)(b) Incident handling
nodes.rationale: Single phrase 'incident handling' is undefined; operational content delegated to standards; polysemy: process vs team vs capability

nodes.label: NIS2-C29 — Art. 21(2)(b) Incident detection (T3 reading: real-time)
nodes.rationale: T3-imposed 'real time' attribute; OJ text contains no timeliness qualifier; detection vs response ambiguity (NIST SP 800-61 vs EU ALTA-IR)
nodes.norm_label: nis2-c29 — art. 21(2)(b) incident detection (t3 reading: real-time)

nodes.label: NIS2-C08 — Art. 21(2)(d) Supply chain security
nodes.rationale: 'direct' is critical scope-limiter (Tier-1 vs n-hop vs contractual); 'suppliers or service providers' distinct categories or hendiadys

nodes.label: NIS2-C23 — Art. 21(3) Sector-specific supplier risk
nodes.rationale: Three coordinated assessment objects (vulnerabilities, overall quality, secure development procedures); 'each direct supplier' universal quantifier; unit unspecified

nodes.label: NIS2-C10 — Art. 21(2)(e) Security in development
nodes.rationale: Covers acquisition, development, maintenance; distinct from secure-SDLC; includes COTS/OSS; three coordinated lifecycle phases

nodes.label: NIS2-C11 — Art. 21(2)(e) CI/CD pipeline (T3 reading)
nodes.rationale: T3-imposed reading; OJ text does not contain 'pipeline', 'CI', 'CD'; imported from NIST SSDF SP 800-218 or ISO 27034; T3-vs-text gap pattern

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RM-06: Standardized risk calculation and prioritization method
nodes.rationale: Meta-methodology anchor for physical-environment risk assessment within the all-hazards approach.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.rm-06: standardized risk calculation and prioritization method

nodes.label: CRA Art. 14(1): AEV notification to CSIRT and ENISA
nodes.rationale: Requires simultaneous notification of actively exploited vulnerabilities to the CSIRT of the Member State of main establishment and to ENISA via the single reporting platform (Art. 16).
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 14(1): aev notification to csirt and enisa

nodes.label: CRA Art. 24(1): OSS steward cybersecurity policy
nodes.rationale: Requires verifiable cybersecurity policy fostering secure development and effective vulnerability handling. Four sub-elements define minimum content. Proportionality preserved by Recital 18.
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 24(1): oss steward cybersecurity policy

nodes.label: SO-CRA-041 — Authorised Representative Appointment
nodes.rationale: Non-EU manufacturer may appoint EU AR by written mandate. Non-delegable obligations: Art. 13(1)–(11), (12) first sub, (14). AR retains technical documentation and cooperates with MSAs.

nodes.label: CRA Article 18 — Authorised Representative
nodes.rationale: Defines AR appointment mechanism, non-delegable carve-out, and EU-side compliance tasks for non-EU manufacturers.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-059: Authorised representative appointment with non-delegable carve-out
nodes.rationale: Art. 18(2) carve-out preserves manufacturer's primary responsibility for Art. 13(1)-(11), 13(12) first subparagraph, and 13(14). AR handles procedural cooperation only.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-059: authorised representative appointment with non-delegable carve-out

nodes.label: SR-CRA-060: Authorised representative EU-side compliance tasks
nodes.rationale: Three tasks: (a) keep technical documentation at MSA disposal, (b) provide conformity info, (c) cooperate on non-conformity action. Bounded by Art. 18(2) carve-out.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-060: authorised representative eu-side compliance tasks

nodes.label: CRA Art. 18 — Authorised Representative Appointment
nodes.rationale: Non-EU manufacturer may appoint EU AR by written mandate. Non-delegable carve-out for Art. 13(1)–(11), (12) first sub, (14). Different object from GDPR Art. 27 (product-compliance vs data-protection representative).

nodes.label: CRA Art. 22 — Third-Party Substantial Modification Trigger
nodes.rationale: Third party carrying out substantial modification becomes manufacturer for affected part or whole product. Different actor and trigger from NIS2 direct-supplier scope-limiter.
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 22 — third-party substantial modification trigger

nodes.label: CRA Art. 23 — Economic Operator Identification + 10-Year Retention
nodes.rationale: Operator-side identification duty (upstream supplier + downstream recipient) with 10-year retention. Points in different direction from DORA audit rights (upstream traceability vs downstream audit).
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 23 — economic operator identification + 10-year retention

nodes.label: DORA Art. 27 — TLPT Tester Requirements
nodes.rationale: Two-track tester regime: external (5 requirements) vs internal (5+3 additional). Most specific tester-qualification regime in the 5-regulation corpus. Justified by high-stakes TLPT on live production systems.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 30(3) — CIF Contract Requirements (9 Elements)
nodes.rationale: Additional contractual elements for critical/important function ICT third-party arrangements: SLAs, notice/reporting, contingency, TLPT cooperation, monitoring/audit rights, exit strategies. Microenterprise derogation for audit delegation.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 30(3) — cif contract requirements (9 elements)

nodes.label: DORA Art. 30(3)(e)(i)/(ii) — Unrestricted Audit Rights
nodes.rationale: Core DORA provision granting financial entities and competent authorities unrestricted rights of access, inspection, and audit over critical/important ICT third-party providers, including on-site documentation copy right. Must not be impeded by other contractual arrangements.

nodes.label: CL30-15 — DORA Art. 30(3)(e)+(f) Monitoring/Exit Block
nodes.rationale: Unrestricted audit rights + alternative assurance + microenterprise derogation + mandatory adequate transition period. 'Unrestricted' is VAG-S3; R1 (absolute) is literal but R2 (reasonableness) recognised in clause itself.

nodes.label: Emergent: Four-Party Boundary Architecture
nodes.rationale: Single non-EU entity subject to multiple regulations must maintain multiple representative relationships (GDPR Art. 27 + CRA Art. 18), satisfy NIS2 direct scope-limiter, and accept DORA audit rights. Phase 2 must produce a representative/rights matrix allocating obligations across four tracks.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 27 — EU Representative Designation
nodes.rationale: Requires non-EU controllers/processors to designate a written EU representative. Distinct mechanism from DORA audit rights (legal-address vs rights assertion).

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(d) — Direct Supplier Security
nodes.rationale: Entity-level supply chain security limited to direct suppliers. DORA audit rights extend beyond this direct-supplier floor into broader critical provider chains.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 22 — Commission Coordinated Risk Assessment
nodes.rationale: Commission identifies specific critical ICT services/systems/products for coordinated security risk assessment. No direct entity-facing obligation; propagation via Art. 21(3) sentence 2.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 22 — commission coordinated risk assessment

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 23 — Cross-MS Incident Notification
nodes.rationale: Cross-border notification routing via SPOCs and ENISA. Different mechanism from GDPR Art. 27 (notification routing vs legal address).

nodes.label: NIS2 CL42 — Art. 23(6) Cross-MS Notification
nodes.rationale: CSIRT/CA/SPOC shall inform other affected MS and ENISA without undue delay where incident concerns 2+ MS. 'Where appropriate' is soft hedge; 'two or more' is indicator not definition.

nodes.label: Pairwise: CRA ↔ DORA (Different-Perspective)
nodes.rationale: CRA Art. 23 imposes identification duty on operators (upstream); DORA Art. 30(3)(e) imposes audit rights on financial entities (downstream). Different mechanisms, different directions. Compose when CRA product supplied via importer/distributor to financial entity.

nodes.label: Pairwise: GDPR ↔ CRA (Equal — Different Objects)
nodes.rationale: Both require written EU-side representative for non-EU entities. Different objects: GDPR = data-protection representative; CRA = product-compliance AR. When same entity is both, both representatives co-exist with different mandates.

nodes.label: Pairwise: GDPR ↔ DORA (Different-Perspective)
nodes.rationale: GDPR Art. 27 is legal-address obligation (designate); DORA Art. 30(3)(e) is rights obligation (assert audit). Different mechanisms. Both apply when non-EU ICT provider is critical/important for financial entity.

nodes.label: Pairwise: GDPR ↔ NIS2 (Complementary)
nodes.rationale: GDPR Art. 27 designates EU representative (legal-address anchor); NIS2 Art. 23(6) routes notifications via SPOCs. Different actors, different purposes. Both apply when non-EU controller operates across multiple MS.

nodes.label: Pairwise: NIS2 ↔ CRA (Different-Perspective)
nodes.rationale: NIS2 direct scope-limiter is about who entity is liable for; CRA Art. 22/23 is about who becomes manufacturer and who provides identification. Different actors, different triggers.

nodes.label: Pairwise: NIS2 ↔ DORA (Complementary — DORA Exceeds)
nodes.rationale: NIS2 direct scope-limiter limits supplier universe; DORA audit rights apply to critical/important providers including non-direct via supply chain. DORA extends beyond NIS2 direct scope.

nodes.label: Req 6.4.4 — DORA Art. 30(3)(e) Audit Rights over CIF ICT Providers
nodes.rationale: MUST-priority requirement operationalising unrestricted access/inspection/audit rights for financial entities over CIF-supporting ICT third-party providers, with narrowly bounded alternative-assurance exception only where other clients' rights are affected.
nodes.norm_label: req 6.4.4 — dora art. 30(3)(e) audit rights over cif ict providers

nodes.label: DORA CL19-1 — Art. 19(1) Major incident reporting
nodes.rationale: Single-CA designation for multi-CA entities; significant CIs report to NCA which transmits to ECB; 'technical impossibility' fallback undefined; cross-reference to NIS2 CSIRTs
nodes.norm_label: dora cl19-1 — art. 19(1) major incident reporting

nodes.label: DORA CL21-1 — Art. 21(1)+(2) Single EU Hub feasibility
nodes.rationale: Feasibility of centralised incident reporting; 7 enumerated elements; 'single EU Hub' architectural choice undefined; report published Q1 2025
nodes.norm_label: dora cl21-1 — art. 21(1)+(2) single eu hub feasibility

nodes.label: NIST CSF RS.AN-03: Analysis performed to determine root cause
nodes.rationale: Measures-envisaged discipline in Art. 35(7)(d): documentation of safeguards traces to specific identified risks, preserved for inspection and after-the-fact learning.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rs.an-03: analysis performed to determine root cause

nodes.label: DORA CL30-1 — Art. 30(1) Written contract + format
nodes.rationale: One written document; SLAs included; downloadable, durable, accessible format; three Berry-classic qualifiers
nodes.norm_label: dora cl30-1 — art. 30(1) written contract + format

nodes.label: DORA CL5-2 — Art. 5(2) Management body 4-verb coordination
nodes.rationale: Define, approve, oversee, be responsible for — four coordinated verbs; ultimate responsibility; high standards (availability, authenticity, integrity, confidentiality)
nodes.norm_label: dora cl5-2 — art. 5(2) management body 4-verb coordination

nodes.label: NIS2-C01 — Art. 20(1) Governance
nodes.rationale: Management bodies approve, oversee, and can be held liable; three coordinated verbs; 'management bodies' polysemy (board vs executive vs senior management)

nodes.label: NIS2-C16 — Art. 21(2)(h) Cryptography
nodes.rationale: 'where appropriate' softens encryption mandate; cryptography vs encryption subordination; T3 splits into at-rest/in-transit/key-management (T3-vs-text gap)

nodes.label: NIS2-C21 — Art. 21(2)(j) MFA + communications
nodes.rationale: Four coordinated obligations via OR and AND; 'where appropriate' closes entire sub-point; parse tree admits ≥6 obligation shapes

nodes.label: NIS2-CL24 — Art. 22(1) s2 Risk-factor scope
nodes.rationale: Technical factors always; non-technical where relevant; 'non-technical' covers organisational, geopolitical, market structure (R4 all)

nodes.label: NIS2-CL49 — Art. 24(1) s2 Qualified trust services
nodes.rationale: Shall encourage use of qualified trust services; cross-reference to eIDAS Art. 6(26)
nodes.norm_label: nis2-cl49 — art. 24(1) s2 qualified trust services

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 22 — Automated Individual Decision-Making
nodes.rationale: Right not to be subject to solely-automated decisions producing legal effects. 'Solely' and 'significantly' are S3 ambiguities. Direct overlap with AI Act Art. 13 high-risk transparency.

nodes.label: EDPB Guidelines 07/2020 — Processor Obligations
nodes.rationale: Proposes factors for 'sufficient guarantees' including commitment to GDPR, TOMs, transparency, ability to assist controller. Referenced for sub-processor authorisation and audit expectations.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 28 — Security Objectives & Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering ICT third-party risk management, standards compliance, and foundational proportionality obligations under Art. 28.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28 — Security Objectives & Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering processor obligations: instruction-bound processing, confidentiality, breach notification, erasure, due diligence, 8-element contract, auditability, sub-processor authorisation, and cross-border transfers.

nodes.label: CRA Annex I Part II (1) — SBOM Authoring Requirement
nodes.rationale: The manufacturer draws up and maintains an SBOM covering components and dependencies in a commonly used and machine-readable format including at minimum top-level dependencies. This is the authoring anchor of the three-anchored SBOM architecture.
nodes.norm_label: cra annex i part ii (1) — sbom authoring requirement

nodes.label: CRA Annex II §9 — Optional SBOM User Access
nodes.rationale: If manufacturer decides to make available an SBOM, identify where it is located. Optional fourth anchor at manufacturer's discretion. Not a separate obligation; does not duplicate the SBOM duty. Typically NOT enabled for B2B products but enabled for consumer products as trust-signal lever.
nodes.norm_label: cra annex ii §9 — optional sbom user access

nodes.label: CRA Annex VII §2(b) — SBOM in Technical Documentation
nodes.rationale: SBOM included in technical documentation surviving the Annex VII §4 retention period (10 years or support period, whichever is longer). This is the retention anchor of the three-anchored SBOM architecture.
nodes.norm_label: cra annex vii §2(b) — sbom in technical documentation

nodes.label: CRA Annex VII §8 — SBOM on MSA Reasoned Request
nodes.rationale: On reasoned request from MSA, SBOM provided where necessary for compliance checking. This is the regulatory-disclosure anchor. 'Where necessary' scope resolved to R1 (necessary subset relevant to compliance question, not comprehensive dump).
nodes.norm_label: cra annex vii §8 — sbom on msa reasoned request

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(24) — Commission Implementing Acts on SBOM
nodes.rationale: Forward-looking clause authorising further specification of SBOM format and elements. Anticipates standardisation work (CEN/CENELEC under Art. 27 + Recital 60). May raise the floor from current top-level dependencies minimum. Format-migration posture required when binding format specified.
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 13(24) — commission implementing acts on sbom

nodes.label: CRA Art. 3(39) — SBOM Definition
nodes.rationale: Formal record containing details and supply-chain relationships of the components included in the software elements of a product with digital elements. Definitional anchor for the entire SBOM obligation.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-053 — SBOM Retention & Disclosure Rule
nodes.rationale: Covers Annex VII §2(b) mandatory retention + Annex II §9 optional user access + Annex VII §8 MSA reasoned request. 'If the manufacturer decides' resolved to R1 (manufacturer's discretion). 'Where necessary' scope resolved to R1 (necessary subset relevant to compliance question). Maps to NIST ID.AM-02 + GV.SC-03.

nodes.label: Three-anchored SBOM Architecture (authoring + retention + regulatory disclosure)
nodes.rationale: The SBOM duty operates across three operational anchors: (1) authoring at product release, (2) retention in technical documentation through support period + 10-year tail, (3) regulatory disclosure to MSAs on reasoned request. Plus optional fourth anchor (user-facing access). All three mandatory anchors must be satisfied for CRA-bound manufacturers.
nodes.norm_label: three-anchored sbom architecture (authoring + retention + regulatory disclosure)

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13 — Security Objectives & Security Rules (per-article split)
nodes.rationale: Per-article split generated from 01_SecurityObjectives.md and 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md. Contains SO-CRA-038 and related SOs. The originals remain the authoritative aggregate indexes.
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 13 — security objectives & security rules (per-article split)

nodes.label: Requirement 6.2 — High-level SBOM Requirement (Volere)
nodes.rationale: Volere audit requirement: manufacturer draws up and maintains SBOM in three-anchored architecture. Priority MUST, verification TEST. Derives from SO-D-06.2.HL. NIST CSF: ID.AM-02, GV.SC-02, GV.SC-03.

nodes.label: Requirement 6.2.1 — Three-anchored SBOM Architecture Sub-requirement
nodes.rationale: Operational sub-requirement specifying the three-anchored SBOM architecture (authoring + retention + regulatory disclosure + optional user access). Derives from SO-D-06.2.CRA / SO-CRA-038. Depends on 6.1.3 for component-tier inventory substrate.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(d): Supply Chain Security
nodes.rationale: Entity-facing supply-chain-security mandate. The `direct` scope-limiter is the single most consequential scope-limiting term in Chapter IV.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(e): Security in Acquisition, Development, Maintenance
nodes.rationale: Three coordinated lifecycle phases (acquisition, development, maintenance) plus vulnerability handling and disclosure. Process limb + substantive vulnerability-management limb.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 21(2)(e): security in acquisition, development, maintenance

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 22(1): Cooperation Group Coordinated Assessments
nodes.rationale: Institutional counterpart to Art. 21(3) sentence 2. Cooperation Group + Commission + ENISA carry out coordinated assessments of critical supply chains.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 22(1): cooperation group coordinated assessments

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-06.2: SBOM and supply chain
nodes.norm_label: sub-domain d-06.2: sbom and supply chain

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-09.4: Market surveillance and compliance
nodes.norm_label: sub-domain d-09.4: market surveillance and compliance

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(10): Substantial-modification compliance scope
nodes.rationale: Permits compliance with Annex I Part II(2) for the last-placed version only, conditional on free user access and no additional hardware/software adjustment costs. The conditional nature means the manufacturer cannot unilaterally apply the carve-out.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 3(30): Substantial modification definition
nodes.rationale: Defines substantial modification as a post-market modification not considered in conformity assessment, which affects compliance with Annex I OR modifies intended purpose. VAG+POLY S3 with three materially distinct readings; chosen reading is R1+R3 (disjunctive literal).

nodes.label: DORA Art. 30 — Security Objectives & Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering contractual arrangements minimum elements (Art. 30(1)-(2)) and unrestricted audit rights (Art. 30(3)(e)).

nodes.label: NIST Privacy Framework (Category-P)
nodes.rationale: Natural broader reference for consent-as-control; outside CSF 2.0 scope; referenced as the appropriate framework for GDPR-specific consent constructs that lack CSF subcategory mapping.

nodes.label: CJEU Bundeskartellamt C-252/21
nodes.rationale: Treated Facebook's combined-terms consent as coercive; confirms Art. 7(4) unbundling rule; process discipline is principal defence against consent-coercion patterns.

nodes.label: CJEU Planet49 C-673/17
nodes.rationale: §73 held pre-ticked boxes do not constitute unambiguous consent; anchors the unambiguous qualifier of Art. 4(11) against default-accept configurations.

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.SC-05: Response and recovery planning with suppliers
nodes.rationale: Third-party-response discipline for cross-border incident handling involving suppliers and peer entities.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.sc-05: response and recovery planning with suppliers

nodes.label: NIST CSF RC.RP-06: End of recovery declared, after-action review completed
nodes.rationale: Recovery-completion discipline on which final report and closing report substantive content depends.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rc.rp-06: end of recovery declared, after-action review completed

nodes.label: Req 6.4: Third-Party Boundary Responsibilities Allocation (Volere)
nodes.rationale: High-level Volere requirement: product shall explicitly allocate third-party boundary responsibilities across four boundary mechanisms preserving each mechanism's role/recipient/record instrument and avoiding collapse into a generic field. Priority MUST, verification TEST.

nodes.label: Req 6.4.2: NIS2 Cross-MS Routing + Direct Supplier Scope Boundary
nodes.rationale: Two-track NIS2 boundary matrix: Track-1 cross-MS routing (Art. 23(6)/(8)) and Track-2 direct-supplier-scope register (Art. 21(2)(d) + Art. 22 coordinated-assessment ingestion). The 'direct' scope-limiter carries three materially distinct readings (R1/R2/R3) with R1 as minimum.
nodes.norm_label: req 6.4.2: nis2 cross-ms routing + direct supplier scope boundary

nodes.label: Req 6.4.3: CRA Authorised Representative + Manufacturer-Equivalent + Substantial-Modification + 10-Year Log
nodes.rationale: CRA economic-operator boundary matrix per non-EU manufacturer/importer/distributor/substantial-modifier. Non-delegable manufacturer obligations remain on manufacturer regardless of AR mandate. CRA AR does NOT replace GDPR Art. 27 representative or DORA CIF audit-rights.
nodes.norm_label: req 6.4.3: cra authorised representative + manufacturer-equivalent + substantial-modification + 10-year log

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 16 - Right to Rectification
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-005, 006, 022. Data subject right to obtain rectification of inaccurate personal data without undue delay.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 19 - Cascade Notification to Recipients
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-006, 022. Communicate rectification/erasure to each recipient unless impossible or disproportionate effort.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 19 - cascade notification to recipients

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 25(2) - Privacy by Default
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-013. By default only necessary personal data processed across four dimensions: amount, extent, period, accessibility.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) - Data Minimisation
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-006, 009, 010, 013, 025, 029, 030. Requires personal data adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary in relation to purposes.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(1)(d) - Accuracy
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-005, 006. Requires personal data accurate and kept up to date; every reasonable step to erase or rectify inaccurate data without delay.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) - Storage Limitation
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-029, 030. Personal data kept in identifiable form no longer than necessary; longer retention only for archiving/research/statistical with Art. 89(1) safeguards.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(2): Accountability and demonstrability
nodes.rationale: Controller must be able to demonstrate compliance; ex-post demonstration standard referenced throughout all SRs as the accountability threshold for supervisory inspection.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(1)(a) - Pseudonymisation and Encryption
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-003, 004. Names pseudonymisation and encryption as illustrative appropriate technical measures under risk-based preamble.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(1)(d) - Regular Testing
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-007, 008, 015. Process for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating effectiveness of technical and organisational measures.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33(1) - 72-Hour Breach Notification
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-014, 016, 018. Notify supervisory authority without undue delay, where feasible not later than 72 hours after becoming aware, unless unlikely to result in risk.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 34(1) - High-Risk Breach Communication
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-019, 020, 021. Communicate breach to data subject without undue delay when likely to result in high risk to rights and freedoms.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 34(3)(a) - Encryption/Unintelligibility Exception
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-004, 015, 020. Notification not required if measures render data unintelligible to unauthorised persons, such as encryption.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(1)(f) - Integrity and Confidentiality
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-005, 007, 024. Appropriate technical and organisational measures ensuring security including protection against unauthorised processing.

nodes.label: CRA Article 23 — Economic Operator Identification and Retention
nodes.rationale: Bilateral supply-chain identification on MSA request + 10-year retention for all economic operators.
nodes.norm_label: cra article 23 — economic operator identification and retention

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-02.2: Vulnerability handling and remediation
nodes.rationale: Most-populated sub-domain in this article (8 SRs). Covers remediation, support period, update availability, and dissemination.
nodes.norm_label: sub-domain d-02.2: vulnerability handling and remediation

nodes.label: CRA-CL132: Annex I Part I (2)(c) security updates + notification
nodes.rationale: Vulnerabilities addressed through security updates, including automatic updates with opt-out, notification of available updates, and option to temporarily postpone. Referenced by 3 SRs.
nodes.norm_label: cra-cl132: annex i part i (2)(c) security updates + notification

nodes.label: 4-Tier Vendor Risk Assessment Chain
nodes.rationale: Layered reconciliation: DORA gates selection → NIS2 specifies direct-supplier scope → CRA certifies product → GDPR requires processor-guarantees documentation. The four target objects are layered, not collapsed. This chain supersedes any single-regulator reading and constitutes the operational convergence point.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 3(48) FOSS Definition
nodes.rationale: CRA-specific operational handle that GDPR/NIS2/DORA do not separately replicate. Extends vendor risk assessment to non-commercial OSS components not made available in commercial activity. OSS-specific calibration: stewardship assessment, CVD policy review, vulnerability disclosure channel, governance-transparency review.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 28(1) Four-Factor Proportionality
nodes.rationale: Nature, scale, complexity, importance of ICT-related dependencies. Operationalises both GDPR sufficient guarantees and NIS2 appropriate and proportionate with sharper explicit factors. DORA exceeds both in the financial-services subset.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(3) Three-Prong Supplier Assessment
nodes.rationale: All three required (COORD-S2 across AND-coordinated limbs): supplier-specific vulnerabilities + overall quality of products and cybersecurity practices + supplier secure-development procedures. More granular than GDPR sufficient guarantees and CRA due diligence tests.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(5) — Third-Party Component Due Diligence
nodes.rationale: Manufacturer obligation to exercise due diligence when integrating third-party components including non-commercial OSS. Product-level (upstream) obligation distinct from entity-level (midstream) DORA obligation. 'Due diligence' is a Berry-classic VAG/S3 term with three readings (procedural, substantive, both).
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 13(5) — third-party component due diligence

nodes.label: CRA-CL23a — Art. 13(5) Supply-Chain Due Diligence Clause
nodes.rationale: The Q6=b split locus for CRA Art. 13(5). Three Berry instances: VAG/S3 'due diligence' (procedural vs substantive vs both), POLY/S2 'third parties' (commercial vs OSS vs both), SCOPE-Q/S2 OSS limitation. R3 (both) is the literal reading for due diligence.
nodes.norm_label: cra-cl23a — art. 13(5) supply-chain due diligence clause

nodes.label: D-06.1 Cross-Regulation Deep Analysis (OJ-Text-Verified)
nodes.rationale: OJ-text-verified pairwise analysis confirming CRDA classifications: GDPR↔NIS2 complementary, GDPR↔CRA different-perspective, GDPR↔DORA complementary (DORA exceeds), NIS2↔CRA different-perspective, NIS2↔DORA equal (DORA exceeds), CRA↔DORA different-perspective.

nodes.label: D-06.1 Cross-Regulation Domain Analysis
nodes.rationale: Static cross-regulation analysis establishing the four-regulation participant set (GDPR, NIS2, CRA, DORA), pairwise relationship matrix, and downstream 4-tier supplier/vendor risk assessment implication.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 28(1) — ICT Third-Party Risk Four-Factor Proportionality
nodes.rationale: Financial entities shall manage ICT third-party risk taking into account (i) nature, scale, complexity, importance of ICT-related dependencies and (ii) risks from contractual arrangements considering criticality or importance of service/process/function. The four-factor AND test is a sharper operationalisation of both GDPR 'sufficient guarantees' and NIS2 'appropriate and proportionate' chapeau.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 28(1) — ict third-party risk four-factor proportionality

nodes.label: DORA Art. 28(5) — CIF Escalator (Highest Quality Standards)
nodes.rationale: For contractual arrangements concerning critical or important functions, the most up-to-date and highest quality information security standards must be used. DORA-unique strictness floor applying only to CIFs. The 'critical or important' distinction is the central DORA POLY-S2 appearing in 18 of 38 DORA clauses without definition.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 28(5) — cif escalator (highest quality standards)

nodes.label: DORA Art. 30(2) — 9-Element Closed-List Contract
nodes.rationale: Nine mandatory contractual provisions (a)–(i) for all ICT third-party service arrangements: function description, locations, data CIA, data access/recovery/return, SLAs, incident assistance cost, authority cooperation, termination rights, awareness/training. Materialises the Art. 28(1) assessment into the contractual instrument.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 30(3) — CIF Contractual Provisions (6 Sub-Elements)
nodes.rationale: Six sub-elements (a)–(f) for critical or important function contracts: full SLAs, notice/reporting, contingency/ICT security, TLPT cooperation, monitoring rights (e), exit/transition (f). The 'critical or important' POLY-S2 distinction applies here with distinct obligations attached.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 30(3) — cif contractual provisions (6 sub-elements)

nodes.label: DORA CL28-1 — Art. 28 Chapeau + Strategy
nodes.rationale: Umbrella principles: integral component of Art. 6 framework, full responsibility at all times, proportionality, multi-vendor strategy, management body review. VAG/S3 on 'at all times, remain fully responsible' + 'principle of proportionality' nexus (3 readings).

nodes.label: DORA CL30-15 — Art. 30(3)(e)+(f) Monitoring Rights + Exit/Transition
nodes.rationale: Combined card: (3)(e) unrestricted access/inspection/audit (4 sub-points) + (3)(f) mandatory adequate transition and migration. The contract-architecture 'coração' — closes the audit loop and ensures exit capability for CIF contracts.
nodes.norm_label: dora cl30-15 — art. 30(3)(e)+(f) monitoring rights + exit/transition

nodes.label: EDPB Guidelines 07/2020
nodes.rationale: 4-factor test operationalising GDPR sufficient guarantees: knowledge, reliability of resources, compliance track-record, financial stability. Referenced as the operational handle for GDPR processor due diligence.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28(1) — Processor Selection / Sufficient Guarantees
nodes.rationale: Controller obligation to use only processors providing sufficient guarantees. Qualitative threshold operationalised by DORA four-factor test in the financial-services subset. EDPB Guidelines 07/2020 provide factors but threshold remains inquiry-resistant (Berry VAG/S2).
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 28(1) — processor selection / sufficient guarantees

nodes.label: GDPR-CP07 — Art. 28(1) Processor Selection Clause
nodes.rationale: Controller-to-processor obligation (PER-PROCESSOR). Berry VAG/S2: 'sufficient guarantees' is inquiry-resistant. EDPB Guidelines 07/2020 propose factors but threshold is qualitative. S2 because same due-diligence documentation applies.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(1) — Risk-Management Core Obligation
nodes.rationale: Essential and important entities must take appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures. The 'appropriate and proportionate' qualifier is the dominant VAG trigger of NIS2 (S3) propagating to all 10 sub-points of Art. 21(2)(a)–(j).

nodes.label: NIS2-CL13 — Art. 21(2)(d) Supply Chain Security Clause
nodes.rationale: Four Berry instances: VAG/S2 'supply chain security' (4 readings), VAG/S2 'security-related aspects' (3 readings), SCOPE-Q/S3 'direct' (5 readings — the single most consequential scope-limiting term in NIS2 Ch. IV), POLY/S2 'suppliers or service providers' (hendiadys vs distinct).
nodes.norm_label: nis2-cl13 — art. 21(2)(d) supply chain security clause

nodes.label: Requirement 6.1 - High-Level Vendor Risk Assessment
nodes.rationale: Volere immunity requirement: vendors, suppliers, components, and ICT service providers undergo risk-anchored due diligence with proportionality documentation and ongoing monitoring before entry to the supply chain. Priority MUST, verification TEST. NIST CSF: GV.SC-01/02/03/04, ID.AM-04, ID.RA-02.

nodes.label: Requirement 6.1.1 - GDPR Processor Due Diligence
nodes.rationale: Processor-as-legal-entity due diligence with documented sufficient guarantees and Art. 28(3) DPA closed-list clauses. EDPB Guidelines 07/2020 4-factor assessment. Sub-processor authorisation chain under Art. 28(2).

nodes.label: Requirement 6.1.2 - NIS2 Direct-Supplier Security
