nodes.rationale: Direct-supplier-as-relationship security with Art. 21(2)(d) direct scope-limiter, Art. 21(1) appropriate and proportionate chapeau, and Art. 21(3) three-prong supplier assessment (vulnerabilities + quality + secure-development procedures).

nodes.label: Requirement 6.1.3 - CRA Component Due Diligence
nodes.rationale: Third-party-component due diligence procedural + substantive including non-commercial OSS per Art. 3(48), with Art. 13(6) vulnerability reporting and Annex VII §2 technical-documentation record. OSS-specific calibration: stewardship assessment, CVD policy review, vulnerability disclosure channel, governance-transparency review.

nodes.label: Requirement 6.1.4 — ICT Third-Party Risk under Four-Factor Proportionality
nodes.rationale: Central requirement defining the DORA Art. 28(1) four-factor proportionality test (nature, scale, complexity, importance) with Art. 28(5) CIF escalator, Art. 30(2) 9-element contract, and Art. 30(3)(e) audit-rights architecture. Operates at the financial-entity ICT-dependency boundary with tier hand-offs to GDPR, NIS2, and CRA legs.
nodes.norm_label: requirement 6.1.4 — ict third-party risk under four-factor proportionality

nodes.label: D-06 Supply-Chain Domain Index
nodes.rationale: Top-level index for the D-06 Supply-Chain domain containing 4 sub-subdomains (D-06.1 through D-06.4), 4 merged files, 55 article copies, and 161 ambiguity sections.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 29 - Processing Under Authority
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-011, 012. Processor and persons under authority shall not process except on instructions from controller, unless required by law.

nodes.label: 4-track contract architecture (emergent tension)
nodes.rationale: GDPR 8 DPA elements + DORA 9 ICT-contract elements + NIS2 supplier-assessment + CRA importer/distributor market-access duties must be sequenced without flattening actors or recipients. Resolved by consolidated matrix, not single stricter regime.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 30: ICT third-party contractual arrangements
nodes.rationale: 9-element minimum list (a)-(i) + Art. 30(3) CIF-only clauses (audit rights, exit strategies). Operationalises NIS2 'security-related contractual aspects' with specific provisions. DORA-exceeds-NIS2 in financial-services subset.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 30: ict third-party contractual arrangements

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28(3): 8-element processor contract
nodes.rationale: Closed 8-element AND-list (a)-(h): documented instructions, confidentiality, Art. 32 measures, sub-processor authorisation, data-subject-rights assistance, incident assistance, deletion/return, audit/inspection. Each sub-clause is mandatory.

nodes.label: Req 6.3: 4-track contractual-security matrix requirement
nodes.rationale: High-level MUST requirement: maintain a 4-track contractual-security matrix keyed by supplier/regulator/instrument/actor/recipient. When ≥2 tracks overlap, apply clause-list union rule. DORA-exceeds-NIS2 in financial subset; CRA duties remain regulatory (non-DPA-converted).

nodes.label: Req 6.3.1: GDPR Art. 28(3) DPA + Art. 46/48 safeguards
nodes.rationale: Materialises controller/processor DPA as 8-element closed-list + transfer safeguards + international-agreement filter. In DORA overlap, GDPR layer is additive (union, not substitution).
nodes.norm_label: req 6.3.1: gdpr art. 28(3) dpa + art. 46/48 safeguards

nodes.label: Req 6.3.2: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(d) supplier contracts + Art. 21(3) assessment
nodes.rationale: Embeds security-related contractual aspects into direct supplier relationships with three-prong assessment evidence. The 'direct' scope-limiter is the single most consequential SCOPE-Q ambiguity in NIS2 Chapter IV.
nodes.norm_label: req 6.3.2: nis2 art. 21(2)(d) supplier contracts + art. 21(3) assessment

nodes.label: Req 6.3.3: CRA importer/distributor market-access duties
nodes.rationale: Enforces importer Art. 19 pre-market verification + distributor Art. 20 due-care + Art. 13(6) component-vulnerability reporting. CRA duties are MSA-facing regulatory obligations, NOT DPA-style negotiated contracts.

nodes.label: Req 6.3.4: DORA Art. 30 ICT-contract + Art. 28(5) standards
nodes.rationale: Structures ICT third-party contracts with 9-element minimum list + standards compliance + CIF-only clauses. CORRECTED CRDA pair resolves to clause-list union with GDPR Art. 28(3). DORA-exceeds-NIS2 in financial-services subset.
nodes.norm_label: req 6.3.4: dora art. 30 ict-contract + art. 28(5) standards

nodes.label: CRA Article 13: Manufacturer obligations
nodes.rationale: Umbrella article covering design/development/production (13(1)), risk assessment (13(2)), documentation (13(3)), technical documentation (13(4)), due diligence (13(5)), vulnerability handling (13(6)), systematic documentation (13(7)), policies (13(8)), substantial modification (13(10)), archives (13(11)), pre-market chain (13(12)), retention (13(13)), series production (13(14)), identification (13(15)/(16)), SPOC (13(17)), Annex II info (13(18)), support period (13(19)), EU declaration (13(20)), corrective measures (13(21)), MSA cooperation (13(22)), cessation (13(23)), implementing acts (13(24)/(25)).

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-02.2: Vulnerability remediation and support period
nodes.norm_label: sub-domain d-02.2: vulnerability remediation and support period

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 44 — General transfer principle
nodes.rationale: Umbrella principle: any transfer to a third country shall take place only if Chapter V conditions are complied with and the GDPR protection level is not undermined.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 45 — Adequacy decisions
nodes.rationale: Commission adequacy decisions exempt transfers from specific authorisation; periodic review at least every four years; amend/suspend/repeal where protection no longer adequate.

nodes.label: EDPB Recommendations 01/2020
nodes.rationale: Supplementary-measures framework operationalising Schrems II essential-equivalence test. §B.1 makes essential-equivalence binding for transfers to countries with extensive public-authority access. Rejects combining multiple Art. 46(2) mechanisms.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 46 — Appropriate safeguards
nodes.rationale: Six mutually exclusive mechanisms (binding instrument, BCRs, Commission SCCs, SA SCCs, codes of conduct, certification). Closed list; one mechanism per transfer. Schrems II requires essential equivalence.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 49 — Derogations for specific situations
nodes.rationale: Seven disjunctive grounds plus catch-all (not repetitive, limited number, compelling legitimate interests, suitable safeguards). Applies only in absence of adequacy and Art. 46 safeguards.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 49 — derogations for specific situations

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-056: Appropriate-safeguards mechanism selection for third-country transfers
nodes.rationale: Requires selection of one of six closed-list Art. 46(2) mechanisms per transfer, with Schrems II essential-equivalence standard and supplementary measures where destination regime is deficient. Mapped to GV.SC-03 and GV.SC-04.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-056: appropriate-safeguards mechanism selection for third-country transfers

nodes.label: EDPB Guidelines 05/2020
nodes.rationale: §3.4: Art. 49(1)(a) derogation consent must be explicit, specific to the transfer, and documented as risk-informed; controller cannot rely on same consent artefact as underlying Art. 6(1)(a) basis.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 9: Processing of special categories of personal data
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(1) prohibition of nine categories, Art. 9(2) ten exceptions. Source for SR-GDPR-028 and referenced in SR-GDPR-038 exception.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 9: processing of special categories of personal data

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 48 — Third-country legal-request filter
nodes.rationale: Third-country judgments/decisions compelling transfer enforceable only on basis of international agreement (e.g., MLAT). Response to extraterritorial legal-process demands like U.S. CLOUD Act.

nodes.label: SO-GDPR-035: Third-country legal requests only on international agreement
nodes.rationale: Court or administrative decisions of third countries requiring transfer/disclosure are enforceable only if based on an international agreement in force between the requesting country and the EU/Member State.
nodes.norm_label: so-gdpr-035: third-country legal requests only on international agreement

nodes.label: CRA Article 13 — Manufacturer Obligations (Security Rules)
nodes.rationale: Primary source document containing the bulk of CRA Art. 13 security rules covering design, risk assessment, updates, CVD, SBOM, identification, retention, and conformity.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33: Breach notification
nodes.rationale: Art. 33(1) 72-hour controller notification to supervisory authority; Art. 33(2) processor-to-controller without undue delay; twin temporal anchor with risk-based carve-out.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 34 — Communication to Data Subject
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-015, 019, 020, 021; establishes high-risk threshold for data-subject communication and three carve-outs (encryption, subsequent measures, disproportionate effort).
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 34 — communication to data subject

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32 — Security of Processing (SO+SR)
nodes.rationale: Per-article split generated from 01_SecurityObjectives.md and 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md. Covers Art. 32(1)(a)-(d), Art. 32(2), Art. 32(4) security measures, pseudonymisation, encryption, testing, and resilience obligations.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33 — Breach Notification (SO+SR)
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering Art. 33(1) 72-hour notification, Art. 33(2) processor-to-controller notification, Art. 33(3) content requirements, and Art. 34 data-subject communication.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-02.3: CVD and vulnerability reporting
nodes.norm_label: sub-domain d-02.3: cvd and vulnerability reporting

nodes.label: GDPR Arts. 44-49: Cross-border transfer regime
nodes.rationale: Art. 44 umbrella principle; Art. 45 adequacy; Art. 46 appropriate safeguards; Art. 47 BCRs; Art. 49 derogations; hierarchical structure where adequacy is preferred, safeguards secondary, derogations last resort.

nodes.label: CJEU Schrems II C-311/18
nodes.rationale: §96 essential-equivalence test for third-country transfers; §94 foreseeability of third-country practice; §134 supplementary measures; procedural legality does not compensate for substantive deficiencies.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 47 — Binding corporate rules
nodes.rationale: BCR approval via consistency mechanism; 14 mandatory content items (closed list); legally binding; enforceable data-subject rights; applies to every group member.

nodes.label: NIST CSF RS.MI-01: Incidents are contained
nodes.rationale: Upstream containment-discipline framing: threat communication extends containment perimeter to recipient side.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rs.mi-01: incidents are contained

nodes.label: ISO/IEC 27001 — Information Security Management
nodes.rationale: EBA Guidelines expect cryptographic keys managed under ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A.10 or successor; also referenced as de facto baseline for 'appropriate technical and organisational measures' under GDPR.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 24 — Security Objectives & Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering the digital operational resilience testing programme (Art. 24-26), including TLPT requirements and 12-way testing modality portfolio.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 4 — Security Objectives & Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering authentication (Art. 9(4)(d)), patching (Art. 9(4)(f)), management-body literacy (Art. 5(4)), staff training (Art. 13(6)), and management-body ownership (Art. 5(2)).

nodes.label: CRA Article 21 — Importer/Distributor Manufacturer-Equivalent Trigger
nodes.rationale: Accountability transfer: importer/distributor becomes manufacturer upon own-name placement or substantial modification.

nodes.label: CRA Article 22 — Third-Party Substantial Modification
nodes.rationale: Closes loophole for integrators/third-party modifiers outside supply chain contract who substantially modify products.

nodes.label: CJEU IAB Europe C-604/22
nodes.rationale: Interpreted 'jointly determine' to include parties with determinative influence on purposes or means even without direct processing; extends joint-controller status to industry-association-managed consent frameworks (TCF).

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 6(1) - Lawfulness Bases
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-026, 027. Six bases: consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public interest, legitimate interests.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 9(1) - Special Categories Prohibition
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-GDPR-028. Prohibits processing of nine special categories unless Art. 9(2) exception applies.

nodes.label: D-02.1 — Vulnerability Identification (downstream consumer)
nodes.rationale: Consumes the SBOM for CVE matching under SR-CRA-007. The machine-readable format enables automated correlation of upstream CVEs against the product's dependency surface.

nodes.label: D-02.2 — Vulnerability Remediation (downstream consumer)
nodes.rationale: Addresses component vulnerabilities identified by the SBOM under SR-CRA-008 + SR-CRA-010. The SBOM provides the component inventory that drives remediation prioritisation.

nodes.label: D-06.1 — Component Due Diligence (downstream consumer)
nodes.rationale: Consumes the SBOM as upstream component-identification artefact for component due diligence under SR-CRA-050. The SBOM feeds the component-tier inventory substrate.

nodes.label: D-06.3 — Contractual Security Obligations (downstream consumer)
nodes.rationale: Consumes SBOM-related Annex VII §1-§2 records as part of the conformity-assessment record but does not address the SBOM duty itself.

nodes.label: D-09.4 — Technical Documentation (downstream consumer)
nodes.rationale: The SBOM is the Annex VII §2(b) artefact in the conformity-assessment bundle under SR-CRA-059. D-09.4 consumes the SBOM as part of the technical documentation record.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 26 — Security Objectives & Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering joint-controller arrangements (Art. 26(1)-(3)), identity verification minimisation (Art. 12(6)), and downstream cascade (Art. 19).

nodes.label: DORA CL19-5 — Art. 19(5) Outsourcing of reporting
nodes.rationale: Entity may outsource reporting to CTPP but remains fully responsible; mirrors Art. 26(3) and Art. 22(1) responsibility non-delegation principle
nodes.norm_label: dora cl19-5 — art. 19(5) outsourcing of reporting

nodes.label: DORA CL19-6 — Art. 19(6) CA→other authorities forwarding
nodes.rationale: 5 recipient categories (EBA/ESMA/EIOPA, ECB, NIS2 CAs/CSIRTs, BRRD/SRB, other public authorities); most extensive multi-supervisory routing in 5-regulation corpus
nodes.norm_label: dora cl19-6 — art. 19(6) ca→other authorities forwarding

nodes.label: DORA CL20-1 — Art. 20 ESAs RTS/ITS mandate
nodes.rationale: Pure RTS+ITS delegation for Ch. III; 5-factor proportionality; consistent approach with NIS2; substantially implemented via Reg. (EU) 2024/2956 as of mid-2025
nodes.norm_label: dora cl20-1 — art. 20 esas rts/its mandate

nodes.label: DORA CL22-1 — Art. 22(1) Supervisory feedback
nodes.rationale: Mandatory acknowledge + discretionary substance; opposite of NIS2 Art. 23(5) mandatory CSIRT response; closed-loop asymmetry: entities must report, CAs may respond

nodes.label: NIS2-CL21 — Art. 21(3) s2 EU-level risk propagation
nodes.rationale: Requires entities to take into account results of Art. 22(1) coordinated assessments; R1 passive consideration is literal reading; 'results' polysemy unresolved
nodes.norm_label: nis2-cl21 — art. 21(3) s2 eu-level risk propagation

nodes.label: NIS2-CL23 — Art. 22(1) s1 Coordinated supply-chain risk assessment
nodes.rationale: Cooperation Group may carry out coordinated assessments; 'critical' undefined (R4 Commission-determined); 'may carry out' is permissive; multi-institutional coordination (Cooperation Group + Commission + ENISA)
nodes.norm_label: nis2-cl23 — art. 22(1) s1 coordinated supply-chain risk assessment

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 21 — Supply-Chain Security and Policy Review
nodes.rationale: Parallel obligations referenced in DORA rules: Art. 21(2)(e) supply-chain security, Art. 21(2)(f) policy review cadence, Art. 21(2)(g) basic security training.
nodes.norm_label: nis 2 art. 21 — supply-chain security and policy review

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.SC-04: Supplier/Third-Party Assessment
nodes.rationale: Operative subcategory for distributor's Art. 20(2) checks: CE marking affixed, Annex II documentation present, manufacturer + importer compliance posture verified — all contractual-obligation confirmation points.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 20 — Distributor Due Care & Corrective Measures
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 20 — distributor due care & corrective measures

nodes.label: DORA CL28-1 — Art. 28 Umbrella principles + strategy
nodes.rationale: Integral component of Art. 6 framework; full responsibility; proportionality; multi-vendor strategy; longest single article in DORA (10 paragraphs)
nodes.norm_label: dora cl28-1 — art. 28 umbrella principles + strategy

nodes.label: DORA CL29-1 — Art. 29(1) Concentration-risk preliminary
nodes.rationale: Non-substitutable CTPP OR multiple contracts with same/closely-connected CTPP; NEW in v0.2 (T3 omitted)

nodes.label: DORA CL4-1 — Art. 4(1) Proportionality chapeau
nodes.rationale: Default proportionality for Ch. II; self-implementing; inherited by every Ch. II–V Sec. I clause; mirrors NIS2 Art. 1(2) and CRA Art. 1(2)

nodes.label: DORA CL5-1 — Art. 5(1) Internal governance framework
nodes.rationale: Three lines of defence model per Art. 6(4); 'effective and prudent' dual qualifiers; target: high level of digital operational resilience
nodes.norm_label: dora cl5-1 — art. 5(1) internal governance framework

nodes.label: DORA CL6-1 — Art. 6(1) Framework chapeau
nodes.rationale: Sound, comprehensive, well-documented ICT risk management framework; integral part of governance

nodes.label: GDPR Article 27: Representatives of controllers or processors not established in the Union
nodes.rationale: Source article for SR-GDPR-038. Art. 27(1) designation requirement and Art. 27(2)(a) conjunctive exception.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 27: representatives of controllers or processors not established in the union

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 4 — Definitions (SO+SR)
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering Art. 4 definitions (personal data, pseudonymisation, controller/processor, consent, BCR) and their downstream security obligations.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 49(1)(a): Explicit Transfer Consent
nodes.rationale: Derogation ground requiring explicit consent after being informed of possible risks due to absence of adequacy decision and appropriate safeguards (Recital 49).

nodes.label: GDPR Article 39: Tasks of the data protection officer
nodes.rationale: Source article for SR-GDPR-042. Art. 39(1)(a) inform/advise and Art. 39(1)(b) awareness/training.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 39: tasks of the data protection officer

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AT-01: All users informed and trained on cybersecurity topics
nodes.rationale: Broad-coverage general-population training duty. Recurring cadence with content updating for emerging threats.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.at-01: all users informed and trained on cybersecurity topics

nodes.label: NIST CSF RS.CO-03: Information shared with designated stakeholders per rules
nodes.rationale: Information-sharing mechanism delivering Art. 34(2) content to data subjects. Satisfies higher Art. 34 threshold above Art. 33.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rs.co-03: information shared with designated stakeholders per rules

nodes.label: NIST CSF RS.CO-04: Coordination with stakeholders consistent with rules
nodes.rationale: Coordination discipline for multi-channel notification (direct, website, public). Ensures equally effective reach and documented high-risk classification.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rs.co-04: coordination with stakeholders consistent with rules

nodes.label: GDPR Article 34: Communication of a personal data breach to the data subject
nodes.rationale: Art. 34(1) high-risk threshold, Art. 34(2) content requirements. Source for SR-GDPR-019. Higher threshold than Art. 33 supervisory notification.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 34: communication of a personal data breach to the data subject

nodes.label: CJEU Schrems II (C-311/18) — Substantial Equivalence Test
nodes.rationale: §96 held procedural legality does not compensate for substantive deficiencies in destination regime; essential-equivalence test binding for transfers to third countries with extensive public-authority access.
nodes.norm_label: cjeu schrems ii (c-311/18) — substantial equivalence test

nodes.label: DORA Art. 28(4) — Pre-Contractual Assessment (5 Sub-Steps)
nodes.rationale: Five sub-steps before entering arrangement: (a) critical/important identification, (b) supervisory conditions, (c) risk + concentration (Art. 29), (d) due diligence, (e) conflicts of interest. Explicitly cross-references Art. 29 for concentration risk.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 29 — Preliminary ICT Concentration Risk Assessment
nodes.rationale: Entity-level preliminary assessment of ICT concentration risk: non-substitutable CTPP or multiple contracts with same/closely-connected CTPP. NEW in v0.2 (T3 omitted). Covers subcontracting risk, insolvency law, 3rd-country law enforcement, long subcontracting chains.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 29 — preliminary ict concentration risk assessment

nodes.label: DORA CL29-1 — Art. 29(1) Concentration Risk Preliminary
nodes.rationale: Non-substitutable CTPP OR multiple contracts with same/closely-connected CTPP. NEW in v0.2 (T3 omitted). Cross-referenced from CL28-3 pre-contractual assessment step (4)(c).
nodes.norm_label: dora cl29-1 — art. 29(1) concentration risk preliminary

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(1): Appropriate and Proportionate Measures Chapeau
nodes.rationale: Meta-clause propagating to every Art. 21(2) sub-point. Four proportionality factors: exposure, size, likelihood/severity, societal/economic impact. Dominant Berry VAG-S3 ambiguity of the Directive.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 21(1): appropriate and proportionate measures chapeau

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2) Chapeau: All-Hazards Approach
nodes.rationale: Meta-methodology clause converting NIS1 cybersecurity-only default into all-hazards reading including physical environment.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(4): Corrective Measures
nodes.rationale: Triggered-response instrument: entity finds non-compliance → takes necessary, appropriate and proportionate corrective measures without undue delay.

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.IM-01: Improvement Processes Identified and Used
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-NIS2-037 and SR-NIS2-042 as the improvement/corrective-action process substrate.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.im-01: improvement processes identified and used

nodes.label: Business continuity, backup, disaster recovery, crisis management
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(c) BC + backup + DR + CM ensuring ability to restore availability and integrity.
nodes.norm_label: business continuity, backup, disaster recovery, crisis management

nodes.label: Management body approves and oversees Art. 21 measures
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 20(1) management body approves, oversees, and can be held liable for Art. 21 compliance. Public-institution carve-out in Art. 20(1) sentence 2.
nodes.norm_label: management body approves and oversees art. 21 measures

nodes.label: DORA CL26-1 — Art. 26(1) TLPT cadence
nodes.rationale: Hard 3-year numeric anchor; CA may reduce/increase frequency; TIBER-EU non-binding definitional anchor; hard numeric anchors are most effective disambiguation technique

nodes.label: DORA CL30-15 — Art. 30(3)(e)+(f) Monitoring + exit
nodes.rationale: Unrestricted access/inspection/audit (4 sub-points); mandatory adequate transition + migration; contract-architecture 'coração'

nodes.label: NIS2-CL48 — Art. 24(1) s1 Certification requirement
nodes.rationale: Member States may require certified ICT products/services/processes under CSA Art. 49; 'may require' is discretionary; cross-reference to Regulation (EU) 2019/881

nodes.label: NIS2-CL50 — Art. 24(2) Commission delegated acts
nodes.rationale: Commission empowered to specify which entities must use certified products; triggered by insufficient cybersecurity levels; implementation period undefined

nodes.label: Regulation (EU) 2019/881 — Cybersecurity Act
nodes.rationale: Referenced by NIS2 Art. 24 for European cybersecurity certification schemes (Art. 49) and ENISA candidate schemes (Art. 48(2))

nodes.label: DORA Art. 18 — ICT Incident Classification (6 Criteria)
nodes.rationale: Six multiplicative criteria for classifying major ICT-related incidents. Combination rule undefined at OJ level; materiality thresholds delegated to ESAs RTS (Art. 18(3)). Single deepest definitional regress in DORA Ch. III.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 18 — ict incident classification (6 criteria)

nodes.label: CL18-8 — DORA Art. 18(3) ESAs RTS Mandate
nodes.rationale: ESAs RTS to specify materiality thresholds for major ICT incidents, cross-MS relevance criteria, and cyber-threat thresholds. Deadline 17 Jan 2024 passed; RTS in adoption pipeline. Defining characteristic of Ch. III: classification threshold has no OJ anchor.
nodes.norm_label: cl18-8 — dora art. 18(3) esas rts mandate

nodes.label: DORA Art. 22 — Supervisory Feedback (Discretionary)
nodes.rationale: CA must acknowledge receipt but may (discretionary) provide feedback. Opposite of NIS2 Art. 23(5) mandatory CSIRT response. Creates closed-loop asymmetry: entities must report, CAs may respond.

nodes.label: Basic cyber hygiene practices
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(g) establishes basic cyber hygiene covering all users of NIS with access to entity systems.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 32 — Security Objectives & Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering BC implementation arrangements (Art. 11(2)) and independent internal audit review (Art. 11(3)).

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 21 — Security Objectives & Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering CIA+resilience baseline (Art. 5(1)(f), Art. 32(1)(b)), timely restoration (Art. 32(1)(c)), and derogation-based transfers (Art. 49).

nodes.label: CRA Article 3 — Definitions and Core Security Rules
nodes.rationale: Contains definitions (Art. 3(13) manufacturer, 3(30) substantial modification, 3(39) SBOM, 3(44) incident, 3(48) FOSS) and core SRs for encryption and SBOM format.
nodes.norm_label: cra article 3 — definitions and core security rules

nodes.label: SO-NIS2-024: Use of Certified ICT Products/Services/Processes Where Required
nodes.rationale: Where required by a Member State in accordance with Art. 24(1), or by a Commission delegated act under Art. 24(2), entities use particular ICT products, services, and processes certified under European cybersecurity certification schemes adopted pursuant to Art. 49 of Regulation (EU) 2019/881.
nodes.norm_label: so-nis2-024: use of certified ict products/services/processes where required

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-043: European Cybersecurity Certification Aligned with Article 21 Requirements
nodes.rationale: REFERENTIAL SR: entity-side obligation is conditional on either Member-State exercise of Article 24(1) permission or Commission adoption of Article 24(2) delegated acts. Until either trigger occurs, the SR is conditional.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-043: european cybersecurity certification aligned with article 21 requirements

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.PS-06 — Secure Software Development Practices
nodes.rationale: Convergent anchor for all 3 regulations at D-07.2. Secure software development practices integrated and monitored throughout SDLC. The structurally significant mapping since no OJ clause prescribes specific coding standards.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ps-06 — secure software development practices

nodes.label: AI Act Article 15 (Accuracy, Robustness, Cybersecurity)
nodes.rationale: Corner-stone substantive duty fusing three AI-technical properties; 3-way AND admits no partial compliance.

nodes.label: AI Act Article 55 (GPAI Systemic Risk Obligations)
nodes.rationale: Title IV Chapter V obligations for GPAI models with systemic risk; parallel to but distinct from Title III high-risk obligations.
nodes.norm_label: ai act article 55 (gpai systemic risk obligations)

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 55(1)(a) — GPAI model evaluation
nodes.rationale: Second-most-consequential AI Act ambiguity; standardised protocols + state of the art + systemic risks triple; parallel to but distinct from Title III high-risk obligations.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 55(1)(a) — gpai model evaluation

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 73 — Serious incident reporting
nodes.rationale: Most temporally complex notification clause: 3 timelines (15/10/2 days) × 2 attribution thresholds; cross-regulation parallel to NIS2 C30, DORA Art. 19, GDPR Art. 33.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 73 — serious incident reporting

nodes.label: SO-AIACT-013: Serious Incident Reporting
nodes.rationale: Art. 73(1)-(4) tiered reporting with differentiated timelines (15/10/2 days) to market surveillance authorities.

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 15(4)–(5) — AI-Specific Attack-Defence
nodes.rationale: AI/ML-specific attack-defence: 6 categories (data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples, model evasion, confidentiality attacks, model flaws). Proportionality qualifier: as appropriate to purpose and conditions of use. Does NOT map to conventional coding practices.

nodes.label: Req 7.2 — High-Level Secure Coding Practices Requirement
nodes.rationale: Common secure-coding duty converging across CRA, DORA, and AI Act; engages only on Conditional-Y integrated stack (AI-enabled CRA product), not on baseline scope-disjoint pairs.
nodes.norm_label: req 7.2 — high-level secure coding practices requirement

nodes.label: 5-Layer By-Design Architecture
nodes.rationale: The layered reconciliation architecture: GDPR controller means-determination → NIS2 entity NIS-lifecycle → CRA manufacturer product-lifecycle → DORA financial-entity change-mgmt + testing → AI Act high-risk AI system design + QMS. The 5 target objects are layered, not collapsed. This is the operational convergence that supersedes any single-regulator reading.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(4) Sentence 2 AI-Act Risk-Assessment Substitution
nodes.rationale: Explicit cross-regulation consolidation rule: CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2 permits a unified risk assessment under AI Act Art. 9 to substitute for the CRA risk assessment when both apply to the same AI-enabled product. The only OJ-level consolidation rule in D-07.1 — does not extend to attack defence.
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 13(4) sentence 2 ai-act risk-assessment substitution

nodes.label: D-07.2 Secure Coding Practices
nodes.rationale: Downstream sub-domain where D-07.1's by-design decision becomes a code-level instruction. Receives pseudonymisation + minimisation + by-default triad from GDPR, AI-attack-defence categories from AI Act, and secure-coding standards from NIS2 development phase.

nodes.label: D-07.4 Change Management
nodes.rationale: Downstream sub-domain where the DORA-side by-design operationalisation manifests via the change-management six-step (recorded/tested/assessed/approved/implemented/verified). Also operationalises NIS2 maintenance phase for ICT-hazard subset.

nodes.label: DORA Dedicated-By-Design Absence
nodes.rationale: Structural Layer 2 review item: DORA has no OJ-mandated dedicated by-design clause. Art. 9(4)(b) is network/infrastructure-management, not a by-design mandate. Secure-by-design is operationalised through Art. 9(4)(e) change-management six-step + Art. 24 testing programme. SR-DORA-004 partial mapping preserved.

nodes.label: AI Act Recital 78 GDPR Preservation
nodes.rationale: AI Act Recital 78 explicitly preserves the GDPR. For a high-risk AI system processing personal data, AI Act Art. 15(1) + QMS design/design-control/design-verification stacks with GDPR Art. 25(1) data-protection by-design as distinct design outputs (AI-system property vs privacy property).

nodes.label: SO-D-07.1.AIACT Sub-SO
nodes.rationale: AI Act-specific sub-security-objective for high-risk AI system accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity with lifecycle consistency + QMS design/design-control/design-verification. Inherits from SO-AIACT-009 + SO-AIACT-010. Trigger: provider places high-risk AI system on market.

nodes.label: State-of-the-Art Anchor (Duplicated, Uncoordinated)
nodes.rationale: The 'state of the art' anchor is duplicated across all 5 regulations but interpreted independently. GDPR weights cost + nature/scope/context/purposes/risks; NIS2 weights appropriate-and-proportionate + cost; CRA weights Annex I essential-requirements; DORA weights EBA Guidelines; AI Act weights harmonised standards + Art. 9 risk-management. Entities implementing all 5 must reconcile through documented decision records.

nodes.label: Requirement 7.1 — 5-Layer By-Design Architecture
nodes.rationale: The top-level Volere requirement (integrity subtype) mandating security integration into the full lifecycle via documented by-design decisions, risk-assessment propagation, proportionate safeguards, and lifecycle consistency. Priority MUST, verification TEST.

nodes.label: Requirement 7.1.1 — GDPR By-Design and By-Default
nodes.rationale: Controller-side data-protection by-design and by-default requirement. 2-tier architecture: by-design is the architectural decision record; by-default is the operational implementation. 4-factor qualitative proportionality.

nodes.label: Requirement 7.1.2 — NIS2 3-Phase Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Entity-level security in acquisition, development, and maintenance of NIS with vulnerability handling and disclosure. 3-phase coordinated lifecycle with explicit hand-offs at acquisition, development, and maintenance gates.

nodes.label: Requirement 7.1.3 — CRA 6-Phase Product By-Design
nodes.rationale: Product cybersecurity via Annex I Part I across 6 lifecycle phases (planning, design, development, production, delivery, maintenance). Risk-assessment propagation is continuous, not one-shot. Support period ≥ 5 years.

nodes.label: Requirement 7.1.4 — DORA Change-Mgmt + Testing
nodes.rationale: Financial-entity infrastructure management with change-management six-step + testing programme. Partial at D-07.1 — no OJ dedicated by-design mandate. By-design compliance demonstrated through change-management + testing outputs.

nodes.label: Requirement 7.1.5 — AI Act QMS + Lifecycle Consistency
nodes.rationale: High-risk AI system accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity with lifecycle consistency + QMS covering design/design-control/design-verification. 13 enumerated QMS aspects. AI-attack-defence categories (6) are AI-specific and do not substitute for CRA Annex I Part I.
nodes.norm_label: requirement 7.1.5 — ai act qms + lifecycle consistency

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(1): Security of processing (risk-based measures)
nodes.rationale: Risk-based preamble with five factors (state of the art, costs, nature, scope, context, purposes, risks). Lists four sub-letters (a)-(d) as floor of expected measures. Operationalises Art. 5(1)(f).
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 32(1): security of processing (risk-based measures)

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(1)(f): Integrity and confidentiality principle
nodes.rationale: One of six Art. 5(1) principles. Requires appropriate security including protection against unauthorised/unlawful processing and accidental loss/destruction/damage. 'Appropriate' anchored to Art. 32(1) risk-based test.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 5(1)(f): integrity and confidentiality principle

nodes.label: SO-AIACT-007 — Transparency to deployers
nodes.rationale: Operation sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret output and use appropriately; instructions for use with characteristics, capabilities and limitations.

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-011 — Instructions for use
nodes.rationale: 8 quality adjectives in twin AND-chains; intersects with CRA Art. 7(4) instructions-for-use obligations.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 25(1) — Open-list test modalities
nodes.rationale: 12 specific test modalities under such-as open-list signal; structurally identical to CRA Annex I Part I §2(d).

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(a)–(j) — Security measures sub-points
nodes.rationale: Ten sub-points covering policies, incident handling, business continuity, supply chain, development security, effectiveness, cyber hygiene, cryptography, HR/access/asset, MFA/communications.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(3) — Supply-chain risk assessment
nodes.rationale: Requires entities to consider vulnerabilities of direct suppliers, overall quality of products, and secure development procedures.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 25(1) — Member State encouragement of standards
nodes.rationale: Encouragement-only provision with technology-neutrality clause; no binding entity obligation.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 25(1) — member state encouragement of standards

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 25(2) — ENISA advice and guidelines
nodes.rationale: One of few mandatory ENISA provisions in Chapter IV; shall draw up advice and guidelines.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 25(2) — enisa advice and guidelines

nodes.label: D-07.2 Secure Coding Practices (Domain)
nodes.rationale: Domain covering secure coding practices across CRA, DORA (partial), and AI Act (partial). GDPR and NIS2 explicitly out-of-scope. P0 disagreement: AEGIS taxonomy marks DORA as sole authority but CRDA-deep finds no OJ-text support.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-04.1: Incident Response (Detection)
nodes.rationale: Covers continuous breach detection enabling the 72-hour notification clock.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-03.3: Access Control (Authorisation)
nodes.rationale: Covers instruction-bound processing and confidentiality undertakings for authorised personnel.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 18 — Classification of ICT-related incidents
nodes.rationale: Six multiplicative criteria for classifying incidents; delegates combination rule and materiality thresholds to ESA RTS.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 18 — classification of ict-related incidents

nodes.label: DORA Art. 19 — Reporting of major ICT-related incidents
nodes.rationale: Three-tier reporting (initial/intermediate/final), voluntary cyber-threat notification, mandatory client notification.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 19 — reporting of major ict-related incidents

nodes.label: DORA Art. 20 — Harmonisation of reporting
nodes.rationale: Pure RTS/ITS delegation; content, time limits, templates wholly dependent on ESAs Joint Committee output; deadline 17 July 2024 passed.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 23 — Payment-sector extension
nodes.rationale: Extends Ch. III to operational/security payment-related incidents for CIs, PIs, AISPs, EMIs.

nodes.label: SO-AIACT-003 — Data governance and bias detection
nodes.rationale: High-risk AI systems developed on basis of quality datasets with data governance practices detecting, preventing and mitigating biases.
nodes.norm_label: so-aiact-003 — data governance and bias detection

nodes.label: SO-AIACT-004 — Special-category data for bias correction
nodes.rationale: Exceptional processing of special-category personal data subject to 6 cumulative conditions including state-of-the-art security and privacy-preserving measures.
nodes.norm_label: so-aiact-004 — special-category data for bias correction

nodes.label: AI Act Article 72 (Post-Market Monitoring)
nodes.rationale: PMM system as ex-post assurance loop; borrows from MDR Art. 83 implicitly. Art. 74(1) extends EU market-surveillance framework to AI.

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-010 — Deployer-interpretable transparency
nodes.rationale: Principal high-risk-specific transparency duty; distinct from Art. 50 user-facing and Art. 70 deployer-information duties; principal locus for AI-explainability expectations.

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 43 — Conformity assessment
nodes.rationale: Conformity assessment examines QMS as umbrella obligation; part of Art. 17 + Art. 9 + Art. 15 accountability chain.

nodes.label: AI Act Article 9 (Risk Management System)
nodes.rationale: Umbrella provision for high-risk AI risk management; central AI Act ambiguity on 'risk management system' (POLY: ISO 31000 / NIST AI RMF / bespoke).

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 10 — Data governance for high-risk AI
nodes.rationale: Requires training/validation/testing datasets meeting quality criteria, 8-element data governance practices, and exceptional special-category data processing for bias detection.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 10 — data governance for high-risk ai

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 13 — Transparency and instructions for use
nodes.rationale: High-risk AI systems must be sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret output; instructions for use with 8 quality adjectives.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 13 — transparency and instructions for use

nodes.label: SO-AIACT-008 — Human oversight design
nodes.rationale: Effectively overseen by natural persons with appropriate human-machine interface tools; 5-element oversight capability list.

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-012 — Built-in human-oversight capability
nodes.rationale: Umbrella provision for human-oversight duty; oversight as built-in architectural feature rather than deployment-time add-on.

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-013 — Five cumulative oversight abilities
nodes.rationale: 5-element AND-coordinated list; automation bias polysemous; as appropriate and proportionate soft hedge modifies entire list.

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 14 — Human oversight
nodes.rationale: High-risk AI systems designed for effective oversight by natural persons; 5-element cumulative oversight abilities list.

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 15 — Accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity
nodes.rationale: Corner-stone substantive duty fusing three AI-technical properties into one continuous lifecycle-wide duty; includes resilience and AI-specific attack mitigation.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 15 — accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 17 — Quality management system
nodes.rationale: Umbrella QMS obligation with 13 enumerated aspects; cross-references Art. 9 risk management; inspired by ISO 9001 but not mandating a specific standard.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 17 — quality management system

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 26 — Deployer obligations
nodes.rationale: Deployer-side mirror of provider obligations; appropriate technical and organisational measures; human oversight assignment with competence, training, authority.

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 72 — Post-market monitoring
nodes.rationale: Ex-post assurance loop complementing ex-ante conformity assessment; borrows from MDR Art. 83; feeds Art. 15(1) lifecycle consistency and Art. 73 reporting.

nodes.label: Integrated ICT Business Continuity Policy Framework
nodes.rationale: Art. 11(1) requires comprehensive ICT business continuity policy, which may be adopted as dedicated specific policy forming integral part of overall BC policy. 'May be adopted' explicitly permits either form-factor.
nodes.norm_label: integrated ict business continuity policy framework

nodes.label: End-to-End ICT Incident Management Process
nodes.rationale: Art. 17(1) requires define, establish and implement ICT-related incident management process to detect, manage and notify. Twin 3-way verb coordinations read cumulatively. Cross-notification interface with GDPR Art. 33 creates composite supervisory exposure.

nodes.label: ICT Change Management Six-Step Process
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(4)(e) requires documented policies for ICT change management: recorded, tested, assessed, approved, implemented, verified. Six-way AND read as cumulative — partial-process compliance is non-compliance.

nodes.label: Compulsory ICT Security Awareness Training
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(6) requires ICT security awareness programmes and digital operational resilience training as compulsory modules. T4-vs-text gap: T4 maps DORA-C26 to Patch Management but OJ text is about training. 'Compulsory' read as completion-mandatory.

nodes.label: Sound and Comprehensive ICT Risk Management Framework
nodes.rationale: Art. 6(1) requires sound, comprehensive, well-documented ICT risk management framework enabling quick, efficient, comprehensive risk addressing. Top-of-stack governance artefact operationalised by Art. 7, 9, and Chapter III.
nodes.norm_label: sound and comprehensive ict risk management framework

nodes.label: Independence of ICT Risk Oversight (Three Lines of Defence)
nodes.rationale: Art. 6(4) requires assigning ICT risk oversight to a control function with appropriate independence per three-lines-of-defence model or internal risk management model. OR with alternative models opens door to COSO, ISO 31000.
nodes.norm_label: independence of ict risk oversight (three lines of defence)

nodes.label: Continuous Monitoring and Control of ICT-System Security
nodes.rationale: Art. 8(1) requires continuously monitor and control security and functioning of ICT systems. OJ-corrective note flags Art. 8(1)→Art. 9(1) misattribution — monitor obligation actually lives under Art. 9.
nodes.norm_label: continuous monitoring and control of ict-system security

nodes.label: Information Security Policy Covering CIA+A
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(4)(a) requires develop and document information security policy defining rules to protect availability, authenticity, integrity, confidentiality of data, information assets, ICT assets. Nested AND of 4x3=12 pairings all in scope.

nodes.label: Threat-Led Penetration Testing (TLPT)
nodes.rationale: Art. 26(1) requires TLPT at least every 3 years. Defined by reference to TIBER-EU framework (Art. 26(11)). Applies to significant entities under Art. 26(8) criteria.

nodes.label: Multi-Class Anomalous Activity Detection with SPOF Identification
nodes.rationale: Art. 10(1) requires mechanisms to promptly detect anomalous activities including network performance issues and ICT-related incidents, and identify potential material SPOFs. Three-class coverage: network, compute, performance.
nodes.norm_label: multi-class anomalous activity detection with spof identification

nodes.label: Multi-Layer Detection with Threshold-Driven Response Triggering
nodes.rationale: Art. 10(2) requires detection mechanisms enabling multiple layers of control, alert thresholds, trigger criteria, and automatic alert mechanisms. Four-verb coordination: enable, define, trigger, initiate.
nodes.norm_label: multi-layer detection with threshold-driven response triggering

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-03.4: Access Control / Default Limits
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation sub-domain for access control and default-necessary processing limits; referenced by SO-GDPR-007 and SR-GDPR-041.
nodes.norm_label: sub-domain d-03.4: access control / default limits

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-01.3: Pseudonymisation/Encryption
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation sub-domain for pseudonymisation and encryption; referenced by SR-GDPR-003, 004, 040 as the de-attribution and unintelligibility domain.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-04.1: Breach Detection
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation sub-domain for breach detection and awareness; referenced by SR-GDPR-014, 049 as the detection-capability domain anchoring the 72h clock.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 25 — Privacy by Design & Default
nodes.rationale: Per-article split generated from 01_SecurityObjectives.md and 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md; covers Art. 25(1) privacy by design and Art. 25(2) privacy by default with four coordinated minimisation dimensions.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 25 — privacy by design & default

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 34 — Breach Communication to Data Subjects
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering Art. 34(1) high-risk communication, Art. 34(2) content, and Art. 34(3)(a)-(c) exceptions (unintelligibility, subsequent measures, disproportionate effort).
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 34 — breach communication to data subjects

nodes.label: DORA Art. 25(2) — CSD/CCP pre-deployment vulnerability assessments
nodes.rationale: Sectoral carve-out unique in Ch. IV; pre-deployment assessment obligation for CSDs and CCPs reflecting FMI-specific risk profile.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 25(2) — csd/ccp pre-deployment vulnerability assessments

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-06.3: Supply Chain (Cross-border Transfers)
nodes.rationale: Covers cross-border transfer governance: adequacy, derogations, BCRs.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-03.1: Access Control (Identity Verification)
nodes.rationale: Covers proportionate identity verification for rights requests and minimised collection of verification data.

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 74(1) — Market surveillance extension
nodes.rationale: Extends Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 market-surveillance framework to AI systems; cross-regulation borrow requiring familiarity with 2019/1020.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 74(1) — market surveillance extension

nodes.label: 3-Track Coding-Architecture (CRA/DORA/AI Act)
nodes.rationale: Explicit layered hand-offs across 3 tracks: CRA product-side outcomes / DORA entity-side process / AI Act AI-system-side attack-defence. No OJ-level consolidation rule; each track demonstrates compliance independently. HL engages only on Conditional-Y integrated stack.

nodes.label: AEGIS Taxonomy §4.1 — DORA Sole-Authority Assignment
nodes.rationale: Marks DORA as SOLE AUTHORITY for D-07.2 Secure Coding Practices. CRDA-deep finds no OJ-text support: Art. 9(4)(e) is change-management, Art. 9(4)(f) is patches-and-updates. Layer 2 review item: either revise taxonomy or identify supporting OJ clause.

nodes.label: ISO/IEC 23894 — AI Risk Management
nodes.rationale: AI/ML-specific framework for AI-attack-defence coding-practices baseline. Part of the AI Act-side evidence base.

nodes.label: ISO/IEC 27034 — Application Security Controls
nodes.rationale: Industry framework for application-security controls. Part of the coding-practices evidence base since no OJ clause prescribes specific coding standards.

nodes.label: MITRE ATLAS — Adversarial Threat Landscape for AI Systems
nodes.rationale: AI/ML-specific framework for AI-attack-defence coding-practices baseline. Part of the AI Act-side evidence base.
nodes.norm_label: mitre atlas — adversarial threat landscape for ai systems

nodes.label: NIST AI RMF — AI Risk Management Framework
nodes.rationale: AI/ML-specific framework for AI-attack-defence coding-practices baseline. Part of the AI Act-side evidence base.
nodes.norm_label: nist ai rmf — ai risk management framework

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.PS-01 — Configuration Management Practices
nodes.rationale: Configuration-management practices established, documented, and applied to assets. Operationalises attack-surface reduction through documented configuration choices: default-closed external interfaces, port suppression, surface-area-baselining.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ps-01 — configuration management practices

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.PS-02 — Software Maintenance Commensurate with Risk
nodes.rationale: CRA anchors on PR.PS-02 for attack-surface/exploitation-mitigation lifecycle. Risk-assessment-driven attack-surface reduction per Art. 13(2) 6-phase propagation.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ps-02 — software maintenance commensurate with risk

nodes.label: OWASP SAMM — Software Assurance Maturity Model
nodes.rationale: Industry framework for software-assurance maturity. Part of the coding-practices evidence base since no OJ clause prescribes specific coding standards.
nodes.norm_label: owasp samm — software assurance maturity model

nodes.label: CRA↔AI_Act Pair — SAME COMPLEMENTARY (Conditional Y)
nodes.rationale: CRA covers conventional product coding; AI Act covers AI/ML-specific attacks. Conditional Y scope overlap on AI-enabled CRA products. No OJ-level consolidation rule for coding practices. AI Act defence categories do not substitute for CRA outcome-level obligations.

nodes.label: CRA↔DORA Pair — SAME COMPLEMENTARY (Scope-Disjoint)
nodes.rationale: CRA covers product-level coding outcomes; DORA covers entity-level process. Substantively scope-disjoint in baseline. Complementary label is more taxonomy artifact than substantive relationship. Different actors (manufacturer vs financial entity), different objects (product vs process).

nodes.label: DORA↔AI_Act Pair — SAME COMPLEMENTARY (Scope-Disjoint)
nodes.rationale: DORA addresses process change-management; AI Act addresses AI/ML coding. Substantively scope-disjoint in baseline. Different actors (financial entity vs AI system provider), different objects (process vs AI-system coding).

nodes.label: CRA Annex I Part I (2)(j) — Attack-Surface Limitation
nodes.rationale: Product-level outcome mandate: limit attack surfaces including external interfaces. OJ-undefined term; open-list marker. Manufacturer-side duty at design/development stage.
nodes.norm_label: cra annex i part i (2)(j) — attack-surface limitation

nodes.label: CRA Annex I Part I (2)(k) — Exploitation Mitigation
nodes.rationale: Product-level outcome mandate: reduce impact of incident using appropriate exploitation-mitigation mechanisms and techniques. Complementary to (2)(j): (j) reduces what attacker can reach; (k) reduces what attacker can do once reached.
nodes.norm_label: cra annex i part i (2)(k) — exploitation mitigation

nodes.label: DORA Art. 25 — Testing Programme (12-Way Open List)
nodes.rationale: 12-way open testing-modality list including vulnerability assessments, scans, source code reviews where feasible, scenario-based tests, penetration testing. Source-code reviews serve as one modality for secure-coding-dimension inference.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 25 — testing programme (12-way open list)

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4)(e) — ICT Change-Management Six-Step
nodes.rationale: Entity-level process mandate: documented policies, procedures and controls for ICT change management. 6-step AND coordination. No OJ clause prescribes secure-coding standards.

nodes.label: Req 7.2.1 — CRA Product Coding Outcomes (Attack-Surface + Exploitation Mitigation)
nodes.rationale: Manufacturer-side product-level outcome mandates: limit attack surfaces (Annex I Part I (2)(j)) and reduce incident impact via exploitation-mitigation (Annex I Part I (2)(k)). No OJ-mandated coding standards; baseline from industry frameworks.
nodes.norm_label: req 7.2.1 — cra product coding outcomes (attack-surface + exploitation mitigation)

nodes.label: Req 7.2.2 — DORA Change-Management Six-Step (Partial, No OJ Coding Mandate)
nodes.rationale: Entity-side ICT change-management six-step with implicit coding-dimension inference through tested/assessed legs + Art. 25 testing modalities. No OJ-mandated secure-coding-standards prescription; P0 disagreement on AEGIS taxonomy sole-authority assignment.
nodes.norm_label: req 7.2.2 — dora change-management six-step (partial, no oj coding mandate)

nodes.label: Req 7.2.3 — AI Act High-Risk AI System Attack-Defence (6 Categories)
nodes.rationale: AI/ML-specific attack-defence across 6 categories (data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples, model evasion, confidentiality attacks, model flaws). Does NOT map to conventional secure-coding mandates; baseline from AI/ML-specific frameworks.
nodes.norm_label: req 7.2.3 — ai act high-risk ai system attack-defence (6 categories)

nodes.label: SO-CRA-046 — CRA Secure Coding Objective
nodes.rationale: Attack-surface limitation (Annex I Part I (2)(j)) + exploitation mitigation (Annex I Part I (2)(k)) at the outcome level. Product-level outcome mandates, not coding-standard mandates.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-067 — Attack Surfaces Including External Interfaces
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part I (2)(j) outcome-level mandate: limit attack surfaces including external interfaces. OJ-undefined term; industry frameworks supply operational definitions. POLY+SCOPE-Q ambiguity.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-067 — attack surfaces including external interfaces

nodes.label: SR-CRA-068 — Exploitation Mitigation Mechanisms and Techniques
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part I (2)(k) outcome-level mandate: reduce incident impact via exploitation-mitigation mechanisms and techniques. OJ-undefined; industry operationalisations include ASLR, DEP/NX, CFI, sandboxing. POLY+COORD ambiguity.
nodes.norm_label: sr-cra-068 — exploitation mitigation mechanisms and techniques

nodes.label: D-08.1 General Security Awareness
nodes.author: SubDomains merge (Executor sub-agent)
nodes.rationale: Unified sub-domain covering general security awareness across GDPR, NIS2, CRA, DORA. AI Act is fully absent. 4 of 5 regulations participate with distinct target audiences and triggers.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 26(1): TLPT triennial cycle
nodes.rationale: Carry out at least every 3 years advanced testing by means of TLPT. Competent authority may adjust frequency based on risk profile.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4)(f): Patch and update policies
nodes.rationale: Appropriate and comprehensive documented policies for patches and updates. Addresses governance instrument rather than operational cadence.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 9(4)(f): patch and update policies

nodes.label: Emergent Tension: Five Regulations, Five Different Audiences
nodes.rationale: The five regulations impose role-specific competence on five different audiences: GDPR DPO-driven processing staff; NIS2 employees (encouraged); CRA integrators (B2B); DORA staff with 'commensurate to the remit'; AI Act high-risk AI human overseers. Audiences overlap in practice but regulation-specific content does not substitute. CRA's role-specific dimension is uniquely integrator-facing, not workforce-facing.
nodes.norm_label: emergent tension: five regulations, five different audiences

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RR-02: Roles, Responsibilities, Authorities, Accountabilities
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF 2.0 subcategory: Roles, responsibilities, authorities, and accountabilities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, understood, and enforced. Additional anchor for AI Act 5-element oversight and DORA commensurate-to-remit mapping.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.rr-02: roles, responsibilities, authorities, accountabilities

nodes.label: CRA ↔ AI Act Pairwise: Scope-Disjoint
nodes.rationale: CRA is product-integrator-facing (B2B information); AI Act is human-overseer-facing (5-element competence for high-risk AI). For products with AI components, CRA covers product-compliance stream and AI Act adds AI-oversight competence stream.

nodes.label: CRA ↔ DORA Pairwise: Scope-Disjoint
nodes.rationale: CRA targets product-integrator information delivery (B2B); DORA targets financial-entity staff training proportional to function. For DORA entities deploying CRA products, both apply — CRA covers product-integrator stream, DORA covers workforce stream.

nodes.label: CRA ↔ GDPR Pairwise: Scope-Disjoint
nodes.rationale: CRA addresses product-integrator information (B2B); GDPR addresses workforce role-specific training (DPO-driven). Different audiences, different content — no overlap; both apply for CRA-regulated products processing personal data.

nodes.label: CRA ↔ NIS2 Pairwise: Scope-Disjoint
nodes.rationale: CRA addresses product-integrator-facing information (B2B for product compliance); NIS2 addresses workforce employee training for risk-identification. Different audiences, different content. AEGIS taxonomy §4.1 marks NIS2/DORA as authorities for full role-specific workforce competence.

nodes.label: DORA ↔ AI Act Pairwise: Complementary
nodes.rationale: DORA's 'commensurate to the remit' covers all staff functions including AI-related ones; AI Act adds the explicit 5-element + competence-training-authority-support set for high-risk AI. For DORA financial entities deploying high-risk AI, both apply and stack.

nodes.label: DORA ↔ GDPR Pairwise: Complementary
nodes.rationale: DORA training is staff-function-wide and proportionate; GDPR role-specific training is DPO-driven for processing staff. For DORA entities processing personal data, both apply — DORA sets programme baseline and GDPR adds processing-staff role-specific layer.

nodes.label: GDPR ↔ AI Act Pairwise: Different-Perspective
nodes.rationale: GDPR role-specific targets processing staff with data-subject-facing responsibilities; AI Act targets human overseers of high-risk AI systems with the 5-element competence set. Different role, different content. Can co-exist for a deployer processing personal data via high-risk AI.

nodes.label: GDPR ↔ NIS2 Pairwise: Complementary
nodes.rationale: GDPR role-specific is DPO-catalysed and tied to processing role; NIS2 employee training is encouraged and tied to risk-identification capability. Different content (data-protection vs. risk-identification) and different governance hooks (DPO vs. encouraged).

nodes.label: NIS2 ↔ AI Act Pairwise: Complementary
nodes.rationale: NIS2 employee training covers general risk-identification; AI Act adds the AI-specific 5-element competence for high-risk AI systems. For NSIEs deploying high-risk AI, both apply — NIS2 covers baseline, AI Act adds AI-specific competency.

nodes.label: NIS2 ↔ DORA Pairwise: Equal
nodes.rationale: Both regulations impose role-specific training obligations. DORA's OJ-literal 'commensurate to the remit' is the operative anchor; NIS2's 'similar training on a regular basis' is the parallel anchor. For DORA financial entities, the DORA programme is the dominant authority.

nodes.label: SO-AIACT-011: Deployer Oversight Assignment
nodes.rationale: Security objective requiring deployers to assign human oversight to natural persons with necessary competence, training, authority, and support. Deployer-side mirror of provider-side Art. 14 obligations.

nodes.label: SR-AIACT-020: Competent Human Overseers Assigned with Training and Authority
nodes.rationale: Deployer obligation under AI Act Art. 26(2) to assign human oversight to natural persons with necessary competence, training, authority, and support. Personnel-qualification anchor of deployer AI-governance. Maps to PR.AT-02, GV.RR-02, GV.RR-04.
nodes.norm_label: sr-aiact-020: competent human overseers assigned with training and authority

nodes.label: SR-CRA-108: Integrator-Facing Information Delivery
nodes.rationale: CRA Annex II §8(f) obligation for product integrator-facing information delivery for compliance with Annex I + Annex VII. B2B audience, not workforce. AEGIS taxonomy §4.1 marks NIS2/DORA as authorities for full role-specific workforce competence.

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-030: Member-State-Encouraged Employee Training
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 20(2) sentence 2 obligation for Member States to encourage essential and important entities to offer similar training to employees on a regular basis for risk identification and assessment. Encouraged-not-mandatory at OJ level; binding force on Member State rather than directly on entity.

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RR-04: Cybersecurity in HR Practices
nodes.rationale: Screening, onboarding, training, awareness, offboarding. Operationalises the 'necessary support' element of AI Act Art. 26(2) across the employment lifecycle.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.rr-04: cybersecurity in hr practices

nodes.label: Recurring Employee Cybersecurity Training on Risk Identification
nodes.rationale: Art. 20(2) sentence 2: Member States encourage entities to offer similar training on regular basis. Mapped to PR.AT-01 and PR.AT-02.
nodes.norm_label: recurring employee cybersecurity training on risk identification

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 13 — Security Objectives & Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split document containing SO-AIACT-007 and SRs SR-AIACT-010 (transparency), SR-AIACT-011 (instructions for use), SR-AIACT-012 (oversight design). Cross-references D-08.2 and D-09.1 sub-domains.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 13 — security objectives & rules

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 14 — Security Objectives & Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split document containing SO-AIACT-008 and SRs SR-AIACT-012, SR-AIACT-013, SR-AIACT-020, SR-AIACT-022 covering human oversight design, 5-element abilities, deployer assignment, and incident reporting.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 14 — security objectives & rules

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 26 — Security Objectives & Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split document containing SO-AIACT-011 and SRs SR-AIACT-019, SR-AIACT-020 covering deployer measures aligned with provider instructions and competent human overseer assignment.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 26 — security objectives & rules

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 27 — Security Objectives & Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split document containing SR-AIACT-019 and SR-AIACT-020, cross-referencing D-08.2 and D-09.1 sub-domains. No standalone SO row.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 27 — security objectives & rules

nodes.label: DORA Art. 13 — Security Objectives & Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split document containing SO-DORA-015 and multiple SRs including SR-DORA-025 (training), SR-DORA-004 (risk identification), SR-DORA-007 (patch governance), SR-DORA-013 (BC policy), SR-DORA-015 (backup), SR-DORA-023 (change management), SR-DORA-029 (asset inventory).

nodes.label: DORA Art. 21 — Security Objectives & Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split document containing SO-DORA-001 and SRs covering CIA+A protection, cryptographic keys, risk identification, risk-scenario refresh, network management, patch governance, resilience testing, and access governance. Cross-references D-08.2 among many sub-domains.

nodes.label: D-08.2 Role-Specific Competence Cross-Regulation Analysis
nodes.rationale: Central cross-regulation deep analysis document covering role-specific competence obligations across GDPR, NIS2, CRA, DORA, and AI Act. Contains pairwise matrix, emergent tensions, SR cross-validation, and per-pair deep analysis.

nodes.label: Requirement 8.2: Role-Specific Competence Architecture
nodes.rationale: High-level Volere requirement (immunity, MUST, TEST). 5-layer architecture with five distinct audience routes. PR.AT-02 is cross-cutting anchor for all five routes.

nodes.label: Requirement 8.2.1: GDPR Role-Specific Training for Processing Staff
nodes.rationale: Quarterly or event-triggered cadence for personnel with data-subject-facing, access-management, breach-response or DPO-deputy responsibilities. Splits from 8.1 general awareness into role-specific layer.
nodes.norm_label: requirement 8.2.1: gdpr role-specific training for processing staff

nodes.label: Requirement 8.2.2: NIS2 Employee Risk-Identification Training
nodes.rationale: Member-State-encouraged, entity-side on adoption. Temporal anchor 'on a regular basis' entity-discretionary under Recital 56. Anchored in NIST NICE Workforce Framework.

nodes.label: Requirement 8.2.4: DORA Commensurate-to-the-Remit Training
nodes.rationale: Compulsory modules with function-specific depth. Completion-mandatory (not mere attendance). Staff in security-critical roles receive calibrated depth rather than uniform baseline.

nodes.label: Requirement 8.2.5: AI Act Human-Overseer Competence Set
nodes.rationale: 5-element closed-list AND (all five must be enabled cumulatively) + 4-element AND (competence, training, authority, support). Provider-design + deployer-assignment twin-trigger.
nodes.norm_label: requirement 8.2.5: ai act human-overseer competence set

nodes.label: D-08.2 Sub-SO: AI Act Human-Overseer 5-Element + 4-Element AND
nodes.rationale: Art. 14(4) 5-element closed-list AND (provider design) + Art. 26(2) 4-element AND competence/training/authority/support (deployer assignment). Provider-design-by-design + deployer-assignment-on-deployment twin-trigger.
nodes.norm_label: d-08.2 sub-so: ai act human-overseer 5-element + 4-element and

nodes.label: D-08.2 Sub-SO: CRA Integrator-Facing Information (Partial)
nodes.rationale: Annex II §8(f): integrator-facing B2B information, not workforce. Partial coverage per AEGIS taxonomy §4.1. Asymmetry: workforce training (NIS2/DORA/GDPR) vs product-integrator training (CRA) is unique to D-08.2.

nodes.label: D-08.2 Sub-SO: DORA Function-Specific Commensurate Training
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(6): compulsory modules with level of complexity commensurate to the remit of their functions. T4-vs-text gap: T4 reads 'role-specific training' but OJ uses only 'commensurate to the remit'.
nodes.norm_label: d-08.2 sub-so: dora function-specific commensurate training

nodes.label: D-08.2 Sub-SO: GDPR DPO-Catalysed Role-Specific Training
nodes.rationale: Art. 39(1)(b) DPO monitors assignment of responsibilities, awareness-raising and training of staff involved in processing. Role-specific layer distinct from general awareness at D-08.1.
nodes.norm_label: d-08.2 sub-so: gdpr dpo-catalysed role-specific training

nodes.label: D-08.2 High-Level SecurityObjective: Role-Specific Competence
nodes.rationale: Engages when ≥2 applicable regs have ≥1 pair with Y scope overlap on same party. 5 of 5 regulations participate. 0 emergent tensions. 5-layer role-specific-competence architecture with explicit audience-routing.

nodes.label: D-08.2 Sub-SO: NIS2 Member-State-Encouraged Employee Training
nodes.rationale: Art. 20(2) sentence 2: binding force on Member State rather than directly on entity. Entity-side SR applies to entities that adopt the encouragement. Purpose: identify risks and assess cybersecurity risk-management practices.
nodes.norm_label: d-08.2 sub-so: nis2 member-state-encouraged employee training

nodes.label: DORA Art. 10(1): Anomalous activity detection and SPOF identification
nodes.rationale: Mechanisms to promptly detect anomalous activities including ICT network performance issues and ICT-related incidents, and identify potential material single points of failure.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 10(1): anomalous activity detection and spof identification

nodes.label: DORA Art. 10(2): Multi-layer detection with alert thresholds
nodes.rationale: Detection mechanisms enabling multiple layers of control, defining alert thresholds and criteria to trigger and initiate ICT-related incident response processes.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 10(2): multi-layer detection with alert thresholds

nodes.label: GDPR Article 39 — Tasks of the Data Protection Officer
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 39 — tasks of the data protection officer

nodes.label: SR-GDPR-063: Independent and Adequately Resourced DPO
nodes.rationale: Operationalises Art. 38(1)–(6) via NIST GV.RR-01/GV.RR-03; embeds DPO independence and resourcing in leadership accountability backed by adequate resource allocation.
nodes.norm_label: sr-gdpr-063: independent and adequately resourced dpo

nodes.label: GDPR Article 38 — Processing under the Supervision of the DPO
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 38 — processing under the supervision of the dpo

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RR-03: Adequate resources allocated commensurate with risk
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.rr-03: adequate resources allocated commensurate with risk

nodes.label: DORA Regulation Article 13(6)
nodes.rationale: Workforce-scale training: ICT security awareness programmes and digital operational resilience training as compulsory modules in staff training schemes. Level of complexity commensurate to the remit of their functions.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 5(2): Management Body ICT Risk Responsibility
nodes.rationale: Top-of-pyramid governance rule establishing personal liability for management body over all ICT risk management framework arrangements.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 5(2): management body ict risk responsibility

nodes.label: DORA Art. 5(4): Management Body ICT-Risk Literacy
nodes.rationale: Literacy underpinning of Art. 5(2) responsibility. Defines personal-capacity threshold for management body to operate meaningfully.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 5(4): management body ict-risk literacy

nodes.label: NIS2 Article 20: Management body obligations
nodes.rationale: Art. 20(1) and 20(2) establish the three-verb management-body governance architecture (approve, oversee, can be held liable) and the training obligations. The article is the governance centrepiece of NIS2.

nodes.label: D-08.3 Management Board Training (Sub-domain)
nodes.rationale: Governance-track counterpart to D-08.1 (general security awareness) and D-08.2 (role-specific competence). 2 of 5 regulations participate (NIS2, DORA); GDPR, CRA, AI Act fully absent. 1 verified pair: NIS2↔DORA = SAME-EQUAL.

nodes.label: D-09.1 Information Security Policies (Sub-domain)
nodes.rationale: Where the management-body approve+oversee+liable architecture is operationalised. NIS2 Art. 20(1) + DORA Art. 5(2) + Art. 6(1) framework. D-08.3 management-body literacy is the personal-capacity prerequisite.

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-031: Management body cybersecurity literacy prerequisite for governance duties
nodes.rationale: Art. 20(2) sentence 1 is the literacy prerequisite for Art. 20(1) management-body obligations. Without trained members, the management body cannot meaningfully discharge approve-and-oversee obligations or be held accountable.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-031: management body cybersecurity literacy prerequisite for governance duties

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-032: Management body formally approves Article 21 risk-management measures
nodes.rationale: Art. 20(1) sentence 1 first clause: 'approve' is the upstream governance gate. Without documented management-body approval, measures lack executive sponsorship, resource allocation, and enforcement standing.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-032: management body formally approves article 21 risk-management measures

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-033: Management body continuously oversees Article 21 implementation
nodes.rationale: Art. 20(1) sentence 1 second clause: 'oversees' is the active-monitoring dimension. Oversight converts one-time approval into recurring governance activity that catches control erosion and residual-risk drift.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-033: management body continuously oversees article 21 implementation

nodes.label: SR-NIS2-034: Management body personal liability for Article 21 infringements
nodes.rationale: Art. 20(1) sentence 1 third clause: 'can be held liable' is the accountability instrument anchoring approve and oversee. Without liability exposure, upstream obligations lack enforcement teeth.
nodes.norm_label: sr-nis2-034: management body personal liability for article 21 infringements

nodes.label: Requirement 8.3: Management-body training programme (high-level)
nodes.rationale: Volere immunity requirement. Product shall establish and maintain a documented management-body training programme delivering executive-literacy substrate, governance competence, and documented training records. Priority MUST, verification TEST.

nodes.label: Requirement 8.3.1: NIS2 management-body cybersecurity training
nodes.rationale: Literacy prerequisite for Art. 20(1) approve+oversee+liable governance duties. Without trained members, the management body cannot meaningfully discharge the approve-and-oversee obligations or be held accountable for infringements.

nodes.label: Requirement 8.3.2: DORA management-body ICT-risk literacy training
nodes.rationale: Literacy underpinning of Art. 5(2) management-body responsibility. Defines the personal-capacity threshold for Art. 5(2) to operate meaningfully. Co-exists with EBA Guidelines on Internal Governance and fit-and-proper frameworks.
nodes.norm_label: requirement 8.3.2: dora management-body ict-risk literacy training

nodes.label: SO-NIS2-020: NIS2 Management Body Training Security Objective
nodes.rationale: Members of management bodies of essential and important entities follow cybersecurity training gaining sufficient knowledge and skills to identify risks and assess cybersecurity risk-management practices (Art. 20(2) sentence 1).
nodes.norm_label: so-nis2-020: nis2 management body training security objective

nodes.label: NIS2 Directive (EU) 2022/2555 Article 20(2) sentence 1
nodes.rationale: Member-State-imposed management-body training obligation. 'Member States shall ensure that members of the management bodies of essential and important entities are required to follow training.' Literacy prerequisite for Art. 20(1) approve+oversee+liable governance duties.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 4 (Definitions)
nodes.rationale: Art. 4(1) personal data, Art. 4(7)/(8) controller/processor, Art. 4(12) personal data breach, Art. 4(22) supervisory authority definitions.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33 - Breach Notification to Supervisory Authority
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-014, 015, 016, 017, 018; establishes 72-hour clock, four-element content requirement, and processor-to-controller notification chain.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 33 - breach notification to supervisory authority

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 34 - Breach Communication to Data Subjects
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-015, 019, 020, 021; higher threshold than Art. 33; three carve-outs (encryption, subsequent measures, disproportionate effort).
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 34 - breach communication to data subjects

nodes.label: CRA (Regulation, partial coverage)
nodes.rationale: Partial coverage in D-08.1: Annex II §8(a)–(f) user-facing instructions, not workforce awareness. Target audience: end-user. Trigger: manufacturer places product on market. Recipient: MSA. Substantively scope-disjoint from workforce programmes.

nodes.label: NIS 2 (Regulation)
nodes.rationale: Participates in D-08.1 via Art. 21(2)(g) first clause entity-wide hygiene baseline. Target audience: entity-wide workforce. Trigger: entity-wide basic-hygiene baseline. Recipient: management body + competent authority.

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AT-01 (Awareness and Training)
nodes.rationale: Convergent anchor for all 4 regulations. All users informed and trained on cybersecurity topics. Broad-coverage leg: phishing, social-engineering, password discipline, removable-media, incident-reporting reflexes.

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AT-02 (Role-Specific Training)
nodes.rationale: Role-specific depth dimension. All members of the workforce understand their roles. Mapped by GDPR (role-specific dimension) and DORA (commensurate to the remit). Discharged at D-08.2 layer.

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.PS-01 (Secure Configuration)
nodes.rationale: System-side hygiene substrate: baseline configurations, secure configuration standards, change management and patch cadence. Mapped by NIS2 only.

nodes.label: Requirement 8.1 (General Security Awareness)
nodes.rationale: Volere immunity requirement: documented training programme with population-wide coverage, audience-routing, and governance hooks. MUST priority, TEST verification. NIST CSF: PR.AT-01, PR.AT-02, PR.PS-01.

nodes.label: Requirement 8.1.1 (GDPR DPO Awareness)
nodes.rationale: DPO-catalysed data-protection awareness programme. Dependencies: 8.1.2 (combined curriculum when controller=NSIE), 8.1.4 (DORA carrier when DORA-controller).

nodes.label: Requirement 8.1.2 (NIS2 Hygiene Baseline)
nodes.rationale: Entity-wide basic cyber-hygiene with proportionate calibration. Dependencies: 8.1.1 (combined curriculum), 8.1.4 (DORA discharges NIS2 for financial entities).

nodes.label: Requirement 8.1.3 (CRA User Instructions)
nodes.rationale: Manufacturer-shipped detailed user-facing secure-use instructions with 10-year support-period accessibility. Dependency: 8.2.3 (integrator-B2B audience at role-specific layer).

nodes.label: Requirement 8.1.4 (DORA Compulsory Training)
nodes.rationale: Financial-entity compulsory-modules-led ICT security awareness. Dependencies: 8.1.1 (DORA carrier), 8.1.2 (DORA discharges NIS2), 8.2.4 (role-specific depth), 8.2.5 (AI Act sub-component).

nodes.label: Scheduled Procedures Operationalise Cybersecurity Effectiveness Measurement
