nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(f) second limb captures procedural dimension of effectiveness assessment. Procedures operationalise policies with concrete assessment cadence, evidence requirements, and responsible-function allocation.
nodes.norm_label: scheduled procedures operationalise cybersecurity effectiveness measurement

nodes.label: Physical-Environment Protection Ensures NIS Substrate Resilience
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2) chapeau second clause extends all-hazards to physical environment of NIS. Structurally a carve-out flag: in-scope for Art. 21 but out-of-scope for software-compliance track.
nodes.norm_label: physical-environment protection ensures nis substrate resilience

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4)(c): Physical/logical access limitation
nodes.rationale: Policies limiting physical or logical access to information and ICT assets to what is required for legitimate and approved functions and activities only.

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 12(2): EU vulnerability database
nodes.rationale: Referenced by CRA Art. 17(5) as the database ENISA populates with publicly known vulnerabilities; cross-regulation dependency.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 12(1): Backup and Restoration Procedures
nodes.rationale: Backup policies based on data criticality/confidentiality + restoration and recovery procedures. Recital 57: restore-time confidence (testing, not merely writing).
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 12(1): backup and restoration procedures

nodes.label: GDPR Article 5 — Principles for Processing of Personal Data
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 5 — principles for processing of personal data

nodes.label: Management Body Cybersecurity Literacy Prerequisite
nodes.rationale: Art. 20(2) sentence 1: management body members required to follow training. Literacy prerequisite for approve/oversee/liability. Mapped to PR.AT-03 and GV.RR-01.

nodes.label: Management Body Formally Approves Article 21 Risk-Management Measures
nodes.rationale: Art. 20(1) sentence 1 first clause: approve as upstream governance gate. Mapped to GV.RR-02 and GV.PO-01.
nodes.norm_label: management body formally approves article 21 risk-management measures

nodes.label: Management Body Continuously Oversees Article 21 Implementation
nodes.rationale: Art. 20(1) sentence 1 second clause: active-monitoring dimension. Mapped to GV.OV-01 and GV.RM-05.
nodes.norm_label: management body continuously oversees article 21 implementation

nodes.label: Management Body Personal Liability for Article 21 Infringements
nodes.rationale: Art. 20(1) sentence 1 third clause: accountability instrument anchoring approve and oversee. Mapped to GV.RR-01 and GV.OC-03.
nodes.norm_label: management body personal liability for article 21 infringements

nodes.label: Information-System-Security Policy Governs NIS Configuration and Operation
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(2)(a) second clause requires policies on information system security. Second of two coordinated sub-domains. AND conjunction read as requiring two distinct policies (one for risk analysis, one for IS security).
nodes.norm_label: information-system-security policy governs nis configuration and operation

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 PR.DS (Data Security Controls)
nodes.rationale: Group of NIST CSF 2.0 Protect-Data Security subcategories (PR.DS-01/02/10/11/12) covering data-at-rest, in-transit, in-use protection and risk-strategy alignment.

nodes.label: AI Act (out-of-scope for D-08.1)
nodes.rationale: Fully absent from D-08.1 per CRDA. No general-security-awareness mandate. Art. 4 (AI literacy) and SR-AIACT-012 (human-oversight training) are mapped to D-08.2 (role-specific competence).

nodes.label: D-08 Human Factors (Parent Domain)
nodes.rationale: Parent macro-domain containing 3 sub-subdomains (D-08.1, D-08.2, D-08.3). 34 article copies, 78 ambiguity sections.

nodes.label: D-08.2 Role-Specific Competence
nodes.rationale: Operational downstream artefact where D-08.1's general awareness becomes role-specific depth. AI Act Art. 4 (AI literacy) and SR-AIACT-012 (human-oversight training) are routed here, not to D-08.1.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 28 — Processor
nodes.rationale: Core processor obligations: sufficient guarantees (28(1)), sub-processor authorisation (28(2)), eight mandatory contract clauses (28(3)(a)-(h)).

nodes.label: GDPR Article 29 — Processing Under Authority
nodes.rationale: Processor and persons under authority shall not process except on instructions from controller, unless required by Union or Member State law.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28 - Processor Obligations
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-011, 012, 030, 031, 033, 034; establishes processor selection, eight mandatory contract clauses, and sub-processor authorisation.

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.AT-04: Integrator Understanding
nodes.rationale: Anchors integrator's understanding of upstream product's threat model, configuration constraints, and vulnerability-handling interface. Used for CRA Annex II §8(f) mapping.

nodes.label: D-05.3: Data Lifecycle — Erasure/Deletion
nodes.rationale: Erasure, deletion, and data return obligations. Primary sub-domain for SR-GDPR-030, 031, 037.

nodes.label: D-06.1: Supply Chain — Processor Selection
nodes.rationale: Sufficient guarantees and due diligence for processor engagement. Primary sub-domain for SR-GDPR-033.

nodes.label: Requirement 8.2.3: CRA Integrator-Facing Information Delivery
nodes.rationale: Where product intended for integration, information necessary for integrator to comply with Annex I + Annex VII. B2B integrator audience. Support period ≥5 years + 10-year Annex II accessibility.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-09: Governance and Documentation
nodes.rationale: Covers D-09.1 (framework), D-09.2 (oversight), D-09.3 (asset documentation). Top-of-stack governance artefacts.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 5 Security Rules Analysis
nodes.rationale: Aggregate document containing SR-DORA-003 through SR-DORA-031, each mapping DORA obligations to NIST CSF 2.0 controls with regulatory and security rationale.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9 Security Objectives & Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split document containing SO definitions and SR-DORA-001/002 for Art. 9, with cross-regulation references to NIS 2, CRA, GDPR, and EBA Guidelines.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 5(2): Management body ICT risk management responsibility
nodes.rationale: Top-of-pyramid governance rule: management body shall define, approve, oversee, and be responsible for all ICT risk management framework arrangements. Source clause for SR-DORA-026.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 5(2): management body ict risk management responsibility

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 20(1): Management body approve, oversee, liability
nodes.rationale: Three-verb coordination: approve Art. 21 measures, oversee implementation, can be held liable for infringements. Source clause for SR-NIS2-032/033/034.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 20(1): management body approve, oversee, liability

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 20(2): Management body and employee training
nodes.rationale: Sentence 1: management body training mandatory. Sentence 2: employee training encouraged. Source clauses for SR-NIS2-030/031.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 20(2): management body and employee training

nodes.label: SO-NIS2-019: Employee cybersecurity training on regular basis
nodes.rationale: NIS2 Art. 20(2) sentence 2 — employees offered similar training to identify risks and assess cybersecurity practices.
nodes.norm_label: so-nis2-019: employee cybersecurity training on regular basis

nodes.label: DORA Art. 5 — Security Rules (D-08.3)
nodes.rationale: Aggregate per-article split document containing SRs mapped to DORA Articles 5, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 17, and 26, all under SO-DORA-001.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 91 — Security Rules (D-08.3)
nodes.rationale: Per-article split for DORA Art. 91 (fit-and-proper cross-reference), containing SR-DORA-024 management-body training rule.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 20 — Security Rules (D-08.3)
nodes.rationale: Per-article split for NIS2 Art. 20 containing management-body governance SRs (approve, oversee, liability, training) as cross-regulation counterparts to DORA Art. 5.

nodes.label: DORA Article 12 (Backup and Recovery)
nodes.rationale: Operationalises Art. 11 BC policy with specific backup and recovery obligations. Recital 57's testing-not-merely-writing principle is the key interpretive anchor.

nodes.label: DORA Article 9 (ICT Security Policies and Controls)
nodes.rationale: The most heavily cited DORA article across these SRs. Art. 9(2) provides the CIA+A cross-state protection mandate; Art. 9(4) provides eight mandatory control domains (a-h) that generate SR-DORA-003, 006, 007, 010, 023.
nodes.norm_label: dora article 9 (ict security policies and controls)

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4)(d): Strong Auth + Key Protection + Encryption
nodes.rationale: Three-control AND: strong authentication mechanisms + protection measures of cryptographic keys + data encryption based on approved data classification and ICT risk assessment.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 9(4)(d): strong auth + key protection + encryption

nodes.label: GDPR Article 12 (Transparent information and communication)
nodes.rationale: Art. 12(6) identity verification provision; referenced by SR-009, 010.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 35 (DPIA)
nodes.rationale: Art. 35(11) DPIA review on material change; referenced by SR-008.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 5 (Principles)
nodes.rationale: Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation and Art. 5(2) accountability referenced across multiple SRs as underlying principles.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 25 - Privacy by Design and Default
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-013; Art. 25(2) requires four dimensions (amount, extent, period, accessibility) to be minimised by default; AND-coordinated per EDPB Guidelines 04/2019.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 25 - privacy by design and default

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32 - Security of Processing
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-007, 008, 011, 012, 014, 015, 016, 019, 024; establishes four security measures (confidentiality, integrity, availability, resilience) plus testing obligation.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 35 - Data Protection Impact Assessment
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-008, 023; DPIA is a living artefact; Art. 35(11) requires review on material change; Art. 35(7) defines content requirements.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 35 - data protection impact assessment

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 6 - Lawfulness of Processing
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-026, 027; six lawfulness bases; bases (b)-(d) carry 'necessary' qualifiers; (f) requires legitimate-interest balancing test per Recital 47.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 9 - Special Categories of Personal Data
nodes.rationale: Referenced by SR-028; nine prohibited categories each independently trigger Art. 9(1); ten Art. 9(2) exceptions; 'explicit consent' adds formal-act requirement above Art. 4(11) baseline.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 9 - special categories of personal data

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 DE.CM (Continuous Monitoring Controls)
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF 2.0 Detect-Continuous Monitoring subcategories (DE.CM-01/09) covering network and compute-layer monitoring for adverse events.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 GV (Govern Controls)
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF 2.0 Govern subcategories (GV.PO-01, GV.OC-01/03, GV.RM-02/04, GV.RR-01/02, GV.SC-02, GV.OV-02) covering policy, organizational context, risk management, roles, supply chain, and oversight.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 ID.AM (Asset Management Controls)
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF 2.0 Identify-Asset Management subcategories (ID.AM-01/02/03/04/05) covering hardware, software, data, supplier inventories and prioritisation.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 ID.RA/IM (Risk Assessment and Improvement Controls)
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF 2.0 Identify subcategories (ID.RA-01/05, ID.IM-04) covering vulnerability identification, threat/likelihood/impact analysis, and risk management improvement.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 id.ra/im (risk assessment and improvement controls)

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 RC.RP (Recovery Planning Controls)
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF 2.0 Recover-Recovery Planning subcategories (RC.RP-01/03/04) covering recovery execution, backup integrity verification, and critical function restoration.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 RS (Respond Controls)
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF 2.0 Respond subcategories (RS.MA-01, RS.AN-03) covering incident management execution and root-cause analysis.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 PR.AT (Awareness and Training Controls)
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF 2.0 Protect-Awareness and Training subcategories (PR.AT-01/02/03) covering user training, workforce role understanding, and senior executive literacy.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 pr.at (awareness and training controls)

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 PR.PS (Platform Security Controls)
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF 2.0 Protect-Platform Security subcategories (PR.PS-01/02/04/06) covering configuration management, software maintenance, logging, and secure SDLC.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 PR.AA (Authentication Controls)
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF 2.0 Protect-Authentication subcategories (PR.AA-03/04) covering user/service/hardware authentication and identity assertion management.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 12(1) — Backup and Recovery
nodes.rationale: Requires backup policies based on criticality/confidentiality and restoration/recovery procedures. Recital 57 emphasizes restore-time confidence.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 17(1) — ICT Incident Management Process
nodes.rationale: Requires define/establish/implement ICT incident management to detect/manage/notify. Chapter III chapeau with Art. 18 classification and Art. 19 reporting.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 17(1) — ict incident management process

nodes.label: DORA Art. 6(1)/(4) — ICT Risk Framework and Independence
nodes.rationale: Art. 6(1) requires sound/comprehensive/well-documented framework. Art. 6(4) requires control function independence per 3LoD or alternative model. OJ-corrective note on Art. 6(2) artefact order.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 6(1)/(4) — ict risk framework and independence

nodes.label: DORA Art. 7(1)/(2) — Asset Identification and Risk Scenarios
nodes.rationale: Art. 7(1) requires identify/classify/document ICT-supported functions and assets. Art. 7(2) requires at-least-yearly risk scenario review. OJ-corrective notes on possible misattribution to Art. 8.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 7(1)/(2) — asset identification and risk scenarios

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4)(a)/(e)/(f) — Protection Controls
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(4)(a) info security policy, (e) change management six-step process, (f) patch/update policies. Part of eight-item control list under Art. 6(8) chapeau.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 13(6) — Staff Training
nodes.rationale: Requires ICT security awareness and digital operational resilience training as compulsory modules. Workforce-scale counterpart to Art. 5(4) management-body training.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 5(4) — Management Body Training
nodes.rationale: Requires management body to actively keep up to date with sufficient knowledge/skills via regular training commensurate to ICT risk. Literacy underpinning of Art. 5(2).

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 21(2): Parallel obligations on NSIEs
nodes.rationale: Referenced by DORA SRs as parallel baseline-risk identification (21(2)(c)), supply-chain security (21(2)(e)), and business-continuity obligations on NSIEs outside DORA scope.
nodes.norm_label: nis 2 art. 21(2): parallel obligations on nsies

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28(3) Processor contract obligations
nodes.rationale: Eight mandatory sub-clauses (a)-(h) forming a closed AND-list; all must appear in the contract

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 45 Adequacy decisions
nodes.rationale: Art. 45(1) adequacy exemption; Art. 45(3) periodic review at least every four years

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 44 — Cross-border Transfer Principle
nodes.rationale: Umbrella principle for cross-border transfers; parent document for SR-GDPR-055.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 49 — Derogations
nodes.rationale: Seven disjunctive derogation grounds plus catch-all; contains SR-GDPR-054, 057, 059.

nodes.label: D-02.1: Vulnerability Management (Identification)
nodes.rationale: Cross-domain for vulnerability identification and risk assessment. Referenced by SO-AIACT-001, SR-AIACT-002, 014, 016, 023 and multiple CRA rules.

nodes.label: D-04.3: Incident Response (Reporting)
nodes.rationale: Cross-domain for incident reporting. Referenced by SO-AIACT-013, SR-AIACT-022, 024.

nodes.label: D-10.1: Monitoring and Audit (PMM)
nodes.rationale: Cross-domain for post-market monitoring. Referenced by SO-AIACT-012, SR-AIACT-021.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-07.3: Secure Development (GPAI)
nodes.rationale: Sub-domain for adversarial testing and model evaluation of GPAI systems. Distinct from D-07.1 in scope (foundation models vs. high-risk systems).

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 26: Deployer Obligations
nodes.rationale: Requires deployers to take appropriate technical and organisational measures to use high-risk AI systems per provider instructions.

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 17: Quality Management System
nodes.rationale: Requires providers of high-risk AI systems to implement a QMS with 13 enumerated aspects. Umbrella obligation for Title III compliance.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 17: quality management system

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 9 — Risk Management System
nodes.rationale: Per-article split for Art. 9 (risk management). The central AI Act ambiguity is the 'risk management system' phrase. Covers SR-AIACT-001 through SR-AIACT-024 spanning risk management, testing, accuracy/robustness/cybersecurity, QMS, SDLC, PMM, incident reporting, and GPAI obligations.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 9 — risk management system

nodes.label: Berry Linguistic Analysis Framework
nodes.rationale: Recurring analytical framework across all DORA clause cards: VAG (vagueness), POLY (polysemy), COORD (coordination) severity levels S2/S3; AND/OR disambiguation; temporal operators; Berry anchors

nodes.label: AI Act SR-AIACT-001: Continuous Risk-Management Governance
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(1) four-way verb coordination; mirrors GDPR Art. 32 and DORA Art. 6; framework-agnostic (ISO 31000, NIST AI RMF, or bespoke); NIST CSF GV.RM-01 + GV.RM-06
nodes.norm_label: ai act sr-aiact-001: continuous risk-management governance

nodes.label: AI Act SR-AIACT-002: Four-Step Risk Identification and Treatment Cycle
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(2)(a)-(d) closed cumulative set; reasonably foreseeable misuse extension; NIST CSF ID.RA-03, ID.RA-04, ID.RA-06
nodes.norm_label: ai act sr-aiact-002: four-step risk identification and treatment cycle

nodes.label: AI Act SR-AIACT-003: Risk-Measure Validation Through Targeted Testing
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(6)-(7) testing for consistency; real-world conditions per Art. 60; NIST CSF ID.RA-01, ID.RA-04, PR.PS-06, GV.SC-04
nodes.norm_label: ai act sr-aiact-003: risk-measure validation through targeted testing

nodes.label: AI Act SR-AIACT-014: Accuracy, Robustness, Cybersecurity Baseline
nodes.rationale: Art. 15(1) three-property duty; 3-way AND no partial compliance; NIST CSF PR.PS-06, PR.IR-03, ID.RA-04; cross-regulation with CRA C07 and NIS 2 C01
nodes.norm_label: ai act sr-aiact-014: accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity baseline

nodes.label: AI Act SR-AIACT-015: Resilience Against Errors, Faults, Environmental Drift
nodes.rationale: Art. 15(3) as resilient as possible; backup or fail-safe plans; NIST CSF PR.IR-03, PR.IR-04, PR.DS-11
nodes.norm_label: ai act sr-aiact-015: resilience against errors, faults, environmental drift

nodes.label: AI Act SR-AIACT-016: AI-Specific Attack Vector Mitigation
nodes.rationale: Art. 15(4)-(5) data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples, confidentiality attacks, model flaws; 5-phase AND + 6-type OR; NIST CSF ID.RA-04, PR.PS-06, RS.MI-01, RS.MA-03
nodes.norm_label: ai act sr-aiact-016: ai-specific attack vector mitigation

nodes.label: AI Act SR-AIACT-017: Documented Quality Management System
nodes.rationale: Art. 17(1) QMS with 13-element closed list; cross-ref to Art. 9 risk management; NIST CSF GV.PO-01, GV.RM-01, GV.RM-04
nodes.norm_label: ai act sr-aiact-017: documented quality management system

nodes.label: AI Act SR-AIACT-021: Post-Market Monitoring Feedback Loop
nodes.rationale: Art. 72(1)-(2) PMM system; Art. 74(1) extends Reg 2019/1020; NIST CSF DE.CM-09, ID.IM-04, GV.OV-03
nodes.norm_label: ai act sr-aiact-021: post-market monitoring feedback loop

nodes.label: AI Act SR-AIACT-022: Tiered Serious Incident Reporting
nodes.rationale: Art. 73(1)-(4) 15/10/2-day timelines; cross-regulation with NIS 2 C30 and DORA Art. 19; NIST CSF RS.CO-02, RS.CO-04, RS.MA-03, RS.MA-01
nodes.norm_label: ai act sr-aiact-022: tiered serious incident reporting

nodes.label: AI Act SR-AIACT-023: Adversarial Evaluation of GPAI Models
nodes.rationale: Art. 55(1)(a) standardised protocols + state of the art + systemic risks; second-most-consequential AI Act ambiguity; NIST CSF GV.RM-06, ID.RA-04, PR.PS-06
nodes.norm_label: ai act sr-aiact-023: adversarial evaluation of gpai models

nodes.label: AI Act SR-AIACT-024: GPAI Serious Incident Reporting to AI Office
nodes.rationale: Art. 55(1)(c) without undue delay to AI Office; distinct from Art. 73 high-risk reporting; cross-regulation with DORA Art. 19 and NIS 2 C30
nodes.norm_label: ai act sr-aiact-024: gpai serious incident reporting to ai office

nodes.label: CRA SR-CRA-001: State-of-the-Art Cryptographic Confidentiality Baseline
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part I (1)+(2)(e); state-of-the-art VAG-S3; NIST CSF PR.DS-01, PR.DS-02; cross-regulation with GDPR Art. 32
nodes.norm_label: cra sr-cra-001: state-of-the-art cryptographic confidentiality baseline

nodes.label: CRA SR-CRA-006: Pre-Market Elimination of Known Exploitable Vulnerabilities
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part I (2)(a); known exploitable VAG+POLY S3; constructive-knowledge baseline; NIST CSF ID.RA-01, PR.PS-02
nodes.norm_label: cra sr-cra-006: pre-market elimination of known exploitable vulnerabilities

nodes.label: CRA SR-CRA-007: Vulnerability and Component Identification with SBOM
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part II (1) + Art. 13(7); top-level dependencies POLY-S2; NIST CSF ID.RA-01, ID.AM-02
nodes.norm_label: cra sr-cra-007: vulnerability and component identification with sbom

nodes.label: CRA SR-CRA-010: Vulnerability Remediation Without Delay
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part II (2) + Art. 13(6); without delay VAG-S3 (Berry classic); NIST CSF PR.PS-02, ID.RA-06
nodes.norm_label: cra sr-cra-010: vulnerability remediation without delay

nodes.label: CRA SR-CRA-012: Effective Vulnerability Handling Across Support Period
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(8) sentence 1; handled effectively VAG-S3; including its components SCOPE-Q-S2; NIST CSF ID.RA-06, PR.PS-02
nodes.norm_label: cra sr-cra-012: effective vulnerability handling across support period

nodes.label: CRA SR-CRA-013: Support-Period Determination (8-Factor Methodology)
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(8) sentence 2-3; 5-year minimum; reasonable user expectations VAG-S3; NIST CSF ID.IM-02, GV.OV-02

nodes.label: DORA CL11-1: ICT Business Continuity Policy (Art. 11(1)+(2))
nodes.rationale: Multi-instance card covering chapeau + 5 enumerated BCP objectives; Art. 4 proportionality applies; cross-refs Art. 6(1), 8, 12, 14, 19
nodes.norm_label: dora cl11-1: ict business continuity policy (art. 11(1)+(2))

nodes.label: DORA CL11-2: Recovery Plans + BCP for Outsourced CIFs + BIA (Art. 11(3)-(5))
nodes.rationale: Covers response/recovery plans, outsourcing BCP, and business impact analysis; microenterprise carve-out for audit reviews
nodes.norm_label: dora cl11-2: recovery plans + bcp for outsourced cifs + bia (art. 11(3)-(5))

nodes.label: DORA CL11-3: BCP Testing + Crisis Management + Records (Art. 11(6)-(9))
nodes.rationale: Testing cadence (at least yearly), crisis management function, records, CSD reporting; non-microenterprise additional scenarios
nodes.norm_label: dora cl11-3: bcp testing + crisis management + records (art. 11(6)-(9))

nodes.label: DORA CL12-1: Backup Policies (Art. 12(1)+(2))
nodes.rationale: Backup scope/frequency, restoration procedures, non-jeopardise condition for backup activation

nodes.label: DORA CL12-2: Restoration + Redundant ICT Capacities (Art. 12(3)+(4))
nodes.rationale: Physical/logical segregation, timely restoration, redundant ICT capacities; CCP and DRSP sectoral carve-outs
nodes.norm_label: dora cl12-2: restoration + redundant ict capacities (art. 12(3)+(4))

nodes.label: DORA CL12-4: RTO/RPO + Data Integrity Checks (Art. 12(6)+(7))
nodes.rationale: Recovery time and point objectives per function; highest level of data integrity with multiple checks and reconciliations
nodes.norm_label: dora cl12-4: rto/rpo + data integrity checks (art. 12(6)+(7))

nodes.label: DORA CL13-1: Threat Intelligence + Post-Incident Reviews (Art. 13(1)-(3))
nodes.rationale: Learn-and-evolve cycle: vulnerability/threat gathering, post-incident reviews, lessons propagation into risk assessment
nodes.norm_label: dora cl13-1: threat intelligence + post-incident reviews (art. 13(1)-(3))

nodes.label: DORA CL14-1: Crisis Communication Plans (Art. 14(1))
nodes.rationale: Responsible disclosure of major ICT-related incidents or vulnerabilities to clients, counterparts, and public

nodes.label: DORA CL15-1: ESAs RTS Mandate (Art. 15)
nodes.rationale: Seven RTS subject areas (a)-(g) mapping to Art. 9-11-6 elements; deadline 17 Jan 2024; Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1774 adopted

nodes.label: DORA CL16-1: Simplified Framework Scope (Art. 16(1))
nodes.rationale: Five exempted entity categories; Art. 5-15 do not apply; documented and reviewed framework with continuous improvement

nodes.label: DORA CL16-2: Simplified Obligations (Art. 16(1)(a)-(h) + (3))
nodes.rationale: Structurally parallel to Art. 9(4) but at lower granularity; omits access control, change management, patches as standalone families; deliberate regulatory choice

nodes.label: DORA CL21-1: Single EU Hub Feasibility Mandate (Art. 21(1)+(2))
nodes.rationale: ESAs joint report on centralisation of incident reporting; 7 enumerated elements; regulator-internal scope
nodes.norm_label: dora cl21-1: single eu hub feasibility mandate (art. 21(1)+(2))

nodes.label: DORA CL22-1: Competent Authority Supervisory Feedback (Art. 22(1))
nodes.rationale: Discretionary CA feedback (may + where feasible); mandatory acknowledge + discretionary substance; opposite of NIS 2 Art. 23(5) pattern
nodes.norm_label: dora cl22-1: competent authority supervisory feedback (art. 22(1))

nodes.label: DORA CL26-1: TLPT Cadence (Art. 26(1))
nodes.rationale: At least every 3 years; CA may reduce or increase frequency; hard numeric anchor reduces temporal ambiguity

nodes.label: DORA CL26-2: TLPT Scope (Art. 26(2))
nodes.rationale: Several or all critical/important functions on live production systems; underlying ICT systems, processes and technologies

nodes.label: Art. 22 Supervisory Feedback
nodes.rationale: CA feedback on receipt of notifications/reports; anonymised threat intelligence; ESAs yearly aggregated report with warnings and high-level statistics.

nodes.label: DORA Chapter IV: Digital Operational Resilience Testing (Art. 24–27)
nodes.rationale: Establishes the testing programme as integral part of Art. 6 ICT risk-management framework; Art. 26 mandates TLPT on 3-year cadence anchored to TIBER-EU; Art. 27 (testers) is NEW in v0.2, omitted by T3.
nodes.norm_label: dora chapter iv: digital operational resilience testing (art. 24–27)

nodes.label: DORA Art. 30(1) — Written Contract Requirements
nodes.rationale: Requires rights and obligations to be clearly allocated in one written document, available on paper or in downloadable, durable, accessible format. Propagated to CTPP contracts.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 12(6)+(7) — RTO/RPO + Data Integrity Checks
nodes.rationale: Recovery time and point objectives; multiple checks and reconciliations for data integrity; specific to financial-sector resilience.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 12(6)+(7) — rto/rpo + data integrity checks

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 9 Risk Management System
nodes.rationale: Continuous, iterative 4-step risk management across AI lifecycle. Subject to CRA Art. 13(4) s2 consolidation rule. Cross-coupled with Art. 27 FRIA for Annex III categories.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 9 risk management system

nodes.label: DORA ICT Risk Framework (Art. 6/7)
nodes.rationale: Three-lines-of-defence + continuous ICT risk identification + at-least-yearly risk-scenario review. Dominant authority for financial entities. No pre-launch DPIA-equivalent.

nodes.label: Five Distinct Risk Assessment Objects & Cadences
nodes.rationale: GDPR DPIA (data-subject rights, pre-launch), NIS2 (entity operational, continuous), CRA (product cybersecurity, pre-market), DORA (ICT operational, continuous+yearly), AI Act (AI-system, continuous iterative). All 5 stack without substitution except CRA↔AI_Act.
nodes.norm_label: five distinct risk assessment objects & cadences

nodes.label: GDPR DPIA Regime (Art. 35)
nodes.rationale: Pre-launch assessment for high-risk personal-data processing with 4 Art. 35(7) content items. Reviewed on change of risk per Art. 35(11). Distinct from all other assessment regimes in D-09.2.

nodes.label: NIS2↔DORA EQUAL Relationship (DORA-Dominant Stack)
nodes.rationale: Both impose continuous operational risk identification. DORA three-lines-of-defence is dominant for financial entities; NIS2 applies only insofar as entity is NSIE outside DORA. DORA Art. 7(2) discharges both obligations.

nodes.label: NIS2 Risk Analysis Policy (Art. 21(2)(a))
nodes.rationale: Entity-level operational continuous risk analysis. Entity-discretionary under Recital 56 proportionality. No codified content template. Cross-links to Art. 22(1) EU-level coordinated assessments.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(4) s2 — Only OJ-Level Cross-Regulation Consolidation Rule
nodes.rationale: The only OJ-level cross-regulation consolidation rule in D-09.2: AI Act Art. 9 risk-management system can substitute for CRA Art. 13(3) cybersecurity risk assessment when both apply to the same product. No other cross-regulation substitution is OJ-permitted.
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 13(4) s2 — only oj-level cross-regulation consolidation rule

nodes.label: Five Overlapping Risk/Impact Assessments
nodes.rationale: CRITICAL: Five separate assessment regimes (GDPR DPIA, NIS2 risk analysis, CRA risk assessment, DORA ICT risk framework, AI Act FRIA) that may all apply to the same entity-product combination. No OJ-level cross-referencing. Phase 1 entities must maintain five separate risk registers. D-09.2 is the most heavily-overlapped sub-domain.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 ID.RA-05 Convergent Anchor
nodes.rationale: All 5 regulations map D-09.2 to NIST CSF 2.0 Subcategory ID.RA-05 (Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, impacts used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response) as the convergent anchor. GDPR additionally maps ID.RA-04; AI Act additionally maps GV.RM-04; CRA additionally maps ID.SC-04.

nodes.label: Pre-launch vs Operational Review Asymmetry
nodes.rationale: GDPR DPIA is pre-launch (reviewed on change of risk); NIS2 is continuous; CRA is pre-market + support-period; DORA is continuous + yearly; AI Act is continuous iterative. Review cadences not synchronised. Entity must satisfy five independent review triggers without unified cadence.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-04.3: Regulatory Notification
nodes.rationale: Primary sub-domain for NIS2 Art. 23 notification obligations. Referenced as cross-domain link from D-09.1 and D-09.2.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-09.1: Information Security Policies
nodes.rationale: Policy upstream artefact where the 5 assessment regimes are calibrated against per-regulation policy architectures. Parent domain for NIS2 Art. 23/33 articles.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 23 — Security Objectives & Security Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split (SO + SR) generated from 01_SecurityObjectives.md and 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md covering incident notification obligations under NIS2 Directive (EU) 2022/2555.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 23 — security objectives & security rules

nodes.label: AI Act Risk Management System (Art. 9)
nodes.source_location: Pair: GDPR ↔ AI_Act; Pair: NIS2 ↔ AI_Act; Pair: CRA ↔ AI_Act; Pair: DORA ↔ AI_Act
nodes.rationale: Continuous, iterative risk management system across AI lifecycle with 4-step process (identify, estimate, evaluate, adopt measures). Recital 78 preserves GDPR. Triggers on high-risk AI system, not high-risk processing.

nodes.label: CRA 6-Phase Lifecycle Propagation (Art. 13(2))
nodes.rationale: Longest single coordination pattern in CRA: planning, design, development, production, delivery, maintenance. Risk assessment outcome must be taken into account during all six phases. R1 (all six required) vs R3 (take-into-account admits partial compliance) produce materially distinct compliance populations.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(4) s2 AI-Act Consolidation Rule
nodes.source_location: Pair: CRA ↔ AI_Act; Emergent tensions section
nodes.rationale: The ONLY OJ-level cross-regulation consolidation rule in D-09.2. Explicitly permits AI Act Art. 9 risk management system to substitute for CRA cybersecurity risk assessment when both apply to the same product. Does NOT extend to GDPR DPIA. No equivalent exists for DORA.
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 13(4) s2 ai-act consolidation rule

nodes.label: CRA Cybersecurity Risk Assessment (Art. 13)
nodes.source_location: CRA-CL14 through CRA-CL50; Art. 13 full text
nodes.rationale: Product-level pre-market + support-period cybersecurity risk assessment with 6-phase lifecycle propagation (planning, design, development, production, delivery, maintenance). Documented and updated during support period. Minimum 5-year support period. 36 atomic clauses for Art. 13 alone.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 11 Response and Recovery
nodes.rationale: Comprehensive ICT business continuity policy with 5 enumerated aims. Recovery plans, BCP for outsourced CIFs, BIA. Yearly BCP testing with cyber-attack scenarios. Crisis management function. Cost/loss estimation reporting to CAs.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 12 Backup and Recovery
nodes.rationale: Backup policies with minimum frequency based on criticality. Physically and logically segregated restoration systems. Redundant ICT capacities. CSD secondary processing site with distinct risk profile. RTO/RPO objectives. Multiple checks and reconciliations for data integrity.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 15 ESAs RTS Mandate
nodes.rationale: ESAs through Joint Committee, in consultation with ENISA, develop draft RTS specifying 7 areas. Deadline 17 January 2024. Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1774 adopted 31 May 2024. Every flagged instance tagged RTS-pending is materially constrained by eventual RTS content.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 8 Identification
nodes.rationale: Identify, classify, document all ICT-supported business functions, assets, dependencies. Continuous risk-source identification. Major-change risk assessment. Legacy ICT system assessment. Critical-asset mapping with links and interdependencies. ICT-TPP dependency mapping.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4) THE HINGE
nodes.rationale: Operational core of DORA's protection regime. Six mandatory control families: info-security policy, network/infrastructure, access control, authentication+encryption, change management (6-way AND), patches/updates. 15 instances within one card. T3 imposed extra-conjunctive terms (need-to-know, least privilege, MFA) not present in OJ text.

nodes.label: DORA ICT Risk Management Framework (Art. 6-16)
nodes.source_location: CL4-1 through CL16-2; Art. 4-16 full text
nodes.rationale: Financial-entity continuous ICT risk management with three-lines-of-defence governance. 26 atomic clauses across Art. 7-16. Most demanding framework chapeau in the 5-regulation corpus (sound, comprehensive, well-documented). Proportionality principle (Art. 4) propagates to every clause.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 4 Proportionality Principle
nodes.rationale: Three distinct proportionality regimes: Ch. II default, Ch. III/IV/V Sec. I by reference, CA review. Self-implementing — no RTS/ITS specifies criteria. Propagates to every Ch. II-V Sec. I clause. More elaborate than NIS2 Art. 1(2) or CRA Art. 1(2).

nodes.label: DORA Three Lines of Defence (Art. 6(4))
nodes.rationale: Control-model option: three lines of defence (business → risk management → internal audit) OR any internal risk management and control model. Specific to EU financial-services law. NIS2, CRA, AI Act have no equivalent. Dominant authority for financial entities under DORA's direct scope.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 35(7) DPIA Content Requirements
nodes.rationale: Four mandatory content items: (a) systematic description of processing, (b) necessity and proportionality assessment, (c) risks to data subjects' rights and freedoms, (d) measures to address risks. 'Necessity and proportionality' has three different senses across GDPR (5(1)(c), 6(1)(b), 35(7)(b)).

nodes.label: GDPR DPIA (Art. 35)
nodes.source_location: Pair: GDPR ↔ NIS2; Pair: GDPR ↔ CRA; Pair: GDPR ↔ DORA; Pair: GDPR ↔ AI_Act
nodes.rationale: Pre-launch impact assessment for high-risk personal data processing with 4 Art. 35(7) content items. Reviewed on change of risk (Art. 35(11)). Distinct from all other assessments in the corpus — assesses impact on data subjects' rights and freedoms, not cybersecurity or operational risk.

nodes.label: NIS2 All-Hazards Approach (Art. 21(2) chapeau)
nodes.rationale: Protects network and information systems AND the physical environment of those systems. Single most distinctive feature of NIS2 vs other four regulations. Physical-environment dimension is out-of-scope for software-compliance track but included for completeness.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 22 Coordinated Supply Chain Assessments
nodes.source_location: NIS2-CL23 through NIS2-CL25; Art. 22 full text
nodes.rationale: EU-level coordinated security risk assessments of critical ICT supply chains by Cooperation Group + Commission + ENISA. Art. 21(3) s2 requires entities to 'take into account' results. Single most important entity-facing propagation hook in NIS2 for supply-chain theme.
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 22 coordinated supply chain assessments

nodes.label: NIS2 Risk Analysis (Art. 21)
nodes.source_location: NIS2-CL07 through NIS2-CL21; NIS2-C03 through NIS2-C29
nodes.rationale: Entity-level operational risk-analysis policy with all-hazards approach including physical environment. Continuous, not pre-launch. Propagates 'appropriate and proportionate' qualifier to all 10 sub-points (a)-(j). Most distinctive feature vs other 4 regulations is physical-environment coverage.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 5(2)(a)-(d) — Responsibility + Standards + Roles + Strategy
nodes.rationale: 'Ultimate responsibility' admits personal-liability vs non-delegable vs top-of-hierarchy readings; 'availability, authenticity, integrity and confidentiality' 4-dimension coordination.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 5(2)(a)-(d) — responsibility + standards + roles + strategy

nodes.label: Five-Policy-Stack Architecture
nodes.rationale: The layered 5-policy architecture with no OJ-level consolidation rule. All 5 regulations impose distinct policy artefacts under distinct anchors at distinct governance hooks. Phase 1 entities must build a governance-architecture mapping that nests all five policies without overlap.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 23(1) — Permissible Restriction Grounds
nodes.rationale: 'Essence' is Charter Art. 52(1) terminology; CJEU case law uses it as a hard-test threshold but does not specify the operational test.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-04 — Incident Response
nodes.rationale: Covers D-04.1 (detection and response triggering).

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-10 — Monitoring & Audit
nodes.rationale: Covers D-10.1 (detection/monitoring), D-10.3 (testing/audit).

nodes.label: BCP Lifecycle (Art. 11)
nodes.rationale: The full BCP lifecycle spans: policy formulation (11(1)-(2)) → recovery plans + BIA (11(3)-(5)) → testing + crisis mgmt + records (11(6)-(9)) → cost reporting + guidelines (11(10)-(11)). Each stage has distinct proportionality carve-outs.

nodes.label: Central Securities Depositories (CSDs)
nodes.rationale: Sectoral carve-out: CSDs must provide competent authorities with copies of ICT BCP test results or similar exercises (Art. 11(9)). Cross-ref Art. 2(1)(s).

nodes.label: Detection-to-Response Chain (Art. 10)
nodes.rationale: The detection-response chain: anomaly detection (10(1)) → multi-layer controls + alert thresholds (10(2)-(3)) → DRSP-specific trade report checks (10(4)). Each layer builds on the previous, with Art. 17 and Art. 25 providing procedural and testing frameworks.

nodes.label: Data Reporting Service Providers (DRSPs)
nodes.rationale: Sectoral entity type with additional Art. 10(4) obligation to check trade reports for completeness, identify omissions/errors, and request re-transmission. Defined via MiFIR cross-ref.

nodes.label: ESA Joint Committee
nodes.rationale: Body mandated to develop common guidelines on estimation of aggregated annual costs and losses by 17 July 2024, per Art. 11(11) and Art. 16 of ESA Regulations.

nodes.label: Six Mandatory Control Families (Art. 9(4))
nodes.rationale: The six control families: (a) info-security policy, (b) network/infrastructure management, (c) access control, (d) authentication+encryption, (e) change management, (f) patches/updates. Described as the operational core of DORA's ICT risk management framework.

nodes.label: T3 Mapping (v0.1 Taxonomy)
nodes.rationale: v0.1 mapping layer with identified gaps: C14 major distortion, C16 major distortion, C26 mis-mapping, C28 major distortion; omitted 19 clauses (Arts 7-12, 14, 15, 16) and 4 Ch. III articles (20-23).

nodes.label: v0.2 Mapping (Expanded Clause Map)
nodes.rationale: Restores single hinge card pattern, adds 19 omitted clauses, expands Ch. III from 3 to 31 atomic clauses, adds Arts 20-23; all T3 gaps are mapping-layer artefacts, not OJ-text artefacts.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 12 — Response and Recovery
nodes.rationale: Referenced in CL11-1 (sub-point c: tailored response and recovery procedures) and CL11-3 (redundant capacity, backups, redundant facilities).

nodes.label: DORA Art. 15 — RTS Pending Specifications
nodes.rationale: Pending regulatory technical standards that will further specify: Art. 9(4)(c) access management (15(b)), Art. 9(2) chapeau (15(a)), Art. 10(1) detection (15(c)), Art. 10(2) criteria (15(c)), Art. 11(1) BCP components (15(d)), Art. 11(3) recovery plans (15(f)), Art. 11(6) BCP testing (15(e)).

nodes.label: DORA Art. 17 — Detection (Cross-Reference)
nodes.rationale: Art. 10(1) detection mechanisms operate 'in accordance with Article 17', establishing the procedural framework for anomaly detection.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 19 — Reporting to Competent Authorities
nodes.rationale: Referenced in CL11-1 (sub-point e: report to competent authorities) as the reporting obligation triggered by BCP activation.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 19 — reporting to competent authorities

nodes.label: DORA Art. 25 — Testing (Cross-Reference)
nodes.rationale: Art. 10(1) requires detection mechanisms to be 'regularly tested in accordance with Article 25', establishing the testing regime.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 8 — Identification Requirements
nodes.rationale: Referenced in CL11-1 as the basis for BCP (identification of critical/important functions). Also referenced in CL11-3 for 'major change' threshold (Art. 8(3)).

nodes.label: CL10-2 — Art. 10(2)+(3) Multi-Layer Controls and Alert Thresholds
nodes.rationale: Requires multiple layers of control, alert thresholds and criteria to trigger ICT-related incident response, automatic alert mechanisms, and sufficient resources for monitoring user activity and cyber-attacks.
nodes.norm_label: cl10-2 — art. 10(2)+(3) multi-layer controls and alert thresholds

nodes.label: CL10-3 — Art. 10(4) DRSP Additional Requirement
nodes.rationale: Sectoral carve-out for Data Reporting Service Providers: must effectively check trade reports for completeness, identify omissions and obvious errors, and request re-transmission. Art. 4 proportionality does not apply (uniform obligation).

nodes.label: CL11-1 — Art. 11(1)+(2) ICT Business Continuity Policy and Five Objectives
nodes.rationale: Requires a comprehensive ICT BCP with five cumulative objectives: continuity of CIFs, quick response to incidents, activation without delay, impact estimation, and communication/crisis management. Based on Art. 8 identification requirements.
nodes.norm_label: cl11-1 — art. 11(1)+(2) ict business continuity policy and five objectives

nodes.label: CL11-2 — Art. 11(3)+(4)+(5) Recovery Plans, Outsourced BCP, and BIA
nodes.rationale: Requires ICT response and recovery plans (subject to independent internal audit for non-microenterprises), BCPs for outsourced CIFs, and a business impact analysis using quantitative and qualitative criteria with full alignment of ICT assets to BIA.
nodes.norm_label: cl11-2 — art. 11(3)+(4)+(5) recovery plans, outsourced bcp, and bia

nodes.label: CL11-3 — Art. 11(6)–(9) BCP Testing, Crisis Management, Records, CSD Reporting
nodes.rationale: Requires at-least-yearly testing of BCPs and recovery plans, cyber-attack and switchover scenarios for non-microenterprises, crisis management function, readily accessible records, and CSD reporting of test results to competent authorities.
nodes.norm_label: cl11-3 — art. 11(6)–(9) bcp testing, crisis management, records, csd reporting

nodes.label: CL11-4 — Art. 11(10)+(11) Cost Reporting and ESA Guidelines
nodes.rationale: Requires non-microenterprises to report aggregated annual costs and losses from major ICT-related incidents upon CA request. ESA Joint Committee to develop common guidelines by 17 July 2024 (non-binding, comply-or-explain per Art. 16 ESA Regulations).
nodes.norm_label: cl11-4 — art. 11(10)+(11) cost reporting and esa guidelines

nodes.label: CL9-4 — Art. 9(4)(a)–(f) ICT Risk Management Framework Core Requirements
nodes.rationale: The operational core of DORA's ICT risk management framework, establishing six mandatory control families: info-security policy, network/infrastructure, access control, authentication+encryption, change management, patches/updates. T3's C15/C16/C17 imposed extra-conjunctive terms (need-to-know, least privilege, MFA) not present in the OJ text.
nodes.norm_label: cl9-4 — art. 9(4)(a)–(f) ict risk management framework core requirements

nodes.label: DORA Art. 4 — Proportionality
nodes.rationale: Every clause card in Ch. IV carries 'proportionality-status: Art. 4 applies'. Art. 4(2) criteria are referenced in Art. 24(1), (3), and (6) as the proportionality anchor for risk-based testing.

nodes.label: ESA Common Guidelines on Cost/Loss Estimation
nodes.rationale: Mandated by Art. 11(11) for development by 17 July 2024 via Joint Committee. Non-binding per Art. 16 of ESA Regulations; carry comply-or-explain obligation. Distinct from RTS.
nodes.norm_label: esa common guidelines on cost/loss estimation

nodes.label: ESA Regulations (EU) No 1093/2010, 1094/2010, 1095/2010
nodes.rationale: Art. 16 of these regulations governs the legal nature of ESA guidelines (non-binding, comply-or-explain). Referenced in Art. 11(11) as the basis for Joint Committee guideline development.

nodes.label: MiFIR Art. 2(1)(34)–(36) — DRSP Definition
nodes.rationale: Cross-reference for DORA Art. 3(63) definition of data reporting service provider, anchoring the CL10-3 sectoral obligation.

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 6(2) — D02 Analogue
nodes.rationale: Cross-referenced as S3 propagation source for the four data-security dimensions (availability, authenticity, integrity, confidentiality) in Art. 9(4)(a).

nodes.label: DORA CL13-2: Effectiveness Monitoring + Training + Tech Developments (Art. 13(4)-(7))
nodes.rationale: Cyber maturity monitoring, yearly reporting to management body, compulsory training, technology monitoring; T3-vs-text gap on role-specific training
nodes.norm_label: dora cl13-2: effectiveness monitoring + training + tech developments (art. 13(4)-(7))

nodes.label: Cross-Regulation Reference Network (DORA-AI Act-CRA-NIS2-GDPR)
nodes.rationale: DORA Art. 6 mirrors AI Act Art. 9; AI Act Art. 15(4) parallels CRA Annex I; DORA Art. 19 parallels AI Act Art. 73 and NIS 2 C30; CRA state-of-the-art parallels GDPR Art. 32 and AI Act Art. 55(1)(a)

nodes.label: DORA 4-Verb Governance Signature
nodes.rationale: Unique to DORA in the 5-regulation corpus; NIS 2 uses single-verb, CRA uses 3-verb, GDPR uses single-verb; adds non-delegable accountability anchor.

nodes.label: Berry COORD (Coordination) Category
nodes.rationale: AND/OR coordination patterns creating parse-tree ambiguity; 3-verb, 4-verb, and multi-element coordination patterns across all regulations.

nodes.label: Berry POLY (Polysemy) Category
nodes.rationale: Terms with multiple valid meanings (training, measures, effectiveness, impact, management body) creating materially distinct compliance populations.

nodes.label: Berry VAG (Vague) Category
nodes.rationale: Recurring vague terms (appropriate, reasonable, sufficient, effective, state-of-the-art) flagged across all 5 regulations; dominant ambiguity category in every chapter.

nodes.label: EDPB Guidelines (Interpretive Anchors)
nodes.rationale: EDPB Guidelines 05/2020, 3/2018, 9/2022, 2/2018, 07/2019, Recommendations 01/2020 serve as disambiguation sources but do not exhaust the ambiguity gap.

nodes.label: Cross-Regulation Proportionality Principle
nodes.source_location: DORA Art. 4, NIS2 Art. 1(2), CRA Art. 1(2), GDPR Art. 5(1)(c)
nodes.rationale: DORA Art. 4 is most elaborate (3 distinct regimes); mirrors NIS 2 Art. 1(2) and CRA Art. 1(2); DORA provides explicit CA-review that NIS 2 and CRA do not have.

nodes.label: Schrems II (C-311/18) Decision
nodes.rationale: Dominant interpretive anchor for GDPR Chapter V; invalidated Privacy Shield; 'essentially equivalent' standard shapes adequacy assessment; non-textual standard.

nodes.label: Cross-Regulation 'State of the Art' Pattern
nodes.rationale: Same Berry-classic vague term in GDPR and NIS 2; propagates from Art. 5(1)(f) 'appropriate security'; appears in 2 GDPR clauses and 1 NIS2 clause.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 24(1) — OSS Steward Cybersecurity Policy
nodes.rationale: 'Foster' admits encourage/require/enable readings; 'document in a verifiable manner' — verified by whom is undefined.
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 24(1) — oss steward cybersecurity policy

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(1) — Design/Development/Production Duty
nodes.rationale: 3-phase coordination (designed, developed, produced); the operational core of CRA — 25 paragraphs, ~35 atomic clauses.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(8) — Support-Period Factors
nodes.rationale: 'Reasonable user expectations' is case-law-laden; proportionality principle same pattern as GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), NIS 2 Art. 21(1), DORA Art. 4.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 11(1)+(2) — ICT Business Continuity Policy
nodes.rationale: Comprehensive ICT BCP with 5 enumerated aims; structurally parallel to NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(c) business continuity.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 11(1)+(2) — ict business continuity policy

nodes.label: DORA Art. 4(1) — Proportionality Chapeau (Ch. II)
nodes.rationale: Self-implementing proportionality principle; propagates to every Ch. II-V Sec. I clause; more elaborate than NIS 2 Art. 1(2) and CRA Art. 1(2).

nodes.label: DORA Art. 5(2) — Management Body 4-Verb Coordination
nodes.rationale: Longest management-body coordination pattern in DORA; 'define, approve, oversee and be responsible for' is unique to DORA in the 5-regulation corpus; adds non-delegable accountability anchor.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 6(1) — Framework Chapeau
nodes.rationale: 'Sound, comprehensive and well-documented' is the most demanding framework chapeau in the 5-regulation corpus; requires three distinct qualities (effectiveness, completeness, traceability).

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 7(4) — Conditional Consent and Contract
nodes.rationale: Anti-coupling clause requiring 'utmost account' and 'not necessary for contract performance' standard; creates recursive ambiguity with Art. 6(1)(b).
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 7(4) — conditional consent and contract

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 8(2) — Reasonable Verification Efforts
nodes.rationale: 'Reasonable efforts' is a recurring vague phrase; 'available technology' qualifier shifts the standard over time.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 9(1) — General Prohibition on Special-Category Processing
nodes.rationale: 9 categories connected by commas and 'and'; each term has poly reference but boundaries are contested.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 9(1) — general prohibition on special-category processing

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 24(1) — General Controller Responsibility
nodes.rationale: 'Appropriate technical and organisational measures' — same pattern as Art. 5(1)(f) and Art. 32(1); 'appropriate' is the recurring Berry-flagged vague term.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 37(1)(b) — DPO Designation (Monitoring Threshold)
nodes.rationale: Three qualifiers combined with AND for monitoring-threshold determination; 'and/or' in secondary clause is Berry §5.1 explicitly-flagged problem.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 20(1) — Three-Verb Governance + Liability
nodes.rationale: Only direct personal-liability provision in NIS 2; three-verb coordination (approve, oversee, held liable); national implementations diverging.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(a) — Risk Analysis / IS Security Policies
nodes.rationale: Opening of 21(1) 'appropriate and proportionate' propagates to all sub-points; 'policies' polysemy (formal vs informal).
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 21(2)(a) — risk analysis / is security policies

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(f) — Effectiveness Assessment
nodes.rationale: Same POLY as GDPR Art. 32(1)(d) and CRA Annex I Part II §3; 'effectiveness' has no measurement criterion.

nodes.label: CRA Annex I Part I: Essential cybersecurity requirements (product)
nodes.norm_label: cra annex i part i: essential cybersecurity requirements (product)

nodes.label: CRA Annex II: Information and instructions to be provided with the product
nodes.norm_label: cra annex ii: information and instructions to be provided with the product

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(1): Design, development, production per Annex I Part I
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 13(1): design, development, production per annex i part i

nodes.label: CRA Art. 3(23): Definition of intended purpose
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 3(23): definition of intended purpose

nodes.label: CRA Art. 6(a): Properly installed, intended purpose, reasonably foreseeable
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 6(a): properly installed, intended purpose, reasonably foreseeable

nodes.label: DORA Art. 28(5): Information Security Standards for Third-Party Contracts
nodes.rationale: Requires contractual arrangements with ICT third-party providers to comply with appropriate information security standards; for critical/important functions, most up-to-date and highest quality standards. Central DORA ambiguity: no specific standard named.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 28(5): information security standards for third-party contracts

nodes.label: DORA Art. 4 Security Rules Document
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering authentication, risk-scenario refresh, patch governance, third-party risk, management-body literacy, staff training, and management-body ownership.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4): Eight mandatory control categories
nodes.rationale: Eight-item control list (a)-(h) each self-implementing under Art. 6(8) chapeau; includes info security policy, network mgmt, access control, authentication, change mgmt, patching.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 9(4): eight mandatory control categories

nodes.label: CRA Annex II: User-facing information requirements
nodes.rationale: Specifies user-facing information including SPOC (§2), unique identification (§3), technical support type and end-date (§7), and detailed instructions (§8).
nodes.norm_label: cra annex ii: user-facing information requirements

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28 – Processor
nodes.rationale: Art. 28(1) sufficient guarantees, Art. 28(2) sub-processor authorisation, Art. 28(3)(a)-(h) eight mandatory contract clauses, Art. 28(3)(g) delete/return at contract end. Closed AND-list for contract elements.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 30 – Records of processing activities
nodes.rationale: Art. 30(1)(f) requires documentation of envisaged time limits for erasure of different data categories in the RoPA.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 30 – records of processing activities

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 35 – Data protection impact assessment
nodes.rationale: Art. 35(1) high-risk DPIA trigger, Art. 35(7) DPIA content (systematic description, necessity/proportionality, risk assessment, mitigation). Feeds into Art. 36 prior consultation.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 35 – data protection impact assessment

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 36 – Prior consultation
nodes.rationale: Art. 36(1) prior consultation where DPIA indicates residual high risk. Art. 36(2) 8-week supervisory response. Pre-launch gate: must consult before processing begins.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5 – Principles relating to processing of personal data
nodes.rationale: Art. 5(1)(a) lawfulness/fairness/transparency, (b) purpose limitation, (c) data minimisation, (e) storage limitation. Art. 5(2) accountability. Gateway principles binding all processing operations.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 5 – principles relating to processing of personal data

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 89 – Conditions for processing for archiving, research, statistics
nodes.rationale: Art. 89(1) safeguards: pseudonymisation, aggregation, access limitation. Binds the Art. 5(1)(e) and Art. 9(2)(j) exceptions for longer retention.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 89 – conditions for processing for archiving, research, statistics

nodes.label: DORA Art. 7(2): Continuous Risk Identification + Yearly Review
nodes.rationale: Sentence 1: continuous identification of all ICT risk sources. Sentence 2: review risk scenarios on regular basis, at least yearly. Hard numeric anchor closes temporal ambiguity.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 7(2): continuous risk identification + yearly review

nodes.label: DORA Art. 8(2): ICT Risk Source Identification
nodes.rationale: Reinforces requirement to identify all sources of ICT risk and assess cyber threats and ICT vulnerabilities relevant to ICT supported business functions.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 8(2): ict risk source identification

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(4) Sentence 2 OJ-Level Consolidation Rule
nodes.rationale: The ONLY OJ-level cross-regulation consolidation rule in D-09.2: permits AI Act Art. 9 risk-management system to substitute for CRA Art. 13(3) cybersecurity risk assessment when both apply to the same product (per SR-CRA-066 ambiguity_notes). No other cross-regulation substitution is OJ-permitted.
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 13(4) sentence 2 oj-level consolidation rule

nodes.label: Layered 5-Assessment Architecture (Distinct Objects, Triggers, Cadences)
nodes.rationale: 5 distinct assessment objects (data-subject rights / entity operational / product cybersecurity / ICT operational / AI-system) with 5 distinct triggers, content templates, cadences, and recipients. 5 cadences not synchronised; no OJ-level cadence harmonisation. Entity must satisfy 5 independent review triggers without unified cadence. 0 emergent tensions; 1 OJ-level consolidation rule.

nodes.label: CRDA Flag: GDPR DPIA Does NOT Address Cybersecurity Risk
nodes.rationale: GDPR Art. 35(7) covers risks to data-subject rights and freedoms; it does not require cybersecurity-risk analysis. For a CRA-regulated product processing personal data, the GDPR DPIA must be a separate artefact even when the CRA risk assessment has been performed. This is the structural basis for all 4 SAME—DIFFERENT-PERSPECTIVE pairs.
nodes.norm_label: crda flag: gdpr dpia does not address cybersecurity risk

nodes.label: NIS 2 ↔ DORA EQUAL Classification (Continuous Operational Risk Identification)
nodes.rationale: Both regulations impose continuous operational risk-identification obligations. DORA Art. 6(4) + Art. 7(2) discharges both DORA's and NIS 2's Art. 21(2)(a) obligations for DORA financial entities (DORA-dominant). For non-financial NSIEs, NIS 2 is the authority. Preserves OJ literal parallel; dominant-authority reading is operational consequence of DORA-direct-applicability vs NIS 2-MS-transposition asymmetry.
nodes.norm_label: nis 2 ↔ dora equal classification (continuous operational risk identification)

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 ID.SC-04 (Supply Chain Risk)
nodes.rationale: Suppliers prioritised by criticality; anchors the supply-chain risk dimension for CRA Art. 13(3) risk assessment.

nodes.label: Volere Requirement 9.2 (High-Level Impact & Risk Assessment)
nodes.rationale: MUST requirement: product shall establish impact and risk assessments through documented assessments with review cadence calibrated to lifecycle phase. Depends on all 5 sub-requirements. NIST CSF: ID.RA-01, ID.RA-04, ID.RA-05.

nodes.label: Volere Requirement 9.2.1 (GDPR Pre-launch DPIA)
nodes.rationale: Controller carries out pre-launch DPIA covering 4-item Art. 35(7) content, reviewed on change per Art. 35(11), prior consultation per Art. 36(1). NIST CSF: ID.RA-04, ID.RA-05. DIFFERENT-PERSPECTIVE with all other regs; no OJ-level consolidation.

nodes.label: Volere Requirement 9.2.2 (NIS 2 Continuous Risk-Analysis Policy)
nodes.rationale: Essential/important entities establish continuous risk-analysis policies with all-hazards methodology, proportionality calibration, and Cooperation Group coordinated-assessments ingestion. NIST CSF: ID.RA-05, GV.OV-01. EQUAL with DORA for financial entities.

nodes.label: Volere Requirement 9.2.3 (CRA Cybersecurity Risk Assessment)
nodes.rationale: Manufacturer documents cybersecurity risk assessment per Art. 13(3) with Annex VII §3 record, updated during support period. Subject to CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2 consolidation rule. NIST CSF: ID.RA-05, ID.SC-04.

nodes.label: Volere Requirement 9.2.4 (DORA ICT Risk Framework)
nodes.rationale: Financial entity continuously identifies ICT risks and reviews risk scenarios at least yearly under three-lines-of-defence. NIST CSF: ID.RA-05, GV.RR-02. EQUAL with NIS 2; no OJ-level consolidation with AI Act.

nodes.label: Volere Requirement 9.2.5 (AI Act Risk-Management System)
nodes.rationale: Provider establishes continuous iterative risk-management system with 4-step Art. 9(2)(a)-(d) process, cross-coupled with Art. 27 FRIA. Subject to CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2 consolidation. NIST CSF: ID.RA-05, GV.RM-04.

nodes.label: Sub-SO SO-D-09.2.AI_Act (Continuous Iterative Risk-Management System)
nodes.rationale: AI Act Art. 9(1) established/implemented/documented/maintained risk-management system with 4-step Art. 9(2)(a)-(d) process across AI lifecycle. Cross-coupled with Art. 27 FRIA. Subject to CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2 consolidation (substitutes for CRA Art. 13(3) when both apply to same product).

nodes.label: Sub-SO SO-D-09.2.CRA (Pre-Market + Support-Period Cybersecurity Risk Assessment)
nodes.rationale: CRA Art. 13(3) documented-and-updated cybersecurity risk assessment on product cybersecurity risk with Annex VII §3 record. Subject to the ONLY OJ-level consolidation rule (Art. 13(4) sentence 2) permitting AI Act Art. 9 risk management to substitute when both apply to the same product.
nodes.norm_label: sub-so so-d-09.2.cra (pre-market + support-period cybersecurity risk assessment)

nodes.label: Sub-SO SO-D-09.2.DORA (Continuous + At-Least-Yearly ICT Risk Framework)
nodes.rationale: DORA Art. 6(4) three-lines-of-defence + Art. 7(2) sentence 1 continuous ICT risk identification + sentence 2 at-least-yearly risk-scenario review. EQUAL with NIS 2 on continuous operational risk identification (DORA-dominant for financial entities). No equivalent to CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2.
nodes.norm_label: sub-so so-d-09.2.dora (continuous + at-least-yearly ict risk framework)

nodes.label: Sub-SO SO-D-09.2.GDPR (Pre-launch DPIA on Data-Subject Rights)
nodes.rationale: GDPR Art. 35(1) pre-launch DPIA on data-subject rights with 4-item Art. 35(7) content and Art. 35(11) on-change review. DIFFERENT-PERSPECTIVE with all 4 other regs; no OJ-level consolidation with any other reg. GDPR DPIA does NOT address cybersecurity risk.
nodes.norm_label: sub-so so-d-09.2.gdpr (pre-launch dpia on data-subject rights)

nodes.label: High-Level Security Objective SO-D-09.2.HL (Impact & Risk Assessments)
nodes.rationale: The high-level SO surfaces the common documented-assessment duty (documented assessment + identified risks + mitigation measures + review cadence) across 5 regulations without collapsing per-reg assessment objects, triggers, content templates, thresholds, recipients, or review cadences. It engages when ≥2 applicable regs have ≥1 Y or Conditional-Y scope-overlap pair on the same party.
nodes.norm_label: high-level security objective so-d-09.2.hl (impact & risk assessments)

nodes.label: Sub-SO SO-D-09.2.NIS2 (Continuous Operational Risk-Analysis Policy)
nodes.rationale: NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(a) continuous operational risk-analysis policy with all-hazards methodology (SR-NIS2-040), proportionality calibration (Recital 56), and Cooperation Group coordinated assessments (Art. 22(1)). EQUAL with DORA for financial entities (DORA-dominant).

nodes.label: CRA Annex I Part II: Vulnerability handling requirements
nodes.rationale: Contains SBOM (1), vulnerability remediation (2), CVD policy (5), contact address (6), secure distribution (7), and dissemination (8) requirements.
nodes.norm_label: cra annex i part ii: vulnerability handling requirements

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(8): Support period and policies
nodes.rationale: Fixes the five-year minimum support period (sentence 3), requires CVD policy (sentence 6), and enumerates support-period determination factors (sentence 2).
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 13(8): support period and policies

nodes.label: DORA Article 10 — ICT-related Incident Detection and Response
nodes.rationale: Referenced in CL15-1 RTS sub-point (c) for anomalous activity detection and incident detection/response criteria.
nodes.norm_label: dora article 10 — ict-related incident detection and response

nodes.label: DORA Article 11 — ICT Business Continuity
nodes.rationale: Referenced in CL13-1 (post-incident reviews reference Art. 11 BCP), CL15-1 (RTS sub-points d, e, f), and CL14-2 (communication during incidents per Art. 11(2)(e)).

nodes.label: DORA Article 15 — ESAs RTS Mandate
nodes.rationale: The parent article mandating ESAs to develop common draft regulatory technical standards across seven subject areas.

nodes.label: DORA Article 9 — ICT Security Policies
nodes.rationale: Referenced in CL15-1 RTS sub-points (a) and (b) for security policies and access management rights.

nodes.label: ENISA — EU Agency on Cybersecurity
nodes.rationale: Consulted by ESAs in developing the Art. 15 RTS.

nodes.label: ESAs Joint Committee
nodes.rationale: The body through which ESAs develop common draft regulatory technical standards under Art. 15.

nodes.label: Art. 16(3) ESA RTS Mandate for Simplified Framework
nodes.rationale: Mandates ESAs to develop common draft RTS specifying elements of the simplified framework; deadline 17 January 2024; implemented via Reg. (EU) 2024/2956 + Delegated Reg. (EU) 2024/1772.
nodes.norm_label: art. 16(3) esa rts mandate for simplified framework

nodes.label: Art. 16(1) Simplified ICT Risk Management Obligations
nodes.rationale: Simplified framework for small entities; structurally parallel to Art. 9(4) but at lower operational granularity; omits access control, change management, and patches as standalone control families. Deliberate regulatory choice to exempt small entities from most operationally demanding controls.
nodes.norm_label: art. 16(1) simplified ict risk management obligations

nodes.label: Art. 17 ICT-Related Incident Management Process
nodes.rationale: Establishes the process to detect, manage and notify ICT-related incidents; 8 atomic clauses covering early warning, classification, roles, communication, escalation, and response.

nodes.label: Art. 18 Classification of ICT-Related Incidents and Cyber Threats
nodes.source_location: Atomic clause map CL18-1 to CL18-9
nodes.rationale: Enumerates 6 multiplicative criteria for classifying incidents and 3 for cyber threats; delegates combination rule and materiality thresholds to ESA RTS (Art. 18(3)); deadline 17 January 2024.
nodes.norm_label: art. 18 classification of ict-related incidents and cyber threats

nodes.label: Art. 19 Reporting of Major ICT-Related Incidents
nodes.source_location: Atomic clause map CL19-1 to CL19-8
nodes.rationale: Mandates 3-tier reporting (initial/intermediate/final), voluntary cyber-threat notification, mandatory client notification, CA forwarding to 5 recipient categories, and cross-MS assessment by ESAs/ECB.
nodes.norm_label: art. 19 reporting of major ict-related incidents

nodes.label: Art. 20 Harmonisation of Reporting Content and Templates
nodes.rationale: Pure RTS+ITS delegation; content, time limits, and templates wholly dependent on ESAs Joint Committee output; deadline 17 July 2024; substantially implemented via Reg. (EU) 2024/2956.
nodes.norm_label: art. 20 harmonisation of reporting content and templates

nodes.label: Art. 21 Centralisation of Reporting (Single EU Hub Feasibility)
nodes.rationale: Mandates joint ESA report assessing feasibility of a single EU Hub for major ICT-related incident reporting; 7 enumerated elements; deadline 17 January 2025; scope is regulator-internal institutional architecture.
nodes.norm_label: art. 21 centralisation of reporting (single eu hub feasibility)

nodes.label: DORA Art. 3(10) — Major ICT-Related Incident Definition
nodes.rationale: Inherits from Art. 3(22) critical or important function (DORA-D22 tautology, S3); classification thresholds delegated to Art. 18(3) RTS.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 3(10) — major ict-related incident definition

nodes.label: DORA Art. 3(22) — Critical or Important Function
nodes.rationale: DORA-D22 tautology (S3); foundational for major incident classification and Art. 16 simplified framework scope.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 3(22) — critical or important function

nodes.label: DORA Art. 3(8) — ICT-Related Incident Definition
nodes.rationale: Operationalised by Chapter III; foundational for Art. 17-23 obligations.

nodes.label: Art. 9(4) Full ICT Risk Management Framework
nodes.rationale: The full-granularity framework that Art. 16 simplifies; includes access control (9(4)(c)), change management (9(4)(e)), and patches (9(4)(f)) as standalone control families.
nodes.norm_label: art. 9(4) full ict risk management framework

nodes.label: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1772
nodes.rationale: Jointly with Reg. 2024/2956, specifies the simplified framework under Art. 16(3).

nodes.label: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1774
nodes.rationale: Adopted 31 May 2024 by the Commission on the basis of ESA Joint Committee draft. Supplements DORA with RTS for Art. 15(a)-(g). Resolves many S3 instances flagged in the analysis.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28(3)(a)/(b): Processor Contract Requirements
nodes.rationale: Requires processor contract to stipulate processing only on documented instructions and that authorised persons have committed to confidentiality.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 28(3)(a)/(b) — Processor Contract Requirements
nodes.rationale: Provides the contractual foundation: processor processes only on documented instructions (a) and authorised persons have committed to confidentiality (b); the binding mechanism for the chain-of-authority pattern.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 89 document: Safeguards for archiving/research/statistics
nodes.rationale: Art. 89(1) safeguards (pseudonymisation, aggregation, access limitation) referenced by SR-GDPR-028 and SR-GDPR-029 for special-category and retention carve-outs.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 89 document: safeguards for archiving/research/statistics

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 37 DPO designation
nodes.rationale: Three triggers: public authority, core-activity monitoring on large scale, core-activity special-category on large scale

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 38 DPO position and independence
nodes.rationale: DPO involvement, resourcing, no instructions, direct reporting, no dismissal, no conflict of interests
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 38 dpo position and independence

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 39 DPO tasks
nodes.rationale: Five mandatory tasks (a)-(e): inform/advise, monitor compliance, DPIA advice, SA cooperation, SA contact point

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OC-03: Legal & Regulatory Requirements Management
nodes.rationale: Anchors liability-shield register (SR-NIS2-045) and CA-CSIRT routing architecture (SR-NIS2-044). Converts legal protections into operational compliance artefacts.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.oc-03: legal & regulatory requirements management

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.SC-05: Response Planning with Third Parties
nodes.rationale: Supplies third-party-response discipline for cross-border notification: response-and-recovery planning with suppliers enables cross-MS flow against rehearsed procedures.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.sc-05: response planning with third parties

nodes.label: NIST CSF RC.RP-06: Recovery Declaration & After-Action
nodes.rationale: Supplies recovery-completion discipline for 1-month final report and ongoing-incident closing report. Ensures defended closure rather than calendar deadline.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rc.rp-06: recovery declaration & after-action

nodes.label: NIST CSF RS.MA-02: Incident Triage & Validation
nodes.rationale: Supplies upstream triage discipline for the 24h early warning: entity must triage against Art. 23(3) test-A/test-B criteria before submitting.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rs.ma-02: incident triage & validation

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 33 — Liability Shield
nodes.rationale: Covers the good-faith notification liability shield (Art. 23(1) ¶1 fourth sentence) as a standalone article split.

nodes.label: Berry Analytical Framework
nodes.rationale: Analytical methodology used to identify and classify ambiguous legal terms. Key sections: §3.3.1 (undefined terms), §5.1 (vague qualifiers), §5.4.6 (catch-all scope), §5.4.7 (AND/OR coordination), §5.5 (multi-way coordination), §5.7 (temporal anchors).

nodes.label: Critical or Important Function (CIF)
nodes.rationale: S3 tautological definition (DORA-D22). Used as substantive threshold in Art. 8(5) (TPP interconnections) and Art. 9(2) (resilience priority). Entity-determined criticality per CL8-3 Instance 1.

nodes.label: Cyber Threat
nodes.source_location: DORA Art. 3(12), CSA Art. 2(8) cross-ref, CL8-1
nodes.rationale: Defined in DORA Art. 3(12) with cross-reference to CSA Art. 2(8). Subject to continuous assessment alongside ICT vulnerabilities in Art. 8(2).

nodes.label: Data Security Dimensions (Availability, Authenticity, Integrity, Confidentiality)
nodes.rationale: Four cumulative data-security dimensions applied across three data states (at rest, in use, in transit). Cross-referenced from NIS 2 Art. 6(2). Appears in Art. 16(1)(c), Art. 9(2), and Art. 9(3)(c).
nodes.norm_label: data security dimensions (availability, authenticity, integrity, confidentiality)

nodes.label: ICT Third-Party Service Provider (CTPP)
nodes.rationale: Referenced in CL13-2 (training inclusion per Art. 30(2)(i)) and CL15-1 (RTS sub-point e on insolvency/failure of CTPPs).

nodes.label: ICT Vulnerability
nodes.source_location: DORA Art. 3(16), NIS 2 Art. 6(15) cross-ref, CL8-1
nodes.rationale: Defined in DORA Art. 3(16) with cross-reference to NIS 2 Art. 6(15). Assessed continuously alongside cyber threats in Art. 8(2).

nodes.label: Legacy ICT System
nodes.rationale: Defined as an ICT system that has reached end of life cycle, is no longer supported/maintained by vendor, or cannot be patched/updated, but is still in use. Three-way OR definition. Subject to specific yearly ICT risk assessment for non-microenterprises.

nodes.label: Major Change (trigger for re-assessment)
nodes.rationale: Undefined threshold triggering risk assessment (Art. 8(3)) and inventory updates (Art. 8(6)). S3: R1 (structural change only) vs R2 (materiality-based). Inherited by CL8-3 Instance 4.

nodes.label: S3 (Unresolved) Reading Status
nodes.rationale: Analytical status indicating that multiple materially distinct readings of a legal term remain unresolved pending RTS adoption or further guidance. All instances in this document carry S3 status.

nodes.label: CL8-1 — Art. 8(1)+(2) Identification and Continuous Risk-Source Identification
nodes.rationale: Covers the obligation to identify, classify, and document ICT-supported business functions, plus continuous identification of ICT risk sources including bidirectional exposure to/from other financial entities and cyber threats.
nodes.norm_label: cl8-1 — art. 8(1)+(2) identification and continuous risk-source identification

nodes.label: CL8-2 — Art. 8(3)+(7) Major-Change Risk Assessment and Legacy ICT
nodes.rationale: Applies to non-microenterprises. Analyzes the undefined 'major change' threshold and the three-way OR definition of legacy ICT systems (end-of-life OR unsupported OR unable-to-patch).
nodes.norm_label: cl8-2 — art. 8(3)+(7) major-change risk assessment and legacy ict

nodes.label: CL8-3 — Art. 8(4)+(5)+(6) Critical-Asset Mapping, Inventory, and TPP Dependencies
nodes.rationale: Covers mapping of critical assets, links and interdependencies, interconnections with ICT third-party service providers supporting critical or important functions, and periodic inventory updates triggered by major changes.
nodes.norm_label: cl8-3 — art. 8(4)+(5)+(6) critical-asset mapping, inventory, and tpp dependencies

nodes.label: CL9-1 — Art. 9(1) Continuous Monitoring and Control
nodes.rationale: Analyzes the coordinated obligation to continuously monitor AND control ICT systems, and the three-category requirement of appropriate ICT security tools, policies, and procedures.
nodes.norm_label: cl9-1 — art. 9(1) continuous monitoring and control

nodes.label: CL9-2 — Art. 9(2) Design, Procure, and Implement ICT Security
nodes.rationale: Covers the three-way coordination of design/procure/implement, the four data-security dimensions across three data states, and the four-category scope of policies/procedures/protocols/tools. RTS-pending per Art. 15(a).
nodes.norm_label: cl9-2 — art. 9(2) design, procure, and implement ict security

nodes.label: CL9-3 — Art. 9(3)(a)–(d) ICT Solutions and Data Security Baseline
nodes.rationale: Analyzes the cumulative four data-security objectives (transfer security, corruption/loss minimization, availability/authenticity/integrity/confidentiality protection, data management risk prevention) under Art. 4 proportionality.
nodes.norm_label: cl9-3 — art. 9(3)(a)–(d) ict solutions and data security baseline

nodes.label: DORA Article 15 — Regulatory Technical Standards (RTS)
nodes.rationale: Art. 15(a) specifies further elements for ICT security policies/procedures/protocols/tools (Art. 9(2)) and the ICT risk management framework (Art. 16(3)). Pending RTS adoption resolves several S3 readings.

nodes.label: DORA Article 3 — Definitions
nodes.rationale: Supplies definitional anchors: Art. 3(2) network and information system (NIS 2 cross-ref), Art. 3(5) ICT risk, Art. 3(6) information asset, Art. 3(7) ICT asset, Art. 3(12) cyber threat, Art. 3(16) vulnerability, Art. 3(19) ICT third-party service provider, Art. 3(43) legacy ICT system.

nodes.label: DORA Article 4 — Proportionality Principle
