nodes.rationale: The proportionality principle referenced in Art. 7(a), Art. 9(3) chapeau, and applied across all cards. Art. 4(2) provides risk-driven criteria that disambiguate 'appropriate' qualifiers.

nodes.label: CRA Article 21: Manufacturer-equivalent trigger (importer/distributor)
nodes.rationale: Triggers manufacturer-equivalent status for importers/distributors placing under own name or through substantial modification. Inherited by SR-CRA-070, 090, 092.

nodes.label: CRA Article 22: Third-party substantial modification
nodes.rationale: Triggers manufacturer-equivalent status for third-party modifiers. Referenced in SR-CRA-070 as part of the substantial-modification architecture.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(1)(b) — Ongoing Confidentiality and Resilience
nodes.rationale: Requires the ability to ensure ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems; achieved only if monitoring is in place to detect personal data breaches.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 32(1)(b) — ongoing confidentiality and resilience

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 34(3) — Notification Exceptions
nodes.rationale: Provides exceptions to data-subject notification where subsequent measures render data unintelligible or eliminate the high risk; the controller must demonstrate that mitigation actually neutralises the risk.

nodes.label: Cyber Maturity and Preparedness
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(4) effectiveness-monitoring qualifier. Literal reading is documented preparedness (BCP testing) rather than CMMI-style levels.

nodes.label: DORA Article 13 — Threat Intelligence and Learning
nodes.rationale: The parent article covering threat intelligence gathering, post-incident reviews, lessons propagation, effectiveness monitoring, training, and technology monitoring.
nodes.norm_label: dora article 13 — threat intelligence and learning

nodes.label: DORA Article 30 — ICT Third-Party Risk
nodes.rationale: Referenced in CL13-2 for including CTPPs in training schemes per Art. 30(2)(i).

nodes.label: DORA-D14 — Cyber-attack
nodes.rationale: Defined in DORA Art. 3(14). Referenced in CL13-1 definitional anchor. S2 status.

nodes.label: DORA-D30 — Management Body
nodes.rationale: Defined in DORA Art. 3(30). Referenced in CL13-2, CL14-2. Composite cross-reference.

nodes.label: ICT Business Continuity Policy (Art. 11)
nodes.rationale: Referenced in CL13-1 (post-incident reviews reference Art. 11 BCP), CL15-1 (RTS sub-point d and e), and CL12-2 (recovery plans).

nodes.label: ICT Response and Recovery Plans (Art. 11(3))
nodes.rationale: Referenced in CL15-1 (RTS sub-point f) and CL13-1 (lessons from activation of response and recovery plans).

nodes.label: ICT Security Awareness and DOR Training
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(6) compulsory training modules. Must be commensurate to remit of functions. T3-imposed 'role-specific' mapping flagged as unsubstantiated by OJ text.
nodes.norm_label: ict security awareness and dor training

nodes.label: Lessons Propagation into ICT Risk Assessment
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(3) obligation to incorporate lessons from four sources (TLPT, incidents, BCP activation, supervisory reviews) into ICT risk assessment on a continuous basis.
nodes.norm_label: lessons propagation into ict risk assessment

nodes.label: Post ICT-related Incident Review
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(2) obligation triggered by major ICT-related incident. Four review dimensions: promptness, forensic analysis, escalation effectiveness, communication effectiveness.

nodes.label: Technological Developments Monitoring
nodes.rationale: Art. 13(7) obligation for non-microenterprises to monitor relevant technological developments on a continuous basis for impact on ICT security and DOR.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 3(2) — Network and Information System Definition
nodes.rationale: Inherits from NIS 2 Art. 6(1); foundational definition for all ICT-related clauses in DORA.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 3(2) — network and information system definition

nodes.label: CL13-1 — Art. 13(1)-(3) Threat Intel + Post-Incident Reviews + Lessons
nodes.rationale: Covers the learn-and-evolve cycle: vulnerability/threat gathering, post-incident reviews with four dimensions, and continuous incorporation of lessons from four sources into ICT risk assessment.
nodes.norm_label: cl13-1 — art. 13(1)-(3) threat intel + post-incident reviews + lessons

nodes.label: CL13-2 — Art. 13(4)-(7) Monitoring + Training + Tech Developments
nodes.rationale: Covers effectiveness monitoring of DOR strategy, yearly reporting to management body, compulsory ICT security awareness training, and continuous monitoring of technological developments.
nodes.norm_label: cl13-2 — art. 13(4)-(7) monitoring + training + tech developments

nodes.label: DORA Art. 24 — Digital Operational Resilience Testing Programme
nodes.rationale: Establishes the testing programme as an integral part of the Art. 6 ICT risk-management framework. Carries 5 atomic clauses (CL24-1 through CL24-5) covering programme establishment, risk-based approach, independence, remediation, and yearly cadence.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 24 — digital operational resilience testing programme

nodes.label: DORA Art. 6 — ICT Risk-Management Framework
nodes.rationale: The testing programme under Art. 24 is explicitly established as 'an integral part of the ICT risk-management framework referred to in Article 6'.

nodes.label: Business Continuity Plans and Recovery Measures
nodes.rationale: Required for continuity of critical or important functions. Must include back-up and restoration measures. Subject to regular testing and post-incident analysis. RTS to specify further components per Art. 16(3)(c)-(d).
nodes.norm_label: business continuity plans and recovery measures

nodes.label: DORA Article 14 — Crisis Communication
nodes.rationale: The parent article covering crisis communication plans, internal/external communication policies, and designated spokesperson.

nodes.label: DORA Article 16 — Simplified Framework
nodes.rationale: The parent article providing a simplified ICT risk management framework for small and exempted entities.

nodes.label: DORA-D53 — Small Institution for Occupational Retirement Provision
nodes.rationale: Referenced in CL16-1 as one of the five exempted entity categories.
nodes.norm_label: dora-d53 — small institution for occupational retirement provision

nodes.label: Electronic Money Institutions (exempted per EMI Directive)
nodes.rationale: Exempted from Articles 5–15 under Art. 16 when exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC. Subject to the simplified framework obligations.
nodes.norm_label: electronic money institutions (exempted per emi directive)

nodes.label: EMD Art. 9(1) — E-money Institution Exemption
nodes.rationale: Cross-referenced in CL16-1 as the basis for e-money institution exemption from DORA Art. 5-15.

nodes.label: ICT Risk Management Framework (Art. 6(1))
nodes.rationale: The overarching framework referenced throughout Art. 12-16. Art. 16(2) requires it to be documented, reviewed periodically and upon major incidents, and continuously improved.

nodes.label: IFR Art. 12(1) — Investment Firm Exemption
nodes.rationale: Cross-referenced in CL16-1 as the basis for small/non-interconnected investment firm exemption.

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 6(1) — Network and Information Security
nodes.rationale: Cross-referenced as definitional anchor for DORA Art. 3(2) in CL12-1, and for vulnerability definition in CL13-1.
nodes.norm_label: nis 2 art. 6(1) — network and information security

nodes.label: Payment Institutions (exempted per PSD2)
nodes.rationale: Exempted from Articles 5–15 under Art. 16 when exempted pursuant to Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (PSD2). Subject to the simplified framework obligations.

nodes.label: PSD2 Art. 32(1) — Payment Institution Exemption
nodes.rationale: Cross-referenced in CL16-1 as the basis for payment institution exemption from DORA Art. 5-15.

nodes.label: Responsible Disclosure
nodes.rationale: Art. 14(1) qualifier for crisis communication. Berry-flagged. Literal reading is timely + accurate with entity latitude, as opposed to CVD-style coordinated disclosure.

nodes.label: Small and Non-Interconnected Investment Firms
nodes.rationale: Exempted from Articles 5–15 under Art. 16. Must still maintain a sound and documented ICT risk management framework, monitor security, minimize ICT risk impact, and ensure business continuity.

nodes.label: DORA Article 16 — Simplified ICT Risk Management Framework
nodes.rationale: Provides a simplified ICT risk management framework for small and non-interconnected investment firms, payment institutions, electronic money institutions, and small occupational retirement provision institutions, exempting them from Articles 5–15 while imposing eight core obligations (a)–(h).
nodes.norm_label: dora article 16 — simplified ict risk management framework

nodes.label: CL14-2 — Art. 14(2)+(3) Internal/External Communication + Designated Person
nodes.rationale: Covers communication policies differentiating staff involved in ICT risk management from those needing information, and the designated public/media function role.
nodes.norm_label: cl14-2 — art. 14(2)+(3) internal/external communication + designated person

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-01 — Data Protection
nodes.rationale: Covers D-01.1 (at-rest), D-01.2 (in-transit), D-01.3 (key management), D-01.4 (in-use).

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-03 — Access Control
nodes.rationale: Covers D-03.1 (authentication), D-03.2 (key protection), D-03.3 (least privilege).

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-09 — Governance & Documentation
nodes.rationale: Covers D-09.1 (management body responsibility), D-09.2 (documentation), D-09.3 (framework).

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9 — ICT Security Policies & Controls
nodes.rationale: Chapter II Section II operational resilience architecture. Art. 9(2) CIA+A cross-state, Art. 9(4) eight-item control list (a)-(h).
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 9 — ict security policies & controls

nodes.label: CRA Art. 14 Dual-Track Notification Architecture
nodes.rationale: Dual-track: AEV track (Art. 14(1)-(2)) and severe-incident track (Art. 14(3)-(5)), each with three-tier temporal pattern; severity categorisation under Art. 14(5) disjunctive tests determines which chain to start.

nodes.label: ENISA Single Reporting Platform (Art. 16)
nodes.rationale: Established under Art. 16(1) for Art. 14/15 notifications; enforces simultaneity architecturally; accessible simultaneously to ENISA when submitted via CSIRT end-point; security per Art. 16(4).

nodes.label: GDPR Article 5: Principles relating to processing of personal data
nodes.rationale: Seven principles (lawfulness/fairness/transparency, purpose limitation, minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity/confidentiality, accountability) with Art. 5(2) demonstrability requirement.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 5: principles relating to processing of personal data

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 58 document: Supervisory authority powers
nodes.rationale: Per-article split document referencing SR-GDPR-044 for accountability and evidence chain grounding the Art. 58 enforcement regime.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 58 document: supervisory authority powers

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 83 document: Administrative fines
nodes.rationale: Per-article split document referencing SR-GDPR-044; Art. 83 fines are the enforcement consequence of the accountability-and-evidence chain.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(21): Corrective measures on non-conformity
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 13(21): corrective measures on non-conformity

nodes.label: CRA Art. 3(48): Free and open-source software definition
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 3(48): free and open-source software definition

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.DS-11: Backup Creation, Protection, Maintenance, Testing
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ds-11: backup creation, protection, maintenance, testing

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(8): Secure-by-Default and Secure-Update
nodes.rationale: Feeds upstream incident-prevention side; parallel to DORA backup and recovery obligations.

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 21: Security Measures for NSIEs
nodes.rationale: Parallel obligations on NSIEs outside DORA scope; Art. 21(2)(a) cross-state, (b) incident-handling, (c) continuity, (d) cryptography, (g) basic security training.
nodes.norm_label: nis 2 art. 21: security measures for nsies

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(2): Cross-State CIA+A Protection
nodes.rationale: Core of Chapter II Section II operational resilience architecture; supplies substantive content to Art. 6(8) chapeau obligation.

nodes.label: CRA Annex I Part II: Vulnerability handling and secure update requirements
nodes.norm_label: cra annex i part ii: vulnerability handling and secure update requirements

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(18): Annex II information accessible for support period
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 13(18): annex ii information accessible for support period

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(24): Commission implementing acts on SBOM format
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 13(24): commission implementing acts on sbom format

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 12(6): Identity Verification for Rights Requests
nodes.rationale: Permits controller to request additional information to confirm identity where reasonable doubts exist concerning the data subject's identity.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 12(6): identity verification for rights requests

nodes.label: Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure (CVD) Policy
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part II (5) + Art. 13(8) sentence 6; structured receive + triage + publish + post-disclosure verification pipeline; aligned with ISO 29147/ISO 30111; extends to OSS stewards via Art. 24(3).

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4)(d): Authentication + Key Protection + Encryption
nodes.rationale: Three-control AND: strong authentication mechanisms + protection measures of cryptographic keys + data encryption based on approved data classification and ICT risk assessment.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 9(4)(d): authentication + key protection + encryption

nodes.label: Central Counterparty (CCP)
nodes.rationale: Sectoral carve-out in Art. 12(3): recovery plans must enable recovery of all transactions at time of disruption to complete settlement on scheduled date.

nodes.label: Central Securities Depository (CSD)
nodes.rationale: Sectoral carve-out in Art. 12(5): must maintain at least one secondary processing site with specific requirements.

nodes.label: Data Integrity (highest level)
nodes.rationale: The 'highest level of data integrity' qualifier in Art. 12(7). Literal reading requires strongest possible integrity (checksum + reconciliation + comparison).

nodes.label: Data Reporting Service Provider (DRSP)
nodes.rationale: Sectoral carve-out in Art. 12(3): must maintain adequate resources and backup/restoration facilities to offer services at all times.

nodes.label: DORA Article 12 — ICT Response and Recovery
nodes.rationale: The parent article covering backup policies, restoration procedures, redundant ICT capacities, CSD secondary sites, RTO/RPO, and data integrity checks.
nodes.norm_label: dora article 12 — ict response and recovery

nodes.label: Redundant ICT Capacities
nodes.rationale: Art. 12(4) obligation for non-microenterprises. Literal reading is qualitative redundancy (backups + failover) rather than quantitative N+1/N+2.

nodes.label: RTO/RPO — Recovery Time and Recovery Point Objectives
nodes.rationale: Berry-flagged hard metrics. Both required for every function per literal reading. Determined based on criticality and market efficiency impact.
nodes.norm_label: rto/rpo — recovery time and recovery point objectives

nodes.label: CSD Secondary Processing Site
nodes.rationale: Art. 12(5) CSD-specific obligation. Must be geographically distant, capable of continuity, and immediately accessible.

nodes.label: CL12-2 — Art. 12(3)+(4) Restoration + Redundant ICT Capacities
nodes.rationale: Covers physically/logically segregated restoration systems, timely restoration, CCP recovery plans, DRSP backup facilities, and redundant ICT capacities with microenterprise carve-out.
nodes.norm_label: cl12-2 — art. 12(3)+(4) restoration + redundant ict capacities

nodes.label: CL12-4 — Art. 12(6)+(7) RTO/RPO + Data Integrity Checks
nodes.rationale: Covers recovery time and recovery point objectives determination, and data integrity checks including multiple checks and reconciliations during recovery.
nodes.norm_label: cl12-4 — art. 12(6)+(7) rto/rpo + data integrity checks

nodes.label: GDPR Article 28: Processor
nodes.rationale: Art. 28(3)(a)-(h) eight mandatory contract clauses form a closed AND-list. Art. 28(3)(c) references full Art. 32; Art. 28(3)(h) provides audit and inspection access. Together they are the controller's principal levers into processor security.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 32: Security of processing
nodes.rationale: Four-element list: pseudonymisation/encryption, ongoing CIA+R, timely restoration, regular testing. Art. 32(2) provides the five-event risk enumeration. The 'state of the art' and 'appropriate level of security' qualifiers are time-dependent and context-dependent.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 33: Notification of personal data breach to supervisory authority
nodes.rationale: 72-hour notification with risk-based carve-out. Art. 33(3)(d) requires description of measures taken or proposed. Art. 33(2) covers processor-to-controller notification.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 33: notification of personal data breach to supervisory authority

nodes.label: GDPR Article 34: Communication of personal data breach to data subject
nodes.rationale: Higher threshold than Art. 33 (high risk vs. risk). Art. 34(3)(a)/(b) provide notification carve-outs where mitigation renders data unintelligible or eliminates high risk. Content must be in clear and plain language.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 34: communication of personal data breach to data subject

nodes.label: GDPR Article 36: Prior consultation
nodes.rationale: Art. 36(1) requires consultation prior to processing where DPIA indicates residual high risk. Art. 36(2) defines the 8-week supervisory response window. 'Prior to processing' is read strictly: before launching, not after.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(1)(b): Ongoing CIA and Resilience of Processing Systems
nodes.rationale: Lists the ability to ensure ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems and services among required measures.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 32(1)(b): ongoing cia and resilience of processing systems

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(2): Risk Enumeration for Security Assessment
nodes.rationale: Requires account be taken of risks from accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to personal data.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 32(2): risk enumeration for security assessment

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-08 — Human Factors
nodes.rationale: Covers D-08.3 (management body training and knowledge).

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RR-02: Roles and Responsibilities for Cybersecurity Risk
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.rr-02: roles and responsibilities for cybersecurity risk

nodes.label: MiFID II Art. 4(1)(36)/(37): Management Body Definition
nodes.rationale: Cross-reference for management body definition; co-exists with Art. 5(2) and Art. 5(4) obligations.
nodes.norm_label: mifid ii art. 4(1)(36)/(37): management body definition

nodes.label: CRA Art. 24 OSS Steward Extension
nodes.rationale: Art. 24(3) extends Art. 14(1)/(3)/(8) to OSS stewards; Art. 3(14) defines steward as legal person systematically providing support on sustained basis; proportionality preserved per Recital 18.

nodes.label: D-06.2: Supply Chain (SBOM)
nodes.rationale: CRA sole authority per taxonomy §4.1. Referenced by SO-CRA-038, SR-CRA-008, 009.

nodes.label: CRA Article 17: ENISA/CSIRT coordination and public disclosure
nodes.rationale: ENISA-EU-CyCLONe hand-off (17(1)), CSIRT public disclosure (17(2)), biennial report (17(3)), EU vulnerability database (17(5)), CSIRT helpdesk (17(6)).
nodes.norm_label: cra article 17: enisa/csirt coordination and public disclosure

nodes.label: EU-CyCLONe (EU Cyber Crisis Liaison Network)
nodes.rationale: Established under NIS 2; receives ENISA submissions for large-scale incident management; manufacturer has no direct submission authority.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32 – Security of processing
nodes.rationale: Art. 32(1)(c) timely restoration of availability, Art. 32(2) risk enumeration (destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure/access). Anchors the five-event vocabulary underlying breach assessment.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 13(2): Cybersecurity risk assessment across lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Requires assessment of cybersecurity risks across planning, design, development, production, delivery, and maintenance phases with health-and-safety qualifier.
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 13(2): cybersecurity risk assessment across lifecycle

nodes.label: DORA Art. 8(1): Continuous Monitoring and Control
nodes.rationale: Requires continuous monitoring and control of security and functioning of ICT systems, minimising ICT risk impact through appropriate tools, policies and procedures.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 8(1): continuous monitoring and control

nodes.label: EDPB Guidelines (various)
nodes.rationale: EDPB Guidelines 05/2020 (consent), 3/2018 (DPO), 07/2019 (accountability), 9/2022 (breach), 4/2019 (DPIA) provide interpretive guidance for GDPR SRs.

nodes.label: Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)
nodes.rationale: Annex I Part II (1): machine-readable format covering at least top-level dependencies; precondition for patching, supply-chain risk management, and CVD; format specified by Art. 13(24) implementing acts.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-02 — Vulnerability Management
nodes.rationale: Covers D-02.1 (risk identification), D-02.2 (patch management), D-02.4 (testing).

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.IM-04 — Risk management improvements informed by context
nodes.rationale: Closes the external-context feedback loop — supervisory guidance, ENISA threat-landscape reports, sectoral near-miss learnings feed scenario recalibration.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.im-04 — risk management improvements informed by context

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.RA-03 — Threats identified, recorded, prioritized
nodes.rationale: Supplies the threat-intelligence layer — internal-source threat catalogues and external-source feeds with priority scoring aligned to entity risk appetite.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.ra-03 — threats identified, recorded, prioritized

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 34(3)(a): Unintelligibility Exception to Notification
nodes.rationale: Exempts data-subject notification if appropriate measures render personal data unintelligible to any unauthorised person, such as encryption.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 34(3)(a): unintelligibility exception to notification

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 30 Records of processing activities
nodes.rationale: Seven content items in Art. 30(1); SA access in Art. 30(4); 250-employee exception in Art. 30(5)
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 30 records of processing activities

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 32(1)(d): Regular Testing and Evaluation of Security Measures
nodes.rationale: Requires a process for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating the effectiveness of technical and organisational measures.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 32(1)(d): regular testing and evaluation of security measures

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(1): Data processing principles
nodes.rationale: Six principles: lawfulness/fairness/transparency, purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity/confidentiality.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 35 Data Protection Impact Assessment
nodes.rationale: Pre-launch assessment for high-risk processing; four content items in Art. 35(7); review on risk change in Art. 35(11)
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 35 data protection impact assessment

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 36 Prior consultation
nodes.rationale: Controller must consult SA prior to processing where DPIA indicates residual high risk; 8-week SA response window

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.IM-02: Improvement Processes Implemented
nodes.rationale: Captures the continuous-improvement layer: improvement processes implemented across organisational tiers, ensuring reassessment outputs feed back into control updates rather than accumulating as static documents.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.im-02: improvement processes implemented

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33 — Breach Notification to Authority
nodes.rationale: 72-hour notification clock, processor-to-controller chain, four-element content requirement. Underpins SR-GDPR-014 through SR-GDPR-018.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 33 — breach notification to authority

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 34 — Breach Communication to Data Subject
nodes.rationale: High-risk threshold communication with cryptographic and subsequent-measures carve-outs. Underpins SR-GDPR-019 through SR-GDPR-021.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 34 — breach communication to data subject

nodes.label: DORA Art. 10 — Detection & Incident Response
nodes.rationale: Art. 10(1) prompt detection of anomalous activities and SPOF identification. Art. 10(2) multi-layer detection with threshold-driven response.

nodes.label: NIST CSF RS.MA-01 — Incident management plan executed
nodes.rationale: Bridges detection to response: alert thresholds and trigger criteria operationalise the transition from detection to declared-incident.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rs.ma-01 — incident management plan executed

nodes.label: DORA Art. 24-26 — Digital Operational Resilience Testing
nodes.rationale: Chapter IV: Art. 24(1) testing programme, Art. 25(1) 12 testing modalities, Art. 26(1) TLPT triennial cycle, Art. 27 advanced testing for significant entities.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 24-26 — digital operational resilience testing

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 15 – Right of access by data subject
nodes.rationale: Art. 15(1) confirmation and access, Art. 15(3) copy in commonly used electronic form, Art. 15(4) third-party-rights limit. Data-subject-facing access right distinct from Art. 20 portability.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 15 – right of access by data subject

nodes.label: NIST CSF RS.AN-06: Investigation Action Recording
nodes.rationale: Actions performed during investigation recorded with integrity and provenance preserved; supports auditable evidence rather than narrative summary.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf rs.an-06: investigation action recording

nodes.label: Art. 23 Ch. III Extension to Payment-Sector Entities
nodes.rationale: Extends entire Ch. III to operational or security payment-related incidents for credit institutions, payment institutions, AISPs, and EMIs; DORA-PSD2 integration point; supersedes PSD2 Art. 96(1) reporting architecture.
nodes.norm_label: art. 23 ch. iii extension to payment-sector entities

nodes.label: DORA Chapter III: ICT-Related Incident Management, Classification, and Reporting (Art. 17–23)
nodes.rationale: The operational reporting arm of DORA; operationalises Art. 3(8) and Art. 3(10) definitions; structurally dependent on RTS/ITS acts; 31 atomic clauses across 7 articles.
nodes.norm_label: dora chapter iii: ict-related incident management, classification, and reporting (art. 17–23)

nodes.label: CRR Regulation 575/2013
nodes.rationale: Source regulation for credit institution definition (Art. 4(1)(1)).

nodes.label: EMD Directive 2009/110/EC
nodes.rationale: Source regulation for electronic money institution definition (Art. 2(1)).

nodes.label: PSD2 Directive 2015/2366
nodes.rationale: Source regulation for payment institution (Art. 4(4)) and AISP (Art. 33(1)) definitions; DORA Art. 23 supersedes PSD2 Art. 96(1) reporting architecture.

nodes.label: CRA 3-Tier Classification Architecture
nodes.rationale: Analogous to AI Act risk tiers: Default (Art. 6) → Important (Art. 7) → Critical (Art. 8); each tier imposes progressively stricter conformity-assessment obligations.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 6(a) — Essential-Requirements Gate
nodes.rationale: Products with digital elements shall be made available only where they meet essential cybersecurity requirements; 'essential' modifier is itself undefined.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 7(1) — Important-Products Classification Gate
nodes.rationale: 'Core functionality' is the single most consequential classification term; R1-R3 admit materially different compliance populations.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 8(1) — Critical-Product Certification Requirement
nodes.rationale: Most consequential single clause in Art. 6-8; requires European cybersecurity certificate at assurance level 'substantial'; no scheme adopted as of mid-2025.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 32(2) — Class I Conformity Assessment
nodes.rationale: Class I important products require module B+C or H when harmonised standards not fully applied; part of 3-tier classification architecture.
nodes.norm_label: cra art. 32(2) — class i conformity assessment

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 35 — Security Objectives & Rules (D-09.2)
nodes.rationale: Per-article split document covering DPIA obligations (Art. 35) with SO and SR definitions mapped to NIST CSF 2.0.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 36 — Security Objectives & Rules (D-09.2)
nodes.rationale: Per-article split document covering prior consultation (Art. 36) with SO and SR definitions mapped to NIST CSF 2.0.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 37 — Security Objectives & Rules (D-09.2)
nodes.rationale: Per-article split document covering DPO designation triggers (Art. 37) with SO and SR definitions mapped to NIST CSF 2.0.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 39 — Security Objectives & Rules (D-09.2)
nodes.rationale: Per-article split document covering DPO tasks (Art. 39) with SO and SR definitions mapped to NIST CSF 2.0.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 4 — Security Objectives & Rules (D-09.2)
nodes.rationale: Per-article split document covering definitions (Art. 4) with SO and SR definitions mapped to NIST CSF 2.0. References 12 cross-regulation domain documents.

nodes.label: D-07.1: Secure Development
nodes.rationale: Cross-domain for secure development lifecycle. Referenced by SO-AIACT-010, SR-AIACT-018, SO-CRA-045, SO-CRA-053.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 GV.RR-04 — Cybersecurity in HR Practices
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF 2.0 control: 'Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices (screening, onboarding, training, awareness, offboarding).' Mapped from SR-AIACT-012 and SR-AIACT-020 for HR-practices dimension.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf 2.0 gv.rr-04 — cybersecurity in hr practices

nodes.label: D-07.1 — Secure-Development Sub-domain
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation sub-domain for secure development. AI Act Art. 14(1) cross-mapping (oversight as built-in architectural feature). DORA Art. 25 pre-deployment testing also relevant.

nodes.label: D-08.2 — Human-Factors Sub-domain
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation sub-domain for human factors. AI Act Art. 14(1)+(4) primary mapping. DORA Art. 27 tester independence and conflict-of-interest avoidance also relevant.

nodes.label: D-09.1 — Governance-Documentation Sub-domain
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation sub-domain for governance and documentation. AI Act Art. 13(1)+(3) mapped here. DORA Ch. IV testing programme documentation also falls under this domain.

nodes.label: D-09.1: Governance and Documentation
nodes.rationale: Primary sub-domain for all documents in this chunk. Cross-referenced by AI Act and CRA rules as the governance/documentation anchor.

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 13(1) — High-Risk AI Transparency
nodes.rationale: Requires high-risk AI systems to be sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret output and use appropriately. Carries S3 ambiguity on 'sufficiently transparent' and 'appropriate type and degree of transparency' — two vague anchors in one sentence.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 13(1) — high-risk ai transparency

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 13(3) — Instructions for Use
nodes.rationale: Requires instructions for use with 8 quality adjectives (concise, complete, correct, clear, relevant, accessible, comprehensible, appropriate digital format). Operationalises the upstream Art. 13(1) transparency duty into a concrete documentation deliverable.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 13(3) — instructions for use

nodes.label: CRA Art. 7(4) — Instructions for Use
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation intersection: AI Act Art. 13(3) instructions-for-use duty intersects with CRA Art. 7(4) instructions-for-use obligations for products with digital elements and CRA Annex I documentation requirements.

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 14(1) — Human Oversight Design
nodes.rationale: Umbrella provision for human-oversight duty. Requires high-risk AI systems to be designed for effective oversight by natural persons with appropriate human-machine interface tools. Principal locus where AI Act bridges technical-design to human-factors obligations.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 14(1) — human oversight design

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 14(4) — Five Oversight Abilities
nodes.rationale: Five-element AND-coordinated list: (a) properly understand, (b) remain aware of automation bias, (c) correctly interpret, (d) decide, (e) intervene. Operationalises the umbrella Art. 14(1) duty. Carries medium severity on 'as appropriate and proportionate' soft hedge.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 14(4) — five oversight abilities

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 27 — Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment
nodes.rationale: Per-article split for Art. 27. No standalone SO row; covered via SR-AIACT-019 and SR-AIACT-020 which reference Art. 27 in the accountability chain.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 27 — fundamental rights impact assessment

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 5 — Prohibited Practices & Log Retention
nodes.rationale: Per-article split for Art. 5. Contains SR-AIACT-008 (log retention, Art. 19(1)) and SR-AIACT-019 (deployer measures). Includes T5 mapping error flag for AIA-C11.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 5 — prohibited practices & log retention

nodes.label: Cross-Clause 'Compelling Legitimate' Propagation
nodes.rationale: Art. 21(1) 'compelling legitimate grounds' (objection) + Art. 49(1) 'compelling legitimate interests' (transfer) — two qualifiers may or may not share interpretation.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 21(1) — Objection Grounds and Overriding
nodes.rationale: 'Compelling legitimate grounds' is stronger than Art. 6(1)(f) 'legitimate interests'; the 'overriding' test is undefined.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 21(1) — objection grounds and overriding

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 49(1) — Compelling Legitimate Interests (Catch-All)
nodes.rationale: Four conjunctive qualifiers; cross-clause propagation from Art. 21(1) 'compelling legitimate grounds' — two 'compelling legitimate' qualifiers may or may not share interpretation.

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.RM-06: Risk Calculation & Prioritisation Method
nodes.rationale: Meta-methodology reference for physical-environment protection (SR-NIS2-041): enumerates physical hazards and assigns to NIS-availability/integrity dimensions.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.rm-06: risk calculation & prioritisation method

nodes.label: Cross-Regulation Training Polysemy
nodes.source_location: GDPR Art. 39, NIS2 Art. 20(2), CRA Annex I Part II §2(c)
nodes.rationale: Three distinct regulations share the same 'training' polysemy pattern: GDPR C27/C28 (DPO training), NIS2 Art. 20(2) (management-body training), CRA Annex I Part II §2(c) (security update procedures including training).

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 20(2) — Mandatory Management-Body Training
nodes.rationale: Second cross-regulation 'training' polysemy hotspot (first was GDPR Art. 39 DPO training; third is CRA Annex I Part II §2(c)).

nodes.label: CRA Art. 14(8) — User Notification (Machine-Readable)
nodes.rationale: 'Structured, machine-readable format that is easily automatically processable' is CRA-unique; no other regulation requires machine-readable user notification.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 23(1) — Cross-Border Information Reporting
nodes.rationale: 'Cross-border impact' — impact in how many Member States? 'Mere act of notification' shield against increased liability.

nodes.label: Management Body
nodes.rationale: Corporate-governance body with collective approve/oversee/liable obligations under NIS 2 Art. 20(1) and define/approve/oversee/be-responsible under DORA Art. 5(2). Distinct from DPO role.

nodes.label: Presumption of Conformity (CRA Art. 27)
nodes.rationale: CRA Art. 27(1)/(2)/(5)/(8)/(9) machinery via harmonised standards / common specifications / CSA certification. Rebuttable presumption. Does NOT extend cross-regulation - discharges CRA conformity-assessment obligation only, not GDPR/NIS2/DORA/AI Act policy obligations.

nodes.label: Quality Management System (AI Act)
nodes.rationale: AI Act Art. 17(1) QMS documented in systematic and orderly manner with 13-element closed list (a)-(m). Becomes a sub-policy of the integrated policy architecture. Most content-codified of the 5 regulators.

nodes.label: Three Lines of Defence Model
nodes.rationale: DORA Art. 6(4) governance model: operational-management (first line), risk-management and compliance (second line), internal-audit (third line). Compatible with AI Act QMS as governance architecture.

nodes.label: Art. 24 General Testing Programme
nodes.rationale: Sets the general testing programme as integral part of Art. 6 ICT risk-management framework; enumerates test modalities in open list (Art. 25).

nodes.label: Art. 26 Threat-Led Penetration Testing (TLPT)
nodes.rationale: Mandates TLPT on hard 3-year cadence; anchored to TIBER-EU framework (non-binding guidance); part of Chapter IV testing programme.

nodes.label: Art. 27 Requirements for Testers
nodes.rationale: NEW in v0.2; T3 omitted Art. 27 entirely; specifies requirements for testers performing TLPT and other testing.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 26 — Advanced Testing (TLPT)
nodes.rationale: Mandates TLPT at least every 3 years on live production systems. 6 atomic clauses covering cadence, scope, CTPP participation, risk controls, entity identification, and RTS per TIBER-EU.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 26(11) — ESAs RTS Mandate per TIBER-EU
nodes.rationale: Mandates draft RTS developed in agreement with ECB, anchored to non-binding TIBER-EU. Covers scope details in (c)(i) and internal tester requirements in (b).
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 26(11) — esas rts mandate per tiber-eu

nodes.label: DORA Art. 27 — Requirements for TLPT Testers
nodes.rationale: New in v0.2. Creates a two-track tester regime: 5 external-tester requirements (suitability, capabilities, certification, assurance, insurance) and 3 internal-tester additional conditions (CA approval, dedicated resources, external threat-intel provider). Most specific tester-qualification regime in the 5-regulation corpus.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 27 — requirements for tlpt testers

nodes.label: DORA Art. 3(17) — TLPT Definition
nodes.rationale: Defines TLPT (Threat-Led Penetration Testing). Referenced as definitional anchor in CL26-1, CL26-2, CL27-1, and CL27-2.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 6(4)+(6) — Independence + 3 Lines of Defence + Internal Audit
nodes.rationale: 3-lines-of-defence model is specific to EU financial-services law; NIS 2, CRA, GDPR have no equivalent; closest analog is CRD IV Art. 74.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 6(4)+(6) — independence + 3 lines of defence + internal audit

nodes.label: NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(e) — Cybersecurity Risk-Management Measures
nodes.rationale: Cross-regulation comparison: requires 'policies and procedures to assess the effectiveness of cybersecurity risk-management measures' without specifying tester qualifications. DORA Art. 27 identified as most specific tester-qualification regime in the 5-regulation corpus.

nodes.label: Requirement 9.1 - Information Security Policies
nodes.rationale: Volere requirement (integrity, MUST, TEST) establishing information security policies through a documented policy architecture with governance hooks and accountability chain. Depends on 9.1.1-9.1.5. Maps to NIST CSF GV.PO-01, GV.PO-02, GV.RR-02.

nodes.label: Requirement 9.1.1 - GDPR Controller Policies
nodes.rationale: Controller implements appropriate data-protection policies with DPO designation, independence, and Art. 5(2) accountability. Maps to NIST CSF GV.PO-01, GV.PO-02, GV.RM-04, GV.RR-01, GV.RR-02, GV.RR-03, GV.OV-03.

nodes.label: Requirement 9.1.2 - NIS2 Entity Policies
nodes.rationale: Essential and important entities establish policies on risk analysis, IS security, and effectiveness assessment, approved and overseen by the management body. Maps to NIST CSF GV.PO-01, GV.RR-02, GV.OV-01, GV.RM-05.

nodes.label: Requirement 9.1.3 - CRA Manufacturer/OSS Policies
nodes.rationale: Manufacturer and OSS-steward cybersecurity policies with verifiable documentation, CVD, support-period, and presumption of conformity. Maps to NIST CSF GV.PO-01, GV.PO-02, GV.SC-01, GV.SC-04, GV.OC-03.

nodes.label: Requirement 9.1.4 - DORA ICT Framework
nodes.rationale: Financial entity operates a sound, comprehensive, well-documented ICT risk-management framework with three-lines-of-defence and identified, classified, documented ICT assets. Maps to NIST CSF GV.PO-01, GV.PO-02, GV.RM-04, GV.RR-01, GV.RR-02, GV.OC-03, GV.OC-04, GV.RM-05.

nodes.label: Requirement 9.1.5 - AI Act QMS
nodes.rationale: Provider of high-risk AI system operates a documented QMS with at least 13 enumerated aspects and instructions for use enabling deployer-interpretable transparency. Maps to NIST CSF GV.PO-01, GV.PO-02, GV.RM-01, GV.RM-04, GV.OC-03, GV.OC-04.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 4 — Security Objectives & Rules
nodes.rationale: Contains SR-GDPR-054 (child/transfer consent), SR-GDPR-055 (adequacy inventory), SR-GDPR-057 (derogation fallback), SR-GDPR-058 (BCRs), SR-GDPR-060 (joint controllers).

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-01.4: Data Protection (Accuracy/Integrity)
nodes.rationale: Sub-domain for accuracy and integrity of stored data. Referenced by SO-GDPR-001, SO-GDPR-003, SR-GDPR-001, SR-GDPR-005, SR-GDPR-006.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 6(1): Six lawfulness bases for processing
nodes.rationale: Core provision listing consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public interest, and legitimate interests as alternative bases.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 6(1): six lawfulness bases for processing

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 19 — Communication of rectification or erasure to recipient
nodes.rationale: Downstream cascade obligation referenced in SR-GDPR-022; controller must communicate rectification/erasure to each recipient unless impossible or disproportionate effort.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 19 — communication of rectification or erasure to recipient

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 5(1) — Principles relating to processing of personal data
nodes.rationale: Gateway principles (a)-(f) referenced throughout: lawfulness/fairness/transparency (a), purpose limitation (b), data minimisation (c), accuracy (d), storage limitation (e), integrity/confidentiality (f).
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 5(1) — principles relating to processing of personal data

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 9 — Processing of special categories of personal data
nodes.rationale: Prohibition on nine special categories with ten exceptions; referenced in SR-GDPR-028; Art. 9(1) prohibition, (2)(a) explicit consent, (2)(g) substantial public interest.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 9 — processing of special categories of personal data

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(2): CIA+A Cross-State Protection
nodes.rationale: Core provision requiring high standards of availability, authenticity, integrity, and confidentiality of data whether at rest, in use, or in transit.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 33 — Notification of personal data breach to supervisory authority
nodes.rationale: 72-hour notification obligation referenced across SR-GDPR-014, 015, 016, 017, 018; Art. 33(1) 72h clock, (2) processor notification, (3) four-element content, (4) phased disclosure.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 33 — notification of personal data breach to supervisory authority

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 34 — Communication of personal data breach to data subject
nodes.rationale: High-risk data-subject notification referenced across SR-GDPR-015, 019, 020, 021; Art. 34(1) high-risk trigger, (2) content, (3)(a) encryption exception, (3)(b) subsequent measures, (3)(c) disproportionate effort.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 34 — communication of personal data breach to data subject

nodes.label: Floor-within-Ceiling Reconciliation (GDPR ↔ AI Act)
nodes.rationale: AI Act Art. 19(1) ≥6-month hard floor is a subset of GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) 'as long as necessary' envelope. NOT a tension — the two regimes operate on different time scales (one is a floor, one is a ceiling). OJ-consistent reconciliation.

nodes.label: GDPR ↔ CRA Substantively Scope-Disjoint
nodes.rationale: GDPR compliance records (RoPA, consent, processor contracts, breach notifications, DPIA) and CRA product documentation (Annex VII §5-§8, Annex VII §3, Annex I Part II (3), SBOM) operate on different record types at different triggers. N (typically) — no overlap on a single event at a single party.

nodes.label: NIS 2 Fully Out-of-Scope at D-10.2
nodes.rationale: NIS 2 OJ Art. 21(2)(j) does not mention logging, audit trails, or traceability. Per CRDA T3-vs-text gap (synthesis §8, NIS2-C22). No NIS 2 sub-SO emitted. Companies with NIS 2 only have no D-10.2 sub-SO to apply.

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 12 (Per-Article SO+SR)
nodes.rationale: Per-article split containing SO-AIACT-005 (Art. 12(1)+(2) logging) and SO-AIACT-006 (Art. 19(1) retention) with SR-AIACT-007/008/009. Documents T5 mapping error on Art. 12(4).

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 19 (Per-Article SO+SR)
nodes.rationale: Per-article split for Art. 19(1) log retention. Contains SR-AIACT-007/008/009 and SR-AIACT-022 (serious incident reporting) + SR-AIACT-024 (GPAI incident reporting).

nodes.label: SO-CRA-069 (CRA Per-Reg SO)
nodes.rationale: Parent SO for CRA technical documentation; inherited by SO-D-10.2.CRA.

nodes.label: SO-DORA-031 (DORA Per-Reg SO)
nodes.rationale: Parent SO for DORA information security policy; inherited partially by SO-D-10.2.DORA.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-080
nodes.rationale: Source security rule for CRA Annex VII §3 risk-assessment documentation.

nodes.label: SR-CRA-088
nodes.rationale: Source security rule for CRA Annex VII §5-§8 technical documentation.

nodes.label: GDPR Article 27: Representative of controller/processor in the Union
nodes.rationale: Non-EU controllers/processors must designate in writing a Union representative. Exception: occasional, small-scale, low-risk processing.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 27: representative of controller/processor in the union

nodes.label: GDPR Article 39: Tasks of the DPO
nodes.rationale: Art. 39(1)(a) inform and advise; Art. 39(1)(b) awareness-raising and training. DPO as internal awareness and training catalyst.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 39: tasks of the dpo

nodes.label: CRA-CL46: Art. 13(21) immediate corrective measures + withdrawal + recall
nodes.norm_label: cra-cl46: art. 13(21) immediate corrective measures + withdrawal + recall

nodes.label: DORA Art. 21 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering the full DORA ICT risk-management framework: CIA+A protection, risk identification, resilience testing, incident management, third-party risk, change management, training, and governance.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 27 — Designation of Representative by Written Mandate
nodes.rationale: Art. 27(1) written designation requirement; Art. 27(2)(a) conjunctive exception (occasional AND small-scale AND low-risk).
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 27 — designation of representative by written mandate

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 39 — Tasks of the DPO
nodes.rationale: Art. 39(1)(a) inform and advise; Art. 39(1)(b) awareness-raising and training. Establishes the DPO as internal awareness and training catalyst.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr art. 39 — tasks of the dpo

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 9 — Security Objectives & Rules
nodes.rationale: Comprehensive per-article split covering the full AI risk-management lifecycle (Art. 9), accuracy/robustness/cybersecurity (Art. 15), QMS (Art. 17), PMM (Art. 72), incident reporting (Art. 73), and GPAI obligations (Art. 55).
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 9 — security objectives & rules

nodes.label: Berry Framework (Linguistic Ambiguity Analysis)
nodes.rationale: A systematic framework for identifying and classifying linguistic ambiguities in regulatory text. Categories include VAG (vague), POLY (polysemous), COORD (coordination), SCOPE-Q (scope qualifier). Used to flag S2/S3 severity readings across all DORA clauses.

nodes.label: T3 Clause Mapping (C14–C38)
nodes.rationale: A prior mapping layer (v0.1) that assigned T3 clauses to DORA articles. v0.2 identified major distortions: C14 imposed need-to-know/least-privilege not in OJ text; C16 imposed MFA not in OJ text; C28 imposed role-specific training not in OJ text. T3 omitted 19 clauses that v0.2 adds.

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 55 — GPAI Systemic Risk Obligations
nodes.rationale: Art. 55(1)(a) requires model evaluation with adversarial testing for systemic risk mitigation. Art. 55(1)(c) requires GPAI serious incident reporting to the AI Office. The 'systemic risks' term is borrowed from financial-services regulation (DORA) but applied more broadly to AI.
nodes.norm_label: ai act art. 55 — gpai systemic risk obligations

nodes.label: CRA Annex I Part I — Product Cybersecurity Baseline
nodes.rationale: The Cyber Resilience Act Annex I provides the parallel product-cybersecurity baseline. DORA's 'appropriate' qualifier follows the same Berry pattern as CRA Annex I Part I(1) chapeau. CRA C07 'cybersecurity' POLY is referenced as a parallel definitional gap.
nodes.norm_label: cra annex i part i — product cybersecurity baseline

nodes.label: DORA Art. 10 — Detection Mechanisms
nodes.rationale: Requires mechanisms to promptly detect anomalous activities, multiple layers of control, alert thresholds, and sufficient monitoring resources. DRSPs have additional trade-report checking obligations.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 11 — Business Continuity
nodes.rationale: Mandates comprehensive ICT business continuity policy with five objectives, recovery plans, BIA, testing cadence, crisis management function, and cost reporting.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 12 — Backup and Recovery
nodes.rationale: Requires backup policies, physically and logically segregated restoration systems, redundant ICT capacities, CSD secondary processing sites, and RTO/RPO objectives.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 13 — Threat Intelligence and Learning
nodes.rationale: Requires capabilities to gather vulnerability and cyber-threat information, post-incident reviews, lessons propagation, effectiveness monitoring, training, and technology monitoring.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 13 — threat intelligence and learning

nodes.label: DORA Art. 14 — Crisis Communication
nodes.rationale: Requires crisis communication plans enabling responsible disclosure of major ICT-related incidents or vulnerabilities to clients, counterparts, and the public, with internal/external communication policies and a designated spokesperson.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 16 — Simplified Framework
nodes.rationale: Provides a simplified ICT risk management framework for small and non-interconnected entities. Structurally parallel to Art. 9(4) but at lower granularity, omitting access control, change management, and patches as standalone control families.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 28 — ICT Third-Party Risk (General Principles)
nodes.rationale: The longest single article in DORA (10 paragraphs). Establishes full responsibility for ICT third-party risk, multi-vendor strategy, register of information, pre-contractual assessment, information security standards, termination/exit strategies, and ESAs ITS/RTS.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 28 — ict third-party risk (general principles)

nodes.label: DORA Art. 29 — ICT Concentration Risk Assessment
nodes.rationale: NEW in v0.2 (T3 omitted). Requires preliminary assessment of ICT concentration risk at entity level, covering non-substitutable CTPPs, multiple contracts with same/closely-connected CTPPs, subcontracting risk, and third-country law enforcement.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 29 — ict concentration risk assessment

nodes.label: DORA Art. 30 — Key Contractual Provisions
nodes.rationale: Enumerates 15 key contractual provisions: 9 in Art. 30(2) for all ICT services and 6 in Art. 30(3) for critical or important functions. The contract-architecture 'coração' of DORA's third-party regime.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 7 — ICT Systems Baseline
nodes.rationale: Establishes the baseline requirement for financial entities to use and maintain updated ICT systems, protocols and tools that are appropriate, reliable, sufficiently capacitated, and technologically resilient.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 8 — Identification and Risk Assessment
nodes.rationale: Requires identification, classification, and documentation of ICT-supported business functions, continuous risk-source identification, major-change risk assessment, and critical-asset mapping.
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 8 — identification and risk assessment

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9 — ICT Security (The Hinge)
nodes.rationale: Art. 9(4) is identified as the operational core of DORA, establishing six mandatory control families: info-security policy, network/infrastructure, access control, authentication+encryption, change management, and patches/updates. The 6-way AND in 9(4)(e) is one of the longest coordinated obligations in DORA.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 17 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split (SO + SR) generated from 01_SecurityObjectives.md and 02_SecurityRules_NIST.md. Covers incident management process, major incident reporting, crisis communication, audit rights, risk management framework, asset inventory, and continuous monitoring.

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-09.1: Governance (Accountability)
nodes.rationale: Sub-domain for controller accountability and demonstrability. Referenced by SO-GDPR-016, SO-GDPR-027.

nodes.label: D-10.2 Audit Logging & Traceability (Main Document)
nodes.rationale: Central aggregation document for the D-10.2 subdomain covering 4 of 5 regulations (GDPR, CRA, DORA, AI Act) with 0 emergent tensions and 1 floor-within-ceiling reconciliation pattern.

nodes.label: CRA Art. 27 — Security Objectives & Rules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split of CRA Art. 27 covering presumption of conformity, support-period determination, effective and regular tests, and Class II conformity routes.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 18 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering NIS2 Article 18 effectiveness assessment policies and procedures, mapped to NIST CSF GV.PO-01, ID.IM-01, GV.OV-03.

nodes.label: D-10.3 Compliance Testing (Volere Requirements)
nodes.rationale: High-level compliance testing requirement establishing 5 parallel testing programmes across GDPR, NIS 2, CRA, DORA, and AI Act with no OJ-level consolidation rule for testing.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 35 — DPIA
nodes.rationale: Art. 35(1) trigger for high-risk processing. Art. 35(7) four content items. Art. 36(1) prior consultation where residual risk remains high.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(e) — Security in acquisition/development/maintenance + vuln handling
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 21(2)(e) — security in acquisition/development/maintenance + vuln handling

nodes.label: DORA Art. 10: Anomaly Detection
nodes.rationale: Establishes detection substrate for anomalous activities and SPOF identification, operationalised by Chapter III incident management.

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 9 — Special Categories
nodes.rationale: Nine prohibited categories, each independently triggering Art. 9(1). Ten Art. 9(2) exceptions. Art. 9(2)(a) explicit consent sits above Art. 4(11) baseline.

nodes.label: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(d) — Supply chain security (direct suppliers)
nodes.norm_label: nis2 art. 21(2)(d) — supply chain security (direct suppliers)

nodes.label: Regulation (EU) 2019/881 (EU Cybersecurity Certification)
nodes.rationale: Framework for European cybersecurity certification schemes. Art. 8(1) sets assurance-level floor at 'substantial' for critical products. CSA schemes adopted under this regulation provide presumption of conformity under CRA Art. 27(8).

nodes.label: GDPR Article 5 – Principles relating to processing of personal data
nodes.rationale: Art. 5(1)(a) lawfulness/fairness/transparency; Art. 5(1)(b) purpose limitation; Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation; Art. 5(1)(f) integrity/confidentiality; Art. 5(2) accountability. Gateway principles for all processing.
nodes.norm_label: gdpr article 5 – principles relating to processing of personal data

nodes.label: CRA Article 14: Actively exploited vulnerability and severe incident reporting
nodes.rationale: Establishes the three-tier temporal notification pattern (24h/72h/14d for AEV; 24h/72h/1m for SI) and the user-notification duty with CSIRT fallback.
nodes.norm_label: cra article 14: actively exploited vulnerability and severe incident reporting

nodes.label: Sub-domain D-04.1: Incident Response — Detection/Management
nodes.rationale: Covers ICT-related incident detection, management, and notification. Primary sub-domain for SR-DORA-016.

nodes.label: DORA Art. 9(4)(a): Information security policy for CIA+A
nodes.rationale: Top-level policy instrument complementing Art. 6(1) framework; co-exists with GDPR Art. 5, NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(d), CRA conformity duties
nodes.norm_label: dora art. 9(4)(a): information security policy for cia+a

nodes.label: GDPR Art. 44-45: Cross-Border Transfer Principles
nodes.rationale: Art. 44 umbrella principle, Art. 45(1) adequacy exemption, Art. 45(3) periodic review at least every four years. Schrems II substantial-equivalence test governs.

nodes.label: GDPR Arts. 44–49 — Cross-Border Transfers

nodes.label: CRDA-Flagged GENUINE TENSION: CRA Opt-out vs Mandatory Monitoring
nodes.rationale: CRA Annex I Part I (2)(l) user opt-out conflicts with GDPR Art. 32(2), NIS2 Art. 21(2)(b), and DORA Art. 8(1) mandatory monitoring. The OJ does not resolve this conflict. Propagates to 3 of 10 pairs (GDPR↔CRA primary, NIS2↔CRA, CRA↔DORA). Requires Layer 2 OJ-level resolution. Phase 1 entities must maintain mandatory monitoring on entity layer regardless of CRA opt-out at product layer.
nodes.norm_label: crda-flagged genuine tension: cra opt-out vs mandatory monitoring

nodes.label: DORA-Led Stack for Financial Entities
nodes.rationale: DORA Art. 8(1)/Art. 9(1) continuous monitoring is broader (security AND functioning) than GDPR Art. 32(2) 5-risk-type detection. For DORA financial entities that are also controllers, DORA monitoring discharges the continuous-monitoring obligation and GDPR detection becomes a sub-component. DORA Art. 10(1) prompt anomalous-activity detection adds the operational detection layer.

nodes.label: Layered 5-Monitoring-Architecture
nodes.rationale: The architectural pattern where 5 distinct monitoring mandates at 5 distinct scope layers (entity personal-data, entity operational, product on-device, entity ICT-system, AI-system lifecycle) are stacked rather than collapsed. Each layer has distinct anchor, trigger, threshold, recipient, and content template. The high-level SO surfaces the common duty without collapsing per-reg perspectives.

nodes.label: NIS2↔DORA EQUAL Classification
nodes.rationale: Both regulations impose continuous-monitoring obligations (NIS2 Art. 21(2)(b) detection capability vs DORA Art. 8(1) continuously monitor and control). For DORA financial entities, DORA Art. 9(1) discharges both obligations — DORA-dominant. For non-financial NSIEs, NIS2 is the authority. The EQUAL classification preserves the OJ literal parallel; dominant-authority reading is the operational consequence of DORA-direct-applicability vs NIS2-MS-transposition asymmetry.

nodes.label: NIS 2 ↔ DORA EQUAL Pair (DORA-Dominant)
nodes.rationale: For DORA significant financial entities that are also NSIEs, the DORA-led stack discharges both DORA's dedicated testing obligation and NIS 2's Art. 21(2)(f) partial-coverage effectiveness-assessment. For non-financial NSIEs, NIS 2 is the authority. Dominant-authority reading is the operational consequence of DORA-direct-applicability vs NIS 2-MS-transposition asymmetry.

nodes.label: No OJ-Level Consolidation Rule for Testing
nodes.rationale: All 5 regulations impose testing with different scopes, methodologies, and cadences. No OJ-level consolidation rule exists. Phase 1 entities must implement 5 parallel testing programmes. Structurally different from 9.2 where CRA Art. 13(4) sentence 2 consolidates AI Act Art. 9 risk-management.
nodes.norm_label: no oj-level consolidation rule for testing

nodes.label: Requirement 10.1 — Layered 5-Monitoring-Architecture
nodes.rationale: Volere requirement (MUST, TEST) establishing continuous security monitoring through a layered 5-monitoring-architecture with 5 distinct monitoring mandates at 5 distinct scope layers. Depends on sub-requirements 10.1.1–10.1.5. NIST CSF: DE.CM-01, DE.CM-09, DE.AE-02, ID.IM-04.

nodes.label: Requirement 10.1.1 — GDPR 5-Risk-Type Detection
nodes.rationale: Controller and processor monitor personal-data processing systems for 5 Art. 32(2) risk types with breach-becoming-aware clock anchoring Art. 33(1) 72-hour notification. Derives from SO-10.1.GDPR. For DORA financial entities, DORA-led stack discharges this obligation with GDPR detection as sub-component.

nodes.label: Requirement 10.1.2 — NIS2 All-Hazards Detection
nodes.rationale: Essential and important entities establish incident-handling capability with 6-action lifecycle covering all-hazards detection. Partial coverage — no dedicated continuous-monitoring mandate. For DORA financial entities, DORA-dominant stack discharges this obligation.

nodes.label: Requirement 10.1.3 — CRA On-Device Monitoring with Opt-out
nodes.rationale: Product with digital elements records and monitors internal activity with user opt-out mechanism and vulnerability-reporting contact address. Origin of the CRDA-flagged GENUINE TENSION — CRA is the only regulator permitting user opt-out from monitoring.
nodes.norm_label: requirement 10.1.3 — cra on-device monitoring with opt-out

nodes.label: Requirement 10.1.4 — DORA Continuous ICT Monitoring
nodes.rationale: Financial entity continuously monitors and controls ICT-system security and functioning with prompt anomalous-activity detection through multi-layered controls and continuous ICT risk identification. DORA-led stack for financial entities. NIS2↔DORA EQUAL on continuous-monitoring dimension.

nodes.label: Requirement 10.1.5 — AI Act Post-Market Monitoring
nodes.rationale: Provider of high-risk AI system establishes post-market monitoring system proportionate to AI technology risks, actively and systematically collecting/documenting/analysing data. Adds analysis-to-risk-management feedback loop. NOT subject to user opt-out (unlike CRA).

nodes.label: Req 10.3 — 5 Parallel Testing Programmes HL
nodes.rationale: The HL does NOT collapse the 5 testing mandates into a single testing programme; the 5 parallel testing programmes are the operative consequence with distinct scopes, methodologies, and cadences. NO OJ-level consolidation rule exists for testing (CRDA-deep line 29).

nodes.label: Req 10.3.1 — GDPR Entity-Level Effectiveness-Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Entity-level effectiveness-evaluation of technical and organisational measures with 'regularly testing' cadence + DPIA review on risk change per GDPR Art. 32(1)(d) + Art. 35(11). Recipient: data subject + DPA.

nodes.label: Req 10.3.2 — NIS 2 Effectiveness-Assessment (Partial Coverage)
nodes.rationale: Entity-level policies and procedures to assess effectiveness of cybersecurity risk-management measures per NIS 2 Art. 21(2)(f). Partial coverage — no dedicated testing-programme mandate beyond the effectiveness-assessment dimension. Cadence entity-discretionary under Recital 56.

nodes.label: Req 10.3.3 — CRA Product-Level Conformity-Assessment
nodes.rationale: Product-level conformity-assessment via OJ-codified modules (Module A or Module B+C and H) + effective and regular tests + test reports per CRA Annex I Part II (3) + Annex VII §6 + Annex VIII. Module selection depends on product classification Class I/II/critical.

nodes.label: Req 10.3.4 — DORA Digital Operational Resilience Testing Programme
nodes.rationale: Financial-entity testing programme with 12-way modalities portfolio + TLPT for significant entities per DORA Art. 24(1) + Art. 25(1) + Art. 26(1). DORA-led stack: broader than GDPR/NIS 2 testing; GDPR effectiveness-evaluation becomes sub-component for DORA financial entities that are also controllers.
nodes.norm_label: req 10.3.4 — dora digital operational resilience testing programme

nodes.label: Req 10.3.5 — AI Act AI-System-Level Testing
nodes.rationale: AI-system-level testing for risk management + real-world-conditions testing per Art. 60 + accuracy/robustness/cybersecurity baseline throughout AI-system lifecycle per AI Act Art. 9(6) + Art. 9(7) + Art. 15(1). Distinct lifecycle anchor from point-in-time testing of the other 4 regulators.

nodes.label: Requirement 10.2 (Volere Audit)
nodes.rationale: Volere requirement 10.2: layered 4-audit-records architecture with 4 distinct mandates at 4 distinct scope layers. Priority MUST, verification TEST. Dependencies: 10.2.1-10.2.4.

nodes.label: Requirement 10.2.1 (GDPR Compliance Records)
nodes.rationale: Controller/processor maintain compliance records in writing/electronic form with integrity + traceability per Art. 30(3) + Art. 5(2) + Art. 31. NIST CSF: PR.DS-11, PR.PT-01, DE.CM-01, GV.PO-02.

nodes.label: Requirement 10.2.2 (CRA Documentation)
nodes.rationale: Manufacturer maintains technical documentation + risk-assessment + test reports + SBOM on MSA reasoned request during support period. NIST CSF: PR.DS-11, PR.IP-06, GV.PO-02, ID.RA-04.

nodes.label: Requirement 10.2.3 (DORA InfoSec Policy)
nodes.rationale: Financial entity develops information security policy with CIA+A rules; logging implicit in CIA+A monitoring (partial coverage). NIST CSF: GV.PO-01, PR.DS-12, GV.OC-03.

nodes.label: Requirement 10.2.4 (AI Act Event Logging)
nodes.rationale: High-risk AI system automatic event logging + traceability appropriate to intended purpose + provider log retention ≥6-month floor. NIST CSF: PR.PS-04, DE.CM-09, DE.AE-03, RC.RP-03.

nodes.label: NIST CSF 2.0 — Respond (RS)
nodes.rationale: NIST CSF 2.0 Respond function subcategories (RS.CO-02, RS.MA-02) for incident reporting and triage

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OC-03: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity are understood and managed

nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.oc-03: legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity are understood and managed

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.PO-02: Cybersecurity processes and procedures for implementing the cybersecurity policy are established, communicated, and enforced

nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.po-02: cybersecurity processes and procedures for implementing the cybersecurity policy are established, communicated, and enforced

nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.at-01: all users are informed and trained on cybersecurity topics

nodes.label: AI Act Art. 5 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
nodes.rationale: Per-article split covering six-month minimum log retention (Art. 19(1)) and deployer measures aligned with provider instructions (Art. 26(1)).

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.RA-01: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded
nodes.rationale: Supplies the asset-vulnerability layer for continuous risk identification — vulnerability scanning, CVE-feed ingestion, authenticated validation, and validated records tied to entity asset inventory.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.ra-01: vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.RA-03: Threats, both internal and external, are identified, recorded, and prioritized
nodes.rationale: Supplies the threat-intelligence layer — internal-source threat catalogues and external-source feeds with priority scoring; must weight interconnectedness, shared CTPP exposure, and shared settlement-infrastructure dependency per DORA inter-entity qualifier.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.ra-03: threats, both internal and external, are identified, recorded, and prioritized

nodes.label: NIST CSF GV.OV-02: Organizational cybersecurity risk management strategy is reviewed and adjusted
nodes.rationale: Anchors the testing programme as a strategic-review instrument whose findings must feed strategy adjustment, ensuring the programme is integral to the framework rather than parallel.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf gv.ov-02: organizational cybersecurity risk management strategy is reviewed and adjusted

nodes.label: NIST CSF ID.RA-01 (testing context): Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded
nodes.rationale: Supplies the validated vulnerability substrate that the twelve-modality portfolio operationalises into concrete testing outputs traceable to known vulnerabilities.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf id.ra-01 (testing context): vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded

nodes.label: NIST CSF PR.PS-06: Secure software development practices are integrated and monitored throughout the SDLC
nodes.rationale: Closes the SDLC dimension by ensuring secure-development controls are themselves tested rather than assumed, completing modality coverage on the application-layer side.
nodes.norm_label: nist csf pr.ps-06: secure software development practices are integrated and monitored throughout the sdlc

nodes.label: DORA Art. 25 — SecurityObjectives & SecurityRules
